items.title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Keep requests with computed context out of the prefill region
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Fix KV-cache context loss under Model Runner V2, originally observed with `ROCM_AITER_FA`.

`sort_batch_req_ids` sorted requests without considering their already-computed context. A request continuing a prompt (an *extend*) could therefore end up after a fresh prefill and be misclassified as a prefill by `split_decodes_prefills_and_extends`. The prefill region is attended **without reading the KV cache**, so the misclassified request silently loses its context — wrong output, no error.

This PR makes the sort context-aware and, separately, protects the prefill boundary for the cases where ordering alone cannot fix it.

Related: #56624 and #58013.

### Changes by file

**`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`** — `sort_batch_req_ids` now receives `num_computed_tokens` and `req_id_to_index`, so it can tell an extend from a fresh prefill instead of inferring it from query length alone. The state array is indexed by **state slot**, not by batch position, which is what made the old key wrong for reordered batches. Drafted rows skip the context lookup, so the extra work is avoided where it cannot matter.

**`vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py`** — `split_decodes_prefills_and_extends` moves the prefill boundary past the last request carrying context:

```python
has_context = (seq_lens != query_lens) & (query_lens > 0)
context_rows = torch.nonzero(has_context).flatten()
if context_rows.numel() > 0:
    first_prefill = max(first_prefill, int(context_rows[-1]) + 1)
```

Sorting alone is not sufficient here: the scheduler can pad a context-less one-token prompt with placeholder draft rows, and those rows must stay at the front of the batch. They can therefore sit ahead of context-bearing requests, leaving no ordering that is safe. The clamp makes the boundary safe regardless of order. Thanks @okorzh-amd for identifying this case.

No GPU kernels, launch configurations or dtypes are changed; the diff contains zero non-Python files.

## Test Plan

```bash
# unit tests
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py -v

# CUDA end-to-end: two arms from the same official image, differing only by this diff
docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0
curl -sL https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59098.diff -o /tmp/pr.diff
docker run -d --name b --entrypoint sleep -v /tmp/pr.diff:/tmp/pr.diff:ro vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0 infinity
docker exec -w /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages b bash -c \
  "git apply -p1 --include='vllm/*' /tmp/pr.diff && find vllm -name __pycache__ -type d -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null; true"
docker commit --change 'ENTRYPOINT ["vllm","serve"]' --change 'CMD []' b vllm-pr59098:with-fix && docker rm -f b

# confirm the patch landed in one arm and not the other (3 params vs 5)
for i in vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0 vllm-pr59098:with-fix; do docker run --rm --entrypoint python3 $i -c \
  'import inspect;from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner import sort_batch_req_ids as f;print(len(inspect.signature(f).parameters))'; done

# serve each arm; <FA> = 3 (Hopper default) or 2; omit <DCP_ARGS> for the DCP=1 control
docker run -d --gpus '"device=0,1,2,3"' --ipc=host --shm-size=16g -p 8000:8000 \
  -e VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN -e VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 <IMAGE> \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 2 --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 16 \
  --attention-config '{"flash_attn_version": <FA>}' --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --block-size 16 --enforce-eager --seed 0

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --limit 200 \
  --model_args "model=Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32"
```

## Test Result

### Correctness

- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py`: **20 passed, 0 skipped** (7 newly added). Against merge-base production code the same file gives **7 failed, 13 passed** — all 7 new tests fail without the fix, so they genuinely cover the bug.
- Relevant suites: **214 passed** on this branch versus **208 passed** on the merge-base. One unrelated gated-model failure occurs on both.
- A nine-scenario splitter probe reproduced **4 incorrect classifications** on the base implementation; all 4 are corrected here.
- Mutation checks: removing the clamp fails 3 tests; replacing state-slot indexing with batch-position indexing fails the dedicated sort-key regression test.
- **MI350, `ROCM_AITER_FA`, MRv2** — @engint-cerebras independently measured improved prompt-logprob agreement against the unchunked reference: **1.23 → 0.015** (GPT-OSS-120B chunked prefill) and **1.82 → 0.11** (prefix-cache reuse). See their review comment for full methodology.

### Performance impact

Both changed functions are host-side Python and launch no kernels. Microbenchmarks on the H200 box (Intel Xeon 8480C) and an AMD EPYC 9575F host, median of 3 interleaved runs, batch 1024, µs per call:

| Workload | Host CPU | `sort_batch_req_ids` | `split_decodes_prefills_and_extends` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Decode-only | Intel Xeon 8480C | 93.60 → 109.92 (+17.8%) | not reached (early return) |
| | AMD EPYC 9575F | 50.47 → 57.27 (+13.5%) | not reached (early return) |
| Mixed | Intel Xeon 8480C | 186.51 → 249.25 (+32.6%) | 45.10 → 65.70 (+45.7%) |
| | AMD EPYC 9575F | 92.23 → 120.40 (+30.9%) | 20.59 → 29.06 (+41.1%) |
| Speculative decode | Intel Xeon 8480C | 102.73 → 119.58 (+16.4%) | 46.06 → 65.97 (+43.2%) |
| | AMD EPYC 9575F | 54.08 → 61.01 (+13.3%) | 20.65 → 29.15 (+41.5%) |



### CUDA-side impact

Both changes are in shared code, so stated explicitly. Measured on 4x H200 (SM 9.0), `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, TP=4, DCP=2, FLASH_ATTN, MRv2, chunked prefill, prefix caching, greedy — the GQA+DCP configuration `tests/distributed/test_context_parallel.py` already uses.

**Summary: no output change on any default NVIDIA configuration.** Three regimes:

- **DCP=1** — the PR cannot apply. `flash_attn.py` only calls `split_dcp_context_queries` when `dcp_world_size > 1`, so the modified splitter is **never entered**. Measured: 0 calls, both arms.

- **DCP=2 with FA3/FA4 (Hopper/Blackwell default)** — the splitter **is** entered (480 calls, all via `split_dcp_context_queries`) and the PR **does** change what it returns: without it, 32 calls per run place a context-carrying request at or after the prefill boundary; with it, 0. But the result is **never read** — its only consumer, `should_split_fa2_dcp_context_attention`, short-circuits on `fa_version == 2`. So the computation is corrected while output stays bit-identical: 38/38 token ids, 0.000000 max logprob delta, gsm8k 0.550 both arms. The defect is therefore **latent rather than absent** on current NVIDIA defaults, and becomes live wherever FA2 is selected — the default on pre-Hopper NVIDIA GPUs, and forced for ALiBi and for Blackwell `head_size=256` under DCP.

- **DCP=2 with FA2** — the gate opens, the value is read, and `run_split_fa2_dcp_context_attention` slices the batch at that boundary, so behaviour genuinely changes (30/38 requests).

<details>
<summary>Why the FA2 accuracy numbers cannot be used to judge this PR</summary>

FA2+DCP carries a **separate pre-existing defect**. Under DCP a rank can legitimately hold zero local context for a request; FA2's varlen kernel returns `+inf` as that row's log-sum-exp where `-inf` is correct, corrupting the cross-rank LSE merge. Measured: 112 calls, 56 with a zero-local-context decode row, the same 56 returning a non-finite LSE.

The configuration does not even reproduce run to run — identical greedy runs agree on 0/6 requests in **both** arms, while FA3+DCP=2 and FA2+DCP=1 both reproduce 6/6. gsm8k is 0.005 with and 0.020 without this PR, both far below the 0.550 reference and statistically indistinguishable (Fisher exact p=0.37).

That corruption is in the **decode** group, whereas this PR's clamp adjusts the **prefill** group, so the two are mechanically independent. It reproduces in the stock `v0.32.0` image, so this PR neither causes nor cures it. I will file it separately.
</details>

### Scope of CUDA validation

H200 testing covered the shared sorting path, confirmed the DCP splitter call path with in-worker instrumentation, and included a full DCP correctness comparison: 38 requests spanning decode-only, chunked prefill, mixed decode/extend/fresh batches, prefix-cache reuse and varied computed-context lengths, run in both arms at DCP=1 and DCP=2 under both FA2 and FA3, compared on exact token ids and prompt logprobs, plus gsm8k on all six arm/DCP/FA combinations.

**Not covered:** the other CUDA consumers of `split_decodes_and_prefills` that the reordering can reach — `gdn_attn.py`, `mamba_attn.py`, `linear_attn.py`, `mla/indexer.py`, `mla/sparse_swa.py`, `turboquant_attn.py`. Only FlashInfer was exercised (bit-identical, 20/20 requests, non-DCP single GPU). My earlier CPU-level sweep saw `num_decodes` drift on 2,115 of 20,000 batches containing a decode, so this is the most valuable remaining target; happy to run any of them before merge. Also not covered: speculative decoding under DCP, DCP > 2, MLA and FLASHINFER DCP backends, CUDA graphs (`enforce_eager=True` throughout), and DCP on pre-Hopper NVIDIA, where FA2 is the default and the boundary would therefore be consumed.

---

<details>
<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

</details>

items.title: [Attention] Allow num_splits > 1 on FA2 for speculative decode
items.body:
> **DRAFT — blocked on [vllm-project/flash-attention#176](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/176).**
> Do not merge until that lands **and** `GIT_TAG` in `cmake/external_projects/vllm_flash_attn.cmake` is bumped past it. Merging earlier replaces a clean `NotImplementedError` with a `RuntimeError` raised from the unpatched `.so` — strictly worse for users.

## What this removes

```python
if num_splits > 1:
    raise NotImplementedError("FA2 does not support num_splits > 1")
```

Two lines, `vllm/vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py`.

## Why it exists, and why it can go

It mirrors the C++ `TORCH_CHECK(num_splits <= 1, "not supported for varlen paged KV")`. That check is real: the FA2 combine kernel addressed O and LSE through `o_batch_stride`, which is **0** in a true varlen call, so it folded every sequence onto sequence 0. Correct at batch 1, silently wrong above it.

flash-attention#176 addresses O and LSE through `cu_seqlens_q` and skips rows past `actual_seqlen_q`, so the restriction no longer holds.

## Why this matters

`set_params_splitkv` is gated on `seqlenq_ngroups_swapped`, which requires `max_seqlen_q == 1`. Speculative decoding makes the verify pass carry `q_len = K+1`, so **split-K is silently disabled for every spec-decode step** — MTP, EAGLE, Medusa, draft-model and n-gram alike. The decode-attention grid collapses from 172 to 12 blocks: 12 of 128 SMs get work, ~3.5% of DRAM peak.

Measured end to end on RTX 4090 sm_89, Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ-INT4, TP2, MTP K=5, batch 1, ISL 16384, bf16 KV, clocks locked:

| arm | tok/s | TPOT ms | accept_len | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (x3) | 70.0 | 14.28 | 3.11 | 44.42 |
| patched (x2) | **108.9** | **9.19** | **3.20** | **29.41** |

**+55.4% tok/s, −35.6% TPOT**, noise ±0.07%, TTFT flat. Acceptance length rises slightly because split-K lands closer to an fp64 oracle. Full correctness matrix (96 cases incl. batch > 1 and non-uniform query lengths, red-before-green against unpatched vs patched `.so`) is in flash-attention#176.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR in this repo touches this guard; searched for `num_splits`/spec-decode/flash-attention combinations.

## AI assistance

**AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change.** The change and all measurements above were produced with AI assistance and reviewed by the human submitter.

items.title: [Attention][Perf] Reduce FlashInfer DCP prefill overhead
items.body:
## Purpose

DCP prefill copies LSE views, allocates suffix attention buffers, and launches a separate base conversion after combining context shards. This PR removes that work and reduces repeated host preparation through the existing FlashInfer interfaces:

- Request suffix `lse_base="ln", lse_layout="NH"` and pass a transposed view to the final merge.
- Let AG/RS, AG/AR and A2A combine independently select the output LSE base. Weights remain in the input base; conversion happens at the final store. Existing callers preserve their input base by default.
- Request natural-log context LSE directly, removing the post-combine conversion and allocation. The final merge consumes the actual strides of the returned head slice.
- Write suffix attention into the caller's final O and merge in place when layout and dtype permit. Other layouts retain the allocating path. Reuse bounded FP32 suffix LSE storage per metadata-builder/ubatch wrapper.
- Reuse the AG/RS compiled correction launcher across layers using the same plan. Every successful replan replaces its context, covering dtype and runtime-scalar specialization changes. Pointers and the current stream are bound on every execution; A2A is unchanged by this host optimization.
- Reuse existing CPU sequence lengths when every row is confirmed to be in prefill. Admission requires no decode rows, CPU-resident length metadata and CPU `is_prefilling` flags that are all true. Missing metadata, mixed batches and speculative decode retain exact GPU readback. DCP clones the lengths before subtracting queries, preserving shared metadata.

FA2 and cuDNN follow the same caller path; attention-provider selection is unchanged. cuDNN can return natural-log suffix Stats directly. FA2 still converts its native base-2 suffix LSE inside FlashInfer. Context attention continues to produce base-2 LSE for collective weighting.

The launcher reuse is scoped to one plan's fixed dtype/device/shape and FI/collective-owned aligned buffers. It does not introduce a general tensor-specialization cache. The two host optimizations add 22 net production lines and extend existing tests; neither adds a public API.

Persistent LSE costs 2 MiB per owner at 16,384 tokens and 32 heads. It can be allocated after normal profiling, so residency remains a memory-accounting consideration. Reusing final O avoids another maximum-sized O allocation.

This extends the existing DCP LSE work. The adjacent [#58953](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58953) removes host-length retrieval when no consumer needs it, particularly non-causal XQA decode. This PR instead reuses proven-exact CPU lengths for prefill consumers that still need host metadata; it does not duplicate that consumer-gating change or substitute optimistic decode bounds.

**Draft dependencies:** the branch still pins `flashinfer-python==0.7.0`, predating the LSE keyword API in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5257. Updating the dependency and full model-level DCP qualification remain required before Ready.

## Test Plan

Cover same/cross-base LSE, context reuse, dtype/token-count changes at replan, empty shards, strided LSE, CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs, caller-owned buffers and CPU metadata alias preservation. Real two-rank collectives and native CUDA/Triton final merge need independent coverage.

```text
python -m pytest -q tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py
python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py \
  -k dcp_prefill_lse_merge_and_replay
python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_merge_attn_states.py \
  -k merge_attn_states_lse_view
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \
  -k flashinfer_prefill_cpu_lengths_require_exact_metadata
```

## Test Result

Validated head: **`85bca13ad4`**. The combined CPU subset passed **53 tests**, comprising 41 DCP reference/configuration cases and 12 CPU-length admission/alias cases. All changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy 3.10 and test tethering; `git diff --check` passed.

On B200, the current tree passed the combined full DCP suite and updated wrapper integration: **92 passed, 4 skipped**. This includes real two-rank AG/RS/A2A capture/replay; the skipped cases require four GPUs. The wrapper fixture exercises real correction with simulated identical shards, replan from BF16 to FP16 and five to four tokens, and preserves the single-rank A2A strided LSE case. The separate native CUDA/Triton strided final-merge suite passed **6 tests** on earlier tree `457dd8d2`; that merge implementation is unchanged in this follow-up.

GPU validation uses two ComputeLab B200s, Python 3.12.12, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, released cuDNN 9.27.0.42, FE `0e64e48c`, CuTe DSL 4.7.1 and NCCL 2.29.7. Tests import the branch's Python/Triton sources into an existing environment and reuse a previously built stable-libtorch vLLM extension. The native merge entry is exercised; this is not a clean full-tree build/install. Final-head remote CI, model/serving evaluation and qualification with the eventual dependency pin remain outstanding.

## Bounded performance evidence

The table below is the earlier **combine-only LSE-conversion experiment at `457dd8d2`**. It includes real two-rank AG/RS communication and correction, but **no attention kernels, `plan()`, metadata builder, full DCP wrapper or whole-vLLM dispatch**. Both arms already used persistent `CPTritonContext` instances. It therefore isolates default log2 output plus a separate conversion versus direct ln output; it measures neither the newly connected wrapper context reuse nor the cumulative PR against main.

Two exclusive ComputeLab B200s, 1000 W each; BF16 partial O, FP32 LSE, H=32 before head scatter, D=128. Five ABBA rounds use **100-call bursts** per timing block. Values are medians of paired round averages using the slower rank. Host submission includes allocation, collective overhead/backpressure and the same O-restoration copy in both arms. It is not synchronized single-call FI timing. CUDA-event graph replay is a separate metric.

| AG/RS tokens | Combine-only host submission before / after, us |
|---|---:|
| 5 | 121.87 / 113.34 |
| 127 | 124.73 / 115.68 |
| 512 | 123.49 / 114.47 |

Every timing block passed an independent FP64 reference, including empty/nonfinite shards; changed O and rank-dependent LSE passed eager and captured replay after timing. Real A2A also passed correctness, but its host samples were more variable, so the table reports AG/RS. Host and replay savings must not be added or interpreted as serving latency.

For the newly connected launcher reuse, two fresh-process ABBA runs on another exclusive 1000 W B200 pair used direct-ln output in both arms. Only the actual caller's `ctx=None` versus retained plan context differed. Same BF16/FP32, H=32, D=128 geometry; real two-rank AG/RS; 100 calls per block:

| Tokens | Combine host before / after, run 1, us | Run 2, us |
|---|---:|---:|
| 5 | 143.34 / 130.83 | 123.87 / 112.77 |
| 127 | 146.82 / 134.59 | 128.16 / 116.98 |
| 512 | 147.43 / 133.93 | 128.09 / 116.73 |

Per-round paired median savings were **10.8–12.5 us**. These are separate experiments from the conversion table and must not be added to it. Absolute totals vary with CPU/communication conditions. Separate hooked diagnostics identify all-gather and reduce-scatter as the largest submission spans; those instrumented times are not substituted for the uninstrumented measurements.

Actual `BatchDCPPrefillWrapper.run()` also passed with real FA2/cuDNN paged context attention, Q all-gather, AG/RS, ragged suffix attention and final merge. With BF16, local Hq/Hkv=16/8, D=128, 1024 total context tokens, NHD pages of 16, and query lengths 5/127, O and both LSE stages were exactly equal across arms, including two changed-input replay passes. cuDNN selected backend engine 8 for the small case and engine 10 for the larger context (suffix engine 8); engine/knobs matched across arms. For the 127-token cuDNN case, warm host submission was **461.56 / 458.85 us** in one process and **471.09 / 445.40 us** in another. Full-wrapper paired savings were more variable than the isolated combine; no fixed percentage or serving improvement is claimed. Plan is outside these timings.

CPU-length reuse is measured separately using actual metadata `build()` plus FI `plan()`, with query lengths [64, 128], KV lengths [1024, 2048], Hq/Hkv=32/8 and D=128. For rank-1 metadata of a two-rank DCP setup, idle time was **394.66 / 368.30 us**. With a calibrated 2 ms of synthetic earlier work queued on the same stream, it was **2392.33 / 384.38 us**. This is avoided synchronization, once per metadata build, not faster attention or a per-layer gain. The semantic-prefill case made zero length readbacks; an intentionally optimistic speculative-decode control retained its readback and correct planned lengths. Shared CPU metadata remained unchanged. This metadata probe does not perform distributed communication.

A separate 5-token two-rank CUDA DAG check found identical kernel functions, launch geometry/attributes and dependencies with and without context reuse. GPU replay correctness passed, but separately captured graphs showed nontrivial A/A variation even with the same context (up to about 7.5 us in a full-wrapper control). Reversing capture order also changed the small deltas. No precise GPU-replay speedup or regression is attributed to this host-only change, and the earlier small replay deltas are not promoted as stable performance gains.

AI assistance was used for implementation, source audit, tests and benchmarking. Human review and full model validation remain required before Ready.

items.title: [Tracking] TurboQuant + Gemma 4 multimodal: 5-gate blocker stack
items.body:
# [Tracking] TurboQuant KV cache + Gemma 4 31B (multimodal) — full blocker stack

## Summary

Trying to enable TurboQuant KV cache compression (`turboquant_4bit_nc`) on Gemma 4 31B FP8 (the multimodal `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` variant) on consumer Blackwell hardware (4× RTX 5060 Ti, sm_120, TP=4). Walking through the failure modes systematically, there are **5 distinct gates** that block this configuration today on `main`. Filing this as a tracking/discussion issue because the gates compose: fixing #1 reveals #2, fixing #2 reveals #3, etc. Hopefully useful as a roadmap item for anyone working on TurboQuant + multimodal hybrid models.

**TL;DR motivation:** on 4× 16 GB consumer Blackwell at TP=4, native 262,144 context with `fp8_per_token_head` doesn't fit (~3.04 GiB needed per GPU vs ~2.15 GiB available at gpu-util 0.97; estimated max 170,560). TurboQuant 4-bit KV would give ~4× compression and unlock native context. So the value proposition is real, not hypothetical.

## Environment

- vLLM `0.20.1rc1.dev119+gc74e90b9e.cu132` = `origin/main` @ `39a7f4f` (2026-04-29) + #40391 (lisp19's rework HEAD `c74e90b9`)
- 4× RTX 5060 Ti (Blackwell consumer, sm_120), CUDA 13.2, Ubuntu 25.10
- Gemma 4 31B FP8 (compressed-tensors block FP8 weights)
- Launch base flags: `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --enforce-eager`
- Target KV dtype: `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` (chose `_4bit_nc` over `_k8v4` because sm_86 lacks FP8 hardware in Triton — same caveat applies as a guard for users on Ampere)

## The 5 gates (encountered in order)

### Gate 1 — `partial multimodal token full attention not supported`
```
ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.TURBOQUANT is not valid for this configuration.
Reason: ['kv_cache_dtype not supported', 'partial multimodal token full attention not supported']
```

**Root cause:** `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` sets `use_bidirectional_attention='vision'` (added in #40534), which propagates `use_mm_prefix=True` on full-attention layers. `TurboQuantAttentionBackend.supports_mm_prefix()` returns `False`.

**Workaround tested:** `--hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}'` removes the flag and the rejection. Sacrifices vision quality (causal vs bidi attention on image tokens) — undesirable for a vision model.

**Real fix:** implement `mm_prefix` handling in `TurboQuantAttentionBackend` (kernel + metadata changes for partial multimodal token attention).

---

### Gate 2 — boundary-skipped layers fall back to `auto` dtype
After clearing Gate 1:
```
ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.TURBOQUANT is not valid for this configuration.
Reason: ['kv_cache_dtype not supported']
```

**Root cause:** `TurboQuantConfig.get_boundary_skip_layers(num_layers, n=2)` auto-skips first 2 + last 2 layers from TurboQuant compression. For those layers, `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:248-262` sets `kv_cache_dtype="auto"`. Then `get_attn_backend(...)` is called for each layer with the user-selected backend (TURBOQUANT) + per-layer dtype. `TurboQuantAttentionBackend.supports_kv_cache_dtype("auto")` → `False` → reject.

So the model is *globally* configured for one backend, but layers 0/1/N-2/N-1 want a different dtype that backend can't serve. Currently no per-layer routing.

**Workaround tested:** monkey-patch `get_boundary_skip_layers` to return `[]` (no skipping). All 60 layers get TurboQuant. Sacrifices boundary protection — first/last layers tend to be the most quantization-sensitive, so this is a quality cost.

**Real fix:** per-layer attention backend routing. When a layer is skipped from TurboQuant, that specific layer should be wired to a backend that can handle its actual dtype (e.g., `TRITON_ATTN`), not have the global backend reject it.

---

### Gate 3 — `Alberto-Codes/turboquant-vllm` plugin conflict
After clearing Gates 1+2 with the workarounds:
```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'TQ4FullAttentionSpec.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'tq_slot_size''
```

**Root cause:** the [`turboquant-vllm`](https://github.com/Alberto-Codes/turboquant-vllm) plugin (1.5.0) registers a backend via `vllm.general_plugins` entry point. Its `TQ4FullAttentionSpec` class has a constructor signature that doesn't match the current in-tree TurboQuant API (signature drifted post-merge of #38479).

**Workaround:** `pip uninstall -y turboquant-vllm`. Easy if you know about it; surprising if you don't.

**Real fix:** the plugin upstream needs to track in-tree changes, OR vLLM's plugin loading should skip plugins that fail compatibility checks gracefully, OR the in-tree `TQ4FullAttentionSpec` should accept legacy kwargs with a deprecation path.

---

### Gate 4 — `ninja` missing for Triton runtime JIT
After clearing Gates 1+2+3:
```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error '[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'ninja'
```

**Root cause:** TurboQuant's Triton kernels need `ninja` for runtime JIT compilation. Not auto-installed via `vllm[turboquant]` extras, not flagged in setup.py, not documented in docs.

**Workaround:** `pip install ninja` into the venv.

**Real fix:** add `ninja` to TurboQuant's runtime requirements (or a `[turboquant]` extras_require), or document it as a hard dep in [the TurboQuant docs page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/turboquant/).

---

### Gate 5 — hybrid head_dim page-size unification fails (THE STOPPING POINT)
After clearing Gates 1+2+3+4:
```
File "vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py", line 1035, in unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size
NotImplementedError: The page size of the layer is not divisible by the maximum page size.
Cannot unify by adjusting block_size.
```

**Root cause:** Gemma 4's heterogeneous head_dim (sliding=256, full=512) produces different per-layer page sizes. With `turboquant_4bit_nc`, the math comes out non-divisible, so vLLM's KV unification raises rather than padding.

**Workaround:** none — this needs upstream code (LCM padding) to handle. JartX's [#39931](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39931) implements exactly this (`_align_hybrid_block_size` + LCM-based padding in `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size`). Still open as of 2026-04-30.

**Real fix:** merge #39931, OR include its core LCM logic in a different PR that doesn't bundle the hybrid-guard removal.

---

## Recommended ordering for closing the gaps

These are roughly in order of how often they'll bite users + how much new code each requires:

1. **Gate 4** (ninja dep) — trivial, document or add to extras
2. **Gate 5** (#39931) — already has a PR, needs review
3. **Gate 3** (plugin compat) — coordinate with [Alberto-Codes/turboquant-vllm](https://github.com/Alberto-Codes/turboquant-vllm) maintainer
4. **Gate 2** (per-layer backend routing) — significant architectural change, but useful beyond TurboQuant (any model with per-layer dtype variance)
5. **Gate 1** (mm_prefix on TurboQuant backend) — most engineering work, but highest unlock value (multimodal models are increasingly the default)

Closing 1+2+5 alone unblocks **Gemma 4 text-only** TurboQuant on hybrid hardware. Closing all five unlocks the multimodal serving config most production users actually want.

## Hardware/perf context for prioritization

We're running Gemma 4 31B FP8 TP=4 on 4× 16 GB consumer Blackwell. With `fp8_per_token_head` (lisp19's #40391, validated) we top out at ~170k context — short of the model's native 262k. **TurboQuant 4-bit KV (~4× compression vs fp8)** would push KV memory budget from 2.15 GiB → ~8.6 GiB per GPU, easily fitting native 262k.

Same dynamic on 2× RTX 3090 (sm_86, 48 GB total) for non-multimodal variants — TurboQuant works on Qwen 3.6 27B AWQ-INT4 there with `turboquant_4bit_nc` (verified, ~22× concurrency at 32k context). The multimodal Gemma 4 case is what the 5 gates above are really about.

## Reproduction recipe

```bash
# Clone + checkout PR head + uninstall plugin if present
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
cd vllm
git fetch origin pull/40391/head:pr-40391
git checkout pr-40391
pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
pip uninstall -y turboquant-vllm  # if installed
pip install ninja                  # gate 4 workaround

# Reproduces Gates 1 → 2 → 5 in order:
vllm serve <gemma4-31b-fp8-multimodal> \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --attention-backend TURBOQUANT \
  --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc

# To skip Gate 1: --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}'
# To skip Gate 2: monkey-patch TurboQuantConfig.get_boundary_skip_layers to return []
# (no workaround for Gate 5 without #39931)
```

## Tagging

cc @lisp19 (#40391 author), @JartX (#39931 author), @lucianommartins (#40534/Gemma 4 vision-bidi), @mgoin, @WoosukKwon — happy to provide any additional diagnostic data.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary On **vLLM 0.31.0**, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` with DFlash2 produces different greedy token sequences from target-only decoding. After removing the initial cross-mode differences, we also isolated a second failure: **the same generated prefix can produce a different next token when rebuilt through prefill rather than continued through decode**. Under load, preemption/recompute exposes this difference. We traced this to several target-forward numerical paths and a separate mixed-batch gate-indexing error. We implemented a local, opt-in consistency patch and verified exact token equality in the tested configuration, including concurrent requests, CUDA decode graphs, prefix-cache hits and preemptions. **This is not evidence that DFlash accepts tokens contrary to the verifier's argmax.** In our audited responses, every chosen token had a maximal returned target logprob. The target forward itself differed between execution paths. We also do not assume that unmodified GDN models already promise batch-invariant operation: some of the work below is a deterministic-mode proof of concept, while the gate-indexing defect is independently testable. ## Environment and scope - GPU: one NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation, 48 GB, SM89; TP=1, PP=1. - Unmodified image used for the original reproduction: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:c1c9f6fd5c109ba7f0546a59f5b2f15fb87f64c77782e90a27b648b42a8e67c3`. - Target: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`, revision `95a723d08a9490559dae23d0cff1d9466213d989`. - Draft: `incoai/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash2`, revision `51ef7b6923ad6c14cb1bb41c37a9041446496ab6`. - FP8 target weights; BF16 compute and KV cache; FP32 SSM states, as configured by this checkpoint. No CPU offload. - V2 runner, context 65,536, `max_num_seqs=32`, `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`, GPU memory utilization 0.98. - Greedy: temperature 0, seed 42, top_p 1, top_k -1, repetition_penalty 1, presence/frequency penalties 0. - Qwen thinking enabled. Comparisons include reasoning tokens, not only visible text. - Full `collect_env.py` output is in the environment field. It was collected from the currently patched container, which shares the original image's libraries. The failure was separately reproduced on the unmodified image above. - We have **not rerun this investigation on the latest main branch** or established equivalent behavior on other hardware/model/SSM precisions. ## Original stock reproduction The `serve-stock.sh` included below reproduces the recorded original launch settings, with public model revisions and a generic served alias. It uses FlashAttention/FA2 and the original `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` policy. Later diagnostic and final patched configurations are described separately below. Run target-only and DFlash **sequentially on the same GPU**, inside the pinned unmodified image: ```bash bash serve-stock.sh target # From another terminal, after readiness: python3 reproduce.py record target.json # Stop the target-only server, then start: bash serve-stock.sh dflash # After readiness: python3 reproduce.py record dflash.json python3 reproduce.py compare target.json dflash.json ``` The reproduction files below contain three synthetic prompts and their frozen input token IDs. A short one-prompt client, usable without the other files, is: ```python import json import sys import urllib.request from pathlib import Path from transformers import AutoTokenizer prompt = ( "Schreibe eine ausführliche Python-Anleitung mit Code für einen robusten " "JSONL-Import. Behandle Streaming großer Dateien, Validierung, doppelte IDs, " "fehlerhafte Zeilen, ein nachvollziehbares Fehlerprotokoll und wiederholbare " "Verarbeitung. Erkläre in mindestens 1200 Wörtern die Entscheidungen und " "zeige mehrere Codebeispiele." ) tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8", revision="95a723d08a9490559dae23d0cff1d9466213d989", ) ids = tok.apply_chat_template( [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True, preserve_thinking=True, ) if hasattr(ids, "keys"): ids = ids["input_ids"] body = { "model": "target", "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0, "top_p": 1, "top_k": -1, "seed": 42, "presence_penalty": 0, "frequency_penalty": 0, "repetition_penalty": 1, "add_special_tokens": False, "return_token_ids": True, "return_tokens_as_token_ids": True, "logprobs": 5, "cache_salt": "fresh-" + sys.argv[1], } req = urllib.request.Request( "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as response: result = json.load(response) Path(sys.argv[1] + ".json").write_text(json.dumps(result)) if Path("target.json").exists() and Path("dflash.json").exists(): a, b = [json.loads(Path(p + ".json").read_text())["choices"][0]["token_ids"] for p in ("target", "dflash")] first = next((i for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(a, b)) if x != y), None) if first is None and len(a) != len(b): first = min(len(a), len(b)) print("exact:", a == b, "first differing token (0-based):", first) ``` Save this as `minimal.py` and run `python3 minimal.py target` against target-only, then `python3 minimal.py dflash` against DFlash. Its tokenization was checked against the frozen original inputs. Only public model artifacts are needed. ### Observed results | Synthetic prompt | First differing output-token index, 0-based | Target-only token ID | DFlash token ID | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Business Central import investigation | 194 | 6478 | 67776 | | Python JSONL import | 124 | 11 | 198 | | SQL query investigation | 39 | 4232 | 57201 | All three generated 512 tokens. Each mode was repeatable on its own in the recorded run; target-only versus DFlash matched on **0/3**. Returned token IDs, logprob arrays and usage counts were checked for alignment. There were **zero chosen-token/non-top1 violations** in these audited responses. Exact first-divergence indices can move if kernel/autotuning choices change. There is no crash or traceback to report: the symptom is a different token sequence. We do not have a new full DEBUG/TRACE_FUNCTION capture; the evidence below comes from targeted forward-operation captures and regression tests. ## What we isolated ### 1. Batch-shape-dependent normalization and GDN execution paths An actual forward trace found identical inputs/residuals at a native Gemma RMSNorm call but one differing BF16 output element out of 2,048 between the one-token and verification shapes. A fixed per-row reduction removed the discrepancy. After serial parity was established, concurrent DFlash requests still diverged. Another first-difference capture isolated GDN `RMSNormGated`: identical inputs, but its row-block choice changed with the number of rows. A captured critical BF16 row differs by `1.52587890625e-05`; twelve random-only probes had missed it. Fixing one row per reduction block removed that captured difference. The exact input fixture and regression test are included in the full patch posted in follow-up comments. The packed GDN decode and general speculative recurrence also used different Q/K normalization/reduction paths. Aligning `x / sqrt(sum(x*x)+eps)` with the other path's `x * rsqrt(sum(x*x)+eps)`, and aligning the reduction layout, made the corresponding direct-kernel parity tests pass. Additional fixed linear/FP8/MoE/attention choices were used in the local consistency mode. These are numerical-consistency measures, not proof that either floating-point formulation is intrinsically mathematically incorrect. ### 2. Independent mixed-batch gate-indexing defect In `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`, the ordinary/non-speculative QKV rows were gathered with `non_spec_token_indx`, but some decode-only mixed paths still consumed ungathered `a`/`b` gate rows. Gate selection was performed inside the prefill branch rather than consistently for the ordinary decode path. We gather `a_non_spec` and `b_non_spec` alongside `mixed_qkv_non_spec` and use those tensors in the ordinary decode recurrence. The CPU metadata/row-routing regression has four cases: **stock fails two and passes two; patched passes four**. This is distinct from #51812's already-merged alignment of the speculative rows. ### 3. Remaining high-load failure: prefill/recompute is not the same forward as decode After the earlier fixes, serial and concurrency-4 runs matched, but a 32-client run still matched only **41/50** sequences and incurred **12 preemptions**. This was an intermediate local build, not a claim about an isolated stock-only failure rate. We reproduced the remaining mechanism without concurrent load: take an already generated token prefix, submit it as a fresh prompt with a new cache salt, and generate one token. **5/9** selected replay probes disagreed with the original next token. For example, a 141-token translation prefix produced token 318 instead of the recorded token 466. A first-difference trace showed identical layer-0 input normalization and QKV/gate projections, but **1,448/4,096** core GDN output values differed before gated normalization. The prefill path used chunked FLA computation and normalized Q/K cast back to BF16; the incremental path used the general per-token recurrence with FP32 normalized Q/K. Recomputing previously decoded context therefore changed recurrent arithmetic and could flip a later greedy argmax. Preemption exposed this difference; we did not find evidence that the scheduler was changing the stored prefix token IDs. ## Local fix and validation Our patch adds an **opt-in local** `VLLM_SPECULATIVE_TOKEN_PARITY=1` mode. This flag is not an upstream option and is not a workaround available in an unmodified vLLM installation. We did not bypass `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`'s unsupported-GDN guard. In addition to the normalization, kernel-choice and gate-routing changes above: - Prefill/replay uses the same per-token GDN recurrence and convolution arithmetic as decode, retaining FP32 SSM states. - The recurrent helper supports a fresh/cached initial-state mask and final-state-only storage. Fresh contexts do not consume stale cache contents, and a one-dimensional final-state index is not treated as per-token speculative indices. - The convolution helper masks history for fresh contexts and only applies speculative history-length adjustment on the speculative path. - Both comparison arms use a common attention/Mamba block size of 1,152. This also removed a long-context boundary discrepancy in our tests. - Target and DFlash CUDA **decode** graphs are enabled (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`); prefill remains eager, with Torch compilation mode 0. Graphs alone were not the fix. The full patch posted in follow-up comments applies cleanly to the actual unmodified pinned image's Python files. Applying it reproduces all **22 runtime source files byte-for-byte** from our tested local image. It is a broad proof of concept, not a claim that all changes should become unconditional upstream defaults. The independent indexing correction and optional numerical-consistency work could be split for review. Results: - 49 common regression tests: stock **30 failed / 19 passed**, patched **49 passed**. Adding 40 recurrent/convolution replay regressions gives **89 passed** on the final patch. - **18/18 initial and 259/259 extended fresh-context replay probes** match, including selected 1,152-token block boundaries. - **50/50** fixed token sequences match between patched target-only and patched DFlash, and between the tested low/high-concurrency runs. - A 32-client DFlash run retained equality despite **18 preemptions**. Its observed active-request peak was 9, not 32. - With actual CUDA decode graphs: **50/50** still match; the 32-client DFlash run had 4 preemptions and observed active-request peak 7. - Concurrent shared-prefix tests: **8/8** long-context and **32/32** short-context sequences match. Actual prefix-cache hits were observed for the long-context test. These 50 sequences were capped at 4,096 generated tokens. Two tasks reached that cap; equality is established for the generated prefixes, not a claim that every task finished or answered correctly. Both cross-mode arms used the same patched arithmetic; equality to the old unpatched wording is not claimed. Stochastic sampling and BF16 SSM-state parity are outside this validation. ### Performance cost A separate controlled measurement used the same vLLM 0.31.0 base, model revision, GPU and serving configuration within each stock/patched pair, with CUDA decode graphs enabled. Each variant generated 18 serial responses of exactly 512 tokens after three excluded warmups: | Mode | Stock tokens/s | Patched tokens/s | Throughput change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Target-only | 103.59 | 90.17 | -12.95% | | DFlash2, 7 draft tokens | 204.22 | 159.16 | -22.07% | | MTP, 3 draft tokens | 176.62 | 132.31 | -25.09% | This measures the full local patch, not the isolated cost of one kernel fix. Output wording and draft acceptance can change when arithmetic is unified. The earlier original stock reproduction used its original FA2/default-backend settings; this controlled performance comparison fixed Triton attention/linear/MoE/GDN choices and decode-graph settings for each stock/patched pair. No AI quality judging or Transformers reference comparison was performed. The comparison here is between vLLM execution paths for the same target prefix, not an allegation of a Transformers implementation defect. ## Related issues and requested guidance - #54928: related DFlash2 greedy-divergence symptom. - #48271 and #58973: related shape-/dispatch-dependent RMSNorm behavior. - #48613: unsupported batch-invariant mode for GDN models. - #51812: speculative gate-row alignment, already merged; the ordinary-row defect above is a separate path. - #55524: conceptually related Mamba2 prefill/decode replay discussion; our traced model path is Qwen GDN. Could maintainers advise whether to split the ordinary gate-indexing regression into a focused bugfix and the GDN exact-replay/numerical-consistency path into an opt-in feature? The reproduction files below and patch comments provide the full patch, captured synthetic fixture, regression tests and frozen public prompts. The numerical observations above summarize the recorded results. No private endpoints, credentials, user chats or production deployment files are included. ## Reproduction files
serve-stock.sh ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Run INSIDE the pinned unmodified vLLM 0.31.0 image specified in the issue. # It loads one model server. Run target and dflash sequentially on the same GPU. set -euo pipefail export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 unset VLLM_SPECULATIVE_TOKEN_PARITY spec=() case "${1:-target}" in target) ;; dflash) spec=(--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash2","revision":"51ef7b6923ad6c14cb1bb41c37a9041446496ab6","num_speculative_tokens":7,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}') ;; *) echo 'Usage: bash serve-stock.sh target|dflash' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac exec vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 \ --revision 95a723d08a9490559dae23d0cff1d9466213d989 \ --dtype bfloat16 --quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \ --served-model-name target --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --max-model-len 65536 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.98 \ --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":0}' \ --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true,"preserve_thinking":true}' \ --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN --mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASH_ATTN \ --logprobs-mode raw_logprobs "${spec[@]}" ```

Start each server separately using serve-stock.sh, then: python3 reproduce.py record target.json python3 reproduce.py record dflash.json python3 reproduce.py compare target.json dflash.json The attached prompts.json contains synthetic prompts and their exact input IDs. 1e-6: violations.append(index) results.append({'case': prompt['case'], 'result': result, 'not_top1': violations}) print(prompt['case'], 'tokens:', len(ids), 'non-top1 positions:', violations) Path(output).write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n') def compare(first, second): a, b = [json.loads(Path(path).read_text()) for path in [first, second]] assert [r['case'] for r in a] == [r['case'] for r in b] for x, y in zip(a, b): ax, by = x['result']['choices'][0], y['result']['choices'][0] ids_a, ids_b = ax['token_ids'], by['token_ids'] position = next((i for i, (u, v) in enumerate(zip(ids_a, ids_b)) if u != v), None) if position is None and len(ids_a) != len(ids_b): position = min(len(ids_a), len(ids_b)) print(x['case'], 'exact:', ids_a == ids_b, 'first difference (0-based):', position) if position is not None and position < min(len(ids_a), len(ids_b)): print(' token IDs:', ids_a[position], ids_b[position]) print(' target top logprobs A:', ax['logprobs']['top_logprobs'][position]) print(' target top logprobs B:', by['logprobs']['top_logprobs'][position]) if __name__ == '__main__': parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__) sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', required=True) p = sub.add_parser('record') p.add_argument('output') p.add_argument('--base-url', default='http://127.0.0.1:8000') p.add_argument('--model', default='target') p = sub.add_parser('compare') p.add_argument('first') p.add_argument('second') args = parser.parse_args() if args.command == 'record': record(args.output, args.base_url, args.model) else: compare(args.first, args.second) ```

items.title: [Bug]: H100 FA3 violates batch invariance when an unrelated prefill changes tiling
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, compute capability 9.0 Driver: 595.71.05 vLLM: 0.25.1 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 CUDA reported by PyTorch: 13.0 cuDNN: 9.19.0 dtype: bfloat16 attention shape: 14 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 64 paged KV block size: 16 (primary), 128 (boundary control) KV sequence length: 19802 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug With vLLM 0.25.1 on H100, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` does not make the FlashAttention 3 path batch invariant for mixed decode+prefill batches. In a legal two-sequence varlen call, the same paged-KV decode row produces different BF16 output when an unrelated prefill row grows from 9 to 10 tokens. The victim's Q, KV, sequence length, and physical block mapping do not change; the neighbor's first nine Q/K/V tokens are also identical. The scalar changes FA3's SM90 specialization: - `max_seqlen_q=9`: `VarlenDynamicPersistentTileScheduler<64,192,...>` - `max_seqlen_q=10`: `VarlenDynamicPersistentTileScheduler<192,128,...>` The calls use exact, self-consistent maxima: `cu_seqlens_q=[0,1,10], max_seqlen_q=9` and `cu_seqlens_q=[0,1,11], max_seqlen_q=10`. They both use `num_splits=1` and disjoint physical KV blocks. Repeated calls with identical complete inputs are bitwise stable, so this is a deterministic cross-tiling numerical difference, not stochastic behavior within one kernel. The arithmetic mechanism is localized to the changed N-block partition and online-softmax/P-times-V accumulation tree. With the same seeded tensors, the outputs are identical through KV length 128 and first differ at length 129, while the FP32 LSE remains bitwise equal. At that boundary the N=128 specialization performs two K-block updates (128+1), while the N=192 specialization performs one. For longer inputs the LSE can differ as well. ## Why this is an issue: This violates the advertised contract `FlashAttentionBackend.supports_batch_invariance()` returns `True`. In BI mode, vLLM disables FA3 AOT scheduling and forces `max_num_splits=1`, but the forward path still passes the batch-global `attn_metadata.max_query_len` unchanged as `max_seqlen_q` to `_vllm_fa3_C.fwd`. Consequently, a decode request with unchanged Q/K/V and KV block mapping can change its attention result when a co-batched prefill raises the global maximum query length. ## Minimal reproduction Self-contained; runs on a single H100 with vLLM 0.25.1 installed. It calls `flash_attn_varlen_func` directly and never goes through vLLM's serving path or its batch-invariance machinery, so no environment variables are needed. ```python import math import torch from vllm.vllm_flash_attn.flash_attn_interface import flash_attn_varlen_func DEV, DT = "cuda", torch.bfloat16 NQ, NKV, HD, BLOCK, VICTIM_KLEN = 14, 2, 64, 16, 19_802 # GQA ratio 7, head dim 64 def randn(seed, shape): g = torch.Generator(device=DEV).manual_seed(seed) return torch.randn(shape, generator=g, device=DEV, dtype=DT) victim_blocks, neighbor_blocks = (VICTIM_KLEN + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK, 1 victim_q = randn(31, (1, NQ, HD)) victim_cache = randn(32, (victim_blocks, 2, BLOCK, NKV, HD)) neighbor_q = randn(33, (10, NQ, HD)) neighbor_cache = randn(34, (neighbor_blocks, 2, BLOCK, NKV, HD)) key_cache, value_cache = torch.cat((victim_cache, neighbor_cache), 0).unbind(1) victim_ids = torch.arange(victim_blocks, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32) neighbor_ids = torch.arange(victim_blocks, victim_blocks + neighbor_blocks, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32) assert not torch.isin(victim_ids, neighbor_ids).any() # disjoint physical blocks def run(neighbor_len): """Victim is row 0: a 1-token decode whose every input is fixed.""" q = torch.cat((victim_q, neighbor_q[:neighbor_len]), 0) cu_q = torch.tensor([0, 1, 1 + neighbor_len], device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32) used_k = torch.tensor([VICTIM_KLEN, neighbor_len], device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32) table = torch.full((2, victim_blocks), -1, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32) table[0, :victim_blocks] = victim_ids table[1, :neighbor_blocks] = neighbor_ids # max_seqlen_q is exactly the longest row present; nothing is over-declared. assert neighbor_len == int((cu_q[1:] - cu_q[:-1]).max()) out = flash_attn_varlen_func( q, key_cache, value_cache, cu_seqlens_q=cu_q, seqused_k=used_k, max_seqlen_q=neighbor_len, max_seqlen_k=VICTIM_KLEN, block_table=table, softmax_scale=1 / math.sqrt(HD), causal=True, fa_version=3, num_splits=1, ) torch.cuda.synchronize() return out[0].clone() # victim row only for _ in range(5): run(9); run(10) a, b = run(9), run(10) print("victim bitwise equal :", torch.equal(a, b)) print("unequal BF16 elements:", int((a != b).sum())) print("max abs delta :", float((a.float() - b.float()).abs().max())) ``` Only the neighbor's length differs between the two calls, and the neighbor's first nine Q/K/V tokens are shared by both. Observed victim result for a fixed seeded input: ```text legal neighbor q=9 vs q=10: 95 unequal BF16 elements maximum abs delta: 0.00006103515625 same-input stability: 30/30 bitwise-identical runs for each case solo max_q=9 == legal q=9: bitwise equal solo max_q=10 == legal q=10: bitwise equal ``` The neighbor's first nine Q/K/V tokens are shared between both cases, unused block-table entries are `-1`, and victim/neighbor physical blocks are asserted disjoint. The earlier one-row scalar probe remains useful as selector localization, but is not needed for the BI claim. The kernel identities above come from `torch.profiler` tables rendered with `max_name_column_width` raised past the 55-character default, so the full demangled scheduler template parameters are visible rather than truncated. Untruncated tables were captured for the single-row, legal-two-row, and head-dim-128 cases; they can be attached on request. ## Numerical-stage evidence Additional controls use the same one-row paged-KV call: - random Q/K/V: 108 unequal BF16 outputs, but FP32 LSE is bitwise equal; - zero Q (uniform logits): output and LSE are bitwise equal; - constant V: output and LSE are bitwise equal; - 64 single-position V impulses across both tile boundaries: output and LSE are bitwise equal; - both tilings have almost identical error relative to an FP64 reference. The K=129 boundary is the concise causal localization: the two separately compiled tile shapes induce different blockwise reduction topologies. No single shared "bad instruction" is required to explain the result. ## Boundary generalization A legal-input sweep tested the selector formula `max_seqlen_q * (nq / nkv) <= 64` over five seeds per case: | GQA ratio | tested boundary | seeds with victim difference | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 64 -> 65 | 5/5 | | 2 | 32 -> 33 | 5/5 | | 4 | 16 -> 17 | 5/5 | | 7 | 9 -> 10 | 5/5 | | 8 | 8 -> 9 | 5/5 | All exact-input repeats were bitwise stable. This establishes agreement with the source formula in the tested configurations; it is not a claim that every GQA model or input necessarily produces an observable numerical difference. With KV page size 128, the primary ratio-7 9 -> 10 violation also occurred in 5/5 seeds. A second source-predicted PagedKV TMA dispatch transition at 27 -> 28 changed one compiled specialization boolean but produced no victim numerical difference in 5/5 seeds. Other page sizes can therefore expose additional dispatch boundaries, not necessarily additional BI violations. ### Head-dim scope control The same legal two-row sweep was repeated with head dim 128 for GQA ratios 1, 2, 4, 7, and 8, using five seeds and three repeats per exact input. Every boundary was 0/5 numerically different. Profiling showed the expected transitions: ```text use_one_mma_wg=true: (kBlockM,kBlockN) = (64,128) use_one_mma_wg=false: (kBlockM,kBlockN) = (128,128) ``` Thus only the Q-side M tile changes; the KV N partition remains identical. The page-128 ratio-7 9 -> 10 control was also 0/5 different. This report therefore limits the demonstrated numerical violation to the tested head-dim-64 path and does not advertise it as a general head-dim-128 model bug. The negative control is evidence for the current N-block/PV-association mechanism, not a proof that every possible d=128 input is mathematically identical. For d=128, page size 128 has a separate PagedKV TMA boundary at q=18 -> 19, because `max_q * 7` crosses `kBlockM=128` there; q=27 -> 28 is already on the same side. That 18 -> 19 transition was tested over five seeds and three repeats per exact input: the predicted TMA boolean changed, while the victim remained bitwise equal in 5/5 seeds. The selector still causes a performance regression for d=128 even when the outputs are equal. At K=19,802, the measured `64x128` versus `128x128` median was 176.23 -> 244.98 us (1.390x); at K=2,048 it was 25.26 -> 33.10 us (1.310x), and at K=8,192 it was 77.43 -> 106.29 us (1.373x). Therefore the correctness scope demonstrated here is d=64, while the decode-performance scope includes both d=64 and d=128. Concrete d=64 examples include Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama-3.2-1B, and TinyLlama-1.1B. The model list is illustrative; the applicable condition is the model's attention head dimension, not its name or parameter count. Speculative decoding is a particularly plausible high-frequency trigger. A verification step commonly has `q_len = proposed_tokens + 1`; for ratio 7, `q_len >= 10` crosses the tested selector boundary, and even shorter verify requests can be affected when co-batched with a prefill whose global maximum crosses it. This is a mechanism-based scope implication, not a separate speculative-decoding reproduction.
Click here to see the evidence ## Some service-level evidence - On vLLM 0.25.1, the exact concurrent Trace reproduced under FA3+BI with verified cache reset in 4/4 comparisons; the same Trace under TRITON_ATTN+BI was stable in 0/4 comparisons. Both new evidence files retain the exact Trace/payload hashes and full run provenance. - A one-layer eager hook counted 527 real FA3 engine-step calls during one exact Trace: 510 had `max_seqlen_q <= 9`, while 17 had `max_seqlen_q >= 10` (3.23%, maximum 8192). The workload therefore crosses the selector gate repeatedly; this histogram is explicitly eager because graph replay bypasses Python hooks. - A vLLM 0.25.1 graph-mode replay with r1 logprobs produced three distinct r1 outputs in five runs. All four comparisons first changed at output-token index 18. To be precise about the strength of this particular flip: the reference run's top1-top2 gap at that position was 0, i.e. an exact argmax tie, so on the taxonomy used in #47069 this is a tie flip rather than a confident flip. (The 0.125 figures are the gaps in the *diverged* trajectories, downstream of the flip, and are not evidence that the flip itself was confident.) A confident flip, reference gap 0.125, not a tie, was demonstrated for this same bug on vLLM 0.19.0 in #47069. The kernel mechanism is identical across both versions; what differs is which token position the workload happened to land on. - A live FA3 hook recomputed a real batched target row alone. Using the target's local maximum differed from the batched output in 153/300 calls. Retaining the original batch-global `max_seqlen_q/max_seqlen_k` reproduced the batched output in 300/300 calls. - Forcing vLLM's persistent SM80 matmul overrides on SM90 did not eliminate the finding. Independently of graph mode, an operator-level FA2 scan over `max_seqlen_q=1..17,32,...,8191` was bitwise equal throughout, including all 136 pairwise comparisons among values 10..8191; FA2 used one `flash_fwd_splitkv_kernel<...64,64,256...>` across 9/10. - As a causal ablation, clamping BI+FA3 `max_seqlen_q` to at least 10 kept both decode-only and mixed calls on the `192x128` side. The exact finding then became stable for all 11 deterministic requests across 20 runs (19/19 comparisons per request), with verified HTTP-200 cache resets before every run. This remains a causal ablation, not a proposed production fix. The slower forced specialization can shift later batch timing, so timeline displacement remains a residual service-level confound; the standalone legal-input probes supply the scheduling-free causal evidence. - The d=128 performance benchmark used nine alternating samples and 500 iterations per sample. It found a 1.390x slowdown at K=19,802 when the batch-global selector moved decode from `64x128` to `128x128`, despite bitwise-equal outputs. This makes the performance impact broader than the demonstrated d=64 correctness impact. - A real service profile contained 52,558 `matmul_kernel_persistent*` launches and no cuBLAS/cuBLASLt/GEMM kernel-name matches. Together with the installed source path, this shows that an independent direct native-`F.linear` Hopper observation is not reachable through the tested unquantized Qwen2 BI service and is not part of this report. In the standalone control, each fixed M was bitwise stable over 30 repeats; cross-M differences reproduced under `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:16:8` (6 elements, max abs 0.125) but disappeared under `:4096:8`, further supporting its treatment as a configuration-specific latent operator note.
## Expected behavior When batch invariance is enabled, adding an unrelated prefill row must not change the attention output of an otherwise identical decode row. Setting the batch-global `max_seqlen_q` to 1 is not a valid fix because the same call contains actual prefill rows longer than 1. Keeping `num_splits=1` alone is already shown to be insufficient. Globally forcing the `192x128` path is also a poor production fix: at KV length 19,802 it measured 251.97 us versus 143.53 us for `64x192` on a single decode row (1.756x). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Model] Support ViT full CUDA graph for Qwen3-Omni
items.body:
## Overview

Add ViT full CUDA graph support for the Qwen3-Omni thinker (`Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration`, for example `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct`), part of #38175. Only the vision encoder is captured; the audio encoder stays eager. The thinker has its own `Qwen3Omni_VisionTransformer`, so this follows the Qwen3-VL integration (#35963, video in #38061) rather than reusing the Qwen3-VL code.

The eager Omni vision encoder now builds its attention metadata the way Qwen3-VL does, which also makes it run on FlashInfer: on main it fails there with "cu_seqlens must be divisible by 2". SyaOtiLan ran the GPU validation below on an RTX 4090 with the real vision weights. That work also found a FlashInfer replay bug shared with Qwen3-VL, fixed for Qwen3-VL in #64984 and for Omni in this PR.

## Claims

- Qwen3-Omni implements `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` for images and videos, with the same buffer keys as Qwen3-VL.
- The eager vision encoder and the graph path build their attention metadata through one new `prepare_encoder_metadata`, following Qwen3-VL.
- This changes the eager encoder for every Qwen3-Omni user, with or without the graph flag. On FlashInfer and with FP8 encoder attention, the eager path now gets the same `cu_seqlens` and `max_seqlen` as Qwen3-VL. On main, the Omni encoder computed `max_seqlen` only for FA, ROCm AITER FA and Triton, and passed raw `cu_seqlens` to every backend. The RDNA3 fallback for `torch.repeat_interleave` is removed because that call is gone.
- On FlashInfer, graph replay copies the packed `cu_seqlens` with `_pad_flashinfer_cu_seqlens_buffer`, the helper Qwen2.5-VL registers (#42796). FlashInfer packs the q/k/o and v offsets into one tensor split at its midpoint, and an image replay is padded to a smaller batch bucket than the capture, so the default copy puts both halves into the first half of the buffer. The hook is registered in `get_encoder_cudagraph_config` only when `self.visual.attn_backend` is FLASHINFER, so other backends keep the default copy. #64984 makes the same change for Qwen3-VL; the two PRs are independent and can merge in either order.
- Graph replay matches eager mode on the same padded buffers exactly on FLASH_ATTN and FLASHINFER in every case run below.
- With FLASH_ATTN and budgets [64, 256, 1024], the encoder is faster with graphs when an input nearly fills its budget and slower when it is heavily padded (table below).

## Validation

GPU results from SyaOtiLan: RTX 4090 (SM 8.9), PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, BF16, the real vision weights of the Qwen3-Omni checkpoint at revision 26291f793822fb6be9555850f06dfe95f2d7e695, loaded through `LLM(mm_encoder_only=True)`, budgets [64, 256, 1024], at most 2 vision items and 16 frames per batch. Raw outputs, logs and scripts are in the bundles: [first run](https://github.com/SyaOtiLan/vllm/releases/download/pr-63809-validation-20261101/63809-validation-complete.zip), [after the hook](https://github.com/SyaOtiLan/vllm/releases/download/pr-63809-validation-20261101/63809-branch-b-verification.zip), [extended](https://github.com/SyaOtiLan/vllm/releases/download/pr-63809-validation-20261101/63809-extended-validation.zip).

- E2E tests ([report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6554846868)): `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k qwen3_omni` gave 2 passed at 3687acad21, on FLASH_ATTN. These tests check that capture and replay run, not output values. The only later commit, a27a27a1ed, adds the FlashInfer-only padding hook described above. In the same run, replay on FLASH_ATTN matched eager on the same padded buffers exactly in the three cases sampled.
- Eager encoder, main compared with this branch, tiny random encoder on CUDA: FLASH_ATTN max abs diff 0 on all three grids of the comparison script. On FLASHINFER, main fails with "cu_seqlens must be divisible by 2" and this branch runs, with max abs error against an FP32 reference of 0.0017 to 0.0028.
- Replay on FLASHINFER before the padding hook, at 3687acad21: three replays of one 224 x 224 image differed by up to 3.84, and the first replay differed from eager by 7.72. With the hook ([report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557439065)): replays identical, and replay equal to eager on the same padded buffers.
- Wider replay checks with the hook ([report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557974253)), on a branch with this PR's Omni code plus the Qwen3-VL fix from #64984: mixed-size and two-image batches, video, alternating input shapes and oversized inputs that fall back to eager. All 110 graph-covered conditions matched eager on the same padded buffers exactly, all 4 fallback conditions matched eager, and the 1,368 calls of a shape-transition stress test were exact. The per-layer run in the same report also checked replay against eager on both FLASH_ATTN and FLASHINFER for both models, all exact.
- Padded compared with unpadded eager: the output for a 49-token image differs by a max of 0.40625 on FLASHINFER and 0.5 on FLASH_ATTN (RMSE about 0.008 to 0.009), without graph replay. A per-layer trace finds the first difference in `patch_embed.proj`, whose inputs match exactly, which is consistent with the linear kernel giving different BF16 results at 256 rows than at 196. A [follow-up trace](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6560437008) used a 448 x 448 image (784 valid patches padded to 1024) with BF16 reduced-precision reduction disabled. The first difference between padded and unpadded eager is in `blocks.0.attn.qkv` (max abs 0.015625), whose valid input rows are identical. The GPU runs a different BF16 GEMM kernel at 784 rows than at 1024, and the padded and unpadded FP64 references round to the same BF16 values for the valid rows. A model-local prototype that pre-fills the output with the bias and calls an output-aliased `addmm` on the 27 vision QKV projections brought the final difference for this image from 0.28125 to 0. It increased CUDA graph time from 11.82 to 12.06 ms and eager time from 18.73 to 19.92 ms, and the number of graph-covered conditions whose output exactly matched unpadded ordinary eager went from 12 to 14 of 25. It depends on how this PyTorch build dispatches `addmm`, has not been shown to improve accuracy or output quality, and is not part of this PR. The effect on generated text was not measured.

Encoder latency on FLASH_ATTN (medians of synchronized single calls over 5 paired rounds of 12 samples after 4 warmups, including metadata, packing and copies, excluding preprocessing):

| Input | Output tokens / budget | Eager ms | Graph ms |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Image 224 | 49 / 64 | 16.28 | 4.71 |
| Image 448 | 196 / 256 | 16.17 | 13.07 |
| Images 224 + 448 | 245 / 256 | 17.01 | 13.63 |
| Image 896 | 784 / 1024 | 42.89 | 47.45 |
| Video, 2 frames at 224 | 49 / 64 | 16.28 | 4.57 |
| Video, 8 frames at 224 | 196 / 256 | 16.29 | 11.84 |
| Video, 16 frames at 224 | 392 / 1024 | 16.86 | 33.41 |

This budget set was chosen for the run and is coarse, so the 896 image and the 16-frame video are padded far past their size. A budget close to the typical input size should avoid that slowdown, though only these budgets were timed. The timings were taken at 3687acad21; the later commit does not touch the FLASH_ATTN path.

CPU checks (no GPU), before the GPU runs:

- Eager encoder, main compared with this branch (`TORCH_SDPA`, fp32): a tiny random `Qwen3Omni_VisionTransformer` (hidden 64, 4 heads, depth 3, deepstack at layers 0 and 1) gives a max abs diff of 0.0 for single and mixed image and video grids, with `grid_thw` as a tensor or a list.
- Capture and replay logic through the real `EncoderCudaGraphManager`, with `torch.cuda.graph` replaced by a replayer that reruns `encoder_cudagraph_forward` on the captured buffers: 3 images in one batch, 2 images plus an oversized one, 5 images across two batches and 2 videos all match eager on each item alone (max abs diff 0.0).
- `ruff` check and format pass. `mypy` on `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py` adds no errors over main's version of the file in the same environment.

## Details

Differences from the Qwen3-VL integration:

- Absolute position embedding is optional. When `apply_vit_abs_pos_embed` is off, `pos_embeds` is `None` in both the captured inputs and the replay values. The existing manager already skips `None` values when it copies replay values (`_run_budget_graph`), and this PR does not change the manager. The encoder then adds no position embedding.
- Deepstack features come after the main merger (`merger_list`). The output is `[main, deepstack...]` along the hidden dimension, so `out_hidden_size` is `visual_dim + multiscale_dim`, where `multiscale_dim` is `visual_dim` times the number of deepstack layers.
- `rot_pos_emb` takes a list of `[t, h, w]` instead of a tensor, so all metadata is built from Python lists.
- Eager metadata comes from the shared `MMEncoderAttention` helpers: `cu_seqlens` is built with NumPy, `max_seqlen` comes from `compute_max_seqlen`, and `cu_seqlens` goes through `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`, for which the encoder now records `tp_size` and `fp8_padded_hidden_size`. Eager and graph share this path so that the graph replays the same metadata the eager encoder uses. If you would rather review the eager change on its own first, I can split it into a separate PR.

Not measured: TTFT and full-model output quality, other budget sets, FlashInfer latency, FP8 encoder attention, ROCm, and GPUs other than the RTX 4090.
