items.title: [Bug]: int8_per_token_head scale-view fill overwrites Gated DeltaNet state in hybrid models
items.body:
### Environment

- vLLM 0.32.0 built from the sdist for sm_70 (Tesla V100 PCIe 32 GB, driver
  580.196.07, CUDA 12.9), torch 2.13.0+cu126. The code path below is the same
  on every architecture, and `main` still contains it.
- `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4`, a Qwen3.5-family hybrid: 48 Gated DeltaNet layers
  and 16 full-attention layers in one paged KV pool.
- `--kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN
  --enable-prefix-caching`.

### What happens

The first request after engine start turns to garbage from its second token.
Every later request is correct. With `--kv-cache-dtype auto` the first request
is correct too.

### Cause

`TritonAttentionImpl._ensure_scale_caches` builds the per-token-head scale
views the first time a layer runs and fills them with 1.0
(`vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py`, abridged):

```python
self._k_scale_cache = torch.as_strided(base_f32, size=(num_blocks, block_size, nkv),
                                       stride=(block_f32, slot_f32, head_f32),
                                       storage_offset=k_scale_off_f32)
self._k_scale_cache.fill_(1.0)
...
self._v_scale_cache.fill_(1.0)
```

In this model the hybrid KV cache manager gives the attention layers and the
Gated DeltaNet layers views of the same physical pages. As #51091 notes, dummy
runs skip attention, so the first attention layer builds its views during the
first real forward pass, after the Gated DeltaNet layers before it have written
their recurrent state into those pages. The fill writes 1.0 over part of that
state.

The int8 K and V themselves match the FP16 values within 1.0-1.5% (K) and
0.9-2.4% (V) relative error on all 16 attention layers. Building
the same views without the fill fixes the first request. A sentinel test
confirms that view creation without the fill leaves the cache bytes unchanged,
and that the current method changes them.

### Relation to #51091

#51091 fixes the same fill for KV-sharing layers by initializing each view's
scale region once. That does not cover this case: here the first and only fill
of the view already happens after another layer type has written into the
pages.

### Suggested fix

Drop the fill. Attention reads scales only for slots that `reshape_and_cache`
has written, and each write stores the scale with its values. The Triton kernel
also masks scale loads to the sequence length (`other=1.0`). If an
initialization is still wanted, it has to run when the pool is allocated,
before any layer writes to it.

We run an out-of-tree workaround that overrides `_ensure_scale_caches` to build
the `torch.as_strided` views without writing.

items.title: Optimize DFlash context KV cache updates
items.body:
## Title

Optimize DFlash context KV cache updates

## Summary

This PR batches DFlash context KV cache writes across draft layers into a single Triton launch, reducing repeated `reshape_and_cache_flash` launches during `precompute_and_store_context_kv`.

## Background

In the DFlash path, `precompute_and_store_context_kv` currently computes K/V for all draft layers in a fused manner, but still writes each layer's KV cache one-by-one. For the profiled Qwen3 DFlash setup, this appears as 8 consecutive `reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel` launches, one per draft attention layer.

That per-layer launch pattern adds avoidable launch overhead even though:

- all draft layers share the same cache layout
- the source K/V tensors are already organized in layer-major form
- the write pattern differs mainly by destination cache base pointer

## What changed

### 1. Added a batched Triton KV-cache update kernel

- added `_dflash_batched_reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash` in `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py:52`
- added `_dflash_batched_reshape_and_cache_flash` in `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py:117`
- used per-layer cache pointer arrays so one launch can update all supported draft layers

### 2. Added a guarded fast path

- added `_can_use_dflash_batched_kv_cache_update` in `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py:194`
- enabled the batched path only for the non-quantized FlashAttention cache layout (`kv_cache_dtype == "auto"`) with matching tensor shape / stride / dtype / device across layers
- preserved the original per-layer `do_kv_cache_update` path as a fallback for unsupported cache configurations

### 3. Integrated the batched path into DFlash context precompute

- updated `precompute_and_store_context_kv` in `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py:531`
- the method now tries the batched cache update path first at `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py:615`
- unsupported configurations continue to use the original behavior

## Why this is safe

The change is intentionally narrow:

- it only affects the DFlash context-KV write path
- it keeps the original fallback path unchanged
- it only activates when all draft attention layers have a compatible cache layout
- it does not change K/V projection, RMSNorm, RoPE, or downstream attention semantics

## Performance change

Micro profile results for the same DFlash KV-cache write path:

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| KV cache write kernel launches | 8 | 1 | -87.5% |
| KV write CUDA total time | 13.823us | 4.320us | -68.7% |
| `cuLaunchKernelEx` total CPU time | 60.984us | 23.406us | -61.6% |
| Self CPU time total | 1.990ms | 1.854ms | -6.8% |

Additional detail:

- old path: `reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash` called 8 times, average CUDA time `1.728us` per call
- new path: `_dflash_batched_reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash` called 1 time, CUDA time `4.320us`

This shows the intended launch consolidation from 8 -> 1, with clear reductions in both kernel-launch overhead and total CUDA time for the KV write portion of the workload.

items.title: [Bug]: padded KV page reshape uses a spec-page stride against a kernel-block size, so as_strided over-requests storage by the split ratio
items.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.1.dev19262+gb6bbf29dd.d20260727` (image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:e90e2603b2781936651ba019804137714367c69e10a7b25a2e57b46995225616`)
- PyTorch 2.x / CUDA, FlashInfer 0.6.16rc5, Python 3.12
- Target: Kimi-K3 (hybrid KDA + MLA), TP=8 on B300; draft: a 5-layer dense Qwen3-style speculator
- Backends selected: draft `FLASHINFER`, verifier `FLASHINFER_MLA`, both HND

The reproducer below needs **none** of that — it is CPU-only and uses `FullAttentionSpec` directly.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`_reshape_attention_kv_cache` computes the block stride of a **padded** KV page from
`kv_cache_spec.page_size_bytes` (one *spec* page), while the `size` it is handed counts *kernel*
blocks. The two agree only when `storage_block_size == kernel_block_size`. As soon as the backend
splits a manager block into smaller kernel blocks, the strided view over-requests storage by exactly
the split ratio and `torch.as_strided` raises.

The padded-page path was added in #45181 ("keeps the logical block size unchanged … pads the smaller
physical page"). All four of its padded-page tests pass `kernel_block_sizes=[spec.block_size]`, i.e.
ratio 1, so the split case is not covered.

In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py`:

```python
# _reshape_kv_cache — size[0] counts KERNEL blocks
num_blocks = kv_raw_tensor.numel() // kv_cache_spec.page_size_bytes
num_blocks_per_kv_block = kv_cache_spec.storage_block_size // kernel_block_size
kernel_num_blocks = num_blocks * num_blocks_per_kv_block
kv_cache_shape = group.backend.get_kv_cache_shape(kernel_num_blocks, kernel_block_size, ...)

# _reshape_attention_kv_cache — stride[0] steps a whole SPEC page
page_stride = kv_cache_spec.page_size_bytes // dtype_size
strides[num_blocks_dim] = page_stride
kv_cache = torch.as_strided(kv_raw_tensor.view(dtype), size=permuted_kv_cache_shape,
                            stride=tuple(strides))
```

#### Minimal reproducer (CPU only, no GPU / no model)

```python
import torch
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import FullAttentionSpec
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.attn_utils import _reshape_kv_cache
from vllm.v1.worker.utils import AttentionGroup

class FakeFlashAttentionBackend:
    @staticmethod
    def get_kv_cache_shape(num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size,
                           cache_dtype_str="auto"):
        return (num_blocks, 2, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)
    @staticmethod
    def get_kv_cache_stride_order(include_num_layers_dimension=False):
        return (0, 1, 2, 3, 4)

def run(block_size, kernel_block_size, page_size_padded, num_blocks=3):
    spec = FullAttentionSpec(block_size=block_size, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=2,
                             dtype=torch.float32, page_size_padded=page_size_padded)
    raw = {"layer": torch.zeros(spec.page_size_bytes * num_blocks, dtype=torch.int8)}
    groups = [AttentionGroup(backend=FakeFlashAttentionBackend, layer_names=["layer"],
                             kv_cache_spec=spec, kv_cache_group_id=0)]
    kv = _reshape_kv_cache(groups, raw, "auto", [kernel_block_size], {})["layer"]
    print("OK", tuple(kv.shape), kv.stride())

run(16, 16, 384)    # ratio 1 -> OK      (the shape #45181's tests cover)
run(48, 16, 1024)   # ratio 3 -> raises
run(48, 16, 2304)   # ratio 3, padded page an exact multiple of the kernel page -> still raises
```

Output:

```
OK (3, 2, 16, 1, 2) (96, 32, 2, 2, 1)

RuntimeError: setStorage: sizes [9, 2, 16, 1, 2], strides [256, 32, 2, 2, 1], storage offset 0,
  and itemsize 4 requiring a storage size of 8448 are out of bounds for storage of size 3072

RuntimeError: setStorage: sizes [9, 2, 16, 1, 2], strides [576, 32, 2, 2, 1], storage offset 0,
  and itemsize 4 requiring a storage size of 18688 are out of bounds for storage of size 6912
```

The third case matters: the padded page is an exact multiple of the kernel page there, and it still
fails. So this is not an alignment problem — the size and the stride are in different units.

#### How it shows up in practice

Serving Kimi-K3 (KDA + MLA) with a dense full-attention draft, all 8 TP workers die identically at
engine init:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 508, in initialize_kv_cache
    kv_caches_dict = init_kv_cache(
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 459, in init_kv_cache
    kv_caches = _reshape_kv_cache(
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 333, in _reshape_kv_cache
    kv_caches[layer_name] = _reshape_attention_kv_cache(
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 244, in _reshape_attention_kv_cache
    kv_cache = torch.as_strided(
RuntimeError: setStorage: sizes [34950, 2, 256, 128], strides [442368, 32768, 128, 1], storage
  offset 0, and itemsize 2 requiring a storage size of 30920769536 are out of bounds for storage
  of size 10307174400
```

`30920769536 / 10307174400 = 3.000`. Consistent reading of those numbers:

```
MLA page  = 768 x 576 x 2 = 884736   <- max_page_size
draft page= 768 x 2 x 64 x 2 = 196608   (884736 % 196608 = 98304, not divisible)
  -> unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size pads: page_size_padded = 884736
kernel_block_size = 256, storage_block_size = 768  -> ratio 3
num_blocks = 10307174400 / 884736 = 11650
size[0]    = 11650 x 3 = 34950     (matches)
stride[0]  = 884736 / 2 = 442368   (matches)
```

Whether the manager `block_size` of 768 came from `CacheConfig` or from an earlier scaling step I did
not confirm — that part needs an instrumented run on the real model, which I could not schedule. Every
other step above is self-consistent with the reported numbers, and the CPU reproducer does not depend
on it.

Note the draft reaches this path only because it has no sliding-window layer:
`_try_get_full_allocation_fallback_groups` requires `has_mla and has_regular_swa`, and with a
`SlidingWindowSpec` draft the specs are instead promoted into one `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group where
each layer keeps its own page size (`KVCacheTensor(size=per_layer_specs[layer].page_size_bytes *
num_blocks)`) — no unification, no padding, no strided view. Swapping the same draft to a
sliding-window spec serves fine on this build, which is what isolates the defect to the padded path.

#### Note on fixing it

Dividing the block stride by the split ratio is not sufficient. The real content occupies
`ratio * unpadded_kernel_page` bytes at the *start* of each padded page, with the padding after it, so
the kernel blocks are not evenly spaced across the padded page. That is a two-level layout and
`as_strided` has a single stride per dimension. Options that do look expressible:

- add a dimension so the view is `[num_blocks, ratio, ...]` (changes the shape contract backends consume);
- forbid the kernel split when `page_size_padded is not None` (force `kernel_block_size == block_size`);
- avoid padding for this combination, e.g. extend the `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` per-layer-page path that
  already handles the sliding-window case.

Happy to send a PR for whichever direction maintainers prefer; the choice affects the backend shape
contract so I did not want to pick unilaterally.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched existing issues. #43626 and #46480 are both closed and are a different failure — they
  raise `AssertionError` *inside* `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` (`MambaSpec.page_size_bytes` not
  scaling with `block_size`). Here unification succeeds via the padded branch and the crash is later, in
  the strided view.

items.title: [RFC]: Stable, versioned plugin contract for out-of-tree attention backends + custom KV-cache specs
items.body:
### Motivation.

## Motivation & Context

I maintain an out-of-tree attention backend implementing a custom compressed KV-cache layout registered via the `vllm.general_plugins` entry point (`AttentionBackendEnum.CUSTOM`).

While the general plugin architecture is fantastic, the internal surfaces for KV-cache spec registration and page-sizing semantics shift frequently across minor releases. For instance, between `v0.20` and `v0.28`, spec registration migrated to `KVCacheSpecRegistry`, and the semantics around `page_size_bytes` and `unpadded_page_size_bytes` changed.

Because these interfaces are not currently governed by a versioned contract or deprecation policy, maintaining out-of-tree KV backends across vLLM releases requires continuous debugging of internal architectural shifts.

---

## Proposal

Would the maintainers consider establishing a documented, versioned contract (or explicit stability tier) for out-of-tree attention and KV-cache backends? Specifically:

1. **Attention-Backend Registration API:** A stable public surface and clear deprecation path across minor versions for custom backend registration.
2. **KV-Cache Spec & Page-Sizing Semantics:** A versioned interface for `KVCacheSpecRegistry` alongside formal semantics for block-byte sizing (`page_size_bytes`, `unpadded_page_size_bytes`, and how custom raw tensors are reshaped for compressed layouts).

---

## Willingness to Contribute

I would be happy to contribute to this effort by:

* Providing a detailed breakdown of the exact breaking changes hit when upgrading from `v0.20` to `v0.28`.
* Drafting an initial *"Writing an Out-of-Tree Attention/KV Backend"* developer guide to document current best practices.

### Proposed Change.

**Feature Request: Documented, Versioned Plugin Contract for Out-of-Tree Attention Backends**

**Context & Problem**
Maintaining out-of-tree attention backends currently requires tracking internal architecture shifts across minor vLLM releases. Key interfaces change between minor versions without explicit deprecation paths, creating significant maintenance overhead for third-party hardware and custom kernel backends.

**Proposed Solution**
Define a documented, versioned plugin contract (e.g., `PluginAPI v1` or explicit stability tiers) for custom attention backends, backed by a developer guide. Specifically, this contract would stabilize three surfaces that recently experienced breaking changes:

* **Attention Backend Registration:** Establish a stable public interface for backend registration (currently using `vllm.general_plugins` + `AttentionBackendEnum.CUSTOM`) with guaranteed compatibility windows or clear deprecation paths across minor releases.
* **KV-Cache Spec Registration:** Standardize the interface for registering custom `KVCacheSpec` managers. This mechanism moved from `spec_manager_map` (`vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager`) in v0.20 to `KVCacheSpecRegistry` (`vllm.v1.kv_cache_spec_registry`) in v0.28 without a versioned abstraction.
* **Page-Size / Block-Byte Semantics:** Document and stabilize the required contract for page and block layout properties. This includes property naming shifts (e.g., `real_page_size_bytes` in v0.20 vs. `page_size_bytes` / `unpadded_page_size_bytes` in v0.28) and the exact semantics for how raw tensors are allocated and reshaped via `get_kv_cache_shape` using `storage_block_size`, `page_size_padded`, and packing.

**Proposed Contributions**
We can contribute an initial "Writing an Out-of-Tree Attention Backend" documentation draft based on our experience maintaining an external backend, alongside a detailed breakdown of historical breaking points to help define the initial API boundary.

items.title: [Perf][KV Connector] Drop the redundant index_select in kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive
items.body:
## Purpose

`kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive` rewrites the blocks that were just copied
into the local cache so that their layout matches what the local attention
backend expects. It gathers them, permutes the two inner dimensions and writes
them back:

```python
blocks_to_update = cache.index_select(0, indices)      # line 283
target_shape = list(blocks_to_update.shape)
target_shape[0] = -1
inv_order = [0, 1, 3, 2, 4] if blocks_to_update.ndim == 5 else [0, 2, 1, 3]
src_shape = tuple(target_shape[i] for i in inv_order)
blocks_to_update = cache.index_select(0, indices)      # line 288 - identical
permuted_blocks = blocks_to_update.reshape(src_shape).permute(*inv_order)
cache.index_copy_(0, indices, permuted_blocks)
```

Line 288 repeats line 283 verbatim and immediately overwrites its result with
an identical tensor, so the reshape/permute/copy are unaffected by it. The
first call is needed (`target_shape`/`inv_order` are derived from its shape and
ndim); the second is not.

`index_select` is a full gather of every received block, and this runs on the
decode side for each received block set, so the duplicate doubles a temporary
allocation proportional to the transferred KV. Deleting the statement is
behaviour-preserving; the only observable difference is one fewer gather.

## Test Plan

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py` wraps a
real `torch` cache tensor so the gathers and the write-back are counted, and
runs the helper for both the 4D and the 5D cache layout:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py -q
```

Besides the call counts it also pins the operation's contract - a layout fix-up
is a permutation, so the received blocks must keep their multiset of values and
untouched blocks must be left alone - which guards against a future change that
"optimises" the remaining gather away or reorders the permutation.

## Test Result

```
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py ..   [100%]
2 passed
```

On the unpatched tree the same test reports two gathers and fails:

```
FAILED .../test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py::test_the_received_blocks_are_gathered_once[4d_cache]
FAILED .../test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py::test_the_received_blocks_are_gathered_once[5d_cache]
2 failed
```

Tested on main (`105a4e09`), Linux x86_64 / Python 3.12, CPU-only `torch`.

items.title: [ROCm][Model] Add fusions for Muse Glimmer for AMD backend
items.body:
## Overview 1) Muse has a pattern rmsnorm + add + rmsnorm. This PR adds a fused kernel for these operations. Previously it had a single kernel that was from inductor but the custom AITER fused kernel has better perf (~2us / 40%) in decode and 30-40us / 50% in prefill. 2) Fuse the rmsnorm + reshape + rope and cache kernel. 3) (2) required AITER FA to be default. Baseline is using using vllm's ROCm FA backend which is not optimized. ## Claims TPOT and total tok/s should speed up substantially. ## Validation Concurrency | A TTFT ms | B TTFT ms | A TPOT ms | B TPOT ms | A total tok/s | B total tok/s -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 1 | 60.4 | 57.2 | 13.5 | 11.0 | 147.5 | 181.9 2 | 88.2 | 98.4 | 14.0 | 11.3 | 283.6 | 350.5 4 | 162.1 | 162.1 | 15.0 | 11.5 | 526.9 | 688.7 8 | 290.0 | 294.3 | 16.4 | 12.6 | 958.2 | 1243.9 16 | 532.3 | 487.2 | 16.8 | 13.0 | 1846.3 | 2364.3 32 | 849.7 | 788.1 | 18.1 | 14.3 | 3379.8 | 4247.4 64 | 1388.2 | 1237.4 | 20.4 | 16.3 | 5888.8 | 7301.0 128 | 2125.1 | 1975.2 | 24.9 | 20.5 | 9462.5 | 11361.2 There should be a ~20% improvement in TPOT and total throughput (latter for decode heavy cases) and a ~5% improvement in TTFT. ## Details Fusions improve performance in decode by amortizing kernel launch latency. Moving to fused kernels improves decode performance and in some cases also TTFT. Before: The three kernels pre-attention are ~4us each (this is (1) from the Overview). The rmsnorm is 6us and is also ~30% larger in prefill (not in screenshot) most likely due to inductor not being great at generalizing for shapes (this is (2) from Overview). Attention is 144us (this is (3) from Overview). After: The fused kernel ((1)) is 4us (vs 12), rmsnorm is 4us (vs 6) and also ~30% faster and attention is 27us vs 144. There should be no changes to any backend other than ROCm. The changes are gated to both rocm and AITER being enabled. There is a new fusion pass added for the rmsnorm+add+rmsnorm as that did not exist before. Same with the qk rope pass. Unit tests are added for both. ---

items.title: [Kernel] Integrate FA4 SM90 FP8 MMA for Gemma-4 full attention
items.body:
## Overview

Enable FP8 MMA in the SM90 FA4 full-attention kernel ([PR199](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/199)) for Gemma-4 while retaining FP8 KV-cache storage.

Gemma-4 uses head dimension 512 for full attention and 256 for sliding-window attention. This change compares FP8 MMA against the existing path that reads FP8 KV, dequantizes it, and performs FP16 MMA.

On H200, FP8 full attention uses FA4, while FP8 sliding-window attention continues to use FA3. FA4 FP8 sliding-window attention with head dimension 256 is currently unsupported.

## Claims

- Integrate the SM90 d512 FP8-MMA kernel while preserving native FP16/BF16 queries and supported FA3 sliding-window routing.
- Gate unsupported kernel combinations and normalize descale layouts.
- Allow FA4 full-attention layers to select splits automatically, removing the previous CUDA-graph cap of 32 for these layers; retain the cap for FA3.
- Report measured gains over the KV-dequantization baseline and the remaining regression against BF16 KV/MMA.

## Validation
The MMA labels describe the **full-attention path**. Both FP8-KV configurations use FA3 FP8 sliding-window attention; the BF16-KV reference uses FA4 BF16 sliding-window attention.

Serving setup:

- Gemma-4-31B-it-FP8 weights for all configurations.
- Four H200 GPUs on one node; TP4.
- Approximately 25K shared prefix plus 3K unique input tokens.
- 128 requests, 200 output tokens per request.
- MTP enabled with three speculative tokens.
- Prefix-cache reuse enabled.
- Concurrency 1–64; median of three rounds.

### Serving performance
The `8k-in-1k-out` benchmark of [`gemma_4_31b_it_h200`](https://github.com/vllm-project/perf-eval/blob/main/workloads/gemma_4_31b_it_h200.yaml) on one H200 at TP=1, with GPU clocks locked. Each number is the median of 3 repetitions, as perf-eval aggregates them; no request failed.

| | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before (`5d35ce3934` + FA `b273a02`) | 796.5 | 126.5 | 75.1 |
| This PR + vllm-project/flash-attention#199 | **831.1 (1.04x)** | **123.2** | **69.3** |
| Delta | +4.3% | -2.6% | -7.8% |

<details><summary>Reproduce</summary>

- Before is this PR's base, `5d35ce3934`, with FlashAttention at vllm-project/flash-attention#199's base, `b273a02`. After is this PR's head, `237043eee6`, with #199's head, `2648f1b`.
- Neither PR changes C++. Both runs use one editable build of `237043eee6` with `VLLM_FLASH_ATTN_SRC_DIR` set to the FlashAttention checkout, and differ only in Python sources.
- The model is a local copy of `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic`. Server and benchmark match perf-eval@5f4e445 (`lib/server.sh`, `lib/run_vllm_bench.sh`, `lib/aggregate_perf.py`).

```bash
VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
vllm serve $MODEL --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4 --enable-auto-tool-choice

# 3 repetitions against the same server; median of each metric
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model $MODEL \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 128 --num-warmups 128
```

</details>

### Model evaluation
Accuracy scores are percentages. **87.19% for AIME 2025, 85.73% for GPQA Diamond (avg@16), and 86.86% for MMLU-Pro are measured in this PR; the two reference columns are reported baselines from [PR #48666](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48666).**

| Benchmark | FP8 KV + FP8 MMA ([PR199](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/199)) | FP8 KV + FP16 MMA (reference FA4) | 	BF16 TRITON |
|---|---|---|---|
| AIME 2025 (avg@64) | 87.19 | 86.88 | 87.29 |
| GPQA Diamond (avg@16) | 85.73* | 86.55 | 85.42 |
| MMLU-Pro | 86.86  | 86.64 | 86.44 |

\* Note that in a paird GPQA Diamond comparison using the same 198 questions and 16 seeds, FP8 MMA scored 85.73% versus 85.32% for the FP8 KV + FP16 MMA. The difference was +0.41 percentage points, with a paired question-bootstrap 95% interval of [−0.51, +1.36] points. Both runs had zero invalid or truncated answers. The table’s 86.55% reference is imported from PR [#48666](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48666) and is separate from this matched control.

### MTP speculative decoding

Mean acceptance length (**AL**), median of three rounds, from the same sweep as the serving-performance table above. All configurations use FP8 model weights, TP4 on four H200 GPUs, three speculative tokens, and prefix-cache reuse enabled. Each measurement completed **128/128 requests without errors**. AL includes the bonus token emitted per speculative step.

| Configuration | cc1 | cc2 | cc4 | cc8 | cc16 | cc32 | cc64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP8 KV + FP8 MMA | 2.9830 | 2.9932 | 3.0002 | 2.9640 | 2.9849 | 2.9860 | 2.9793 |
| FP8 KV + FP16 MMA | 2.9924 | 2.9691 | 3.0130 | 2.9995 | 2.9993 | 2.9857 | 2.9979 |
| BF16 KV + BF16 MMA | 3.0053 | 2.9823 | 2.9940 | 2.9935 | 2.9995 | 3.0002 | 2.9982 |

## Reproduction commands
The Hopper FP8 MMA path supports text-only workloads. The commands use --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' to disable Gemma-4’s bidirectional/mm-prefix attention. Multimodal Gemma-4 with FP8 KV uses Triton instead of this kernel. FP8 sliding-window layers use FA3, so do not force FA4 globally.

Serve and benchmark: 25K shared prefix, TP4, MTP3, cache reuse on

* FP8 KV + FP8 MMA (this PR):

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --compilation-config '{"use_inductor_graph_partition":1,"pass_config":{"eliminate_noops":true,"fuse_allreduce_rms":true}}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$ASSISTANT\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"
```

* FP8 KV + FP16 MMA (PR [#164](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/164) baseline kernel environment):
(The two FP8-KV serving commands are identical because MMA selection depends on the FlashAttention kernel source, not a CLI flag. For the control, we kept the same vLLM integration but replaced its vendored CuTe sources with the PR [#164](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/164) dequantizing kernel, including the baseline safety fixes, then restarted the server. --kv-cache-dtype fp8 selects FP8 cache storage in both cases)

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --compilation-config '{"use_inductor_graph_partition":1,"pass_config":{"eliminate_noops":true,"fuse_allreduce_rms":true}}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$ASSISTANT\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"
```

* BF16 KV + BF16 MMA:

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --compilation-config '{"use_inductor_graph_partition":1,"pass_config":{"eliminate_noops":true,"fuse_allreduce_rms":true}}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$ASSISTANT\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"
```

These recorded runs left the FA version unset. The dequantized control uses the PR [#164](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/164) baseline kernel environment.

Benchmark:

```bash
aiperf profile \
  --model "$MODEL" --tokenizer "$MODEL" --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --endpoint-type chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --streaming \
  --use-legacy-max-tokens --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --input-file "$DATASET" \
  --extra-inputs max_tokens:200 --extra-inputs min_tokens:200 \
  --extra-inputs ignore_eos:true --extra-inputs skip_special_tokens:false \
  --random-seed 1234 --use-server-token-count \
  --concurrency 16 --request-count 128 --num-dataset-entries 128
```

Run at concurrency 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64; report the median of three rounds.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation commands</summary>

Evaluation server on four H200 GPUs. AIME and GPQA use `--max-num-seqs 16`; MMLU-Pro uses `32`. No MTP.

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL" --served-model-name gemma \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 101716968203 --enforce-eager \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --attention-config.flash_attn_version=3 --block-size 64 \
  --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=false \
  --kernel-config.enable_cutedsl_warmup=false \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}'
```

**AIME 2025, avg@64**

Use `aime.yaml` with 64 samples per problem, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, and the GPT-4.1 judge configuration. Export `INFERENCE_API_KEY`.

```bash
docker run --rm --network host --shm-size=100g \
  -e DUMMY_API_KEY=dummy -e INFERENCE_API_KEY \
  -v "$PWD/aime.yaml:/config.yaml:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/aime-results:/results" \
  --entrypoint bash nvcr.io/nvidia/eval-factory/simple-evals:26.03 \
  -lc 'runner=$(command -v nemo-evaluator || command -v eval-factory); exec "$runner" run_eval --run_config /config.yaml'
```

**GPQA Diamond, avg@16**

Use `gpqa.yaml` with all 198 questions, the `eval/aai/mcq-4choices` prompt, temperature 1.0, and top-p 0.95. Run seeds 0–15.

```bash
pids=()
for seed in $(seq 0 15); do
  docker run --rm --network host --shm-size=4g \
    -e DUMMY_API_KEY=dummy -e HF_TOKEN \
    -e NEMO_EVALUATOR_TELEMETRY_LEVEL=0 -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
    -v "$PWD/gpqa.yaml:/config.yaml:ro" \
    -v "$PWD/gpqa-results/seed-$seed:/results" \
    --entrypoint bash "$EVAL_IMAGE" \
    -lc 'runner=$(command -v nemo-evaluator || command -v eval-factory); exec "$runner" run_eval --run_config /config.yaml "$@"' \
    -- --overrides "config.params.extra.args=++prompt_config=eval/aai/mcq-4choices ++inference.random_seed=$seed" &
  pids+=("$!")
done

status=0
for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do
  wait "$pid" || status=1
done
test "$status" -eq 0
```

**MMLU-Pro**

Restart the evaluation server with `--max-num-seqs 32`. Use `mmlu.yaml` with all 12,032 questions, one sample per question, the `eval/aai/mcq-10choices-boxed` prompt, temperature 1.0, and top-p 0.95.

```bash
mkdir -p mmlu-results
chmod 777 mmlu-results

docker run --rm --network host --shm-size=4g \
  -e DUMMY_API_KEY=dummy -e HF_TOKEN \
  -e NEMO_EVALUATOR_TELEMETRY_LEVEL=0 -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  -v "$PWD/mmlu.yaml:/config.yaml:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/mmlu-results:/results" \
  --entrypoint bash "$EVAL_IMAGE" \
  -lc 'runner=$(command -v nemo-evaluator || command -v eval-factory); exec "$runner" run_eval --run_config /config.yaml'
```

</details>

## Details

### Why FP8 is slower than BF16

Nsight shows that faster FP8 full attention does not necessarily produce faster end-to-end execution.

#### Sliding-window attention and KV-cache operations offset full-attention gains

The profiling setup uses 25K inputs, TP4, MTP enabled, prefix reuse enabled, and offered concurrency 64.

| Target-model kernel work | FP8 KV + FP8 MMA | BF16 KV + BF16 MMA | FP8 time reduction vs. BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full attention | **6.681 ms** | 7.584 ms | **+11.9%** |
| Sliding-window attention | 5.482 ms | **4.206 ms** | −30.3% |
| KV-cache writes | 0.261 ms | **0.157 ms** | −66.2% |
| Attention preparation | 0.105 ms | 0 | N/A |
| Whole-cycle GPU span | 29.879 ms | **29.391 ms** | −1.7% |

Time reduction is `100 × (BF16 time − FP8 time) / BF16 time`, calculated from the displayed times. Positive values mean less time (faster); negative values mean more time (slower). 

Full attention is approximately **12% faster**, but sliding-window attention is approximately **30% slower**, with additional KV-write, preparation, and combine work.

KV-write overhead refers to the kernels that reshape and write newly generated keys and values into the paged cache, including the FP8 conversion/quantization path. Attention reads and prefix-cache reuse accounting are separate from this kernel category.

Reuse-off profiles show the same pattern.
The following comparison uses **cc16**, 25K inputs, TP4, MTP enabled, and prefix-cache reuse disabled. These matched pure-decode cycles process **16 active requests per target step**. Values are medians across four GPU ranks of each rank's per-cycle medians, with 69 matched cycles per rank for BF16 and 87 for FP8.

| Target-model kernel work | FP8 KV + FP8 MMA | BF16 KV + BF16 MMA | FP8 time reduction vs. BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full attention | **1.9670 ms** | 2.4358 ms | **+19.2%** |
| Sliding-window attention | 1.9593 ms | **1.3867 ms** | −41.3% |
| KV-cache writes | 0.2551 ms | **0.1413 ms** | −80.5% |
| Attention preparation | 0.1098 ms | 0 | N/A |
| Whole-cycle GPU span | 14.6594 ms | **14.2903 ms** | −2.6% |

Full attention is faster, but SWA, KV-cache writes, and attention preparation/combine offset the gain. The whole-cycle GPU span is **2.6% longer** for FP8. This is a profiling comparison, not an unprofiled end-to-end throughput measurement.

---

items.title: [GDN] Avoid two per-layer copies in the FlashInfer prefill path
items.body:
[GDN] Avoid two per-layer copies in the FlashInfer prefill path

## Purpose

Each GatedDeltaNet layer pays two extra `[num_tokens, num_v_heads, head_v_dim]` copies per prefill step in the FlashInfer chunk path:

1. The chunk kernel writes a fresh tensor which is then assigned into the pre-allocated `core_attn_out` (`core_attn_out[:n] = out.squeeze(0)`).
2. `_rms_norm_gated_cuda` reshapes the gate `z` to `[n * heads, head_v_dim]`. `z` is a strided slice of the fused `in_proj_qkvz` output, so the reshape materializes a clone (`aten::reshape -> aten::clone` in the profiler).

This PR removes both:

- The prefill rows of `core_attn_out` are passed to `flashinfer.gdn_prefill.chunk_gated_delta_rule` as its `output` buffer, so the kernel writes in place. It is applied only when there is no MTP merge (`spec_sequence_masks is None`); with peeled decode tokens the prefill tail is written directly and only the decode rows are stored afterwards.
- The gated RMSNorm runs on `[n, heads * head_v_dim]` rows with `group_size=head_v_dim` and a per-head weight tiled once and cached, so the strided `z` stays a view. Numerics are unchanged: max abs diff 0.0 against the previous formulation at T=8192 (see below).

Both changes are Python-only and apply to every model using `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` with the FlashInfer prefill backend (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next).

Related work: #45717 (draft, needs rebase) proposes the same output-buffer idea behind an opt-in env flag and skips mixed decode+prefill batches; it does not address the `z` clone. This PR is unconditional, covers the split batch, and adds the norm change. Happy to coordinate if that PR is revived.

## Test Plan

Norm equivalence (old `reshape(-1, V)` formulation vs. grouped rows):

```bash
python - <<'EOF'
import torch
from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.layernorm_guard import layer_norm_fwd
n, HV, V = 8192, 48, 128
x = torch.randn(n, HV, V, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
z = torch.randn(n, 16384, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)[:, 10240:].reshape(n, HV, V)
w = torch.randn(V, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1 + 1
a = torch.empty_like(x); b = torch.empty_like(x)
layer_norm_fwd(x.reshape(-1, V), w, None, 1e-6, z=z.reshape(-1, V), out=a.reshape(-1, V), group_size=V, norm_before_gate=True, is_rms_norm=True, activation="silu")
layer_norm_fwd(x.view(n, -1), w.repeat(HV), None, 1e-6, z=z.view(n, -1), out=b.view(n, -1), group_size=V, norm_before_gate=True, is_rms_norm=True, activation="silu")
print((a.float() - b.float()).abs().max().item())
EOF
```

Serving benchmark (1x B300 SXM6, TP=1, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --served-model-name qwen-flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 10240 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,16,32]}'

for case in "8192 1024 1" "8192 1024 8" "2048 128 32" "128 128 1"; do set -- $case
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
    --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --served-model-name qwen-flash \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len $1 --random-output-len $2 \
    --random-range-ratio 0 --random-prefix-len 0 --num-prompts $((5*$3)) \
    --num-warmups $((3*$3)) --request-rate inf --max-concurrency $3 \
    --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 42
done
```

Accuracy: GSM8K, full 1319-question test split, 5-shot as multi-turn chat, `enable_thinking=false`, greedy, max 2048 output tokens, 32 concurrent requests against the same server.

## Test Result

Norm equivalence: max abs diff `0.0`; the norm call drops from 185 us to 114 us per layer at T=8192.

Serving (single-run p50; measured on top of two unrelated local decode changes that do not touch the prefill path, so the TTFT delta is attributable to this PR):

| case | before TTFT / TPOT (ms) | after TTFT / TPOT (ms) | tok/s before -> after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c=1 | 238.5 / 5.00 | 236.6 / 5.00 | 191.1 -> 191.3 |
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c=8 | 1153.7 / 9.25 | 1131.7 / 9.08 | 774.9 -> 783.4 |
| 2048 in / 128 out, c=32 | 558.8 / 20.62 | 541.9 / 20.60 | 1263.3 -> 1275.3 |
| 128 in / 128 out, c=1 | 107.1 / 4.96 | 103.6 / 4.96 | 173.6 -> 174.6 |

GSM8K strict exact match: 96.82% (1277/1319) after, 96.82% baseline main.

AI-assisted implementation and testing; reviewed and tested by the submitter.

items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix direct NVFP4 KV writer V-scale layout on SM12x
items.body:
## Overview

Fix the retained `reshape_and_cache_flash` CUDA operation's NVFP4 V-scale layout on SM120/SM121, including `nvfp4_4over6`. This addresses the direct-operation mismatch in #50084. Current SM12x serving uses FlashInfer's replacement writer from #46963; this PR does not fix that serving path.

## Claims

- Capability family 12 writes linear V scales, matching the existing operation tests and reader layout. K scales remain linear.
- Valid SM100 layouts retain their V-scale swizzle. Invalid swizzle dimensions are rejected before launch.
- Extend the existing K/V roundtrip tests to `nvfp4_4over6` and enable their existing head-size-80 cases on family 12.

## Validation

Tested main `18c19eaf23` with refreshed head `1be231ee8c` on ThinkStation PGX / GB10 SM121, CUDA 13.0 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. A fresh isolated environment built and installed the full upstream `_C_stable_libtorch` component. Tests use the actual exported `_C_cache_ops` binding without an adapter; the patched arm rebuilt the changed CUDA object and relinked.

`pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k 'nvfp4 and 1024' -q`: **stock 36 failed; patched 36 passed**. Both arms had 252 skips and 1256 deselected cases. Coverage includes BF16, NHD/HND, head sizes 64/80/256, page sizes 8/16/32, and both NVFP4 variants. The existing test halves the selected 1024-block/42-token parameters to 512 blocks/21 tokens.

Stock failures were numerical assertions: 34 V failures and two K failures in the NHD/head-80/page-8 cases, where the invalid V swizzle can overrun its page. SM100 hardware was unavailable; its valid branch is unchanged by inspection. Configured scoped pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` pass.

On October 10, after the author confirmed line-by-line review and requested tests under their oversight, the same patched binding passed again: **36 passed**, 252 skipped, 1256 deselected. Codex operated the tests. No serving-model quality or performance claim is made.

## Details

#46963 bypasses this operation in SM12x serving; #60452 retains that replacement writer when enabling XQA decode. The exported CUDA operation and its tests still admit SM12x NVFP4, so their layout contract remains worth fixing.

The architecture gate targets family 12 exactly. The device guard precedes the capability query; four-token/four-scale alignment checks apply only to the swizzle path; launch errors are checked immediately. The separate MiniMax-M3 fused writer is unchanged.

AI assistance was used for the original patch and refresh. Original authorship and attribution are retained; Codex assisted with the audit, refresh and validation under human review and oversight.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Fold Q fp8 quantization into QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass (drop per-layer scaled_quant)
items.body:
### Summary

In `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass`, the fp8-attention (`quant_query`) path runs the AITER fused kernel (`fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_pts_quant_shuffle`, which returns Q in bf16) and then a **separate** Q -> fp8 quantization in `replacement_fp8_quant_query` / `_quantize_query` — the code notes *"the fused operation does not quantize Q."* This shows up as one `aiter::scaled_quant_kernel<bf16, fp8>` per attention layer, between the fused prologue kernel and unified attention.

### Observed

Gemma4-31B (FP8-block), `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Per-layer decode prologue in the GPU trace:

`fused_mrope_rms_kv_kernel` -> `aiter::scaled_quant_kernel<bf16, fp8>` (Q -> fp8) -> `kernel_unified_attention_2d`

The K/V fp8 quant is already inside the fused kernel (written to the fp8 cache); only Q is quantized by a separate launch.

### Proposed change

Once the AITER kernel can emit fp8 Q + scale (blocked on ROCm/aiter#5912): update `replacement_fp8_quant_query` to pass `q_scale` into the fused op and consume the kernel's fp8 Q directly, dropping the `_quantize_query` post-step and the extra bf16 `q_out` buffer.

Scope: the **static per-tensor** `quant_query` path only. The per-head / group-shape static-quant form (degenerate one-KV-head via `static_scaled_fp8_quant`) and the bf16-attention path are unaffected.

### Expected impact

Removes one small (~5 us) kernel per attention layer. Like the already-fused `reshape_and_cache`, the win is mainly in prefill / eager batches (decode is CUDA-graph-replayed and weight-bandwidth-bound), so this is kernel-count / prefill-latency cleanup rather than a large decode gain.

### Depends on / relates to

- Depends on: ROCm/aiter#5912
- Relates to: #58841, #53918, #58838

---
*Filed with Claude Code assistance; reviewed by @mpashkovskii.*

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Qwen3.8-2.4T specialized decode on MI355X (--monokernel)
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Opt-in `--monokernel` decode for Qwen3.8-2.4T (`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`) at TP8 on MI355X. Laid out per the specialized-decode RFC #60904 under `vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/specialized_decode/`, as Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's (#63032). A decode step of 1–16 rows runs two persistent FlyDSL launches a layer; everything else runs vLLM's forward. No core changes beyond the `--monokernel` docstring.

## Claims

- Decode TPOT at 1–16 concurrent requests on MI355X TP8: −33% at 1 (8.36 → 5.61 ms, 8k/1k), −18% at 8, −9% at 16; above 16 rows steps run stock (within 1%).
- Accuracy within noise of stock: GSM8K 0.976 vs 0.973, GPQA Diamond (thinking, 198 questions) 0.919 vs 0.934 (±0.019 per run). GSM8K under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (Triton GDN prefill, since AITER's FlyDSL GDN prefill metadata syncs the host on prefills) completes with 0.968: no host syncs in the decode path. RULER NIAH at 64k / 128k: being measured.
- Follows RFC #60904: `--monokernel` switch, default-deny refusals in three stages (each listing every reason, TP ranks agreeing), one `plan()` per step, MRV2 only, model-owned code, weights and caches read in place.
- A rank whose cross-rank wait gives up (10 s) marks itself failed; the TP ranks raise together within 16 steps, so the engine stops rather than hangs (tested with a stalled rank).
- Kernel numerics tests (TP8, MI355X) and CPU refusal/routing tests, with a Buildkite MI355 (8 GPU) step.

## Validation

**Serving** (MI355X TP8, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9` with this branch's `vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/` and model hook overlaid; both arms `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, AITER fused shared experts, FULL CUDA graphs, FP8 KV cache, prefix caching off, `--max-num-seqs 256`; stock adds nothing, the candidate adds `--monokernel`; `vllm bench serve` random dataset, about 4× concurrency prompts (at least 8), as many warmups as concurrency; mean TPOT, ms):

| concurrency | 8k/1k stock | 8k/1k `--monokernel` | 1k/1k stock | 1k/1k `--monokernel` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 8.36 | 5.61 (−33%) | 8.33 | 5.59 (−33%) |
| 2 | 8.82 | 6.45 (−27%) | 8.81 | 6.46 (−27%) |
| 4 | 10.47 | 8.38 (−20%) | 10.35 | 8.15 (−21%) |
| 8 | 13.78 | 11.30 (−18%) | 12.80 | 10.39 (−19%) |
| 12 | 18.51 | 16.98 (−8%) | 16.34 | 14.83 (−9%) |
| 16 | 19.23 | 17.55 (−9%) | 16.51 | 15.00 (−9%) |
| 24 | | | 19.25 | 19.28 |
| 32 | | | 21.99 | 22.14 |
| 48 | | | 26.51 | 26.71 |
| 64 | | | 29.55 | 29.76 |

**Per launch** (µs, TP8 on MI355X, each launch in a CUDA graph of 46, weights rotated over enough copies that the 256 MB MALL does not hold a layer's weights across launches, random routing):

| rows | GDN block | layer block (out_proj MXFP4) | layer block (o_proj BF16, gated) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 13.3 | 32.2 | 35.9 |
| 2 | 15.3 | 38.2 | 42.9 |
| 4 | 19.8 | 54.8 | 59.0 |
| 8 | 25.4 | 74.1 | 78.8 |
| 12 | 30.6 | 99.0 | 104.7 |
| 16 | 34.7 | 120.8 | 127.2 |

From 8 rows up the layer block's routed experts stream about 6 TB/s of MXFP4 weights; the rest is the all-reduce, norm and route hand-offs (about 3 µs each between CTAs).

**Tests** (MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9` with this branch's `vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/` overlaid, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v -s tests/models/qwen3_5/amd_specialized_decode`): all 41 tests pass.

- `test_kernels.py`: the GDN block against the Gemma residual add + norm, in_proj, AITER's conv update and fused gated delta rule and `RMSNormGated` at widths 1, 5, 8, 9, 16 (pad rows included, first layer included), on either MXFP4 GEMM layout; the layer block against o_proj / out_proj, the all-reduce, `fused_add_rms_norm`, the router's softmax top-10, the MXFP4 experts with the fused shared expert and the MoE all-reduce at widths 1, 3, 8, 9, 15, 16 (each twice: both epoch parities), on all 8 ranks with rank agreement and the health words left clear. A stalled-rank test launches the layer block on rank 0 only: its waits give up after ~10 s, the failed word and rank 0's flag are set, the given-up waits name only mailbox regions of this kernel, and the next launch returns at once.
- `test_runtime.py` (host side, no kernels launched; skipped off ROCm like `test_kernels.py`): off without the flag, every-reason refusal messages, parallel/feature refusals, the PIECEWISE warning, and `plan()` routing.
- Serving: `--monokernel` compiles 64 builds (92 layers, widths 1–16) at startup, captures FULL graphs, and takes specialized steps.

## Details

**Launches.** Per layer: (1) on the GDN layers, the GDN block: residual add + input_layernorm, in_proj_qkvz (MXFP4) and in_proj_ba, the conv update, the gated delta rule on the cached states, RMSNormGated; on the full attention layers vLLM's input norm and attention run instead, up to o_proj's input. (2) The layer block: out_proj (MXFP4) / o_proj (BF16, with the output gate), the TP all-reduce, the residual add + post_attention_layernorm, the router's softmax top-10 and the shared-expert gate, the MXFP4 experts with the fused shared expert (expert 512), the TP all-reduce. Embeddings, final norm, head and sampling stay vLLM's.

**x without an LDS tile.** At H = 8192 a 16-row bf16 x is 262 KB, more than a CU's LDS, so neither launch holds it. The norm CTAs put their columns' sums of squares and every consumer builds what it reads of x from global memory (in the GDN block at up to 3 rows every CTA computes the rows' rstd itself, cheaper than the hand-off); from 4 (GDN) / 5 (layer) rows, the norm CTAs instead quantize their columns once into a shared MXFP4 image that in_proj_qkvz and the experts copy, as every CTA rebuilding all of x would move 256 × 2 [S, H] bf16 through the L2s each launch.

**MoE.** At decode widths stock runs AITER's `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` path with x and silu(g)·u through dynamic MXFP4 (1×32 blocks, RCEIL scales); the layer block does the same, the intermediate quantized where it is produced, and feeds the codes to the scaled fp4 MFMA. From 4 rows the fused shared expert's gate/up runs before the route is known; from 8 rows down starts on the union slots whose gate/up finished in the full rounds, under the last, partial round.

**MXFP4 layouts.** The GDN projections are read in the layout of whichever AITER FP4 GEMM vLLM picked for the shape (`runtime/guards.py`, `mxfp4_shuffled`), quantizing their inputs with the matching rounding (Triton's vs ASM's RCEIL). Both layouts are covered by `test_kernels.py`. No weights are duplicated.

**Refusals.** Config (model `__init__`): an architecture other than `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, TP≠8, PP, DP, EP, EPLB, DCP, PCP, DBO, sequence-parallel MoE, LoRA, KV connectors, routed-expert capture, speculative decoding, sleep mode, CPU weight offload, weight updates, GDN prefix caching, other GDN cache dtypes, an unfused shared expert, MRV1, `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE`, other shapes, unnormalized top-k weights, layer scale, non-gfx950 or partitioned GPUs. Model (after load): every layer's modules, quant methods, weight layouts and shapes. Caches (every bind): GDN state dtypes, shapes and slot layout. Without `--monokernel` none of this runs.

**Steps.** `plan()` returns a `Step` for a pure decode of 1–16 rows with int32 GDN state indices, else None (stock forward). Every width is compiled when the executor is built (FlyDSL `COMPILE_ONLY`), so no JIT on the first step of a width. PIECEWISE steps run stock.

**Shared helpers.** The launch ABI and health words, the tagged mailbox with its bounded waits, the build keys, the GEMV stage, peer memory and `FailStop` are adapted from the Kimi-K3 decode (#60683, by @hyukjlee, after ROCm/ATOM), as in #63032, and trimmed to what these kernels use. The package imports nothing from other models; the kernel cache key covers every source under its `mono/`, and the Buildkite step triggers only on this model's directories.

**Limitations / follow-ups.**
- Speculative decoding is refused; MTP verify steps are a follow-up.
- At 4–8 rows the CTAs that run the routed gate/up's last, partial round still own two down row groups each and set the launch's end; moving row groups off them is a follow-up (~3 µs at those widths).
- Failure: every cross-rank wait is bounded (10 s). A rank that gives up records the wait, flags the output rank and sets its sticky failed word; `FailStop` reads that word after each step without blocking and the TP ranks agree every 16 steps, then raise together. There is no fallback to the stock forward after a failure.
- Startup does not check the FlyDSL version.

---

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] `ROCM_ATTN` returns wrong attention (and can fault the GPU) on RDNA for head size ≥ 96 with KV block size ≠ 16, and for MHA with head size 192/256
items.body:
### Used environment

- GPU: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4), ROCm 10.2, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.2, triton 3.8.0
- vLLM: `main` @ dde9aca41c (2026-10-19); also seen on 426f3bd36 (2026-10-14)
- Backend: `ROCM_ATTN` (the default attention backend on RDNA)

### The bug

On RDNA, `ROCM_ATTN` decodes with its HIP paged-attention kernel only for head 128, block 16 and GQA 3–16. Everything else uses its Triton fallback: `kernel_paged_attention_2d` for decode, `context_attention_fwd` for prefill. For some layouts that path returns wrong attention outputs, and in some batches it crashes the process with a GPU memory-access fault inside `kernel_paged_attention_2d`.

**How it was found:** an A/B harness runs `ROCM_ATTN` as vLLM does:
- vLLM's KV-cache allocator;
- the backend's own `do_kv_cache_update()`, metadata builder and `forward()`;
- outputs compared to an fp32 PyTorch attention reference.

On correct layouts the error is ~0.001–0.01. On the failing ones it's 0.02–0.57; correct is within 0.02 + 0.02·|ref|. `TRITON_ATTN`, on identical inputs and the same cache shapes, matches the reference in all 14,608 batches.

**Results:** 12,389 batches where `ROCM_ATTN` is vLLM's default backend; 635 wrong outputs and 119 GPU faults.

| head size | KV block size | wrong | GPU fault | ok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 96 | 528 | 175 | 57 | 120 |
| 128 | 32 | 0 | 24 | 66 |
| 128 | 64 | 24 | 0 | 66 |
| 128 | 528 | 42 | 12 | 500 |
| 192 | 16 (GQA 1 only) | 30 | 0 | 309 |
| 192 | 528 | 150 | 13 | 176 |
| 256 | 16 (GQA 1 only) | 33 | 0 | 1485 |
| 256 | 32 | 8 | 12 | 68 |
| 256 | 64 | 0 | 1 | 87 |
| 256 | 528 | 173 | 0 | 341 |

- **Never failed:** head 64 at any block size (16 / 32 / 64 / 528); head 96 at block 16; head 128 at block 16 (HIP kernel and Triton path).
- **Not specific to a dtype:** bf16 and fp16 both fail.
- **KV cache dtype:** all failures but one are with a 16-bit cache. An fp8 KV cache with the same shapes didn't fail.

Block 528 is a real configuration: hybrid models (e.g. Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next) use large KV blocks, and `ROCM_ATTN` declares `MultipleOf(16)` block sizes.

**There are two distinct patterns.**

**Pattern A: block size ≥ 32 (32, 64, 528) at padded head size ≥ 128 (head 96, 128, 192, 256).** Decode reads the cache wrongly.
- **Wrong:** decode batches, and the decode rows of mixed batches. These run `kernel_paged_attention_2d`, which also faults sometimes.
- **Correct:** prefill and short-query batches *on the same cached context*, e.g. a 1024-token chunk on 8192 cached tokens, read by `context_attention_fwd`. The repro also reads the cache back and finds it **exactly** equal to what was written. So the cache is correct, and the reader `kernel_paged_attention_2d` is wrong.
- **The error shrinks with context:** about 0.33 at 1k, 0.10 at 8k, 0.05 at 32k (head 96, block 528, 32 q / 8 KV heads). That suggests a bounded number of keys/values per request are read wrongly (e.g. one tile or one block), not every tile.
- In this kernel the tile is `TRITON_BLOCK_SIZE = min(block_size, 128)` for power-of-two blocks and 32 for other blocks. So every failing case has tiles of ≥ 32 tokens with `HEAD_SIZE_PADDED` ≥ 128; block 16 (16-token tiles) and head 64 never fail.

**Pattern B: block 16, MHA (GQA 1: 32 q / 32 KV heads), head 192 / 256.** Every batch that reads cached tokens is wrong:
- decode (`kernel_paged_attention_2d`);
- short queries;
- prefill chunks on cached context (`context_attention_fwd`).

Fresh prompts with no cached context (128–8192 tokens) are correct. **The repro confirms the KV cache is written wrongly:**
- reading the cache back through `ROCM_ATTN`'s own K/V views gives values up to 5.3 away from the keys and values written, while at GQA 4 (8 KV heads) it's exact;
- for block 16 with a native layout, `do_kv_cache_update()` uses the HIP `reshape_and_cache` (`PagedAttention.write_to_paged_cache`);
- so the writer is wrong for this shape, when `num_kv_heads × head_size` is large (6,144 / 8,192 elements per token).

Both readers are then fed bad data.

Example rows (bf16, error = max |out − ref|):

| layout | batch | `ROCM_ATTN` | `TRITON_ATTN` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32/8 heads, head 96, block 528 | decode, 1 × 1k | wrong, 0.355 | ok |
| same | decode, 8 × 8k | wrong, 0.104 | ok |
| same | 1024-token chunk on 8k cached | ok | ok |
| 32/32 heads, head 256, block 16 | decode, 1 × 1k | wrong, 0.230 | ok |
| same | 1024-token chunk on 8k cached | wrong, 0.109 | ok |
| same | fresh 1024-token prompt | ok | ok |
| 32/8 heads, head 192, block 528 | decode, 1 × 8k | GPU fault in `kernel_paged_attention_2d` ("Page not present") | ok |

### Repro

`repro_rocm_attn.py` ([gist](https://gist.github.com/nemanjaudovic/d14acb71c4a21641dd791750225d4be5)) builds `ROCM_ATTN` exactly as vLLM does, with `TRITON_ATTN` as a control. For each case it prints three things:
- **write:** the cache, read back through `ROCM_ATTN`'s own K/V views, vs what was written (separates writer from reader);
- **output:** error vs fp32;
- **inputs:** whether query / keys / values were modified (stray writes).

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 repro_rocm_attn.py --case p1-d192-bs528   # pattern A
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 repro_rocm_attn.py --case p2-d256-bs16-gqa1 # pattern B
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 repro_rocm_attn.py                          # all cases
```

A GPU fault kills the process; run pattern A cases one at a time.

Output on gfx1201 (vLLM `ROCM_ATTN` code identical to `main` @ dde9aca41c):

```
### ok-d64-bs528 (exit 0)
# gfx1201 AMD Radeon AI Pro R9700S, vLLM 0.32.0rc1.dev443+g3b4de701f (/host/vllm/vllm/__init__.py), torch 2.13.0+rocm10.2.0a20261005
== ok-d64-bs528: q/kv heads 32/8, head 64, block 528, bfloat16, 1 request(s), q 1, context 1024
   layout KVCacheLayout.LHBNC, key_cache (3, 8, 8, 528, 8) strides (270336, 33792, 4224, 8, 1), value_cache (3, 8, 64, 528) strides (270336, 33792, 528, 1)
```

[Gist](https://gist.github.com/nemanjaudovic/d14acb71c4a21641dd791750225d4be5) with:
- `repro_rocm_attn.py`: the standalone repro;
- `repro_output_gfx1201.txt`: its output;
- `gpu_memory_fault_kernel_paged_attention_2d.log`: the GPU-fault log;
- `rocm_attn_sweep_all_batches.csv`: all 12,389 `ROCM_ATTN` batches of the sweep, with status and error.

The repro uses vLLM's own backend API, as vLLM does; nothing is patched:
- `AttentionBackendEnum[...]`;
- the KV-cache allocator and `create_kv_cache_views`;
- `do_kv_cache_update()`, the metadata builder and `forward()`.

- #50603: gfx1100, corruption from the same Triton fallback (`kernel_paged_attention_2d`) at GQA 2 / long context.
- #48043: `kernel_paged_attention_2d` illegal memory access on gfx950.
- #42420: a fix for the HIP paged-attention kernel with custom KV layouts (a different kernel).

### Impact

- Any RDNA user on `ROCM_ATTN`, the default on RDNA today:
  - hybrid models with large KV blocks and head size ≥ 96;
  - `--block-size 32/64` with head ≥ 128;
  - MHA models with head 192 / 256.
- PR #60418 makes `TRITON_ATTN` the default on gfx1201 / gfx1100, which avoids this there. gfx1200, gfx1101, gfx1151, and anyone forcing `ROCM_ATTN`, are still affected.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to run the sweeps and the repro and to write this report; the submitter reviewed it.
