items.title: [v1] Allow attention backends to declare custom KV cache page size
items.body:
## Summary

Third-party attention backends registered via the `vllm.general_plugins`
entry-point currently cannot request a per-block page size that differs
from `2 × block_size × num_kv_heads × head_size × dtype_size`. This
blocks plugins that pack KV more tightly than one element per (head, dim)
— e.g., quantized-KV backends storing a few bytes of quantized data plus
a scalar norm instead of `head_size` fp16s.

This PR adds three opt-in seams. **All default to existing behavior**, so
no in-tree backend is affected:

1. `AttentionBackend.get_kv_cache_page_size(...) -> int | None` — new
   classmethod on the backend base; returns `None` (default formula).
2. `AttentionSpec.custom_page_size: int | None` — new dataclass field;
   `real_page_size_bytes` returns it verbatim when set. Propagates
   through `FullAttentionSpec.merge` / `MLAAttentionSpec.merge`.
3. `GPUModelRunner._reshape_kv_cache_tensors` views a prefix of the
   allocation when the backend's shape packs fewer elements per entry.

## Motivation

TurboQuant (arXiv:2504.19874) compresses KV cache to 4-bit with Hadamard
preconditioning (3.76× vs fp16). As an out-of-tree plugin on stock vLLM
it's capped at 2× because the allocator reserves 128 bytes/head for the
underlying fp8 dtype while only ~68 bytes/head carry real data. With
this PR the backend can declare its true page size.

## Benchmarks

A100-40GB, Qwen3-8B, `max_model_len=1024`, 5 prompts × 32 tokens, best of 3
(TurboQuant plugin applied):

| Config | TPOT | KV tokens |
|---|---|---|
| FP16 eager | 4.36 ms | 83,280 |
| FP16 graphs | 3.15 ms | 83,216 |
| TQ fp8 eager | 5.76 ms | 266,512 |
| TQ fp8 graphs | **3.53 ms** | **266,144** |

TQ fp8 gets **3.20× more KV tokens** in the same memory at 1.12× the
FP16-graphs TPOT.

## Tests

`tests/v1/core/test_custom_page_size.py` — 6 pure-CPU tests covering
default return value, custom override, spec formula fallback, and
`merge` preservation for both `FullAttentionSpec` and `MLAAttentionSpec`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest tests/v1/core/test_custom_page_size.py`
- [ ] Existing FP16/FP8 workloads unchanged (no backend overrides `get_kv_cache_page_size`)
- [ ] TurboQuant plugin (out-of-tree) reaches 3.20× KV-token memory with this PR applied

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse the MXFP4 activation quant into the GDN gated RMSNorm
items.body:
> **Needs AITER >= 0.1.27** (ROCm/aiter#6038, `fused_rms_gated_mxfp4_quant` with `transpose_scale`). It is imported directly, with no fallback. Draft until `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` pins it.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On GDN models whose `out_proj` runs AITER's Triton MXFP4 linear (online MXFP4 through `quantization-config.targets`, or a Quark MXFP4 checkpoint), `RocmAiterRMSNormQuantFusionPass` replaces the gated RMSNorm, the separate MXFP4 activation quant and the GEMM with one op. The quant runs inside the norm kernel. The pass also starts matching GDN's `flatten(-2)`, which the gated-norm patterns missed in serving; that rewrite runs only when the MXFP4 pattern is registered, so FP8 graphs are unchanged. Linears on the ASM GEMM are not matched.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "gated rmsnorm mxfp4", "rms_norm_gated fusion", "GDN out_proj quant" and "fused_rms_gated". #58802 fuses the gated norm into a BF16 `out_proj`; this PR applies where `out_proj` is quantized. #61902 and #59483 fuse the quant into other norms. #64509 fuses the gated norm into a static FP8 `out_proj` on NVIDIA.

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MXFP4, TP2, MI355X: +0.6% geomean output throughput over the 9 cells of the 8k/1k and 60k/600 ladders, 3 repeats. The gain is at concurrency 4-32 (+0.6 to +1.3%); from 64 up it is within +0.4%.
- Per decode step, 108 launches become 72, and the step's kernel time falls 7.99 → 7.92 ms.
- The kernel is 20-49% faster per layer at M <= 512 and 2-18% at M = 1024-8192 (table in ROCm/aiter#6038).
- GSM8K 5-shot: no change beyond run-to-run noise (exact McNemar p = 0.50, 1.00, 1.00).
- On Flash-Next the gated-norm patterns did not fire in serving before this PR (`Replaced 0 patterns`); with it, a TP2 start logs `Replaced 1 patterns` 12 times across the two ranks.

## Validation

**Unit tests.** MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-df3bd094aeea829f27baa0a5282830464f601d9f` with this branch (merged with main at d0d3005aff) and AITER v0.1.27's three quant Python files over it:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/compile/passes/test_fusion.py -q -k gated_mxfp4
```

```text
3 passed, 121 deselected in 33.87s
```

`test_aiter_fusion_rmsnorm_gated_mxfp4_gemm` builds a real `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` at K=2048 and checks the match count, the fused op after the pass, and the output against the unfused graph.

- Fails if the symbolic-reshape rewrite is dropped: `triton-sigmoid-flatten` (GDN's `flatten(-2)`).
- Fails if the pattern stops registering on the Triton path: `triton-sigmoid-flatten` and `triton-swish-reshape`.
- `asm-not-fused` (N=8192, an ASM-tuned shape) checks that the pass matches nothing.

**Decode trace.** Torch profiler, TP2 server below, 128 decode steps, rank 0. 36 GDN layers: the Inductor gated norm (36 launches, 162 µs) and the `out_proj` quant disappear into 36 `_fused_rms_gated_mxfp4_quant_kernel` launches (169 µs); the 36 `in_proj` quants stay (171 µs). The step falls by less than the 146 µs saved because the unchanged kernels ran about 5% slower in the candidate trace.

**End to end.** MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` TP2 with the GDN `in_proj_qkv`, `in_proj_z` and `out_proj` in online MXFP4, 3 repeats, both arms on HIP 2,3 in turn (stock first in repeats 1 and 3, candidate first in repeat 2), fresh compile caches. Stock: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-e68efc685ab1e6f1eda004ced7157e3ca411da2f`; candidate: the same nightly with this PR and ROCm/aiter#6038's three Python files. Both arms set `fuse_norm_quant` and the same targets. These runs used an earlier revision of the pass; the Triton path they exercise is unchanged. Mean over the repeats:

| ISL / OSL | Conc | Output tok/s, stock → candidate (higher is better) | Mean TTFT ms (lower is better) | Mean TPOT ms (lower is better) | Output tok/s Δ per repeat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1024 | 4 | 439 → 443 (+1.1%) | 1470 → 1475 (+0.3%) | 7.69 → 7.59 (-1.3%) | +2.1%, +0.6%, +0.6% |
| 8k / 1024 | 8 | 654 → 663 (+1.3%) | 2302 → 2275 (-1.2%) | 9.99 → 9.86 (-1.3%) | +3.4%, +0.1%, +0.3% |
| 8k / 1024 | 16 | 956 → 961 (+0.6%) | 3486 → 3319 (-4.8%) | 13.35 → 13.41 (+0.5%) | +0.6%, +0.6%, +0.6% |
| 8k / 1024 | 32 | 1188 → 1200 (+1.0%) | 4601 → 4596 (-0.1%) | 22.45 → 22.19 (-1.2%) | +2.7%, +0.3%, +0.0% |
| 8k / 1024 | 64 | 1374 → 1380 (+0.4%) | 6642 → 6859 (+3.3%) | 40.09 → 39.68 (-1.0%) | +0.5%, +0.4%, +0.4% |
| 8k / 1024 | 128 | 1542 → 1545 (+0.2%) | 12785 → 12965 (+1.4%) | 70.44 → 70.09 (-0.5%) | +0.1%, +0.3%, +0.2% |
| 8k / 1024 | 256 | 1666 → 1669 (+0.2%) | 23190 → 23128 (-0.3%) | 130.77 → 130.55 (-0.2%) | -0.0%, +0.3%, +0.3% |
| 60k / 600 | 4 | 130 → 130 (+0.3%) | 9168 → 9161 (-0.1%) | 15.56 → 15.49 (-0.4%) | +0.1%, +0.4%, +0.3% |
| 60k / 600 | 16 | 155 → 155 (+0.1%) | 14949 → 14852 (-0.6%) | 78.25 → 78.29 (+0.1%) | +0.1%, +0.1%, +0.1% |

Geomean output tok/s, candidate / stock: +0.57%. The TTFT differences go both ways and are within the spread between repeats.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 problems, greedy, flexible-extract, from the runs above. Exact McNemar test on the paired per-problem results.

| Repeat | Stock → candidate | Fixed / broken | McNemar p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0.9651 → 0.9613 | 15 / 20 | 0.50 |
| 2 | 0.9613 → 0.9613 | 13 / 13 | 1.00 |
| 3 | 0.9613 → 0.9621 | 14 / 13 | 1.00 |

Stock against stock (repeats 1 and 2) gives p = 0.49: about 89% of generations differ between any two runs, because batch composition changes the reduction order.

MTP was not measured. Loading the MTP draft needs the checkpoint's `exclude` fix ([amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 discussion #1](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4/discussions/1)) and, for its `mtp.layers.0.*` names to reach the draft's `mtp.layers.48.*`, #61770. Independent of this PR.

**Reproduce:**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 \
    --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*linear_attn.in_proj_qkv": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.in_proj_z": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.out_proj": "mxfp4"}' \
    --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_norm_quant": true}}'
vllm bench serve --model amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
    --max-concurrency <4..256> --num-prompts <8 x concurrency, 32 to 768>
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
    --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_gen_toks=2048 \
    --seed 4321 --log_samples --output_path <dir>
```

## Details

**Before.** GDN's `_output_projection` normalizes the core attention output with `RMSNormGated` (per-head RMSNorm times a SiLU or sigmoid gate of `z`), flattens the heads, and calls `out_proj`. With MXFP4 `out_proj` that is `gemm_with_dynamic_quant`: a separate activation-quant kernel, then the GEMM. Since #61278, `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel.use_asm_gemm` is true only when the `a4w4` ASM CSV has the (N, K) and a preshuffled config is tuned. Flash-Next's `out_proj` (N=2560, K=6144/TP) has no ASM rows at any TP, so it runs `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` and the Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4`.

**After.** `AiterRMSNormGatedMxfp4GemmPattern` matches `RMSNormGated → reshape → gemm_with_dynamic_quant` for linears with `use_asm_gemm=False` and lowers it to `rocm_aiter_fused_rms_gated_mxfp4_gemm`. AITER's `fused_rms_gated_mxfp4_quant` writes the activation and its per-1x32 scales column-major (`transpose_scale=True`), as `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` returns them; row-major scales give the same result but `gemm_afp4wfp4` reads them 20-100% slower from M=1024 up. The pattern registers once per (epsilon, heads per rank, head dim, gate activation, output dtype) the GDN layers use, for `norm_before_gate=True`, `group_size=None` and a head dim divisible by 32.

**Matching `flatten(-2)`.** GDN flattens heads with `core_attn_out.flatten(-2)`, which compiles under a dynamic token count to `reshape(x, [s, hidden])` with `s` a graph input. The pattern is traced with `reshape(-1, hidden)`, so it would never match in serving. `reshape_symbolic_dim_to_minus_one` rewrites a reshape with exactly one symbolic size to `-1`, the same op. The pass runs it only when the MXFP4 pattern is registered and hashes it into the pass `uuid`, so FP8 graphs and their cache keys are unchanged.

**`MatcherRMSNormGated`** gains an `activation` argument in `forward_native` (default `swish`, as before), so sigmoid-gated models such as Flash-Next match.

**Limitations and CI gaps.**

- gfx950 only: MXFP4 does not run on gfx942.
- The gain is small: the fused launches save about 1.8% of a decode step's kernel time.
- Serving was measured at TP2. Norm and quant are row-local per head, so TP only changes the head count per rank (48/TP) and K; the AITER PR's kernel table covers TP1, 2, 4 and 8.
- ASM-GEMM linears are not fused.
- The `in_proj_qkvz` activation quant is not covered: on Flash-Next its input comes from the HyperConnection kernel, not from an AR+RMSNorm, so #59483 does not reach it either.
- CI: `compile/passes` runs only in the MI300 job, where the gfx950 cases skip, so the new test ran on MI355X outside CI.

items.title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Keep image bidirectional attention within the sliding window on the V2 model runner
items.body:
## Purpose

#47217 fixed Gemma4 vision models silently falling back to **causal-only** image
attention whenever a single image's soft-token span exceeded the text sliding
window (e.g. ~1120 soft tokens at `max_soft_tokens=1120` vs
`sliding_window=1024`). The runner was dropping the *entire* bidirectional
`mm_prefix` range for such an image; the fix gated that skip on a model
capability flag, `mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window`, so models that bound
`mm_prefix` **in-kernel** keep the full range and let the kernel clamp it
per-query — matching HF's `(causal OR blockwise) AND sliding_window` on local
layers.

That fix only landed in the **V1** `GPUModelRunner`. The V2 model runner has its
own copy of the range-building logic in
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py::compute_mm_prefix_ranges`, which still drops
oversized ranges unconditionally:

```python
for r in mm_feature.mm_position.extract_embeds_range():
    if sliding_window is not None and (r[1] - r[0] + 1) > sliding_window:
        continue  # <- no opt-out, unlike V1
```

So the original defect is still reachable today on `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.
This matters more than it did at the time of #47217, because V2 is no longer
opt-in for these configs — `VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner` force-enables V2 for
DSpark speculative decoding and for hybrid DFlash drafters, both of which are
used with Gemma4. A user who serves Gemma4 with images and DSpark drafting gets
the degraded mask with no warning and no error.

The kernel-side clamp (`flash_attn.py`, `triton_attn.py`,
`triton_unified_attention.py`) is already shared by both runners and needs no
change — V2 simply never delivers the range to it.

### Fix

- `compute_mm_prefix_ranges` gains a `clamp_in_kernel: bool = False` parameter
  that gates the oversized-range skip, mirroring V1's `_clamps_in_kernel`. The
  default preserves current behavior for every other PrefixLM model.
- `DefaultModelState.build_attn_metadata` reads
  `mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window` off the model and forwards it, exactly as
  `GPUModelRunner` does.

No behavior change for V1, for non-Gemma4 models, or for images that already fit
within the sliding window.

### Not a duplicate

Checked before opening, per `AGENTS.md`:

```bash
gh search issues "compute_mm_prefix_ranges" --repo vllm-project/vllm --include-prs   # 0 results
gh search issues "mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window" --repo vllm-project/vllm --include-prs  # only #47217
gh search issues "mm_req_doc_ranges" --repo vllm-project/vllm --include-prs
```

No open issue or PR covers the V2 side. The nearest open PRs touch adjacent code
but not this logic: #47646 (revert of an FA4 mm_prefix *kernel* mask change,
`flash_attn.py` only), #46558 (FlashInfer mm-prefix, `flashinfer.py` only), and
#48907 / #46963 (V2 `attn_utils.py`, but KV-cache reshape). #47217 is the V1 fix
being ported here — its changed-file list contains no V2 file.

## Test Plan

Added four unit tests to `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py` covering
`compute_mm_prefix_ranges` (previously untested):

- `test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_skips_oversized_range_by_default` — default
  path still drops an oversized span (regression guard for other models).
- `test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_keeps_oversized_range_when_clamped_in_kernel` —
  the fix: an oversized span survives when the model clamps in-kernel.
- `test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_keeps_fitting_range_either_way` — spans within
  the window are unaffected by the flag.
- `test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_ignores_non_visual_modalities` — audio is
  still skipped.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -q
```

## Test Result

All tests pass with the fix:

```
........                                                            [100%]
8 passed, 14 warnings in 4.15s
```

Reverting only the two source files and re-running (tests kept) fails, confirming
the tests exercise the fixed behavior rather than passing vacuously:

```
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_keeps_oversized_range_when_clamped_in_kernel
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_keeps_fitting_range_either_way
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_compute_mm_prefix_ranges_ignores_non_visual_modalities
3 failed, 5 passed
```

`ruff format --check` and `ruff check` are clean on all three changed files (the
one remaining `UP038` in `attn_utils.py` is pre-existing on `main`, in
`build_attn_metadata`, and untouched here).

### Model evaluation

This change affects generated output for one narrow case: Gemma4 vision requests
under the V2 model runner where a single image's soft-token span exceeds
`sliding_window` (i.e. `max_soft_tokens=1120` against `sliding_window=1024`; the
default `num_soft_tokens=280` on the released checkpoints is unaffected, so most
serving configurations see no change at all). The expected effect is the one
measured in #47217 — restoring blockwise-bidirectional image attention instead of
causal-only — with V1 as the reference implementation.

I have not re-run the end-to-end vision eval from #47217 under V2; I don't have a
Hopper box free for it right now. Flagging that gap explicitly rather than
implying coverage I don't have. If a reviewer wants those numbers before merging,
say so and I'll get them.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used on this PR: tracing the V1/V2 divergence,
drafting the patch and tests, and drafting this description. The commit carries a
`Co-authored-by:` trailer. I have reviewed every changed line, run the tests and
linters reported above, and can defend the change end-to-end.

## Related

- #47217 — the V1 fix this ports (merged)
- #42175 — introduced Gemma4 FA4 + FlashAttention `mm_prefix` support

items.title: [Kernel] Honor ND group FP8 input contract
items.body:
## Overview

Make group FP8 CUDA quantization preserve the ND input contract already supported by the native path. This is API consistency for direct/OOT callers: current in-tree CUDA callers flatten their input, and no production-model trigger has been established.

## Claims

- Quantize 3D/4D inputs through the existing 2D kernels and restore logical value/scale shapes.
- Preserve caller-provided contiguous `out_q` storage and per-batch column-major/TMA scale layouts.
- Keep the existing 2D quantization arithmetic; compare ND values and logical scales exactly against the flattened call.

## Validation

Base `2eae56c4ba0c`; A100-SXM4-80GB, PyTorch 2.14/cu130. Test commands, source identities, environment details and raw assertion logs are in [validation.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34240984/validation.zip). Baseline comparisons apply the candidate tests to this pinned base.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant_group.py
```

October 30 GPU evidence, with the same final test file and unchanged executable logic: **base: 25 failed, 11 passed; candidate: 36 passed**. The 24 ND combinations cover FP16/BF16, 3D/4D, row-major/column-major/TMA scales, and power-of-two scaling. One additional case checks `out_q` aliasing and exact value/scale bytes against the flattened 2D call. Existing 11 cases remain covered. The changed matrix uses group size 64 to keep CI cost bounded. A separate probe passed eight output-buffer/layout checks and one `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` check.

Recorded pytest output with the candidate tests on both trees:

```text
Base:      25 failed, 11 passed in 14.38s
Candidate: 36 passed in 13.89s
```

Baseline failures include `RuntimeError: dimensionality of sizes (4) must match dimensionality of strides (3)` and dimensionality checks in the native quantization op.

## Details

The native kernels consume 2D scale tensors. Flattening only the kernel input prevents malformed ND allocation/stride arguments; the wrapper then restores the public shape. Column-major scales require an extra layout copy, and reshaping a strided input may allocate. No performance or model-quality improvement is claimed.

The obsolete 3D allocation branch is removed. Shape, strides, uninitialized padding and the contiguous-output requirement are documented in `per_token_group_quant_fp8`; the CustomOp page links to that API instead of duplicating layout details. The changed autoref was built with MkDocs/mkdocstrings and verified against the generated API file and anchor. The full documentation site was not built. The separate packed UE8M0 DeepGEMM representation is outside this change and was not tested on Blackwell. November 1 duplicate-work checks found no equivalent open PR. #60903 optimizes 2D group quantization, #41115 changes per-token quantization, and #45151 fuses quantization into attention; they do not restore this wrapper's ND output contract.

**TMA/DeepGEMM scope:** Tests validate logical scales and storage strides, not a downstream GEMM. Padding remains uninitialized. #49783 reports DeepGEMM scale-padding failures, and #56290 proposes initialization in this same helper; this PR does not resolve that issue or claim DeepGEMM 2.6+ consumer compatibility.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests and documentation. Hosted CI and full repository tests have not run.

items.title: [ROCm][DCP] Pad the AITER MLA decode query without byte-wise strided copies
items.body:
## Purpose

With DCP on ROCm, the cprr AITER MLA decode pads the gathered query to a native head count (96 -> 128 for Kimi-K3 at DCP8). `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` did this with `repeat` (2x heads) followed by `[:, :m].contiguous()`. For an FP8 query both go through PyTorch's one-element-per-lane strided copy for a 1-byte dtype, which is slow on MI355X.

`get_mla_padded_q` now writes exactly `m` heads into the padded buffer, copying through an int64 view of the rows (`_copy_rows`). Results are bit-identical.

The change is ROCm-only. The shared DCP query gather in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/dcp.py` is unchanged; its relayout copy can be a follow-up.

## Test Result

MI355X, Kimi-K3 TP8 / DCP8, DSpark k=4, cprr verify, conc 48. Decode-step torch profile (batch 48 x 5 verify tokens), same node, image and capture window for both arms:

| | query gather + pad copies per decode step |
|---|---:|
| before | 1.88 ms (72 byte-wise copies) |
| this PR | 0.91 ms |

The remaining 0.91 ms is the gather relayout in `dcp.py` (0.59 ms, unchanged here) plus the int64 pad copies (0.33 ms).

### Accuracy

gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, `lm_eval --model local-completions` against the served model, `num_concurrent=64`; Kimi-K3 MXFP4, 8x MI355X, TP8 / DCP8 (a2a), FP8 KV cache, async scheduling, FULL CUDA graphs, DSpark k=4 with real (block) rejection. Measured with the earlier revision of this PR, which contained this padding change plus a gather change; both are bit-exact.

| configuration | strict-match | flexible-extract | mean acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| without this PR (vLLM 36768d1b + #58887) | 0.9568 ± 0.0056 | 0.9568 | 3.78 |
| with this PR | 0.9583 ± 0.0055 | 0.9583 | 3.84 |

## Why this is not a duplicate

No open PR changes `get_mla_padded_q`. #54494 (Kimi-K3 query replication) removes the DCP gather when `dcp_q_replicate` is on and does not touch the cprr padding.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_head_padding.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py` in the ROCm image: 37 passed, 5 skipped (cprr 96 -> 128 tile pad, bf16 and fp8).
- `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD`: pass.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above. The padding-only scope follows @GirasoleY's rework (hyukjlee/vllm#1).

items.title: [Perf][Kernel] Reduce shared-memory staging for per-tensor FP8 KV dequantization
items.body:
## Overview

For BF16/FP16 queries with per-tensor FP8 KV, the current dequantization code can cause Triton to store dequantized K/V tiles in shared memory and reload them for matrix multiplication. This PR loads each dequantization scale as a one-element tensor and broadcasts it to the tile shape, allowing Triton to eliminate these intermediate shared-memory buffers while preserving the original order of scaling and casting. On SM90, this PR also uses two pipeline stages for selected large-head 2D configurations.

## Claims

- **H20, Gemma 4 26B-A4B, FP8 KV:** for single requests containing approximately 8k or 32k text tokens followed by a screenshot, this PR reduces TTFT from **708.5 ms to 660.6 ms (7.08% lower)** and from **3914.5 ms to 3366.0 ms (14.01% lower)**, respectively.
- **H20 kernel benchmark:** across 37 tested 2D prefill and decode configurations, this PR reduces attention execution time by **23.9%**, measured as the geometric mean of paired PR/original execution-time ratios.

## Validation

On H20, all 96 cases in the FP8 KV regression test and all 72 cases in a separate numerical check passed. In the numerical check, all 72 outputs were bitwise identical to those from the unmodified kernel. Model and kernel performance were each measured over six paired rounds. Test configurations, timing methods and paired results are provided below.

## Details

### 1. Extra shared-memory buffers in the generated code

The TTGIR excerpts in Sections 1–3 compare the original and rewritten kernels for a causal prefill configuration on H20 with Triton 3.8: BF16 queries, FP8 KV, KV-cache block size 64, query length 15931, KV length 32315, head size 512, 16 query heads and 2 KV heads. Both kernels use four warps and three pipeline stages.

The original kernel loads FP8 K/V tiles from shared memory into registers, converts them to FP32, multiplies them by the dequantization scales and casts them to BF16. The resulting BF16 tiles use a blocked layout, which differs from the layout required by the matrix multiplication. To convert between these layouts, the generated code writes each BF16 tile to an intermediate shared-memory buffer and reloads it in the dot-operand layout. The following TTGIR excerpt shows this sequence for K:

```mlir
%K_228 = tt.fp_to_fp %K_load_226
    : tensor<512x32xf8E4M3FN, #blocked1>
   -> tensor<512x32xf32, #blocked1>
%K_229 = arith.mulf %K_228, %K_123
    : tensor<512x32xf32, #blocked1>
%K_230 = arith.truncf %K_229
    : tensor<512x32xf32, #blocked1>
   to tensor<512x32xbf16, #blocked1>
%K_231 = ttg.local_alloc %K_230
    : (tensor<512x32xbf16, #blocked1>)
   -> !ttg.memdesc<512x32xbf16, #shared4, #smem>
%K_240 = ttg.local_load %K_231
    : !ttg.memdesc<512x32xbf16, #shared4, #smem>
   -> tensor<512x32xbf16, #dot>
```

Source locations are omitted, and `#dot` is shorthand for the `#ttg.dot_op` attribute. `#blocked1` and `#dot` describe how tensor elements are distributed across threads and registers; `#smem` denotes shared memory. The `ttg.local_alloc` operation writes the BF16 K tile to shared memory, and `ttg.local_load` reloads it in the layout required by `tt.dot`. V follows the same pattern.

These intermediate buffers hold the dequantized BF16 K/V tiles and are separate from the existing FP8 input buffers. After dequantization, each tile is therefore written from registers to shared memory and then read back into registers.

### 2. Why Triton does not eliminate these buffers

The original dequantization code loads the scale as a scalar:

```python
return (data.to(tl.float32) * tl.load(tensor_scale)).to(Q.dtype)
```

To multiply the tile by this scalar, Triton expands the scale to the tile shape using `tt.splat`:

```mlir
%K = tt.load %k_scale, %acc : !tt.ptr<f32>
%K_123 = tt.splat %K
    : f32 -> tensor<512x32xf32, #blocked1>
```

Triton's layout-conversion pass attempts to move the conversion to the dot-operand layout before dequantization, so that FP8 K/V tiles can be loaded from shared memory directly into registers in that layout and dequantized there. This would avoid writing the resulting BF16 tiles to intermediate shared-memory buffers and reloading them for matrix multiplication. However, the pass cannot move the layout conversion past the scalar `tt.splat` shown above. The compiler debug log reports:

```text
Leaves must be Load, descriptor load-like ops, or Constant.
Got ... tt.splat ... : f32 -> tensor<512x32xf32, ...>
```

In Triton 3.8, [`LayoutRematerialization::hoistConvertDotOperand`](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/v3.8.0/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/RemoveLayoutConversions.cpp#L1237) traces the operations that produce the values used by dequantization to determine whether the layout conversion can be moved earlier. It can traverse pure elementwise operations, including multiplication, as well as supported broadcasts and views. However, the scalar `tt.splat` above is not covered by these rules, so the pass leaves the layout conversion after dequantization, retaining the intermediate BF16 shared-memory buffers.

>The same extra buffers were also observed with Triton 3.7.1 on SM89; the compiler diagnostics and source-code analysis described here were performed with Triton 3.8.

### 3. Load the scale as a one-element tensor

This PR loads the dequantization scale as a one-element tensor, reshapes it to `(1, 1)` and broadcasts it to the K/V tile shape:

```python
scale_1d = tl.load(tensor_scale + tl.arange(0, 1))
scale_tile = tl.broadcast_to(scale_1d.reshape((1, 1)), data.shape)
return (data.to(tl.float32) * scale_tile).to(Q.dtype)
```

`tl.arange(0, 1)` contains only index zero, so the load reads the same dequantization scale from the same address as before. The scale remains a runtime value, and no array of per-element scales is added. Loading it as a one-element tensor produces a load/reshape/broadcast sequence instead of the scalar `tt.splat` shown above. The layout-conversion pass can traverse this sequence and move the layout conversion before dequantization.

The compiler debug log reports that the K/V layout conversions have been moved before dequantization. The resulting TTGIR shows FP8 K/V tiles being loaded from shared memory directly into registers in the dot-operand layout, followed by the FP32 conversion, scaling and BF16 cast in the same layout. For K:

```mlir
%K = ttg.local_load %K_load_171 token %K_load_220
    : !ttg.memdesc<512x32xf8E4M3FN, #shared2, #smem, mutable>
   -> tensor<512x32xf8E4M3FN, #dot>
%K_221 = tt.fp_to_fp %K
    : tensor<512x32xf8E4M3FN, #dot>
   -> tensor<512x32xf32, #dot>
%K_222 = arith.mulf %K_221, %scale_tile_115
    : tensor<512x32xf32, #dot>
%K_223 = arith.truncf %K_222
    : tensor<512x32xf32, #dot>
   to tensor<512x32xbf16, #dot>
```

`%K_223` is passed directly to `tt.dot`, without an intermediate BF16 shared-memory write and reload. V follows the same pattern. The existing FP8 input buffers remain, while the two intermediate BF16 K/V buffers are eliminated.

| Implementation | Shared memory per thread block| Static `ttg.local_alloc` count |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original kernel | 114,944 B | 8 |
| One-element scale load + broadcast | 50,432 B | 6 |

We compared the original and rewritten kernels across 37 configurations with both two and three pipeline stages. The matrix covers KV-cache block sizes 16 and 64, head-size-512 prefill and decode, and additional prefill configurations with head sizes 128 and 256. Both implementations use four warps; comparisons below hold the stage count fixed.

With three stages, the rewrite reduces execution time in 31 configurations and increases it in six; all six regressions are page-size-16, head-size-512 2D decode cases with 8 query heads and 2 KV heads. With both implementations using two stages, all 37 paired confidence intervals lie below 1.

<details>
<summary>Performance by configuration group at matching pipeline depths</summary>

All cases use BF16 queries, per-tensor native FP8 KV and the 2D path. Ratios are geometric means of paired execution-time ratios within each group; values below 1 indicate lower execution time. Confidence intervals are computed per configuration without multiple-comparison correction.

| Configuration group | KV-cache block size | Configurations | Rewrite / original, both three stages | Rewrite / original, both two stages |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Prefill, head size 512, query/KV heads 8/2 and 16/2 | 16 | 10 | 0.7893× | 0.7549× |
| Prefill, head size 512, query/KV heads 8/2 and 16/2 | 64 | 10 | 0.7984× | 0.7527× |
| Prefill matching the model workload below, head size 512, query/KV heads 16/2 | 64 | 1 | 0.8034× | 0.7468× |
| Decode, head size 512, query/KV heads 8/2 | 16 | 6 | 1.0776× | 0.8995× |
| Decode, head size 512, query/KV heads 8/2 | 64 | 6 | 0.8491× | 0.7541× |
| Prefill, head sizes 128 and 256, query/KV heads 16/2 | 64 | 4 | 0.7555× | 0.7754× |

The head-size-512 controlled prefill groups cover query lengths 512, 8192 and 16384 and KV lengths 8192 and 32768, excluding query lengths greater than the KV length. The Gemma-shaped case uses query length 15931 and KV length 32315. These are synthetic causal attention inputs without a multimodal mask; the Gemma-shaped case matches dimensions, not the model's actual tensors or multimodal execution.

</details>

### 4. Adjust pipeline depth for large-head 2D kernels

The rewrite removes the BF16 shared-memory buffers, but can increase register pressure. We compared two and three pipeline stages to balance this cost against overlap between memory loads and computation: fewer stages may keep fewer values live at once, but also reduce that overlap.

For a synthetic causal prefill case matching the observed Gemma dimensions—query length 15931, KV length 32315, head size 512, 16 query heads, 2 KV heads and KV-cache block size 64—the results are:

| Implementation | Pipeline stages | Execution time (ms) | Registers per thread | Stack size (B) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Original kernel | 3 | 358.848 | 246 | 0 |
| Rewritten kernel | 3 | 288.683 | 255 | 32 |
| Original kernel | 2 | 333.413 | 242 | 0 |
| Rewritten kernel | 2 | 248.965 | 255 | 16 |

Two stages reduce execution time by 13.75% within the rewritten kernel and by 7.22% within the original kernel. The rewrite still reduces execution time by 25.32% when both use two stages. Two stages reduce, but do not eliminate, spill-related stack usage in this example.

The page-size-16 decode group that regresses with three stages also improves with two stages. Page size matters: the corresponding page-size-64 decode group already benefits from the rewrite at three stages. Lower shared-memory usage alone therefore does not determine the best pipeline depth.

The wrapper sets `num_stages=2` for SM90-family 2D kernels with per-tensor FP8 KV, non-FP8 queries and head size ≥512, unless a stage count has already been selected. This setting was evaluated at head size 512. Reported PR performance includes both changes.

<details>
<summary>Streaming TTFT setup and results</summary>

**Environment:** NVIDIA H20 (SM90), driver 580.105.08, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 and vLLM build `4e591657157a`. The four implementations differ only in the dequantization expression and the two-/three-stage setting for the targeted head-size-512 path; other paths retain their existing settings.

**Model and input:** `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, revision `4d7ae4984b7d`. Each fixed input contains Python source code, a screenshot at the end and a question. The 8k and 32k workloads contain 8,315 and 32,315 prompt tokens after preprocessing.

**Runtime settings:** default `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN`, FP8 KV, KV-cache block size 64, prefix caching disabled, `max_model_len=131072`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`, `num_gpu_blocks_override=25000`, one image per prompt, seed 0, temperature 0 and `max_tokens=1`.

A client on the same machine sends requests serially over a persistent HTTP connection to the vLLM OpenAI API server. TTFT is measured from sending the pre-serialized request to receiving the first non-empty generated-text delta, excluding role-only and empty events. This is client-observed loopback streaming TTFT at concurrency one.

Each of six rounds launches a separate server for each implementation, with the implementation order varied across rounds. Each server runs both workloads, with one warm-up and seven timed requests per workload. In total, 24 server instances produce 336 timed requests; startup, warm-up and diagnostics are excluded.

| Workload | Original, three stages (ms) | Rewrite, three stages (ms) | Original, two stages (ms) | This PR, two stages (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8k | 708.529 | 676.295 | 697.999 | 660.558 |
| 32k | 3914.496 | 3564.066 | 3788.256 | 3366.013 |

Times are medians of six server medians, each based on seven requests. Paired ratios are geometric means across the six rounds; 95% bootstrap intervals resample rounds.

| Comparison | 8k TTFT ratio | 32k TTFT ratio |
|---|---:|---:|
| Rewrite / original, both three stages | 0.95359× | 0.91080× |
| Rewrite / original, both two stages | 0.94508× | 0.88860× |
| This PR / original three-stage kernel | 0.92924× | 0.85994× |

For this PR relative to the original three-stage kernel, the 95% intervals are [0.92538, 0.93288] at 8k and [0.85939, 0.86051] at 32k.

In this workload, `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN` routes the image-containing prefill chunk to Triton. The head-size-512 layers retain BF16 queries with FP8 KV, so they execute the dequantization branch modified by this PR.

Untimed tracing confirmed five head-size-512 calls per workload with BF16 queries, FP8 KV, 16 query heads and 2 KV heads. The target query/KV lengths are 8315/8315 at 8k and 15931/32315 at 32k. Actual pipeline depths were checked, and tracing was removed before timing. Inputs were identical across implementations within each workload, generated text was identical, and warm-up/post-run token-ID checks agreed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Kernel benchmark setup and results</summary>

The kernel matrix uses the same H20 software environment, BF16 queries, native per-tensor FP8 KV, K/V scales 0.37/0.021, four warps and explicit two-/three-stage settings. All cases are 2D causal attention without sliding windows, softcap or a multimodal mask.

The 37 configurations include 20 head-size-512 prefill cases across block sizes 16/64 and query/KV heads 8/2 and 16/2; one page-size-64 case matching the Gemma dimensions; 12 head-size-512 decode cases with query/KV heads 8/2, batch sizes 1/8/64 and KV lengths 8192/32768; and four page-size-64 prefill cases with head sizes 128/256. The prefill dimensions are listed in Section 3.

All four implementations use identical inputs, verified by full input hashes. One complete warm-up round is excluded, followed by six paired rounds with randomized implementation order and a separate process per implementation. Timing uses `triton.testing.do_bench(warmup=25, rep=100, quantiles=[0.25, 0.5, 0.75])`, including its L2-cache clearing between repetitions. The CUDA-event interval covers the attention operation.

The following table applies the PR's launch rule: the rewritten kernel uses two stages for head size 512 and retains three stages for head sizes 128/256. The baseline uses the original three-stage setting. Each ratio is the geometric mean of paired execution-time ratios within the group.

Across all 37 configurations, the geometric mean of paired PR/original execution-time ratios is 0.7613, corresponding to 23.9% lower execution time. Each configuration is weighted equally.

| Configuration group | KV-cache block size | Configurations | PR / original execution time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **All tested configurations** | 16 / 64 | **37** | **0.7613×** |
| Prefill, head size 512, query/KV heads 8/2 and 16/2 | 16 | 10 | 0.7609× |
| Prefill, head size 512, query/KV heads 8/2 and 16/2 | 64 | 10 | 0.6962× |
| Prefill matching the model workload, head size 512, query/KV heads 16/2 | 64 | 1 | 0.6929× |
| Decode, head size 512, query/KV heads 8/2 | 16 | 6 | 0.9573× |
| Decode, head size 512, query/KV heads 8/2 | 64 | 6 | 0.7184× |
| Prefill, head sizes 128/256, query/KV heads 16/2 | 64 | 4 | 0.7555× |

Of the 37 configurations, 36 have paired 95% bootstrap intervals below 1. The remaining case—block size 16, batch size 8, KV length 8192, head size 512 and query/KV heads 8/2—has a ratio of 0.99935 with interval [0.99776, 1.00065]. No configuration has an interval entirely above 1. Intervals resample the six rounds and are not corrected for multiple comparisons.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Correctness checks and CI coverage</summary>

The added `test_triton_unified_attn_fp8_kv_dequantization` passed all 96 cases on H20. It covers BF16 queries, query/KV head counts of 8/2 and 5/1, head sizes of 128, 256 and 512, sliding windows, softcap, both 2D and 3D paths, and dequantization scales that are not powers of two. Results are compared against an FP32 attention reference computed from dequantized K/V.

A separate 72-case numerical check covers BF16 and FP16 queries, head sizes of 128, 256 and 512, query/KV head counts of 8/2 and 16/2, 2D decode, 3D decode and prefill, and two pairs of dequantization scales. All cases passed the predefined error thresholds against a double-precision attention reference computed from FP32-dequantized K/V. All 72 outputs were also bitwise identical to those from the original kernel.

The new 37-configuration matrix also passed finite-output and sampled numerical checks for all four implementations. Selected query rows were compared against double-precision attention over FP32-dequantized K/V, and the sampled outputs were bitwise identical to the original three-stage kernel.

Local lint and type checks, along with `git diff --check`, passed. The added test is included in Buildkite's existing `kernels/attention` job. Local regression runs targeted the tests described above; the full test file was not run.

</details>

items.title: int4 per-token-head KV cache: triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_per_token_head_quant returns wrong values
items.body:
Observed on main @ eac636a7fa476983cdae34b45a984e9852aad375 (NVIDIA H200, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0).

`tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py::test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head` fails in the int4 branch (`kv_quant_mode=INT4_PER_TOKEN_HEAD`, `quant_min=-8.0`, `quant_max=7.0`): the dequantized round-trip (unpack nibbles → zero-point → scale → inverse RHT) lands far outside the assertion tolerance (atol=rtol=0.5) vs the bf16 reference.

**Deterministic failure** — head_size=64, num_kv_heads=1, num_tokens=42 (seed 0, block_size 16), i.e. `[int4-0-16-64-1-42]`. Fails on every run with identical mismatch statistics (inputs are seed-deterministic):

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
Mismatched elements: 35 / 64 (54.7%)
Greatest absolute difference: 3.0546875 at index (0, 38) (up to 0.5 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: 3651.2666015625 at index (0, 52) (up to 0.5 allowed)
```

**Flaky failures** — pass/fail flips across runs on identical code:

- head_size=128, num_kv_heads=1, num_tokens=42 (`[int4-0-16-128-1-42]`): 64/128 (50.0%) mismatched, abs 4.002 @ (0, 70), rel 25.5 @ (0, 101)
- head_size=64, num_kv_heads=4, num_tokens=7 (`[int4-0-16-64-4-7]`): 149/256 (58.2%) mismatched, abs 3.93 @ (2, 26), rel 256 @ (0, 37)

All int8 and fp8 parametrizations, and the remaining int4 combos, pass consistently.

**Minimal repro:**

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py \
  -k "test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head and int4-0-16-64-1-42"
```

**Analysis:** the kernel under test is `vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_per_token_head_quant` (assertion at `tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py:256`). A deterministic 54.7% element mismatch at ~6x the allowed absolute tolerance rules out tolerance noise and points to a correctness defect in the int4 pack/RHT path (candidate causes: zero-point packing or nibble ordering). The two shape-dependent flaky combos additionally suggest a race or uninitialized/leftover cache state whose manifestation depends on shape/head layout.

The qcfg fixture carries IDs int4/int8/fp8; the stacked parametrize resolves bottom-up, so `[int4-0-16-64-1-42]` = seed 0, block_size 16, head_size 64, num_kv_heads 1, num_tokens 42. All failing combos share seed 0 / block_size 16, but those are the only values in `SEEDS`/`BLOCK_SIZES`, so there is no signal there.

Happy to collect a failing-tensor dump if that helps isolate it.

items.title: [ROCm] Fixing GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-V3.2, DeepSeek-V4 on gfx942 and gfx950
items.body:
* An in-tree Triton paged MQA kernel.  It is required unconditionally for DeepSeek V4 (Flash and Pro): V4 shares KV-cache blocks between the indexer and the main MLA cache, so its indexer cache is a non-contiguous strided slice of a larger per-block record written in plain pos-major layout, whereas aiter assumes a contiguous 16×16-preshuffled cache. It is also required when speculative decoding is enabled, because the current AITER implementation of paged_mqa_logits does not work correctly in these cases (the exact cause is yet to be determined).
* Periodically synchronizing the device during FP8-BMM precompilation. Without it, vLLM emits a flood of short kernel launches that sometimes ends in a segfault. 
* A fix to cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache for unaligned block_stride.

Test results, MI325 and MI355, AITER 0.1.21 branch (2026/Aug/28) + the fix from https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5202, https://github.com/ekuznetsov139/llm-comprehension/ (average errors per iteration in a 190 multiple-choice question corpus, lower is better, sigma ~ 0.8 in all cases):

Model               | Upstream  | Upstream + init fix  | Upstream + init fix + spec   |    PR     |    PR + spec

GLM-5.1, MI325      | crash     |    2.8    |  9.0+1.2   |   2.8     |    3.0
GLM-5.2, MI325      |               |     1.6  |            |   1.0     |    1.6
GLM-5.3, MI325      |              |     1.4      |  10.0+3.6   |   2.2     |    1.2
DS3.2, MI325        | crash       |    5.0    |  10.6+3.8   |   3.0     |    3.0
DS4-Flash, MI325    | junk      |           |            |   3.6     |    4.0
DS4-Pro, MI325      | junk      |           |            |   3.4     |    3.2
GLM-5.1, MI355      |   1.8     |           |   7.2+1.0  |     |  2.8
DS4-Flash, MI355    | junk      |           |            |     |  5.2
DS4-Pro, MI355      | junk      |           |            |     |  3.2

As a reference: 

Model                  | Error rate
------------------------------------------|-------------------
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8           | 7.2
Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV | 9.6
gpt-oss-120b  | 16.0

* Entries with '+' (e.g. 9.0+1.2): the value after "+" is the average number of unparseable responses, expected to be 0 in healthy models.
* "junk" = runs, emits locally coherent sequences of tokens that have only a tenuous connection to supplied text, error counts of 50+ and large numbers of unparsed responses.


The two optimization commits previously in the PR have been broken out into a separate PR.

items.title: Starscream Changes to support CPX NPS4
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose
To add support for Starscream when operating AMD Instinct lineup GPUs in CPX+NPS4 operating mode. The is expected to improve the performance of attention kernels on Instinct GPUs.


## Test Plan
include `--enable-starscream` argument when running vllm to launch the updated code. If `--enable-starscream` argument is not set, the default vllm code is launched. 

A sample command would be as follows:
`python3 /app/vllm/benchmarks/benchmark_throughput.py --model $model --num-prompts 2 --input-len $in_len --output-len $out_len --dtype float16 --tensor-parallel-size $tp --distributed-executor-backend mp --enforce-eager --enable-starscream`

## Test Result
The output should look exactly the same but with improved performance for attention.

## Additional Documentation
When the instinct node is set to CPX NPS4 operating mode, each node will now have 64 VGPUs. This would result in replication of KV caches in cases where the num_kv_heads are less than 64. What the code is attempting to do is split the KV caches across XCDs within a GPU instead of replicating it when operating it in CPX NPS4 mode. This requires changes in slot_mapping, KV cache population, and how attention operation is performed with this split. 

1. The changes to slot_mapping is done in `gpu_model_runner.py`
2. The changes to KV cache population by splitting the KV entries is done in `triton_attn.py`
3. The changes to attention implementation to support this change is done in `triton_unified_attention.py`
4. There are additional inter-XCD collectives needed (specifically 2 Allgather operations) for which support for custom calls are made in `communication_op.py` and `parallel_state.py`

items.body: _Requested by **Tun Jian**_ ## Overview Stacked on #63675 (the ROCM_AITER_FA test suite). Only the last commit is new; please review it after #63675 lands. ## Overview

Add ViT full CUDA graph support for the Qwen3-Omni thinker (`Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration`, for example `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct`), part of #38175. Only the vision encoder is captured; the audio encoder stays eager. The thinker has its own `Qwen3Omni_VisionTransformer`, so this follows the Qwen3-VL integration (#35963, video in #38061) rather than reusing the Qwen3-VL code.

The eager Omni vision encoder now builds its attention metadata the way Qwen3-VL does, which also makes it run on FlashInfer: on main it fails there with "cu_seqlens must be divisible by 2". SyaOtiLan ran the GPU validation below on an RTX 4090 with the real vision weights. That work also found a FlashInfer replay bug shared with Qwen3-VL, fixed for Qwen3-VL in #64984 and for Omni in this PR.

## Claims

- Qwen3-Omni implements `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` for images and videos, with the same buffer keys as Qwen3-VL.
- The eager vision encoder and the graph path build their attention metadata through one new `prepare_encoder_metadata`, following Qwen3-VL.
- This changes the eager encoder for every Qwen3-Omni user, with or without the graph flag. On FlashInfer and with FP8 encoder attention, the eager path now gets the same `cu_seqlens` and `max_seqlen` as Qwen3-VL. On main, the Omni encoder computed `max_seqlen` only for FA, ROCm AITER FA and Triton, and passed raw `cu_seqlens` to every backend. The RDNA3 fallback for `torch.repeat_interleave` is removed because that call is gone.
- On FlashInfer, graph replay copies the packed `cu_seqlens` with `_pad_flashinfer_cu_seqlens_buffer`, the helper Qwen2.5-VL registers (#42796). FlashInfer packs the q/k/o and v offsets into one tensor split at its midpoint, and an image replay is padded to a smaller batch bucket than the capture, so the default copy puts both halves into the first half of the buffer. The hook is registered in `get_encoder_cudagraph_config` only when `self.visual.attn_backend` is FLASHINFER, so other backends keep the default copy. #64984 makes the same change for Qwen3-VL; the two PRs are independent and can merge in either order.
- Graph replay matches eager mode on the same padded buffers exactly on FLASH_ATTN and FLASHINFER in every case run below.
- With FLASH_ATTN and budgets [64, 256, 1024], the encoder is faster with graphs when an input nearly fills its budget and slower when it is heavily padded (table below).

## Validation

GPU results from SyaOtiLan: RTX 4090 (SM 8.9), PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, BF16, the real vision weights of the Qwen3-Omni checkpoint at revision 26291f793822fb6be9555850f06dfe95f2d7e695, loaded through `LLM(mm_encoder_only=True)`, budgets [64, 256, 1024], at most 2 vision items and 16 frames per batch. Raw outputs, logs and scripts are in the bundles: [first run](https://github.com/SyaOtiLan/vllm/releases/download/pr-63809-validation-20261101/63809-validation-complete.zip), [after the hook](https://github.com/SyaOtiLan/vllm/releases/download/pr-63809-validation-20261101/63809-branch-b-verification.zip), [extended](https://github.com/SyaOtiLan/vllm/releases/download/pr-63809-validation-20261101/63809-extended-validation.zip).

- E2E tests ([report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6554846868)): `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k qwen3_omni` gave 2 passed at 3687acad21, on FLASH_ATTN. These tests check that capture and replay run, not output values. The only later commit, a27a27a1ed, adds the FlashInfer-only padding hook described above. In the same run, replay on FLASH_ATTN matched eager on the same padded buffers exactly in the three cases sampled.
- Eager encoder, main compared with this branch, tiny random encoder on CUDA: FLASH_ATTN max abs diff 0 on all three grids of the comparison script. On FLASHINFER, main fails with "cu_seqlens must be divisible by 2" and this branch runs, with max abs error against an FP32 reference of 0.0017 to 0.0028.
- Replay on FLASHINFER before the padding hook, at 3687acad21: three replays of one 224 x 224 image differed by up to 3.84, and the first replay differed from eager by 7.72. With the hook ([report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557439065)): replays identical, and replay equal to eager on the same padded buffers.
- Wider replay checks with the hook ([report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557974253)), on a branch with this PR's Omni code plus the Qwen3-VL fix from #64984: mixed-size and two-image batches, video, alternating input shapes and oversized inputs that fall back to eager. All 110 graph-covered conditions matched eager on the same padded buffers exactly, all 4 fallback conditions matched eager, and the 1,368 calls of a shape-transition stress test were exact. The per-layer run in the same report also checked replay against eager on both FLASH_ATTN and FLASHINFER for both models, all exact.
- Padded compared with unpadded eager: the output for a 49-token image differs by a max of 0.40625 on FLASHINFER and 0.5 on FLASH_ATTN (RMSE about 0.008 to 0.009), without graph replay. A per-layer trace finds the first difference in `patch_embed.proj`, whose inputs match exactly, which is consistent with the linear kernel giving different BF16 results at 256 rows than at 196. A [follow-up trace](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6560437008) used a 448 x 448 image (784 valid patches padded to 1024) with BF16 reduced-precision reduction disabled. The first difference between padded and unpadded eager is in `blocks.0.attn.qkv` (max abs 0.015625), whose valid input rows are identical. The GPU runs a different BF16 GEMM kernel at 784 rows than at 1024, and the padded and unpadded FP64 references round to the same BF16 values for the valid rows. A model-local prototype that pre-fills the output with the bias and calls an output-aliased `addmm` on the 27 vision QKV projections brought the final difference for this image from 0.28125 to 0. It increased CUDA graph time from 11.82 to 12.06 ms and eager time from 18.73 to 19.92 ms, and the number of graph-covered conditions whose output exactly matched unpadded ordinary eager went from 12 to 14 of 25. It depends on how this PyTorch build dispatches `addmm`, has not been shown to improve accuracy or output quality, and is not part of this PR. The effect on generated text was not measured.

Encoder latency on FLASH_ATTN (medians of synchronized single calls over 5 paired rounds of 12 samples after 4 warmups, including metadata, packing and copies, excluding preprocessing):

| Input | Output tokens / budget | Eager ms | Graph ms |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Image 224 | 49 / 64 | 16.28 | 4.71 |
| Image 448 | 196 / 256 | 16.17 | 13.07 |
| Images 224 + 448 | 245 / 256 | 17.01 | 13.63 |
| Image 896 | 784 / 1024 | 42.89 | 47.45 |
| Video, 2 frames at 224 | 49 / 64 | 16.28 | 4.57 |
| Video, 8 frames at 224 | 196 / 256 | 16.29 | 11.84 |
| Video, 16 frames at 224 | 392 / 1024 | 16.86 | 33.41 |

This budget set was chosen for the run and is coarse, so the 896 image and the 16-frame video are padded far past their size. A budget close to the typical input size should avoid that slowdown, though only these budgets were timed. The timings were taken at 3687acad21; the later commit does not touch the FLASH_ATTN path.

CPU checks (no GPU), before the GPU runs:

- Eager encoder, main compared with this branch (`TORCH_SDPA`, fp32): a tiny random `Qwen3Omni_VisionTransformer` (hidden 64, 4 heads, depth 3, deepstack at layers 0 and 1) gives a max abs diff of 0.0 for single and mixed image and video grids, with `grid_thw` as a tensor or a list.
- Capture and replay logic through the real `EncoderCudaGraphManager`, with `torch.cuda.graph` replaced by a replayer that reruns `encoder_cudagraph_forward` on the captured buffers: 3 images in one batch, 2 images plus an oversized one, 5 images across two batches and 2 videos all match eager on each item alone (max abs diff 0.0).
- `ruff` check and format pass. `mypy` on `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py` adds no errors over main's version of the file in the same environment.

## Details

Differences from the Qwen3-VL integration:

- Absolute position embedding is optional. When `apply_vit_abs_pos_embed` is off, `pos_embeds` is `None` in both the captured inputs and the replay values. The existing manager already skips `None` values when it copies replay values (`_run_budget_graph`), and this PR does not change the manager. The encoder then adds no position embedding.
- Deepstack features come after the main merger (`merger_list`). The output is `[main, deepstack...]` along the hidden dimension, so `out_hidden_size` is `visual_dim + multiscale_dim`, where `multiscale_dim` is `visual_dim` times the number of deepstack layers.
- `rot_pos_emb` takes a list of `[t, h, w]` instead of a tensor, so all metadata is built from Python lists.
- Eager metadata comes from the shared `MMEncoderAttention` helpers: `cu_seqlens` is built with NumPy, `max_seqlen` comes from `compute_max_seqlen`, and `cu_seqlens` goes through `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`, for which the encoder now records `tp_size` and `fp8_padded_hidden_size`. Eager and graph share this path so that the graph replays the same metadata the eager encoder uses. If you would rather review the eager change on its own first, I can split it into a separate PR.

Not measured: TTFT and full-model output quality, other budget sets, FlashInfer latency, FP8 encoder attention, ROCm, and GPUs other than the RTX 4090.

items.title: [Bug]: fuse_rope_kvcache breaks draft_model/EAGLE spec decode when the drafter's attention shape differs from the target's (ROCm)
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text collect_env.py output was not captured in this container; versions and settings: GPU: 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), one node vLLM: 0.32.0rc1.dev280+g0e939af8a, built from main at 642c18d64c (2026-10-16) plus out-of-tree model-support commits that do not touch the files below. Model Runner V2. Line numbers in the tracebacks are from this build. AITER: amd-aiter 0.1.26.dev124+ga3158e480 PyTorch: 2.12.0+rocm7.14.0 Triton: 3.7.1 Python: 3.14 Environment: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1 VLLM_USE_AITER_TRITON_ROPE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_PAGED_ATTN=0 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=2560 VLLM_TRITON_FP4_GEMM_BPRESHUFFLE=1 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112 AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=1 TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=1 TRITON_HIP_ASYNC_COPY_BYPASS_PERMUTE=1 TRITON_HIP_USE_BLOCK_PINGPONG=1 TRITON_HIP_ASYNC_FAST_SWIZZLE=1 TRITON_HIP_PRESHUFFLE_SCALES=1 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug With speculative decoding that uses a separately compiled drafter (`draft_model` or `eagle`), `RopeKVCacheFusionPass` (`fuse_rope_kvcache`) makes the drafter's torch.compile fail when the drafter's attention geometry differs from the target's. The server never comes up. `RopeKVCacheFusionPass.__init__` registers its patterns from `get_layers_from_vllm_config(config, Attention)`. With `_USE_LAYERNAME` (the default on torch >= 2.11) the layer name is a wildcard, so it registers the patterns once, from the first attention layer, and breaks out of the loop ("all layers produce the same pattern"). That first layer belongs to the target. The pattern's `qkv.split([q_size, k_size, v_size])` uses the target's per-rank sizes. When the pass runs on the drafter's graph, the pattern matches structurally. Re-tracing it in `check_fn` with the drafter's `qkv` then raises instead of rejecting the match. The pass is on by default at -O2/-O3 on ROCm when AITER is enabled, `+rotary_embedding` is a custom op, and inductor graph partitioning is used or the KV-cache update is not a splitting op (`enable_rope_kvcache_fusion` in `vllm/config/vllm.py`). Leaving `fuse_rope_kvcache` out of `pass_config` therefore does not avoid it (we get the same traceback): it has to be disabled explicitly with `"pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache": false}`. `speculative_config.enforce_eager` does not help either, because the drafter still goes through torch.compile with the target's pass config (Model Runner V2, `v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/standalone_ar/speculator.py` `_run_model`). Repro (MI355X / gfx950, ROCm): ```bash vllm serve amd/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-MXFP4-Preview \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 40960 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 6144 --max-num-seqs 512 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend mp --trust-remote-code --seed 42 \ --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \ --speculative-config '{"method":"draft_model","num_speculative_tokens":4,"model":"meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct"}' \ --compilation-config '{"custom_ops":["+quant_fp8","+rotary_embedding"],"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","use_inductor_graph_partition":true,"pass_config":{"fuse_rope_kvcache":true}}' ``` ```text [torch/inductor frames trimmed] File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/piecewise_backend.py", line 189, in __init__ self.compile_all_ranges() File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/piecewise_backend.py", line 265, in compile_all_ranges range_entry.runnable = self.vllm_backend.compiler_manager.compile( self.graph, ...<6 lines>... is_encoder=self.vllm_backend.is_encoder, ) File ".../site-packages/vllm/tracing/otel.py", line 175, in sync_wrapper return func(*args, **kwargs) File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/backends.py", line 372, in compile compiled_graph, handle = self.compiler.compile( graph, ...<3 lines>... maybe_key, ) File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/compiler_interface.py", line 398, in compile compiled_graph = standalone_compile(graph, example_inputs, **compile_kwargs) File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/passes/pass_manager.py", line 83, in wrapper return fn(*args, **kwargs) File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/passes/pass_manager.py", line 112, in __call__ pass_(graph) File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/passes/vllm_inductor_pass.py", line 67, in wrapped call_fn(self, graph) File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/rope_kvcache_fusion.py", line 454, in __call__ self.matched_count = self.patterns.apply(graph) File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/rope_kvcache_fusion.py", line 396, in fwd_and_view_to_reshape gm = pm.fwd_only(*args, **kwargs) File ".../site-packages/vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/rope_kvcache_fusion.py", line 329, in pattern q, k, v = qkv.split([self.q_size, self.k_size, self.v_size], dim=-1) torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: ValueError: Split sizes add up to 2304 but got the tensor's size of 384 ``` The same failure occurs with Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (MXFP4) at TP8 with three drafters: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and the EAGLE-1 head `leptonai/EAGLE-Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct`. The split sizes always add up to the target's per-rank qkv width (2304 = 2048 + 128 + 128). The tensor size is the drafter's: 384 for the 1B (2048 + 512 + 512) / 8, 768 for the 8B, and 2560 for the EAGLE head, whose 16 KV heads differ from the target's 8. With the same flags, `ngram_gpu` (no drafter graph) and the no-spec configuration both run. Expected: the pass registers patterns for every distinct attention geometry it finds (or per compiled model), or rejects a match whose shapes do not fit instead of raising. One possible fix: with `_USE_LAYERNAME`, register one pattern per distinct `(num_heads, num_kv_heads, head_size, head_size_v)` instead of only the first, and give each an `extra_check` that the matched `qkv`'s last dim equals `q_size + k_size + v_size`. A pattern with the wrong geometry is then rejected rather than re-traced. Workaround: `--compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache": false}}'`. This also disables the fusion for the target. The code is the same on `main` as of d14f72c7fe13: `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/rope_kvcache_fusion.py` has not changed since the build above. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing issues and PRs (closest: #55687, a performance issue with the same pass; nothing on spec decode).

items.title: [KV Cache] Skip the zero fill in allocate_kv_cache when the platform does not need it
items.body:
**What this changes**

`allocate_kv_cache()` always zero-fills the backing buffer (`torch.zeros`). On a device whose KV cache lives in unified memory that memset writes every page of a multi-GB pool at startup — the pool is resident before the first request and stays that way, even though a serving run only ever writes the blocks it allocates.

The function now takes `zero_fill: bool = True`. With `zero_fill=False` it builds the same layout from `torch.empty`, so a platform can skip the fill. Default behaviour is unchanged.

**Why the fill is not always needed**

The kernels already assume the invariant `KVCacheConfig.needs_kv_cache_zeroing` encodes: every position below the sequence length is written before a reader runs (the same layer writes K/V with `reshape_and_cache`, or an earlier chunk did), and attention masks everything at or past the sequence length. The caches that genuinely read before writing — Mamba state, mixed-precision caches — are exactly the ones that set that flag, and they keep their zeros (up front, or per block as the scheduler hands blocks out).

So the fill is a convenience for the unified-memory case, not a correctness requirement for uniform-precision attention caches. Making it opt-out lets an out-of-tree platform (vllm-metal, Apple Silicon) stop paying for it; the caller takes on the guarantee above.

**What the opt-in caller also takes on: residency**

The flag changes *when* the pages become resident, not whether the OS can take
them back. On unified memory the pool is an ordinary anonymous allocation that
nothing pins — MLX's `set_wired_limit()` covers its own buffers, not memory it
imports in place — so the kernel may compress or swap any of it under pressure,
zeros or live KV alike. The fill never bought a reservation; it only made the
pages resident up front.

The ceiling is unchanged: resident KV is bounded by the blocks in use, so a run
that fills the pool peaks where the eager build peaked, and never needs bytes
the fill had not already committed. Measured on an Apple M4 (16 KiB pages):

| | allocation | first write |
|---|---|---|
| `torch.empty(2 GiB)` | RSS flat, ~0 extra faults | 2 GiB resident, 131,477 faults (= 2 GiB / 16 KiB) |
| `torch.zeros(2 GiB)` | 2 GiB resident, 131,489 faults | another 131,451 faults — the kernel had already reclaimed them |

There is no new error path either: a fault into an already-mapped page is
satisfied from the compressor or the swap file, it does not return `ENOMEM`, so
Python never sees a `MemoryError` here. A machine that exhausts both ends the
process the same way it would end a startup zero-fill.

Two caveats belong to the platform that opts out:

- **Admission.** An uncommitted pool is invisible to anything that sizes itself
  off free memory (`psutil`, a second server, any app), where the eager fill's
  resident pages at least showed up as used. On a shared machine,
  `--gpu-memory-utilization` bounds cache *capacity*, not admission.
- **Timing.** The faults now land during serving — a long prefill can demand
  hundreds of megabytes at once — rather than before the first request.

Neither is a correctness issue, and neither reaches CUDA: `cudaMalloc` commits
the device allocation regardless of the memset, so no platform that exists today
changes behaviour under the `True` default.

**Measurement**

Apple M4, vllm-metal serving Qwen3-0.6B-4bit / Qwen3-1.7B-4bit at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.5`. Same five fixed workloads, one process per model:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| peak RSS | 6.45 GB | 2.16 GB (−67%) |
| paired runs | 3887 / 4008 MB | 1269 / 1270 MB |
| KV cache capacity | 44,368 tokens | 44,368 tokens (unchanged) |

Adversarial check on the plugin side: filling the whole pool with a bf16 NaN pattern produces byte-identical outputs to the zeroed build, and served-path parity against native `mlx-lm` is unchanged before and after.

**Tests**

`tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py::test_allocate_kv_cache_zero_fill_can_be_skipped` asserts that the default fill still happens, that `zero_fill=False` does not fill, and that both produce the identical layout (shapes, strides, storage offsets, dtypes). It fails if `zero_fill` is accepted but ignored. `ruff check` / `ruff format` (0.14.0, the pre-commit pin) are clean on both files.

items.title: [Attention][MLA] fp8_ds_mla for rope-free NoPE models (head_dim 512) on SM90 via zero-padded-rope envelope
items.body:
## 🚀 Description

Enables `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache for rope-free NoPE sparse-MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`, head_dim 512, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash) on **SM90/Hopper** via the FlashMLA sparse backend, served through a zero-padded 576/656B envelope.

Today on H200, GLM-5.3-Flash must either use bf16 KV (~2x memory) or the plain per-tensor-fp8 `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` backend, which returns no LSE and therefore cannot run DCP (decode context parallel) or compose with the MTP fused-draft path. The only SM90 sparse-MLA backend with `fp8_ds_mla` support (`FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, #47090) hard-rejects head_dim 512 because the FlashMLA kernels assume the fixed 576 geometry.

**Approach**: keep the 656B packed row layout unchanged and zero-pad the rope section:
- The rope bytes [640:768] of every cached token are written as bf16 zeros, and the query-side `q_pe` is zero-padded to 64 dims. Since RoPE is baked into the cache at write time, `q_pe · 0 = 0` exactly in IEEE arithmetic — the padding contributes nothing to any logit. This was verified end-to-end with a standalone kernel probe on H20 (SM90): output rel-err vs a bf16 NoPE-512 reference matches the fp8 block-quant noise floor (~2.5e-2), and a garbage-rope control diverges, proving the test has teeth.
- `FLASHMLA_SPARSE.get_supported_head_sizes()` → `[576, 512]`; `supports_combination` accepts 512 **only** for quantized DS-MLA dtypes (`fp8_ds_mla`/`nvfp4_ds_mla`), so bf16 NoPE-512 traffic keeps flowing to the FlashInfer/TRITON backends.
- A shared helper in `mla_attention.py` promotes the rope dims of rope-free MLA layers to the padded 576 geometry when the effective KV dtype is quantized DS-MLA on `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, emitting persistent zero buffers (CUDA-graph capture stable). Models with rope dims > 0 are untouched.
- `SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder` now derives its MLA dims from the instantiated runtime layers instead of the raw HF config, so the chunked-prefill workspace is sized from the promoted (576) geometry — without this, `cp_gather_and_upconvert_fp8_kv_cache` asserts `head_dim must be 576` (found in e2e).
- Backend selection: on SM90, `fp8_ds_mla` + head_size 512 now prefers `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` over `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`; plain `fp8` keeps FlashInfer as the documented stopgap (the two fp8 flavors remain distinguishable, no silent dtype reinterpretation).

**No csrc changes; no cache geometry changes.** The existing 576 traffic (DeepSeek family) is bit-identical. DCP mixed-batch LSE merge, MTP spec-decode reshape plumbing and CUDA-graph capture behavior are inherited unchanged (shapes and kernels are identical to the 576 path).

**Memory tradeoff (honest accounting)**: 656B/token vs a hypothetical "true NoPE fp8" 528B = +24% KV footprint; vs bf16 1152B/token it is still a 43% reduction. No SM90 kernel consumes a 512-only packed fp8 layout, so the padded envelope is the only way to get block-scaled fp8 KV on Hopper today.

### Not a duplicate of

- #47090 — FlashMLA fp8_ds_mla for SM90/SM100, but 576 geometry only; this PR extends it to NoPE-512 via the padded envelope.
- #53969 / #55277 — SM120 NoPE work on the FlashInfer SM120 backend (SM120 later moved to native `pe_dim=0`); this PR is the SM90 FlashMLA counterpart and cross-references them as siblings of the same technique.
- #54563 — fp8_ds_mla tile-scale reading; orthogonal.
- `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` plain-fp8 path — remains available and unchanged; it lacks LSE (no DCP) and per-tensor scaling.
- #54790 — fused draft metadata updates for sparse MLA backends (FlashMLA no-op + DSV3.2 indexer refresh + KPOOL_TAIL tail-cache mapping); orthogonal spec-decode change with no code dependency, but both were deployed and validated together on the same 8xH200 GLM-5.3-Flash stack (MTP K=3, full CUDA graphs).

## 📋 Tests

- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashmla_nope_sm90_backend_selection.py` — head-size/dtype acceptance matrix + SM90 priority (CPU-runnable): 14 passed, 4 skipped (no `vllm._C_stable_libtorch` on macOS dev host; CI-eligible on Linux CPU runner).
- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashmla_nope_sm90_fp8_ds_mla.py` — GPU suite (auto-skip without CUDA): zero-pad helper shape/zero/persistence, cache-write contract (rope bytes 640:768 bf16 zero, NoPE bytes match per-128-block fp8 reference), kernel equivalence vs bf16 NoPE-512 reference (rel-err < 0.08) with garbage-rope control, ragged mixed-batch (valid counts 0/1/partial, `-1` tails, all-invalid rows → (0, -inf)).
- Pre-commit (ruff-check/format, typos, mypy-3.10, SPDX) on all commits.

**E2E (8xH200, GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8/EP8, fp8_ds_mla, FLASHMLA_SPARSE, MTP K=3, chunked prefill, prefix caching, full CUDA graphs)**:

items.title: [Bug][DSV4-Flash][DSpark] Startup dies in kernel warmup with "ragged spec decode batch: 7 tokens over 2 requests"
items.body:
Hitting a deterministic startup crash on the V2 model runner with DSV4-Flash + DSpark. The engine gets through model load, KV cache allocation, and CUDA graph capture, then dies in kernel warmup.

**Environment**
- 2x DGX Spark (GB10/SM121), TP=2, no-Ray
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, dspark (`num_speculative_tokens=5`, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`)
- vLLM main 0f102c3ba (v0.26.1rc1.dev1114), FlashInfer fb28d724
- `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, `max_model_len=1000000`, `max_num_seqs=8`

**Failure**

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'ragged spec decode batch: 7 tokens over 2 requests'
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py, _run_decode_step
```

**Cause**

The warmup harness (`warmup.py`) deliberately runs a mixed spec/non-spec decode step:

```python
decode_steps.append(([0, 1], [use_spec_decode, False]))
```

with a comment noting GDN/KDA reclassify non-spec decodes as prefill. For dspark `decode_query_len=6`, that feeds 6 tokens to request 0 and 1 token to request 1. `_forward_decode` in the DSV4 FlashInfer sparse backend (guard added in PR #52499) then asserts:

```python
assert num_decode_tokens % num_decodes == 0, "ragged spec decode batch: ..."
```

`7 % 2 != 0` → abort.

The backend can't express that batch in one call: flashinfer's dsv4 decode API needs a uniform `[batch, q_len_per_request, heads, 512]` shape, and a flattened ragged batch gets misrouted to the varlen prefill kernel (which asserts `num_tokens > 64` on SM120). GDN handles this via reclassification; the DSV4 sparse path has no equivalent split. This is also worth noting against the DSpark bring-up tracker (#51303), which lists "DSV4 Attention" as supporting variable-length decode batches — on the SM120 FlashInfer sparse path that capability is currently absent.

I don't think a genuinely mixed batch can occur at serving time for dspark (the drafter proposes for every scheduled request), so this looks warmup-only — but startup is fully blocked either way.

**Workaround (current):** patched `warmup.py` to catch that specific assertion, log it, and continue warming the rest. Unblocks startup; not a fix.

**Possible fixes**
1. Gate the mixed spec/non-spec warmup step on backends that can express it (its own comment scopes it to reclassifying models like GDN/KDA).
2. Make `_forward_decode` split ragged decode batches into two uniform sub-calls (spec group `next_n=6`, non-spec flat), using per-request `query_start_loc` boundaries.

Related: runs with PR #52499 applied (see my comment there on contiguity); sibling SM120 issues #50720; DSpark tracker #51303.
