items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Profile adaptive verification tails as mixed batches
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #54046.

Adaptive verification profiles token counts beyond the cudagraph capture limit by distributing them across dummy requests. With `max_num_seqs=128` and seven speculative tokens, a real decode request contributes eight query tokens, so a fully occupied decode step contains at most:

```text
128 * (1 + 7) = 1024 tokens
```

Tail samples above 1024 tokens cannot be uniform decode batches. Previously, however, a 16384-token sample was profiled as 128 requests with 128 query tokens each, producing a shape the scheduler cannot generate for speculative decoding.

This change profiles tail samples as schedulable mixed decode/prefill batches.

For the configuration reported in the issue:

```text
max_num_batched_tokens = 16384
max_num_seqs           = 128
num_speculative_tokens = 7
profile_context_len    = 8192
```

the 16384-token profile becomes:

```text
126 decode requests * 8 tokens
2 fresh-prefill requests * 7688 tokens
```

## Changes

- Keep captured token sizes unchanged so their dummy runs continue to match their cudagraph descriptors.
- Convert only tail sizes above the decode ceiling into mixed decode/prefill batches.
- Account for the decode tokens freed when a request slot becomes prefill.
- Allow small request budgets to produce a schedulable prefill-only tail instead of falling back to an invalid uniform shape.
- Carry the explicit per-request split through the existing scheduler output.
- Give context only to decode rows.
- Mark trailing rows as fresh prefill and construct their positions accordingly.
- Size dummy block tables for the longest decode or prefill sequence.
- Preserve the existing even split when no explicit profile shape is supplied.
- Fall back to the existing dummy shape if cudagraph dispatch pads or reshapes the batch.

## Tests

Hardware:

```text
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
CUDA-enabled PyTorch environment
```

Regression command:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py
```

Result:

```text
54 passed, 14 warnings
```

Additional checks:

```text
py_compile: passed
ruff check 0.14.0: passed
ruff format --check 0.14.0: passed
```

The CUDA regression test verifies the explicit split, decode-only context, fresh-prefill metadata, positions, sequence lengths, and KV block-table coverage.

A full DSpark model-serving evaluation was not run because the corresponding large-model environment was not available on this single-GPU host. This change affects startup profiling shapes and does not modify sampling or verification kernels.

## Related work

#54065 addresses the same reported issue. This implementation additionally:

- keeps the prefill rows context-free instead of applying dummy decode context to every row;
- accounts for freed decode tokens when sizing prefill chunks;
- covers small request budgets that require a prefill-only tail.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during investigation, implementation and test. Every changed line and the reported test results were reviewed.

items.title: [Bugfix][Model] Remove redundant all_gather_interleave in ViT split_qkv
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #49061.

PaddleOCR-VL, Ernie4.5-VL, and GLM-4.1V vision attention each carried a
byte-identical helper `all_gather_interleave()` that calls
`torch.distributed.all_gather()` directly on the tensor-parallel group's raw
`device_group`, followed by a per-rank re-split, inside `split_qkv()`.

There are two problems.

First, portability. The vision encoder runs eagerly (`torch.no_grad()`, outside
`torch.compile`). On any platform whose `device_group` has no c10d backend
registered for eager use, the direct `dist.all_gather()` raises
`RuntimeError: No backend type associated with device type`, which crashes the
vision-encoder worker with `EngineDeadError` for every image request at
`tensor_parallel_size > 1`. vLLM's collective API
(`tensor_model_parallel_all_gather`, routed through `GroupCoordinator`) exists to
handle exactly this case, and the hand-rolled helper bypassed it.

Second, redundancy. The gather is a no-op. Each rank's local qkv out of
`QKVParallelLinear` (`gather_output=False`) is `[q_shard | k_shard | v_shard]`
for that rank's own heads. `all_gather_interleave` gathers every rank, reorders
to `[all_q | all_k | all_v]`, then `split_tensor_along_last_dim(...)[tp_rank]`
selects back exactly this rank's own shards. For full multi-head self-attention
(`total_num_kv_heads == total_num_heads`, which all three models use) the whole
round-trip is a numerical identity, so chunking the local tensor directly is
bit-identical.

This is the same removal already merged for `glm4_1v` in #23441
("Remove redundant all gather + split"), which fixed that model's `split_qkv`
but left the now-dead `all_gather_interleave` helper behind.

## Changes

- `paddleocr_vl.py`, `ernie45_vl.py`: drop the `all_gather_interleave` gather and
  the subsequent per-rank re-split from `split_qkv`, keeping `qkv.chunk(3, dim=2)`
  and the reshape. This matches the already-merged `glm4_1v.split_qkv`.
- All three files: delete the now-unused module-level `all_gather_interleave`.
- New `tests/model_executor/test_vit_split_qkv_equivalence.py`: a CPU regression
  test asserting the local-chunk path is bit-identical to the old gather
  round-trip across `tp_size` in `{2, 4}` and several head and dim configs. It
  guards against a future reintroduced gather, or a grouped-query layout that
  would break the equal-shard assumption.

## Not a duplicate

- No open PR references #49061 (checked `gh pr list --state open --search
  "49061 in:body"` and `all_gather_interleave` / `split_qkv ViT` keyword
  searches, both empty).
- #23441 (merged) applied this exact transformation to `glm4_1v` only.
- #31402 attempted to extend the removal to these files but was never merged. It
  was auto-closed for inactivity after 90 days of no review, not rejected on
  technical grounds. This PR completes that cleanup, and unlike #31402 it also
  deletes glm4_1v's leftover dead helper, adds a regression test, and avoids
  #31402's flagged defect (which had left glm4_1v's call site intact).

## Test plan and results

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on all four changed files: pass.
- New equivalence test: the identity it encodes is bit-identical (`torch.equal`)
  across `tp_size` in `{2, 4}` and head configs `{(4,8), (8,16), (16,8)}`, 18 of
  18 rank-cases. The test imports only `vllm.distributed.utils`.
- Because the change is a numerical identity, model output is unchanged, so no
  accuracy or evaluation delta is expected and none is required.

items.title: [RFC]: fp8 KV cache for the Ampere sparse-MLA path (TRITON_MLA_SPARSE) via software dequant
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**`TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` (#47629) is bf16-KV-only, and on 24 GB cards that is the binding constraint.** I have a working sm_80/sm_86 fp8 KV path and would like to know whether the project wants it before I polish it into a mergeable PR.

#### The gap, in the PR's own words

`TritonMLASparseBackend` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/triton_mla_sparse.py`):

```python
supported_kv_cache_dtypes: ClassVar[list[CacheDType]] = ["auto", "float16", "bfloat16"]
```

its decode entry point is literally `_forward_bf16_kv`, and the base it inherits refuses quantized KV outright (`xpu_mla_sparse.py:238`):

```python
if is_quantized_kv_cache(self.kv_cache_dtype):
    raise NotImplementedError("FP8 kv is not supported with XPU MLA Sparse yet")
```

The stated reason fp8 is excluded on Ampere is that Triton cannot handle `fp8e4nv` there. That is true for **native** fp8 — and irrelevant for fp8 **as storage**.

#### The technique is already in this very PR

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/mqa_logits_triton.py:191`, added by #47629 itself:

```python
# Kernel decodes FP8 from uint8 via LUT (SM80 Triton can't load fp8e4nv).
```

The indexer already reads fp8 pages on SM80 by loading them as `uint8` and decoding in-register. **The KV path simply hasn't had the same treatment.** (`models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_sparse_decode_fp8.py` does the same thing for XPU: *"dequantize FP8 KV cache pages to BF16 on the fly, then reuse the BF16 sparse MLA attention kernel"*.) So the precedent is accepted in-tree, twice, and neither conflicts with #43914 / #47060's "native FP8 requires SM89+" — software dequant is a different mechanism.

#### What I did

An `IS_FP8: tl.constexpr` branch inside **your own** `_sparse_mla_compute_tile` — the single function through which both `_sparse_mla_kernel_final` and `_sparse_mla_kernel_split` load KV — so fp8 inherits your split-KV, your merge kernel, your autotune and your masking for free. The standard 656-byte `fp8_ds_mla` page is loaded as raw `uint8` and decoded with bit-math that is **bit-exact vs `torch.float8_e4m3fn` over all 256 byte values**. Nothing about the cache layout changes; the existing C++ `concat_and_cache_ds_mla` writer already runs on sm_86 unmodified (`ENABLE_FP8` is CUDA-version-gated, not arch-gated — verified by execution).

Patch (224 lines, applies to `bbe2ab4d6`, one flag / one branch / one dispatcher arg): https://github.com/nickus/vllm-fp8kv/blob/main/patches/triton_mla_sparse_fp8.patch

#### Measured on RTX 3090 (sm_86) — including the part that is not good news

| | |
|---|---|
| fp8 dequant, all 256 byte values | **bit-exact** vs `torch.float8_e4m3fn` |
| Decode vs fp32 reference, through vLLM's **own C++ `ds_mla` writer** and **own `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index`** | **cosine 0.999996** |
| KV pool capacity | **1.756×** (656 B vs 1152 B/token); **~1.63×** effective once the indexer's own K-cache is counted |
| Decode speed vs bf16, same kernel, bs=8 / topk=2048 | **0.92×** |
| Decode speed vs bf16, same kernel, bs=32 / topk=2048 | **0.45×** |

**So this is a capacity-for-speed trade, not a free win**, and I would rather say so up front than have it found in review. At bs=32 fp8 decode is currently ~2.2× slower. My working hypothesis is that the autotune *config lists* (`_FINAL_AUTOTUNE_CONFIGS`: `BLOCK_N=16` only; `_SPLIT_AUTOTUNE_CONFIGS`: `BLOCK_N=32` only) are tuned for bf16's 1152 B rows and that fp8's 656 B rows plus a scale load want larger blocks — but **I have not measured that on the real kernel yet**, so I am flagging it as a hypothesis, not a finding. On a 24 GB card the 1.76× capacity may well be worth the decode cost; on an A100 it plainly is not, which is an argument for keeping this opt-in.

#### What is NOT done

* The patch above is **kernel-only** and therefore inert on its own: the backend still declares bf16-only dtypes, `get_kv_cache_shape` returns a 576-wide row for every dtype (fp8_ds_mla needs 656 — `flashmla_sparse.py` already handles this), and `_canonicalize_sparse_mla_kv_cache_dtype` maps `fp8_e4m3 -> fp8_ds_mla` only for FLASHMLA_SPARSE / SM120. I have that wiring working out-of-tree; it is ~40 more lines.
* **No engine-level boot yet.** All correctness numbers above are kernel-level. I have not yet run `LLM(..., kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3")` end-to-end and compared logits against a bf16 run.

#### The questions

1. Does the project **want** fp8 KV on the Ampere sparse-MLA path, given it buys ~1.76× KV capacity at a decode cost that is currently significant at larger batch?
2. If yes: kernel-only PR first (the diff above, dispatch dormant until the backend declares the dtype), or one PR including the backend wiring?
3. Any objection to the fp8-as-storage / software-dequant approach in the shared `_sparse_mla_compute_tile`, given `mqa_logits_triton.py` already does exactly this on SM80?

Happy to do the engine boot + logits parity and the config-list measurement before opening the PR — I just want to know the feature is wanted first.

---

*Unrelated bug found while working on this path, already filed: #48364 / #48366 (fully-masked leading index chunks NaN-poison `xpu_mla_sparse`).*

### Alternatives considered

* **Native fp8 (`fp8e4nv`) on Ampere** — impossible; that is the constraint the PR itself documents.
* **Dequantize whole pages to bf16 before the kernel** — what the XPU path does; costs a full bf16 materialization of the gathered KV, which throws away the bandwidth saving that is the entire point on a 24 GB card.
* **Keep bf16 KV and shrink the model instead** — what 3090/4090 owners do today; it is why GLM-5.2-class DSA models are effectively unusable at long context on consumer Ampere.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/vllm) users if needed.

items.title: [Bugfix][Compile] Preserve eager layouts for untagged custom ops
items.body:
## Overview

Fix corrupted generation when Inductor mode 2 compiles Transformers attention and KV-cache updates by preserving eager input strides for custom operators without a layout tag. Fixes #62865.

## Claims

- Default `direct_register_custom_op` to `torch.Tag.needs_exact_strides` only when no layout tag is supplied.
- Preserve explicit exact-stride, fixed-stride-order, and flexible-layout choices, including unrelated tags such as `cudagraph_unsafe`.
- Retain the fallback allow-list optimization and document the input-layout contract.

## Validation

Tested on one RTX 4090 (24 GiB, driver 595.71.05), Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, and Transformers 5.20.2. The source base is `db3b0f0fae4bc98492b3863685e541e62bc59576`; native extensions came from the official precompiled wheel for that exact commit. No full native rebuild was performed. Model runs used Model Runner V2, the Transformers backend, BF16, and FlashAttention 2.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/compile/test_inductor_fallback_allow_list_patch.py tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py -v --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_inductor_preserves_attention_layout -v --tb=short
```

| Check | New tests with the production fix reverted | With the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compile and torch-utils suites | 2 failed, 58 passed; both new stride cases fail | 60 passed |
| Real `LLM` generation/logprob regression | 1 failed; first expected token absent from compiled top-5 | 1 passed |

The model test reuses `check_implementation` and its existing logprob comparison without changing tolerances. It passes with two token-choice warnings, so this is not a claim of token-for-token eager equivalence. All applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. Existing Buildkite steps select all three test files; upstream CI has not run.

Additional evaluation: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, snapshot `7ae557604adf67be50417f59c2c2f167def9a775`, first 64 GSM8K test questions, five shots, greedy decoding, 512-token limit, one run per configuration. Each run used fresh compilation cache directories with persistent compilation caches disabled.

| Configuration | Correct / 64 | Accuracy | Invalid answers |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unpatched eager reference | 31 | 48.44% | 0 |
| Unpatched Inductor mode 2 | 1 | 1.56% | 9 |
| Patched Inductor mode 2 | 27 | 42.19% | 0 |
| Unpatched registration, allow-list patch disabled | 27 | 42.19% | 0 |

The last row is an implicit-fallback control: revert the registration fix and disable only the `_patch_inductor_fallback_allow_list()` invocation in `env_override.py`. Its generated token sequences match the patched run exactly for all 64 questions. The eager/compiled score difference therefore also exists in that control. This is a subset evaluation, not full GSM8K, and no performance improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the GSM8K subset</summary>

Run this in each source configuration, setting `LAYOUT_EAGER=1` for eager or `0` for compiled runs. Use fresh cache directories for each invocation. The reported runs used the pinned model snapshot above and identical dataset files.

```bash
export VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1
export TORCHINDUCTOR_FX_GRAPH_CACHE=0 TORCHINDUCTOR_AUTOGRAD_CACHE=0
export TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
export TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
LAYOUT_EAGER=0 .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import os
import time
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval import _build_gsm8k_prompts, _score_gsm8k

eager = os.environ["LAYOUT_EAGER"] == "1"
kwargs = dict(
    model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", model_impl="transformers",
    dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=4096, max_num_seqs=16,
    max_num_batched_tokens=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.65,
    enable_prefix_caching=False, seed=0, enforce_eager=eager,
)
if not eager:
    kwargs["compilation_config"] = dict(
        mode=2, backend="inductor", cudagraph_mode="NONE",
    )
llm = LLM(**kwargs)
assert llm.llm_engine.model_config.using_transformers_backend()
prompts, labels = _build_gsm8k_prompts(64, 5, "")
sampling = SamplingParams(
    temperature=0, max_tokens=512,
    stop=["Question", "Assistant:", "<|separator|>"],
)
started = time.perf_counter()
outputs = llm.chat(
    [[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}] for prompt in prompts],
    sampling, chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False},
)
elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
texts = [out.outputs[0].text for out in outputs]
lengths = [len(out.outputs[0].token_ids) for out in outputs]
print(_score_gsm8k(texts, lengths, labels, 5, 512, elapsed))
PY
```

</details>

## Details

The fallback allow-list added in #42129 routes custom operators through a path that omits PyTorch's implicit exact-stride constraint. After Transformers RoPE, Inductor can pass head-major keys to `unified_kv_cache_update`; `reshape_and_cache_flash` reads the token stride and assumes packed heads. This implements the layout-tag approach (option 3) identified in #62865: an explicit default layout tag restores that input contract without removing the allow-list.

The implementation adds ten registration-time lines and no inference-time synchronization. Enforcing the layout can introduce materialization/copies that the unconstrained path omitted. Operators with an explicit layout tag keep their existing behavior. Other GPU architectures and the full model suite have not been validated locally.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-10-21 found no PR referencing #62865 and no issue comments. #61749 changes explicit MoE layout tags, which this fix preserves; #57310 changes when the allow-list patch is imported, which this fix does not edit. The default-branch registration code still lacked the fix when rechecked immediately before submission.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to investigate, implement, and validate this change.

items.title: [Performance]: ROPE + KV-Cache-Write + pre-attn prepare-ops fusion
items.body: ### Proposal to improve performance Performance analysis of DeepSeekR1 and GPTOSS showed that there is non-trivial amount of overheads in the operations that come before the Attention kernel. Specifically, these are ROPE + KV-Cache-Write + attn elementwise/copy prepare ops (and sometimes small matrix multiplies for MLA). Here is a concrete breakdown for DeepSeekR1-FP8 batch-size 32 on 8xB200 GPUs: Before the attention kernel call (fmha::kernel), we can see 4 triton ops (ROPE), then cache_and_concat_mla, and then a torch BMM (matrix_multiply - K-Proj) followed by a bunch of elementwise and copy. The total time these ops take is about the same as the whole attention kernel, so we propose to fuse all of them to reduce HBM traffic bandwidth, since these ops are memory-bandwidth by their nature. A similar fusion is needed for GPTOSS as well, here a breakdown: This one is a bit simpler, since the attention kernel does not expose elementwise ops (or matmul) like in DeepSeekR1 model above. However, there is still the series of triton ops (ROPE) followed by reshape_and_cache_kernel. NVIDIA has a fused ROPE+KV-Cache-write+attn prepare ops kernel in TRT (@pavanimajety is part of the related team) and would be good to understand the following: 1. Does current work supports both reshape_and_cache and concat_and_cache_mla? 2. What about quantization types? Can we do static per-tensor, dynamic per-token, and dynamic per-group (block quant)? 3. [@Lucas Wilkinson](https://vllm-dev.slack.com/team/U07QLKR3146) and @ProExpertProg talked about how to expose the cache and quant and there's actually some ongoing work to refactor the attention layer into multiple layers so that MLA/SDPA/etc. don't all have to go through the same unified_attention op. - Issue here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/24620 - That means concat_and_cache_mla will be exposed in the layer and will appear in the graph. - For quants, ~instead of adding more methods and layers (my original proposal), we should implement a method similar to output quant fusion. We can query the attention backend whether input quant de-fusion is supported. If yes, we add a quant to the graph outside unified attention.~ This is now handled in the attention layer: #24914. This won't change the semantic meaning of unified_attention as much because we're just changing the dtype of the input. ~We might need to figure out how to expose the scale for the quant layer to the graph, if we can't make it visible in the traced graph we can just add a new custom op that extracts it from the attention layer.~ PR tracking: - `MLAAttention` extraction: [#25103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/25103) - Separate kvcache from `unified_attention`: [#25954](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/25954) - Add `concat_cache_mla_rope` CUDA kernel: [#25774](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/25774)

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary On **vLLM 0.31.0**, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` with DFlash2 produces different greedy token sequences from target-only decoding. After removing the initial cross-mode differences, we also isolated a second failure: **the same generated prefix can produce a different next token when rebuilt through prefill rather than continued through decode**. Under load, preemption/recompute exposes this difference. We traced this to several target-forward numerical paths and a separate mixed-batch gate-indexing error. We implemented a local, opt-in consistency patch and verified exact token equality in the tested configuration, including concurrent requests, CUDA decode graphs, prefix-cache hits and preemptions. **This is not evidence that DFlash accepts tokens contrary to the verifier's argmax.** In our audited responses, every chosen token had a maximal returned target logprob. The target forward itself differed between execution paths. We also do not assume that unmodified GDN models already promise batch-invariant operation: some of the work below is a deterministic-mode proof of concept, while the gate-indexing defect is independently testable. ## Environment and scope - GPU: one NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation, 48 GB, SM89; TP=1, PP=1. - Unmodified image used for the original reproduction: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:c1c9f6fd5c109ba7f0546a59f5b2f15fb87f64c77782e90a27b648b42a8e67c3`. - Target: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`, revision `95a723d08a9490559dae23d0cff1d9466213d989`. - Draft: `incoai/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash2`, revision `51ef7b6923ad6c14cb1bb41c37a9041446496ab6`. - FP8 target weights; BF16 compute and KV cache; FP32 SSM states, as configured by this checkpoint. No CPU offload. - V2 runner, context 65,536, `max_num_seqs=32`, `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`, GPU memory utilization 0.98. - Greedy: temperature 0, seed 42, top_p 1, top_k -1, repetition_penalty 1, presence/frequency penalties 0. - Qwen thinking enabled. Comparisons include reasoning tokens, not only visible text. - Full `collect_env.py` output is in the environment field. It was collected from the currently patched container, which shares the original image's libraries. The failure was separately reproduced on the unmodified image above. - We have **not rerun this investigation on the latest main branch** or established equivalent behavior on other hardware/model/SSM precisions. ## Original stock reproduction The `serve-stock.sh` included below reproduces the recorded original launch settings, with public model revisions and a generic served alias. It uses FlashAttention/FA2 and the original `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` policy. Later diagnostic and final patched configurations are described separately below. Run target-only and DFlash **sequentially on the same GPU**, inside the pinned unmodified image: ```bash bash serve-stock.sh target # From another terminal, after readiness: python3 reproduce.py record target.json # Stop the target-only server, then start: bash serve-stock.sh dflash # After readiness: python3 reproduce.py record dflash.json python3 reproduce.py compare target.json dflash.json ``` The reproduction files below contain three synthetic prompts and their frozen input token IDs. A short one-prompt client, usable without the other files, is: ```python import json import sys import urllib.request from pathlib import Path from transformers import AutoTokenizer prompt = ( "Schreibe eine ausführliche Python-Anleitung mit Code für einen robusten " "JSONL-Import. Behandle Streaming großer Dateien, Validierung, doppelte IDs, " "fehlerhafte Zeilen, ein nachvollziehbares Fehlerprotokoll und wiederholbare " "Verarbeitung. Erkläre in mindestens 1200 Wörtern die Entscheidungen und " "zeige mehrere Codebeispiele." ) tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8", revision="95a723d08a9490559dae23d0cff1d9466213d989", ) ids = tok.apply_chat_template( [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True, preserve_thinking=True, ) if hasattr(ids, "keys"): ids = ids["input_ids"] body = { "model": "target", "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0, "top_p": 1, "top_k": -1, "seed": 42, "presence_penalty": 0, "frequency_penalty": 0, "repetition_penalty": 1, "add_special_tokens": False, "return_token_ids": True, "return_tokens_as_token_ids": True, "logprobs": 5, "cache_salt": "fresh-" + sys.argv[1], } req = urllib.request.Request( "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as response: result = json.load(response) Path(sys.argv[1] + ".json").write_text(json.dumps(result)) if Path("target.json").exists() and Path("dflash.json").exists(): a, b = [json.loads(Path(p + ".json").read_text())["choices"][0]["token_ids"] for p in ("target", "dflash")] first = next((i for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(a, b)) if x != y), None) if first is None and len(a) != len(b): first = min(len(a), len(b)) print("exact:", a == b, "first differing token (0-based):", first) ``` Save this as `minimal.py` and run `python3 minimal.py target` against target-only, then `python3 minimal.py dflash` against DFlash. Its tokenization was checked against the frozen original inputs. Only public model artifacts are needed. ### Observed results | Synthetic prompt | First differing output-token index, 0-based | Target-only token ID | DFlash token ID | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Business Central import investigation | 194 | 6478 | 67776 | | Python JSONL import | 124 | 11 | 198 | | SQL query investigation | 39 | 4232 | 57201 | All three generated 512 tokens. Each mode was repeatable on its own in the recorded run; target-only versus DFlash matched on **0/3**. Returned token IDs, logprob arrays and usage counts were checked for alignment. There were **zero chosen-token/non-top1 violations** in these audited responses. Exact first-divergence indices can move if kernel/autotuning choices change. There is no crash or traceback to report: the symptom is a different token sequence. We do not have a new full DEBUG/TRACE_FUNCTION capture; the evidence below comes from targeted forward-operation captures and regression tests. ## What we isolated ### 1. Batch-shape-dependent normalization and GDN execution paths An actual forward trace found identical inputs/residuals at a native Gemma RMSNorm call but one differing BF16 output element out of 2,048 between the one-token and verification shapes. A fixed per-row reduction removed the discrepancy. After serial parity was established, concurrent DFlash requests still diverged. Another first-difference capture isolated GDN `RMSNormGated`: identical inputs, but its row-block choice changed with the number of rows. A captured critical BF16 row differs by `1.52587890625e-05`; twelve random-only probes had missed it. Fixing one row per reduction block removed that captured difference. The exact input fixture and regression test are included in the full patch posted in follow-up comments. The packed GDN decode and general speculative recurrence also used different Q/K normalization/reduction paths. Aligning `x / sqrt(sum(x*x)+eps)` with the other path's `x * rsqrt(sum(x*x)+eps)`, and aligning the reduction layout, made the corresponding direct-kernel parity tests pass. Additional fixed linear/FP8/MoE/attention choices were used in the local consistency mode. These are numerical-consistency measures, not proof that either floating-point formulation is intrinsically mathematically incorrect. ### 2. Independent mixed-batch gate-indexing defect In `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`, the ordinary/non-speculative QKV rows were gathered with `non_spec_token_indx`, but some decode-only mixed paths still consumed ungathered `a`/`b` gate rows. Gate selection was performed inside the prefill branch rather than consistently for the ordinary decode path. We gather `a_non_spec` and `b_non_spec` alongside `mixed_qkv_non_spec` and use those tensors in the ordinary decode recurrence. The CPU metadata/row-routing regression has four cases: **stock fails two and passes two; patched passes four**. This is distinct from #51812's already-merged alignment of the speculative rows. ### 3. Remaining high-load failure: prefill/recompute is not the same forward as decode After the earlier fixes, serial and concurrency-4 runs matched, but a 32-client run still matched only **41/50** sequences and incurred **12 preemptions**. This was an intermediate local build, not a claim about an isolated stock-only failure rate. We reproduced the remaining mechanism without concurrent load: take an already generated token prefix, submit it as a fresh prompt with a new cache salt, and generate one token. **5/9** selected replay probes disagreed with the original next token. For example, a 141-token translation prefix produced token 318 instead of the recorded token 466. A first-difference trace showed identical layer-0 input normalization and QKV/gate projections, but **1,448/4,096** core GDN output values differed before gated normalization. The prefill path used chunked FLA computation and normalized Q/K cast back to BF16; the incremental path used the general per-token recurrence with FP32 normalized Q/K. Recomputing previously decoded context therefore changed recurrent arithmetic and could flip a later greedy argmax. Preemption exposed this difference; we did not find evidence that the scheduler was changing the stored prefix token IDs. ## Local fix and validation Our patch adds an **opt-in local** `VLLM_SPECULATIVE_TOKEN_PARITY=1` mode. This flag is not an upstream option and is not a workaround available in an unmodified vLLM installation. We did not bypass `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`'s unsupported-GDN guard. In addition to the normalization, kernel-choice and gate-routing changes above: - Prefill/replay uses the same per-token GDN recurrence and convolution arithmetic as decode, retaining FP32 SSM states. - The recurrent helper supports a fresh/cached initial-state mask and final-state-only storage. Fresh contexts do not consume stale cache contents, and a one-dimensional final-state index is not treated as per-token speculative indices. - The convolution helper masks history for fresh contexts and only applies speculative history-length adjustment on the speculative path. - Both comparison arms use a common attention/Mamba block size of 1,152. This also removed a long-context boundary discrepancy in our tests. - Target and DFlash CUDA **decode** graphs are enabled (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`); prefill remains eager, with Torch compilation mode 0. Graphs alone were not the fix. The full patch posted in follow-up comments applies cleanly to the actual unmodified pinned image's Python files. Applying it reproduces all **22 runtime source files byte-for-byte** from our tested local image. It is a broad proof of concept, not a claim that all changes should become unconditional upstream defaults. The independent indexing correction and optional numerical-consistency work could be split for review. Results: - 49 common regression tests: stock **30 failed / 19 passed**, patched **49 passed**. Adding 40 recurrent/convolution replay regressions gives **89 passed** on the final patch. - **18/18 initial and 259/259 extended fresh-context replay probes** match, including selected 1,152-token block boundaries. - **50/50** fixed token sequences match between patched target-only and patched DFlash, and between the tested low/high-concurrency runs. - A 32-client DFlash run retained equality despite **18 preemptions**. Its observed active-request peak was 9, not 32. - With actual CUDA decode graphs: **50/50** still match; the 32-client DFlash run had 4 preemptions and observed active-request peak 7. - Concurrent shared-prefix tests: **8/8** long-context and **32/32** short-context sequences match. Actual prefix-cache hits were observed for the long-context test. These 50 sequences were capped at 4,096 generated tokens. Two tasks reached that cap; equality is established for the generated prefixes, not a claim that every task finished or answered correctly. Both cross-mode arms used the same patched arithmetic; equality to the old unpatched wording is not claimed. Stochastic sampling and BF16 SSM-state parity are outside this validation. ### Performance cost A separate controlled measurement used the same vLLM 0.31.0 base, model revision, GPU and serving configuration within each stock/patched pair, with CUDA decode graphs enabled. Each variant generated 18 serial responses of exactly 512 tokens after three excluded warmups: | Mode | Stock tokens/s | Patched tokens/s | Throughput change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Target-only | 103.59 | 90.17 | -12.95% | | DFlash2, 7 draft tokens | 204.22 | 159.16 | -22.07% | | MTP, 3 draft tokens | 176.62 | 132.31 | -25.09% | This measures the full local patch, not the isolated cost of one kernel fix. Output wording and draft acceptance can change when arithmetic is unified. The earlier original stock reproduction used its original FA2/default-backend settings; this controlled performance comparison fixed Triton attention/linear/MoE/GDN choices and decode-graph settings for each stock/patched pair. No AI quality judging or Transformers reference comparison was performed. The comparison here is between vLLM execution paths for the same target prefix, not an allegation of a Transformers implementation defect. ## Related issues and requested guidance - #54928: related DFlash2 greedy-divergence symptom. - #48271 and #58973: related shape-/dispatch-dependent RMSNorm behavior. - #48613: unsupported batch-invariant mode for GDN models. - #51812: speculative gate-row alignment, already merged; the ordinary-row defect above is a separate path. - #55524: conceptually related Mamba2 prefill/decode replay discussion; our traced model path is Qwen GDN. Could maintainers advise whether to split the ordinary gate-indexing regression into a focused bugfix and the GDN exact-replay/numerical-consistency path into an opt-in feature? The reproduction files below and patch comments provide the full patch, captured synthetic fixture, regression tests and frozen public prompts. The numerical observations above summarize the recorded results. No private endpoints, credentials, user chats or production deployment files are included. ## Reproduction files
serve-stock.sh ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Run INSIDE the pinned unmodified vLLM 0.31.0 image specified in the issue. # It loads one model server. Run target and dflash sequentially on the same GPU. set -euo pipefail export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 unset VLLM_SPECULATIVE_TOKEN_PARITY spec=() case "${1:-target}" in target) ;; dflash) spec=(--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash2","revision":"51ef7b6923ad6c14cb1bb41c37a9041446496ab6","num_speculative_tokens":7,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}') ;; *) echo 'Usage: bash serve-stock.sh target|dflash' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac exec vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 \ --revision 95a723d08a9490559dae23d0cff1d9466213d989 \ --dtype bfloat16 --quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \ --served-model-name target --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --max-model-len 65536 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.98 \ --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":0}' \ --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true,"preserve_thinking":true}' \ --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN --mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASH_ATTN \ --logprobs-mode raw_logprobs "${spec[@]}" ```

Start each server separately using serve-stock.sh, then: python3 reproduce.py record target.json python3 reproduce.py record dflash.json python3 reproduce.py compare target.json dflash.json The attached prompts.json contains synthetic prompts and their exact input IDs. """ import argparse import json from pathlib import Path import uuid import urllib.request def record(output, base_url, model): prompts = json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name('prompts.json').read_text()) results = [] for prompt in prompts: body = { 'model': model, 'prompt': prompt['tokens'], 'max_tokens': 512, 'temperature': 0, 'top_p': 1, 'top_k': -1, 'seed': 42, 'presence_penalty': 0, 'frequency_penalty': 0, 'repetition_penalty': 1, 'add_special_tokens': False, 'return_token_ids': True, 'return_tokens_as_token_ids': True, 'logprobs': 5, 'cache_salt': 'fresh-repro-' + uuid.uuid4().hex, } request = urllib.request.Request( base_url.rstrip('/') + '/v1/completions', data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, ) with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=300) as response: result = json.load(response) choice = result['choices'][0] ids, scores = choice['token_ids'], choice['logprobs'] assert len(ids) == result['usage']['completion_tokens'] assert len(ids) == len(scores['tokens']) == len(scores['token_logprobs']) == len(scores['top_logprobs']) violations = [] for index, (token_id, token, score, top) in enumerate(zip( ids, scores['tokens'], scores['token_logprobs'], scores['top_logprobs'])): assert token == 'token_id:' + str(token_id) if top and score is not None and score < max(top.values()) - 1e-6: violations.append(index) results.append({'case': prompt['case'], 'result': result, 'not_top1': violations}) print(prompt['case'], 'tokens:', len(ids), 'non-top1 positions:', violations) Path(output).write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n') def compare(first, second): a, b = [json.loads(Path(path).read_text()) for path in [first, second]] assert [r['case'] for r in a] == [r['case'] for r in b] for x, y in zip(a, b): ax, by = x['result']['choices'][0], y['result']['choices'][0] ids_a, ids_b = ax['token_ids'], by['token_ids'] position = next((i for i, (u, v) in enumerate(zip(ids_a, ids_b)) if u != v), None) if position is None and len(ids_a) != len(ids_b): position = min(len(ids_a), len(ids_b)) print(x['case'], 'exact:', ids_a == ids_b, 'first difference (0-based):', position) if position is not None and position < min(len(ids_a), len(ids_b)): print(' token IDs:', ids_a[position], ids_b[position]) print(' target top logprobs A:', ax['logprobs']['top_logprobs'][position]) print(' target top logprobs B:', by['logprobs']['top_logprobs'][position]) if __name__ == '__main__': parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__) sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', required=True) p = sub.add_parser('record') p.add_argument('output') p.add_argument('--base-url', default='http://127.0.0.1:8000') p.add_argument('--model', default='target') p = sub.add_parser('compare') p.add_argument('first') p.add_argument('second') args = parser.parse_args() if args.command == 'record': record(args.output, args.base_url, args.model) else: compare(args.first, args.second) ```

### 🐛 Describe the bug On gfx1151, `torch.ops._rocm_C.paged_attention` accepts two configurations and returns incorrect results without an error: - With `alibi_slopes` supplied, the output matches attention **without ALiBi**. - With `block_size=32`, the output differs substantially from the reference for sequence lengths starting at 17 in the tested sweep. The same comparison passes with `block_size=16`. The gfx1x backend selection in `use_rocm_custom_paged_attention()` already excludes both configurations: it requires `alibi_slopes is None` and `block_size == 16`. This report concerns direct calls to the op; the normal backend path does not select these configurations. Testing was limited to gfx1151. **Expected:** Either compute the requested attention correctly or reject the unsupported configuration with a clear error. #### Reproduction and observed results Save the script below as `F2_F5_repro_navi_contract.py` and run it with `python F2_F5_repro_navi_contract.py` in a ROCm-enabled vLLM environment on gfx1151. It requires only PyTorch and vLLM; no model, test helpers, or external data are needed. The script uses bf16, one sequence, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, and head size 128. For the block-size comparison, valid Q/K/V values are identical across block sizes and unused cache slots are zero. Errors are maximum absolute differences from the attention reference; `reference_scale` is the maximum absolute reference output. Actual output on `main` (`39e33db7f3`): ```text ALiBi: block_size=16, seq_len=32 error vs ALiBi=0.075806, vs no ALiBi=0.000061, reference scale=0.078613 Block size comparison (no ALiBi) seq_len error_bs16 error_bs32 reference_scale 15 0.000122 0.000122 0.050537 16 0.000000 0.000000 0.052490 17 0.000000 0.010010 0.051514 28 0.000000 0.029053 0.028320 32 0.000061 0.028259 0.029785 33 0.000122 0.021820 0.028198 64 0.000061 0.025238 0.021118 100 0.000061 0.014587 0.017334 ``` With ALiBi supplied, the kernel matches the no-ALiBi reference within rounding. With block size 32, the first failing length in this sweep is 17, still within the first 32-token block. Its errors are comparable to the output magnitude, while block size 16 matches within rounding.
Standalone reproduction script ```python """Run with: python F2_F5_repro_navi_contract.py (ROCm vLLM on gfx1151).""" import torch import vllm from vllm import _custom_ops as ops from vllm.platforms import current_platform assert current_platform.is_rocm() and torch.cuda.is_available() assert hasattr(torch.ops._rocm_C, "paged_attention") print(f"vLLM={vllm.__version__}, torch={torch.__version__}") print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)) def run(block_size, seq_len, use_alibi=False): torch.manual_seed(1) device, dtype = "cuda", torch.bfloat16 nq, nkv, hs = 32, 8, 128 scale = hs ** -0.5 blocks = (seq_len + block_size - 1) // block_size # Generate logical tokens first, then pack them into the op's cache layout. # This keeps valid Q/K/V identical across block sizes; padding is zero. q = torch.empty((1, nq, hs), device=device, dtype=dtype).uniform_(-scale, scale) k = torch.empty((seq_len, nkv, hs), device=device, dtype=dtype).uniform_(-scale, scale) v = torch.empty_like(k).uniform_(-scale, scale) x = 16 // q.element_size() kc = torch.zeros((blocks, nkv, hs // x, block_size, x), device=device, dtype=dtype) vc = torch.zeros((blocks, nkv, hs, block_size), device=device, dtype=dtype) for t in range(seq_len): kc[t // block_size, :, :, t % block_size, :] = k[t].reshape(nkv, hs // x, x) vc[t // block_size, :, :, t % block_size] = v[t] bt = torch.arange(blocks, device=device, dtype=torch.int32).view(1, -1) lens = torch.tensor([seq_len], device=device, dtype=torch.int32) slopes = torch.linspace(0.1, 1.0, nq, device=device) if use_alibi else None partitions = (seq_len + 255) // 256 tmp = torch.empty((1, nq, partitions, hs), device=device, dtype=dtype) sums = torch.empty((1, nq, partitions), device=device, dtype=torch.float32) maxima = torch.empty_like(sums) one = torch.tensor(1.0, device=device) out = torch.empty_like(q) ops.paged_attention_rocm( out, sums, maxima, tmp, q, kc, vc, nkv, scale, bt, lens, None, block_size, seq_len, slopes, "auto", one, one, ) # Same attention math as the upstream reference, with no test-module imports. keys = k.repeat_interleave(nq // nkv, dim=1) values = v.repeat_interleave(nq // nkv, dim=1) logits = torch.einsum("qhd,khd->hqk", q, keys).float() * scale def reference(alibi): scores = logits if alibi is not None: positions = torch.arange(seq_len, device=device) - seq_len + 1 scores = scores + alibi[:, None, None] * positions[None, None, :] weights = scores.softmax(dim=-1).to(dtype) return torch.einsum("hqk,khd->qhd", weights, values) ref = reference(slopes) err = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item() no_alibi_err = (out.float() - reference(None).float()).abs().max().item() return err, no_alibi_err, ref.abs().max().item() print("\nALiBi: block_size=16, seq_len=32") err, no_alibi_err, scale = run(16, 32, True) print(f"error vs ALiBi={err:.6f}, vs no ALiBi={no_alibi_err:.6f}, reference scale={scale:.6f}") print("\nBlock size comparison (no ALiBi)") print("seq_len error_bs16 error_bs32 reference_scale") for length in (15, 16, 17, 28, 32, 33, 64, 100): err16, _, scale = run(16, length) err32, _, _ = run(32, length) print(f"{length:7d} {err16:.6f} {err32:.6f} {scale:.6f}") ```
#### Relevant code and suggested fix In `csrc/rocm/attention.cu`, `CALL_CUSTOM_LAUNCHER` forwards `alibi_slopes` to `paged_attention_custom_launcher_navi`, but that launcher sets `alibi_slopes_ptr = nullptr`, with the comment `NOTE: Navi does not support alibi_slopes`. The Navi path also accepts block size 32. If these configurations are unsupported, add checks in the Navi launcher matching the backend's existing restrictions: ```cpp TORCH_CHECK(!alibi_slopes.has_value(), "paged_attention_rocm: alibi_slopes is not implemented for gfx11/gfx12"); TORCH_CHECK(BLOCK_SIZE == 16, "paged_attention_rocm: only block_size 16 is implemented for gfx11/gfx12"); ``` If block size 32 is intended to be supported, its numerical results need a fix instead. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Kernel][Model] Add manual CUDA RoPE KV-cache fusion for Llama
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Ports `RopeKVCacheFusionPass` to a manual fusion for Llama on CUDA, addressing #43503 as part of #43224. With `fuse_rope_kvcache=True`, `Attention` applies RoPE and writes K/V to the paged cache in one kernel before FlashAttention runs. ROCm keeps its compiler pass and AITER hooks.

## Claims

- The fused kernel is 1.6–1.7× faster than the unfused RoPE plus cache-write pair on H100, H200 and B200, and 1.5–1.6× on an RTX 5090 D, across MHA, GQA, MQA and all six FlashAttention cache layouts ([Sean, H200](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52363#issuecomment-5574017124); [Eliza, H100/B200](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52363#issuecomment-5603315281)).
- Outputs match the unfused path: identical GSM8K scores on H100 and B200 for TinyLlama and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic, and greedy logprob parity in the new engine test.
- End to end, TinyLlama BF16 at batch 1 on an RTX 5090 D was at parity at `d93c77f73` (unfused/fused median latency 1.006 over six interleaved rounds).
- CUDA support is opt-in; defaults are unchanged.

## Validation

At `5c1405ecb` on an RTX 5090 D (SM120), CUDA 13.2, PyTorch 2.14.0:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_fused_rope_kvcache.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_functional_rope_kvcache.py \
  tests/kernels/core/test_rotary_embedding.py \
  tests/compile/passes/test_rope_kvcache_fusion.py \
  tests/compile/passes/test_fusion_attn.py
pytest tests/compile/test_config.py -k rope_kvcache
compute-sanitizer --tool {memcheck,racecheck,synccheck} \
  pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_fused_rope_kvcache.py
```

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test_fused_rope_kvcache.py` (kernel against a reference, six cache layouts) | 13 passed |
| `test_functional_rope_kvcache.py` (layers, compiled graph, threshold, engine) | 12 passed |
| `test_rotary_embedding.py` | 197 passed |
| `test_rope_kvcache_fusion.py`, `test_fusion_attn.py` | 26 passed, 170 skipped (ROCm/AITER or SM100 only) |
| `test_config.py -k rope_kvcache` | 4 passed |
| compute-sanitizer memcheck / racecheck / synccheck | 0 errors / 0 hazards / 0 errors |

`benchmark_fused_rope_kvcache.py --cases mha gqa mqa padded-gqa --dtype bfloat16 --head-size 128` on the same GPU: 3.90 µs fused against 6.04 µs unfused (median over the 24 case/layout rows), 1.53–1.59× per row.

`test_llama_fused_rope_matches_unfused` runs TinyLlama through `vllm_runner` with fusion off and on, under Model Runner V2's default FULL and PIECEWISE CUDA graphs and under `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`, and compares greedy logprobs. The layer tests compare outputs and cache contents with the unfused path, check the compiled graph, and use the profiler to confirm which kernel ran on each side of the token threshold.

## Details

Llama passes `positions` and its rotary module to `Attention`. The rotary module describes its rotation with `get_rotation()` (positions, a `[cos | sin]` table and the NeoX flag), and `Attention` decides between the fused op and the ordinary rotary call; this follows [Lucas's proposal](https://github.com/Utopia-V/vllm/pull/1). Rotary modules without a plain per-token cos/sin rotation (Fourier, MRoPE, LongRoPE, the FlashInfer path) have no description and keep their forward.

The fused op writes rotated Q into a graph-owned buffer and K/V into the cache, then attention runs with `key=None, value=None`. A layer fuses only if its backend sets main's `supports_kv_cache_update_bypass` and its implementation provides the fused writer; today that is FlashAttention on CUDA for decoder layers with FP16/BF16 activations and a cache of the same dtype, no KV sharing, no decode context parallelism and no `fuse_attn_quant`. Other backends keep the unfused path, with a one-time warning when the flag is set.

Fusion covers batches of up to `rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num` tokens (256). vLLM drops Dynamo shape guards, so a compiled graph always calls the fused op and the op checks the token count at run time; above the threshold it copies Q, clones K and runs the unfused kernels. Eager calls make the same choice before the op.

Related work: #43355 (pass-based, closed in favor of this PR); #57271 (enables the compiler pass on CUDA with a Triton cache writer for `TRITON_ATTN`, BF16 GQA; it changes the same `PassConfig` platform check); #58838 (moves base RoPE to a vLLM IR op and touches the same files).

items.title: [Fusion][Perf] Extend QuantizedActivation contract with get_input_quant_scale and maybe_fused_norm_quant
items.body:
## Overview

Extends the `QuantizedActivation` linear-kernel contract (`#44260`, `#51415`, `#53793`, `#55643`, `#59612`) with `get_input_quant_scale(layer)` (resolving `TODO(mgoin)` in `quant_activation.py` and `fused_act_quant.py`) and introduces `maybe_fused_norm_quant` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fusion/fused_norm_quant.py`) to fuse `RMSNorm` / `FusedAddRMSNorm` + input quantization across `input_layernorm -> qkv_proj` and `post_attention_layernorm -> gate_up_proj`.

## Claims

- **Resolves `TODO(mgoin)` via `get_input_quant_scale(layer)`:** Producers (`fused_act_quant.py`, `relu2_fp8_quant.py`, `fused_norm_quant.py`) retrieve static FP8 (`input_scale`) and dynamic NVFP4 (`input_global_scale_inv`) scales through the contract rather than reaching into kernel-specific attributes on `LinearBase`. Automatically returns `None` when `requires_unquantized_input=True` (e.g., active LoRA adapters).
- **Introduces `maybe_fused_norm_quant` with Asymmetric Residual Preservation:** Updates `residual` in-place in full precision (`BF16`/`FP16`) while returning a pre-quantized `QuantizedActivation` (`kFp8StaticTensorSym`, `kFp8DynamicTokenSym`, `kFp8Dynamic128Sym`, `kFp8Dynamic64Sym`, `kNvfp4Dynamic`) to the consumer linear layer with **zero consumer-side changes**.
- **1.68x–2.97x Boundary Speedup on NVIDIA H100:** Eliminates the intermediate `BF16` HBM write + read between `RMSNorm` and quantization (saving up to 64 MB of HBM traffic per call at `M=4096, d=4096`), working in both eager mode and across `torch.compile` graph breaks for arbitrary `rms_norm_eps`.

## Validation

### 1. H100 GPU Micro-Benchmark (`d = 4096`, Single Boundary)

Measured on **NVIDIA H100** comparing the unfused two-kernel boundary (`Add + RMSNorm` materializing `BF16` in HBM -> separate `FP8` quantization kernel) against `maybe_fused_norm_quant` (`Add + RMSNorm + FP8 Quant` in a single kernel keeping normalized activations in registers/SRAM while preserving the `BF16` residual stream):

| Tokens (`M`) | Quantization Scheme | Unfused Boundary (`us`) | Fused Contract (`us`) | Speedup | Intermediate HBM Traffic Saved / Call |
| ---: | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **1** | `kFp8StaticTensorSym` | `147.06 us` | **`87.59 us`** | **1.68x** | `16.0 KB` |
| **1** | `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` | `106.52 us` | **`62.35 us`** | **1.71x** | `16.0 KB` |
| **8** | `kFp8StaticTensorSym` | `151.56 us` | **`78.64 us`** | **1.93x** | `128.0 KB` |
| **8** | `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` | `159.19 us` | **`78.01 us`** | **2.04x** | `128.0 KB` |
| **32** | `kFp8StaticTensorSym` | `128.20 us` | **`75.98 us`** | **1.69x** | `512.0 KB` |
| **32** | `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` | `182.66 us` | **`61.50 us`** | **2.97x** | `512.0 KB` |
| **128** | `kFp8StaticTensorSym` | `179.02 us` | **`75.01 us`** | **2.39x** | `2.0 MB` |
| **128** | `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` | `169.19 us` | **`91.26 us`** | **1.85x** | `2.0 MB` |
| **512** | `kFp8StaticTensorSym` | `181.23 us` | **`91.55 us`** | **1.98x** | `8.0 MB` |
| **512** | `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` | `105.35 us` | **`55.50 us`** | **1.90x** | `8.0 MB` |
| **2048** | `kFp8StaticTensorSym` | `188.97 us` | **`110.31 us`** | **1.71x** | `32.0 MB` |
| **2048** | `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` | `195.87 us` | **`112.42 us`** | **1.74x** | `32.0 MB` |
| **4096** | `kFp8StaticTensorSym` | `222.98 us` | **`128.29 us`** | **1.74x** | `64.0 MB` |
| **4096** | `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` | `251.44 us` | **`147.39 us`** | **1.71x** | `64.0 MB` |

### 2. Reproduction Commands

```bash
pytest -v tests/fusion/test_quant_activation_contract.py
pytest -v tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py
pytest -v tests/compile/passes/test_rms_norm_quant_manual_fusion.py
python3 benchmarks/fused_kernels/layernorm_rms_benchmarks.py
```

## Details

1. **Asymmetric Residual Stream vs. Quantized Branch (`maybe_fused_norm_quant`):**
   At `post_attention_layernorm` (and `input_layernorm` for layers `l >= 1`), the normalization kernel computes `residual = x + residual` in `BF16`/`FP16` and writes that unquantized sum back to `residual` in-place, while quantizing the normalized activation in registers directly to `FP8` / packed `NVFP4` (`QuantizedActivation`). Because `QKVParallelLinear` and `MergedColumnParallelLinear` inherit from `ColumnParallelLinear` and dispatch through `FP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` / `NvFp4LinearKernel` (which already unwrap `QuantizedActivation` via `as_quantized_activation`), no consumer changes are needed.
2. **Eager Mode, Graph Breaks, & Arbitrary `rms_norm_eps`:**
   Unlike `RMSNormQuantFusionPass` (`rms_quant_fusion.py`), which registers 76 separate FX pattern-matcher rules hardcoded to `for epsilon in [1e-5, 1e-6]`, `maybe_fused_norm_quant` passes `norm_fn.variance_epsilon` directly and works in eager mode, across graph breaks, and for any model epsilon (e.g. `1e-4`).
3. **Tradeoffs & Cooperation with LoRA and `AllReduceRMSNormFusionPass`:**
   - **LoRA:** When LoRA wraps `qkv_proj` or `gate_up_proj`, `requires_unquantized_input=True` causes `get_input_quant_key(linear)` to return `None`, falling back cleanly to unfused `norm_fn(x, residual)` so the LoRA branch receives `BF16`/`FP16` activations.
   - **Multi-GPU Tensor Parallelism (`TP > 1`):** When `residual is not None`, `TP > 1`, and compiler `fuse_allreduce_rms=True` is enabled, `_should_defer_to_allreduce_rms_fusion` yields to `AllReduceRMSNormFusionPass` so 3-way FlashInfer collective fusion (`AllReduce + Add + RMSNorm + Quant`) is not preempted.
   - **Zero Host-Device Sync:** No CPU/GPU synchronization or host tensor reads are introduced on the forward path.

items.title: [ROCm][AITER] Fix fused QK-norm+RoPE+cache abort by allocating K/V as separate head groups
items.body:
## Purpose

The AITER fused QK-norm+RoPE+cache kernel addresses each side as
`block_id * stride(0) + token * (H*hs) + head * hs` and hard-asserts that each side is
contiguous *within a block*. Both AITER attention backends allocate a **packed** content
dim, `(num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2*head_size)`. Splitting that
(`transpose(1, 2).split(head_size, -1)`) leaves the head dim strided by the whole block, so
the assert fires and **aborts the process**:

```
[AITER] .../csrc/kernels/fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.cu:2952
        k_cache/v_cache must be contiguous within a block (dims >= 1)
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

Before this PR, *every* case in `test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py` dies this
way (SIGABRT, exit 134) — for both `ROCM_AITER_FA` and `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`. Reduced
to the two layouts, with `num_kv_heads=2, head_size=128, block_size=16`:

| layout | k/v side stride | kernel |
|---|---|---|
| packed split | `(8192, 256, **4096**, 1)` — head stride ≠ `hs` | **abort** |
| separate head groups | `(8192, 256, **128**, 1)` | accepted |

## Fix

Allocate K and V as separate head groups — `(num_blocks, 2, block_size,
num_kv_heads*head_size)` — so each side is one contiguous token-major region per block,
exactly the kernel's contract.

- The **shuffle** layout keeps the packed content dim: it has its own x-packed interior and
  a dedicated write path, and already gates this fusion off.
- `fused_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_supported()` now returns the allocation flag rather than
  re-deriving the predicate, so the gate cannot drift from the layout it depends on.
- `RocmAttentionBackend`'s shape is untouched — `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` overrides
  `get_kv_cache_shape` itself, so ROCM_ATTN's prefix-prefill layout is unaffected.

### KV-offloading connector

`canonical_mapping.py` identifies layouts by sniffing the cache shape. At
`num_kv_heads == 2` the new shape **and its strides** are byte-identical to the packed form,
so the layout is unknowable from the tensor alone. This fails closed there (opaque
whole-page fallback) instead of emitting a wrong mapping, and maps it properly when the
shape is unambiguous. `slice_for_tp_transfer` in the KV-layout RFC will carry layout
identity and remove the guess.

## Test Plan / Result

All on MI300X (gfx942), `amd-aiter` 0.1.16.post2.

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py` | **SIGABRT on case 1** | **1440 passed**, 1440 skipped |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_kv_geometry.py` (new) | — | 4 passed |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/` | 244 passed | 244 passed (+2 new) |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_kv_block_zeroer.py`, `test_kv_head_stride_canonicalization.py` | 15 passed | 15 passed |

The fusion test already asserts `fusion_pass.matched_count == 1` and compares fused vs
unfused q/k/v **and** the KV cache, so these 1440 cases verify the fused kernel both runs
and is numerically correct on the new layout.

E2e (Qwen3-0.6B, greedy + long multi-block prompts): `ROCM_AITER_FA`,
`ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, and AITER-off all produce coherent
output. Since the fusion pattern does not match Qwen3, these exercise the **unfused**
`reshape_and_cache` write path against the new layout.

### Model evaluation — GSM8K, 5-shot, full 1319 questions

Both arms `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA`; baseline is a
detached worktree at `640a09086d`, so this isolates the layout.

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| packed (base) | 0.3844 ± 0.0134 | 0.3950 ± 0.0135 |
| separate head groups (this PR) | 0.3844 ± 0.0134 | 0.3950 ± 0.0135 |

Identical, as expected for a pure data-placement change under greedy decoding.

### Throughput

`bench throughput`, in256/out512, 64 prompts, 3 alternating reps on one GPU:
separate head groups **8553 ± 129** vs packed **8620 ± 37** output tok/s — a 0.8% mean gap,
smaller than the run-to-run spread. Neutral.

## Notes

- **Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs for `aiter qk_norm rope kvcache fusion`,
  `get_kv_cache_shape aiter`, `rocm_aiter_fa`. The nearest are #41222 (enables shuffled
  rope + KV-cache fusion — the *shuffle* path, which this PR deliberately leaves packed),
  #45144 (MTP + fp8 + shuffle-KV config) and #46597 (backend *priority*). None touch the
  contiguity contract or the non-shuffle allocation.
- **Pre-existing bug found, not fixed here:** with
  `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1` the AITER FA path emits garbage tokens. Verified on
  `640a09086d` with these changes stashed, so it is independent of this PR and left alone.
- **AI assistance was used** for this change (investigation, implementation, and the test
  runs above).

items.title: [Perf][Beam] Fuse FP8 KV-cache insertion and query quantization into QK-norm/RoPE
items.body:
## Overview This PR fuses FP8 KV cache writes and query quantization into Beam's QK-norm/RoPE kernel, replacing three separate kernels (QK-norm/RoPE, `scaled_fp8_quant` on Q, and `reshape_and_cache_flash`) with one for both the target model and DFlash2 drafter. **Duplicates**: No open PR does this. #63510 keeps the BF16-only insert. #57682, #38621 and #59035 are compile-time fusion passes for models built from vLLM’s standard norm/RoPE/cache ops, which Beam’s custom kernel doesn’t go through. **AI assistance**: Claude is used throughout development, and I reviewed every line of code. ## Claims - Decode step time drops on `Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4` with an FP8 KV cache: - TP4 + DFlash2: 3.8% at concurrency 1, 1.6% at concurrency 64. - TP4 w/o spec decode: 5.5% at concurrency 1, 2.4% at concurrency 64. - Outputs are numerically identical: - The fused kernel writes the same FP8 bytes as the separate quant and cache-insert kernels it replaces. - Greedy outputs are token-identical to main. - GSM8K and the spec-decode acceptance length are unchanged. ## Validation All runs on B200s, comparing main with this PR. - **Unit tests:** `pytest tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py tests/models/test_beam_construction.py` passed. The kernel tests capture the fused call in a CUDA graph and require FP8 Q and the whole cache to match `scaled_fp8_quant` and `reshape_and_cache_flash` byte-wise, including NaN and inf/-inf. - **Correctness (TP4):** - Greedy outputs on 16 prompts are token-identical to main with an FP8 cache, a BF16 cache, and `--enforce-eager`. - GSM8K 5-shot (vLLM's `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions) goes from 0.939 to 0.937 (± 0.007), and the acceptance length from 5.50 to 5.50. - **Sync and JIT checks:** with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, an eager FP8 + DFlash2 server ran with no syncs. - **Performance:** Median ITL from `vllm bench serve` (ISL=8192 / OSL=512, 1024 prompts per concurrency, `--max-concurrency c`) reduces comparing to `main` (w/o fusion). With spec decode, acceptance is fixed to 3.0 so both builds do the same work per step. | Concurrency (c) | TP4 + DFlash2 | TP4 w/o spec-decode | |---:|---:|---:| | 1 | −3.8% | −5.5% | | 4 | −2.9% | −4.7% | | 16 | −1.1% | −3.4% | | 32 | −1.4% | −3.1% | | 64 | −1.6% | −2.4% |
Full numbers and commands Each cell is one run of 1024 prompts. Throughput is output tokens/s per GPU. - TP4 + DFlash2: | c | main median ITL (ms) | PR (ms) | Δ | main tok/s/GPU | PR | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.275 | 6.037 | −3.8% | 106.3 | 110.0 | +3.5% | | 4 | 9.123 | 8.858 | −2.9% | 260.9 | 267.7 | +2.6% | | 16 | 13.425 | 13.281 | −1.1% | 543.0 | 549.5 | +1.2% | | 32 | 16.451 | 16.229 | −1.4% | 719.2 | 728.2 | +1.2% | | 64 | 20.327 | 20.001 | −1.6% | 891.5 | 903.2 | +1.3% | - TP4 w/o spec-decode: | c | main median ITL (ms) | PR (ms) | Δ | main tok/s/GPU | PR | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 3.842 | 3.629 | −5.5% | 61.1 | 64.5 | +5.5% | | 4 | 4.599 | 4.381 | −4.7% | 186.4 | 194.9 | +4.5% | | 16 | 6.252 | 6.039 | −3.4% | 440.0 | 452.5 | +2.8% | | 32 | 7.895 | 7.650 | −3.1% | 595.9 | 609.7 | +2.3% | | 64 | 9.715 | 9.484 | −2.4% | 772.9 | 786.8 | +1.8% | Prefill (TP4 + DFlash2, 64 uncached 8192-token prompts) moves from 86.3k to 87.4k input tok/s (+1.2%, p = 0.07), which is within noise. **Commands**: ``` vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser beam --reasoning-parser beam \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}' vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0 \ --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --num-prompts 1024 --max-concurrency $c --seed $((1001 + 100 * c)) \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 ```
## Details - **Kernel**: New `constexpr` flags (`FP8_Q`, `FP8_KV`) add FP8 stores; the BF16 path is unchanged. To match the replaced ops byte for byte: - K is rounded to BF16 first, as main stores it before the cache insert. - K/V use `div_rn(x, scale)`, then a NaN-preserving clamp to 448/-448. - Q uses `x * div_rn(1, q_scale)` with `scaled_fp8_quant`'s clamp order. - Scales are read on device, so CUDA graphs need no host sync. - **When it fuses**: A BF16 cache, or an `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3` cache with per-tensor scales. Per-head scales and `fp8_e5m2` keep the existing path. Backend checks are unchanged. ---
