items.title: [Bug]: TurboQuant `_continuation_prefill` OOMs and kills engine at long-context prefill (~185K actual tokens)
items.body:
### Summary

On the open hybrid-TurboQuant stack (umbrella PR #39931), a single chat-completion request whose tokenized prompt exceeds ~185K tokens reliably kills the entire vLLM engine (CUDA OOM in the prefill path), not just the individual request. The server has to be restarted. This is well below the `--max-model-len=262144` the model advertises and KV cache reports as provisioned.

### Environment

- GPU: RTX 5090 (sm_120, 32 GiB)
- Model: `cyankiwi/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit`
- `--kv-cache-dtype=turboquant_4bit_nc --max-model-len=262144 --max-num-seqs=16 --gpu-memory-utilization=0.87`
- GPU KV cache size reported at startup: 548,864 tokens · 2.00x concurrency at 256K
- Base image: `vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly` + PR #39931 + the 6 open follow-up PRs I've been tracking (LCM page-size #40128, GDN dual-stream #39748, FA3/4 passthrough #40092, FLA TMA gate #37700, hybrid kv-token capacity #40384, triton decode OOB clamp #40074).

### Reproducer

1. Start the stack with `--kv-cache-dtype=turboquant_4bit_nc --max-model-len=262144 --gpu-memory-utilization=0.87`.
2. Send one chat completion whose tokenized prompt is between ~185K and 262K tokens (e.g. a long NIAH-style haystack).

OOM-probe boundary:

| target tokens (haystack) | actual prompt tokens | result |
|--------------------------|---------------------|--------|
| 200,000 | 160,083 | PASS |
| 215,000 | 172,080 | PASS |
| 230,000 | 184,079 | PASS |
| 245,000 | ~196,000 | **CRASH (engine dies)** |

Short-context (up to ~154K actual), stress_32k, and 5-way concurrent story generation all pass clean on the same config — this is purely a long-prefill path issue.

### Stack (reproduced twice, identical)

```
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/turboquant_attn.py", line 619, in _prefill_attention
    out = self._continuation_prefill(...)
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/turboquant_attn.py", line 729, in _continuation_prefill
    v_full = torch.cat([v_cached_trim.to(qdtype), val_chunk], dim=0)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 184.00 MiB.
  GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.36 GiB of which 169.75 MiB is free.
```

### Root cause

`_continuation_prefill` has two redundant peak-memory materializations at long context:

1. **FP32 intermediate for the inverse Hadamard rotation of MSE keys.** `k_cached[0, :, :cached_len, :].reshape(-1, D).float() @ Pi` allocates a `cached_len*Hk*D*4 B` FP32 tensor, then the `.to(torch.float16)` cast allocates another FP16 copy. This FP32 widening serves no purpose — the keys were reconstructed from 3-4 bit MSE indices, so FP16 roundoff on the rotation is orders of magnitude below the quantization noise already in the cache.
2. **Redundant `.contiguous()` on transposed K/V views before `torch.cat`.** `torch.cat` always produces a contiguous output regardless of input contiguity, so the upstream `.contiguous()` calls doubled the transient footprint for no reason.

Together these spikes exceed the remaining activation headroom on a 32 GiB card once `cached_len` approaches ~190K.

### Severity

**Engine-wide, not request-scoped.** The engine dies with `EngineDeadError` / `EngineCore encountered an issue`, the API surface returns 500 for subsequent calls, and the container needs a restart. Any public-facing deployment built on this stack is one long-prompt-per-session away from an outage.

Effective usable `max-model-len` on 32 GiB is ~230K target (~185K actual) — not the 256K the config advertises.

### Fix

PR against JartX/vllm#feature-hybrid-turboquant (cross-fork): surgical two-change fix in `_continuation_prefill` — rotate in FP16, drop redundant `.contiguous()`. Verified to push the ceiling from ~196K actual to at least 208K actual tokens (260K target), covering the full `max-model-len`. NIAH retrieval accuracy unchanged. Will link here once opened.

items.title: [Bug]: gfx1100 (RDNA3): first-call non-determinism + long-seq corruption from Triton paged-attention fallback (ROCm 7.14)
items.body:
> **TL;DR** — On **gfx1100/RDNA3**, vLLM 0.25.1's **Triton paged-attention fallback** is (A) **non-deterministic on the first `generate()` call of a process** (at *any* sequence length — not a long-seq threshold) and (B) **garbled at long context**. The ROCm CK custom paged kernel is gated out because the model's decoder is GQA with **`gqa_ratio=2`** (CK requires `≥3`), forcing the Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d`. A warmup call fixes (A) but not (B); **transformers `sdpa` is deterministic + correct on the same stack**. Full repro (3 scripts + build note + expected outputs): https://gist.github.com/AIwork4me/030fc6a872de36197178c9e8217949d1 ### Your current environment
The output of collect_env.py (trimmed) ```text OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) PyTorch version : 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : 7.14.60850 Python version : 3.12.3 Is CUDA available : True GPU models and configuration : 4x AMD Radeon Pro W7900D (gfx1100, RDNA3) HIP runtime version : 7.14.60850 MIOpen runtime version : 3.5.2 [pip3] torch==2.11.0+rocm7.14.0 [pip3] transformers==5.13.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1+git0263a6a6.rocm7.14.0 vLLM Version : 0.25.1 (built from source, PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1100) ```
Note: vLLM 0.25.1 is **built from source** on ROCm 7.14 (no official gfx1100 wheel at this version), and the hardware is **RDNA3 (gfx1100)**. Reproducing requires gfx1100/RDNA3; **gfx1100 (Radeon Pro W7900) cloud instances** are available from AMD-Radeon GPU providers such as [Radeon Cloud](https://radeon-global.anruicloud.com/) (no affiliation — linked only to lower the hardware barrier, not an endorsement). Build caveat: the implicated `kernel_paged_attention_2d` is a pure-Triton kernel JIT-compiled at runtime, but in this env vLLM's pre-compiled HIP kernels were built against 7.2.1 system headers and run on the 7.14 torch — if a cleanly-7.14-built vLLM does not reproduce, that mismatch is the first thing to rule out (details in the gist README). See the scope question at the end. ### 🐛 Describe the bug On **gfx1100 (RDNA3, Radeon Pro W7900D)**, vLLM 0.25.1 serving a VLM (`tencent/HunyuanOCR`, `HunYuanVLForConditionalGeneration`) shows **two distinct problems**, both rooted in the ROCm paged-attention **Triton fallback** that vLLM selects on gfx1100 (the CK custom paged kernel is gated out — see root-cause trail): **Symptom A — first-call non-determinism (not length-gated).** The **first** `generate()` call in a process produces different output from subsequent identical calls. With greedy decoding, three identical (image, prompt) runs give `sha8 = ba29b5a1, fd0cc624, fd0cc624` — run 0 (the cold/JIT-compiled first call) diverges, runs 1 & 2 are identical. This reproduces at **both** ~15k vision tokens (2048×1920 page) **and** ~3.8k tokens (1024×960 page) — i.e. it is **not** a long-sequence-threshold effect. A single warmup `generate()` before the measured runs eliminates it: after warmup, three identical runs are byte-identical (`sha8 = fd0cc624, fd0cc624, fd0cc624`). **Symptom B — incorrect (garbled) output at long sequence, even when deterministic.** At full resolution (~15k vision tokens), the warmed/deterministic vLLM output is garbled OCR (`lial Oswuamtntnralglyy Flinamie …`) and does **not** contain the ground-truth text, whereas **transformers** with `attn_implementation="sdpa"` on the **same** ROCm 7.14 / gfx1100 / torch 2.11 stack, on the **same** image, is deterministic **and correct** (GT title present). So the ROCm stack *can* do correct long-sequence bf16 attention for this model; vLLM's path cannot. #### Minimal repro ```python from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams # 2048x1920 page = 15360 ViT patches (long-seq case). Use 1024x960 = 3840 for the short-seq case. W, H = 2048, 1920 im = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), "white"); d = ImageDraw.Draw(im) f = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf", 96) d.text((120, 120), "Quarterly Financial Summary", font=f, fill="black") im.save("/tmp/page.png") PROMPT = ("提取文档图片中正文的所有信息用markdown格式表示，其中页眉、页脚部分忽略，" "表格用html格式表达，文档中公式用latex格式表示，按照阅读顺序组织进行解析。") llm = LLM(model="tencent/HunyuanOCR", dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=32768, gpu_memory_utilization=0.90, enforce_eager=True, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1}, trust_remote_code=True) sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=-1, max_tokens=1024, repetition_penalty=1.08) prompt = llm.get_tokenizer().apply_chat_template( [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image"}, {"type": "text", "text": PROMPT}]}], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) img = Image.open("/tmp/page.png").convert("RGB") for i in range(3): # Symptom A: run 0 differs from runs 1 & 2 print(i, llm.generate({"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"image": img}}, sampling_params=sp, use_tqdm=False)[0].outputs[0].text[:80]) ``` Observed (3× identical input, full-res): ```text sha8 = ba29b5a1, fd0cc624, fd0cc624 # run 0 != run 1 == run 2 byte-identical: False GT title present in any run: False # garbled even on the deterministic (warmed) runs ``` #### Evidence summary | experiment (greedy ×3 identical input) | sha8 | deterministic? | correct? | |---|---|---|---| | full-res (15360 tok), no warmup | `ba29b5a1, fd0cc624, fd0cc624` | ❌ no (symptom A) | ❌ garbled (symptom B) | | short-seq (3840 tok), no warmup | `f00c87f2, f31888d4, f31888d4` | ❌ no (symptom A is not length-gated) | (image too small to judge) | | full-res (15360 tok), 1 warmup then ×3 | `fd0cc624, fd0cc624, fd0cc624` | ✅ yes (warmup fixes A) | ❌ still garbled (B remains) | | transformers `sdpa`, full-res | `a313e63a ×3` | ✅ yes | ✅ correct | #### Root-cause trail (what I verified) 1. **It is not the vision encoder.** Forcing the ViT/mm-encoder backend to `TORCH_SDPA` (which routes through `F.scaled_dot_product_attention`, via `mm_encoder_attn_backend="TORCH_SDPA"`) changed the output **zero** — byte-identical to the default `FLASH_ATTN` (Triton) ViT path (same sha8s). So the ViT is deterministic in both backends and is not the source. By elimination the divergent path is the **decoder**. 2. **The decoder runs through vLLM's standard paged-attention path.** `HunYuanVLForConditionalGeneration` (`vllm/model_executor/models/hunyuan_vision.py`) uses a HunYuan V1 language backbone (`hunyuan_v1.py: HunYuanAttention`), which builds a **standard `Attention`** (head_dim=128, num_kv_heads=8 → **gqa_ratio=2**), not `MLAAttention`. 3. **The ROCm CK custom paged-attention kernel is gated out**, so vLLM uses the Triton kernel. On gfx1100, `use_rocm_custom_paged_attention()` (`vllm/platforms/rocm.py`) requires `gqa_ratio∈[3,16]`; **gqa_ratio=2 fails**, so the CK kernel is disabled and vLLM falls back to **Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d`** (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py`). The run logs confirm both: ``` WARNING [chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:419] Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation. WARNING [jit_monitor.py:129] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: kernel_paged_attention_2d. ... consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config. ``` Symptom A (first-call non-determinism) lines up with that kernel being JIT-compiled on first use (hence warmup eliminates it). Symptom B (long-seq corruption) lines up with that Triton kernel not matching the (correct) torch-SDPA numerics at long bf16 sequences on gfx1100. #### Ask 1. **First-call determinism (symptom A):** vLLM's own `jit_monitor` says to "extend warmup to cover this shape/config." Can engine warmup be extended to cover the paged-attention decode shape so the **first** real request is deterministic (not just the second onward)? 2. **Long-seq correctness (symptom B):** can the Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d` numerics on gfx1100 be made to match torch-SDPA at long bf16 sequences — or can the **CK custom paged kernel** be extended to `gqa_ratio=2` (and the HunYuan V1 GQA config) so RDNA3 uses the deterministic CK path instead of the Triton fallback? 3. **Scope:** gfx1100/RDNA3 is a consumer GPU. Is paged-attention determinism/correctness on RDNA3 within vLLM's ROCm support scope (which I understand to be CDNA/MI-series focused)? If RDNA3 is community-supported only, happy to move/dupe this to the right place. Happy to attach the rendered page image, raw token ids, or full run logs on request. Thanks! > Note: vLLM 0.25.1 is not a HunyuanOCR-model-card-listed vLLM version (card lists 0.18.1 / nightly / 0.13). I'm reporting because the failure looks like a platform/kernel-architecture issue (gfx1100 paged-attention), not a model-compat one.

items.title: [RFC]: NixlConnector: convert standard KV pages to ROCm AITER shuffled pages on the decode side
items.body:
### Motivation.

**TL;DR**

- On ROCm, AITER's shuffled KV pages give the fastest decode at high batch. Prefill doesn't benefit from them, and a different backend is the fastest for prefill.
- P/D disaggregation could give each side its best format, but NixlConnector requires both sides to use the same format.
- I propose letting a ROCm decoder accept standard pages and convert them to shuffled pages after the transfer.
- Decisions I'm asking for now:
  - whether the connector should compare a page-format tag and call a converter owned by the backend;
  - whether prefill and decode may use different backends once their page formats are negotiated;
  - whether a conversion on the decoder's step path is acceptable.
- The measurement that decides whether to merge the conversion comes after this discussion (see the go/no-go plan).

**Depends on #59110** (bug: NixlConnector can't see the KV page format). That issue's two fixes are:

- a per-region page-format tag in `NixlAgentMetadata`;
- splitting the K and V slots separately in NIXL descriptors.

**Background.** With `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1` (#29887), `ROCM_AITER_FA` writes each block's K as `[H, D/x, N, x]` and its V as `[H, N/x, D, x]`, where `x = 16 // element_size`. AITER's asm and gluon decode kernels read this format. The other backends write standard pages, where each head's tokens hold K and V side by side (`[H, N, 2*D]`). These are CUDA FlashAttention, unshuffled `ROCM_AITER_FA` and `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`. Neither kernel family reads the other's pages.

**Decode: shuffled pages win at high batch.** I timed full decode steps on one MI300X (Qwen3-8B, BF16, TP 1, 16-token pages). The shuffled arm used the non-gluon asm/ll4mi path, with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`. Each cell is the shuffled speedup over `ROCM_AITER_FA`, the backend ROCm selects by default with a KV connector. The number in parentheses is the speedup over the fastest unshuffled backend at that shape (`TRITON_ATTN`, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` or `ROCM_AITER_FA`):

| context \ batch | 1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1k | +2.6% (+0.2%) | +4.3% (+0.8%) | +5.7% (+5.7%) | +6.0% (+6.0%) | +9.2% (+3.6%) |
| 4k | +3.3% (−0.5%) | +2.5% (+2.5%) | +5.3% (+3.2%) | +5.5% (+2.3%) | +7.7% (−1.5%) |
| 16k | +2.4% (+1.2%) | +1.4% (−0.4%) | +10.2% (+5.1%) | – | – |
| 32k | +3.7% (+1.3%) | +1.2% (−2.0%) | – | – | – |

A dash marks a shape that exceeded the harness's 95% KV-capacity margin. Each configuration ran once, so treat gaps under about 2% as ties.

- **Against `ROCM_AITER_FA`,** the gain rises with batch once AITER's asm decode kernel takes over. For Qwen3-8B on MI300X that happens above batch 19, when batch × query heads exceeds twice the CU count.
- **Against the fastest unshuffled backend,** shuffled pages are 2.3–6.0% faster at 6 of 7 shapes with batch ≥ 32. At batch 128 the margin narrows to +3.6% at 1k and −1.5% at 4k.
- **Across all 15 shapes,** the median gain over the fastest unshuffled backend is +1.3%.

Kernel-level evidence comes from profiler traces at batch 64 and 8k context. There, shuffled (asm) attention took 10.6% less time than `ROCM_AITER_FA`'s ll4mi kernel and 4.4% less than AITER unified, measured as time reduction over 12 steps. Below the asm threshold there is no consistent attention gain.

Qwen3-32B's shuffled decode ran on the gluon path (128-token pages). There it was roughly a wash: a median of −0.6% against the fastest unshuffled backend, ranging from −2.3% to +3.8% at batch ≥ 32. #54805 (open) would remove gluon until a follow-up restores it.

Separately, #29887 reported +19.4% output throughput (+26.5% TPOT) against unshuffled `ROCM_AITER_FA` for Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8. That was on MI308 with TP 2 + EP, in a colocated benchmark at concurrency 200 with about 3.8k input and 1k output tokens. MI308 has fewer CUs, so asm engages at a smaller batch, and a small-active-parameter MoE spends more of each step in attention. Either may explain part of the difference, but I haven't measured it.

My hypothesis is that the gain holds or grows at the larger batch × context shapes the table doesn't reach. P/D decode instances run in that regime. The go/no-go run below tests this.

**Prefill: shuffling doesn't help.** I measured prompt extension after prefix reuse, the prefill path that reads cached context, over 63 shapes on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B:

- Shuffled pages were never the fastest.
- With 16-token pages, shuffled `ROCM_AITER_FA` was a median 2.8–3.5% slower than unshuffled `ROCM_AITER_FA` (up to 12.7%). The cost is in gathering the cached context.
- The fastest unshuffled backend was `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` (64-token pages) at 44 of 63 shapes.
- Cold prefill was not measured.

**Why not just shuffle both sides?** Shuffling both sides gets shuffled decode without any conversion, but it has three costs:

1. Prefill pays the shuffled-page penalty above, about 3% of extension time.
2. Prefill must stay on `ROCM_AITER_FA`, the same backend as the decoder, so it can't use AITER unified. That is also true under this proposal unless prefill and decode may use different backends. `attn_backend_name` is a compatibility-hash factor, so a `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` prefill can't pair with a `ROCM_AITER_FA` decoder today, even though both write standard pages. This is decision 2 below, and the go/no-go includes a measurement of it.
3. An NVIDIA prefill can't write shuffled pages (the AMD–NVIDIA item on #33702). There, conversion is the only way to use shuffled decode.

**What blocks it today.** NixlConnector's receive-side conversions are:

- the HND→NHD and block-size permutes (#26556, #30275);
- a CPU_ATTN repack (#38935) keyed on the backend name, which re-runs the CPU cache writer on received standard pages.

None is negotiated at handshake. NixlConnector can't tell a convertible pair from an incompatible one: shuffled `LBHNC` pages even pass the handshake as standard pages (#59110).

### Proposed Change.

**Scope of the first version:**

- standard → shuffled only, on a ROCm decoder with 16- or 32-token pages at `LHBNC` (the non-gluon path);
- homogeneous TP, BF16/FP16, non-HMA, non-MLA, equal block sizes, pull mode.

Everything else fails closed:

- the reverse direction;
- gluon-configured decoders;
- FP8, where the shuffle writer's scale handling and MI300's `e4m3fnuz` vs OCP `e4m3fn` storage need their own treatment;
- push mode, for now.

I'm happy to implement it.

**1. Negotiate the pair.** Make the decision in the `kv_cache_layout` check of `_validate_remote_agent_handshake`, per remote engine. It uses the page-format tag from #59110. A remote with standard pages at `LBHNC` and a local shuffled decoder at `LHBNC` is accepted only when:

- conversion is enabled;
- the pair is in scope.

Any other mismatch is rejected. The existing `enable_permute_local_kv` branch will also require the local layout to be `LBNHC`, so that it can never permute shuffled caches. A missing tag follows the #59110 rule: it's rejected whenever the local pages aren't standard.

**2. Layout.** The non-gluon shuffled path already requires `LHBNC` on main: it asserts that the K and V sides are dense planes. NixlConnector, however, requests `LBHNC`, and that request wins layout resolution. So the decoder needs `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` today. I'd change `get_required_kvcache_layout` to defer to the backend when the shuffle layout is on.

**3. Descriptors.**

- Under `LHBNC`, the decoder registers a K plane and a V plane per layer, each half a page. A standard `LBHNC` prefill registers one full-page region per layer.
- Present the remote side as two virtual regions per layer, at offsets 0 and `block_len/2`, each of length `block_len/2`. They are ordered like the local K-plane and V-plane regions.
- The contract with the converter: after the read, the local K-plane block followed by the V-plane block holds the remote standard block's bytes. These are the block's first and second byte halves, not K and V.
- Code changes:
  - `_build_fa_remote`;
  - the remote region metadata recorded in `add_remote_agent`;
  - the remote `_compute_desc_ids` call in `pull_worker.read_blocks`;
  - the region count, region names and `block_len` checks;
  - tests in `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`.
- This is the same descriptor machinery as the K/V-slot split in #59110.

**4. Convert, in a hook owned by the backend.**

- The connector only compares tags and calls a backend hook with the caches, the received block ids and the remote tag. The hook could be a classmethod on the AITER FA backend or live in `_aiter_ops`. This follows #38935, where `Platform.pack_kv_cache` does the CPU_ATTN repack.
- The simplest correct implementation gathers the received K/V and re-runs the backend's own writer, `reshape_and_cache_shuffle_triton`, with a synthetic `slot_mapping` for those blocks. That matches the writer by construction and would carry over to a later FP8 path. A per-block view/permute version serves as the test reference.
- It runs in the receive post-process in `get_transfer_results`, one layer at a time. That is inside the decoder's `execute_model`, on the main stream, so each arriving request delays every running request's next step. If that shows up in ITL, the mitigation is a side stream plus an event that must complete before the request is scheduled.

<details>
<summary>Per-block conversion reference (checked element by element against the shuffle writer's offsets, including odd and single-head ranks)</summary>

```python
# One block, standard (H, N, 2*D) -> shuffled; x = 16 // element_size
K, V = std[..., :D], std[..., D:]
k_shuf = K.reshape(H, N, D // x, x).permute(0, 2, 1, 3)   # (H, D/x, N, x)
v_shuf = V.reshape(H, N // x, x, D).permute(0, 1, 3, 2)   # (H, N/x, D, x)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cost estimate (not measured)</summary>

- **Data per request.** A Qwen3-8B request carries 0.6 GB of BF16 KV at 4k context and 2.4 GB at 16k.
- **Conversion time.** Generic torch ops move at least about 4× those bytes. At 1.5–3 TB/s effective, that is roughly 1–2.5 ms per 4k request and 3–10 ms per 16k request.
- **Decode savings.** For comparison, shuffled decode saves 0.6–2.7 ms per step at batch 32–64 against `ROCM_AITER_FA`, and 0.4–1.3 ms against the fastest unshuffled backend.
- **Break-even.** That is roughly 40–150 output tokens against `ROCM_AITER_FA`, and 70–360 against the fastest unshuffled backend (4k–16k context, batch 32–64).

</details>

**5. Knob.** Off by default. Because it is NIXL-specific, I'd make it a `kv_connector_extra_config` key like `enforce_handshake_compat`. (`enable_permute_local_kv`, by contrast, is a top-level `KVTransferConfig` field.) The key would be named after the #59110 tag and read by the decoder. It would come with an entry in the NIXL compatibility docs.

**Go/no-go measurement (before the conversion PR is reviewed).** Conversion adds decode-side work, so it can't beat "shuffle both sides" on TPOT. Its possible wins are on the prefill side (TTFT and prefill throughput) and in pairings that shuffling both sides can't provide.

<details>
<summary>Plan</summary>

- **Setups:**
  - (a1) unshuffled FA → FA;
  - (a2) unshuffled UNIFIED → UNIFIED;
  - (b) shuffled FA → FA;
  - (c) unshuffled FA → shuffled FA, with conversion;
  - (d) UNIFIED (16-token pages) → shuffled FA, with conversion. This one is prototyped with `"enforce_handshake_compat": false` because of the backend-name hash.
- **Configuration:**
  - MI300X, decoder at TP 2 so that 32k context fits.
  - Batches above the asm threshold for that TP (48, 64, 128), with a profiler check of which decode kernel ran.
  - Models: Qwen3-8B, and Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 weights with BF16 KV.
  - Contexts 4k–32k; output lengths 128, 512 and 1024.
  - Both cold-prefill and prefix-hit prefill workloads.
  - At least 3 repeats per configuration.
- **Metrics:**
  - TTFT, split into prefill, transfer and conversion time;
  - prefill throughput;
  - TPOT;
  - p50/p99 ITL of other running requests;
  - goodput at fixed TTFT/TPOT SLOs.
- **Decision rules:**
  - (c) and (d) vs (a1)/(a2): better TPOT or output throughput at equal TTFT.
  - (c) and (d) vs (b): better TTFT or prefill throughput, with TPOT no more than 2% worse.
  - A result counts only if it is ≥ 3% with non-overlapping repeat ranges.
- An NVIDIA → AMD run would cover the other pairing that shuffling both sides can't. I'll add it if a mixed setup is available.

</details>

**Test plan.**

- CPU round-trip tests of the converter against a reference that reproduces the shuffle writer's offsets. These include the two byte-halves `LHBNC` read and single-head and odd-head ranks.
- Descriptor-geometry tests for the split read.
- Handshake tests: the convertible pair is accepted only when enabled, and every other mismatch, including the reverse direction and the `enable_permute_local_kv` branch, is rejected.
- A ROCm 1P1D accuracy run (`tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration`, `DECODER_KV_LAYOUT=LHBNC`) with shuffle on the decoder only.

**Compatibility.** Pairs with matching page formats see no change. Conversion runs only when enabled and the pair is in scope. Older peers already fail the compatibility hash unless that check is disabled.

**Decisions for reviewers.**

1. **Where the format and converter live.** I'd propose an opaque page-format tag from an `AttentionBackend` hook, which the connector only compares, plus a converter hook owned by the backend. This keeps NIXL free of AITER's tile layout, in line with #42082 keeping the page content opaque (#47095 discusses layouts that aren't permutations). @LucasWilkinson @heheda12345
2. **Different backends on each side.** Once page formats are negotiated, should prefill and decode be allowed to use different backends when their formats match or are convertible? Examples are AITER unified → AITER FA, or FLASH_ATTN → CPU_ATTN, which today needs `enforce_handshake_compat: false`. Setup (d) measures what this is worth. NIXL owners.
3. **Converter implementation.** Should the converter re-run the backend writer in torch, or use a dedicated AITER kernel? AITER owners.

### Feedback Period.

About one week.

### CC List.

@NickLucche @xuechendi (NIXL), @tjtanaa @ganyi1996ppo @ukannika (AITER, shuffle layout), @LucasWilkinson @heheda12345 (KV cache layout)

### Any Other Things.

**Pilot setup.**

- Hardware and software: one MI300X (gfx942), vLLM 0.30.0 ROCm image (AITER 0.1.21.post2, ROCm 7.2.3), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` in every compared configuration, BF16 weights and KV, TP 1.
- Decode timing: median of 96 steps at a constant batch, CUDA graphs `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`.
- Excluded baselines:
  - `ROCM_ATTN`, because ROCm doesn't select it automatically with a KV connector and it is affected by #59110. Including it narrows the batch ≥ 32 range to +2.3% to +5.1%.
  - Patched, unsupported NHD configurations of AITER.
- Restricting the baselines to `LBHNC`-capable backends (NIXL's default) leaves both ranges unchanged.

**Related:** #59110, #54805, #33702, #38935, #42082, #47095, #26556, #30275.

### Before submitting a new issue...

items.title: [ROCm][Kernel] New "hip" GDN backend for gfx1151
items.body:
## Purpose

GATED_DELTA_NET prefill runs as a chain of Triton kernels that communicate through DDR. At 2048 tokens, 32 MiB are stored and loaded back per layer.

This adds the chunked delta rule (WY representation / UT transform) as a single HIP kernel for RDNA3.5. One block walks the chunks of one (head, sequence) with the state resident in registers and the per-chunk intermediates in LDS, so `h`, `w` and `u` are never formed. A chunk of 32 tokens and the identity `v_new = Tinv (V beta - (K beta exp(g_cs)) S)` keep a whole chunk inside the 64 KB LDS budget.

The kernel is also more accurate than the path it replaces: everything between the inputs and the output stays fp32, where the Triton kernels round `h`, `w`, `u`, `Tinv` and `v_new` to bf16. Against an fp64 token-by-token reference its relative RMS error is 0.53x theirs, and the final state comes out at fp32 precision.

The kernel is exposed as a new GDN prefill backend, `hip`, next to `triton`, `flashinfer`, `cutedsl` and `aiter_flydsl`:

- `auto` selects it on gfx1151, the only RDNA3.5 part run on hardware. Elsewhere `auto` keeps Triton.
- `--gdn-prefill-backend hip` enables it on gfx1150–gfx1153 and fails closed where the op is not built. `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` opts out.
- Built only for gfx1150–gfx1153. bf16 and fp16 Q/K/V/output and head dimension 128; other models resolve to Triton, and any call the kernel cannot serve falls back to Triton per call.
- The Triton/FLA path is untouched.

Also adds a single-GPU benchmark that compares the two paths correctness-first, with model presets, mixed-cache preparation and incremental JSONL output.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_chunked_rocm.py \
    tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py -v

# correctness against an fp64 token-by-token reference
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gdn_chunk.py \
    --hv 48 --hg 16 --seqlens 32,33,64,1 --check --exact --raw-hip

# the timing grid below: four head shapes, 16 batches each
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gdn_chunk.py --jsonl results.jsonl

# model-level accuracy
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --port 8765 --max-model-len 4096
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8765 \
    --num-questions 400 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0
```

<details>
<summary>What the benchmark does</summary>

**What it compares.** The Triton side calls the FLA entry point, `chunk_gated_delta_rule`; the HIP side calls the backend's wrapper, `chunk_gdn_hip_fwd`. Both are timed with their wrapper allocations, so the numbers are what each prefill backend costs per call.

**What it runs.** With no arguments it runs a fixed grid: 16 batches, from a single 32-token sequence up to 256 sequences of 256 tokens, against each of the four head shapes, which are the complete head counts of the Qwen3.5/3.6 family on one GPU. `--preset small|medium|dense|large` restricts the shapes. `--seqlens 941 --seqlens 1,4095` runs an explicit workload instead, repeatable, with `--hv`/`--hg` for its head counts and `--limit` to cut a run short. `--dtype` selects bf16 or fp16. `--dry-run` plans on CPU without importing torch, which is useful to see what a run would cover.

**How it times.** `triton.testing.do_bench` with quantiles, as elsewhere in this repository: it derives the repetition count from a first measurement and clears the L2 cache before each run, so every sample starts cold. Timing the public entry point means the samples include wrapper allocations and host launch gaps, which is what the model actually pays; `--raw-hip` additionally times the preallocated op on its own to separate that overhead from device time.

**What it checks before timing.** Output and final state are compared against the Triton path per sequence and head, with relative RMS and a finite check. `--check` skips timing entirely, and `--exact` adds an independent fp64 token-by-token recurrence, which is what decides whether the kernel is more accurate rather than merely different.

**Reading the output.** Progress goes to stdout; `--jsonl` writes one record per case with the median and the p10/p90 quantiles, the shapes, the inferred launch mode and the environment. Speedup is the Triton median over the HIP median, so above 1× is faster. Compare p10 and p90 before calling a small difference a regression: where those ranges overlap, the two paths are not conclusively different.

</details>

Hardware: one AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151). PyTorch `2.12.0+rocm10.1.0a20260803`, Triton `3.8.0+git4cff872c.rocm10.1.0a20260803`. Only gfx1151 has been run on hardware; the other three targets are compile-tested.

## Test Result

`tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_chunked_rocm.py`: **39 passed**. Coverage includes ratio-three heads, absent initial state, optional final state, continuation across aligned and unaligned splits, adversarial gates and fp16 inputs, all against an independent fp64 recurrence.

`tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py`: **27 passed**. Covers backend selection (`auto` on and off gfx1151, explicit `hip`, unsupported head dims and dtypes, missing op) and, on gfx1151, the production `ChunkGatedDeltaRule` resolving to `hip` against a token-wise reference.

items.title: [Bug]: --load_format fastsafetensors produces corrupted/incoherent generation for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with TP+EP (works with default loader)
items.body:
### Your current environment

- **Hardware**: 2× NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), one GPU per node, 2-node cluster joined via Ray (TCP/RoCE interconnect)
- **Compute Capability**: SM121 (12.1), `aarch64`
- **vLLM**: 0.26.0 (PyPI release)
- **torch**: 2.11.0+cu130
- **CUDA**: 13.0
- **Distributed executor**: `ray`, `--tensor-parallel-size 2` (one GPU per node), `--enable-expert-parallel`

### Model

```
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--load_format fastsafetensors`, the server starts and serves requests without error, but generation output is incoherent (not just low-quality — literal token salad mixing unrelated languages/scripts/digits), **even under greedy decoding (`temperature=0`)**. Switching to the default loader (removing the flag entirely) with an otherwise-identical launch command produces fluent, well-formed text for the same prompt and sampling parameters.

This looks like a weight-loading correctness bug specific to `fastsafetensors` for this model's TP+EP sharding, not a config or template issue — we independently ruled out chat-template/prompt-encoding as the cause (verified via `/tokenize` that the prompt's special tokens resolve to the exact expected IDs), and ruled out sampling randomness (reproduced identically at `temperature=0`).

### Launch command (bugged)

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --load_format fastsafetensors \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8
```

### Repro

Prompt (raw `/v1/completions`, DeepSeek-V4's own chat-mode encoding, `add_special_tokens=false`):
```
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜User｜>What is 2+2? Answer in one word.<｜Assistant｜></think>
```

**With `--load_format fastsafetensors`** (`temperature=1.0`, `max_tokens=32`):
```
eBook '++lang()' non e 'undefined'.
        // In quel caso non deve essere tradotto.
        // Nota: menzionare un OG
```

**Without `--load_format fastsafetensors`** (identical prompt/params, only the loader changed):
```
eBook. Please don't try to read it directly.","price":0,"duration":0,"currency":null,"url":"https://www.smashwords.com/books/view/860089"}]...
```
(Still doesn't answer the question — that's a separate, likely attention/kernel-level issue we're still isolating — but the text is grammatically well-formed English/JSON rather than token salad.)

### Expected behavior

Output coherence (grammaticality) should not depend on the weight-loading backend used, given both claim to load the same checkpoint bit-for-bit. This suggests `fastsafetensors` is either mis-mapping tensors (e.g. quantization scale tensors paired with the wrong weight tensor) or mis-sharding weights for this model's TP+EP configuration.

items.title: Enable split-KV for paged multi-token queries (spec-decode verify)
items.body:
`set_params_splitkv` only applies split-k in the
`seqlenq_ngroups_swapped` case (q_len == 1): "Only apply split-k for
decoding". Any paged varlen call with 1 < q_len ≤ 64 — exactly the
shape of a speculative-decode verify — is forced to `num_splits ≤ 1`
and walks the whole KV serially in one CTA per (batch, head). At long
context this is a kernel-level cliff:

- Ampere (RTX 3090 Ti, unmodified vLLM 0.13.0 wheel, 31k paged KV):
  verify q=2 is **22.8×** slower than the equivalent split decode call;
  q=4: 16.5×; q=8: 7.3×. The restriction is unchanged in today's main
  (`STD_TORCH_CHECK(num_splits <= 1, ...)`).
- The absolute verify time is context-bound, not head-bound (~1.4 ms at
  31k regardless of q_len and head count) — the signature of a serial
  KV walk.

The fix enables splits for `paged_KV && max_seqlen_q <= 64` and makes
the combine kernel varlen-correct, which the old gate had masked:

- final O write used `batch_idx * o_batch_stride` (unset in varlen) —
  now cu_seqlens_q packing with a row guard;
- unpadded LSE write assumed uniform sequence lengths — now cu_seqlens
  packing;
- `softmax_lse_accum`/`out_accum` are pre-initialized (-inf / 0) so
  early-exit splits cannot leak garbage into the combine.

Measured end to end (2× Quadro RTX 8000, 27B W4A8, MTP spec decode,
31k context): long-context decode 23 → 34 tok/s; speculation at long
context flips from a loss to a win. Numerics: max abs err 2.4e-4 vs
fp32 reference across q_len 1–8, splits 1/2/4 bitwise-consistent.

items.title: Apply split-K to varlen paged KV when max_seqlen_q > 1 (spec decode)
items.body:
FA2 silently disables split-K for **every speculative-decode step**. `set_params_splitkv` is gated on `seqlenq_ngroups_swapped`, which requires `max_seqlen_q == 1`; spec decode makes the verify pass carry `q_len = K+1`, so the gate never opens. This affects MTP, EAGLE, Medusa, draft-model and n-gram equally.

Measured impact: the decode-attention grid collapses from **172 to 12 blocks**, so 12 of 128 SMs get work — **3.5% of DRAM peak instead of ~79%**.

## Why the gate could not simply be removed

The n-groups swap is the only path that sets `cu_seqlens_q_d = nullptr`, and that is the sole branch in `set_params_fprop` that assigns `o_batch_stride` — which is what `combine_attn_seqk_parallel` uses to address O. In a true varlen call `o_batch_stride` stays **0**, so the combine kernel folds every sequence onto sequence 0. At batch 1 `batch_idx * 0 == 0`, so a naive gate flip passes a single-sequence benchmark and silently corrupts batch > 1. That hazard is exactly what the existing `TORCH_CHECK(num_splits <= 1, "not supported for varlen paged KV")` encodes.

This PR therefore addresses O and LSE through `cu_seqlens_q` in the combine kernel and skips rows past `actual_seqlen_q`, **then** drops the gate. The n-groups swap stays gated on `max_seqlen_q == 1`, where it belongs. 40 changed lines across `flash_api.cpp` and `flash_fwd_kernel.h`.

## Not a duplicate

Searched `vllm-project/flash-attention` open PRs for `split-K spec decode`, `seqlenq_ngroups_swapped`, and `varlen paged num_splits` — no open PR addresses this.

## Tests run, and results

Added coverage exercises the batch > 1 case the old guard was protecting, including **non-uniform query lengths**, where the padded scratch layout and the unpadded output layout diverge:

```
seq_lens: [(6, 16384)]                       batch 1
          [(6, 8192), (6, 8191), (6, 4097)]  batch 3
          [(1, 4096), (6, 4096), (37, 4096)] batch 3, non-uniform q (1, 6, 37)
          [(4, 129), (1, 8000), (12, 33)]    batch 3, non-uniform q and kv
```
crossed with `num_splits` {2, 5, 16}, `num_heads` {(12,2), (4,4)}, `head_size` {128, 256}, `sliding_window` {None, 256} = 96 cases.

Run red-before-green against two images differing **only** in `_vllm_fa2_C.abi3.so`, with each arm verified to load its own binary (md5 `39d84a04` unpatched vs `3ab40ce6` patched) before trusting the result:

```
unpatched .so : 96 failed
patched   .so : 96 passed
```

## Effect on model output

RTX 4090 sm_89, Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ-INT4, TP2, MTP K=5, batch 1, ISL 16384, bf16 KV, clocks locked 2700 MHz:

| arm | tok/s | TPOT ms | accept_len | TTFT p50 | step ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (x3 reps) | 70.0 | 14.28 | 3.11 | 6041 | 44.42 |
| patched (x2 reps) | **108.9** | **9.19** | **3.20** | 6027 | **29.41** |

**+55.4% tok/s, -35.6% TPOT.** Noise band ±0.07%. The base arm was repeated non-adjacently on a fresh boot *after* the patched arm (70.1) to rule out drift. TTFT is flat, as a decode-only change must be.

Accuracy is not degraded — it improves slightly. Acceptance length rises 3.11 → 3.20 because split-K replaces one long sequential fp32 accumulation with 19 shorter ones and lands closer to an fp64 oracle (rel-L2 0.002195 vs 0.002292), so the target rejects its own draft marginally less often. A paired greedy check gave **6/6 prompts byte-identical** over 1152 sampled positions, and `q_len == 1` is bit-identical. Boots clean under full CUDA-graph capture.

The win concentrates at low batch, long context and few KV heads; at high batch the grid already fills and the change is inert.

## AI assistance

**AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change.** The C++ change, the test design, and every measurement above were produced with AI assistance and reviewed by the human submitter.

Note for maintainers: I have not added a `Signed-off-by` trailer, as DCO sign-off is the submitter's own attestation — happy to amend if required.

items.title: Enable split-KV for varlen + paged KV when explicitly requested via n…
items.body:
Enable split-KV for varlen + paged KV when explicitly requested via num_splits
Summary
combine_attn_seqk_parallel's O and LSE write-back assumed a fixed-shape
(non-varlen) output tensor. #2448 widened split-KV eligibility to any
paged_KV call, which exposed this pre-existing bug whenever a real split
(num_splits > 1) was actually reached with cu_seqlens_q set: every batch
collided on the same output address (o_batch_stride is 0 in varlen layout,
so batch_idx * o_batch_stride collapses to 0 regardless of batch_idx), and
the LSE write-back had the analogous issue in its gLSE_unpadded addressing
(assumes every batch occupies exactly params.seqlen_q slots, which only
holds for non-ragged batches). #2550 added a TORCH_CHECK as a stopgap,
disabling num_splits > 1 for this case entirely. #2542 attempted the real
fix but was closed ("performance gains are minimal") — its own benchmark
showed splits=2/4 slower than splits=0 across kv_len 512–16384, because gating
on paged_KV alone re-enables splitting for every paged_KV call regardless
of caller intent, diluting the average with cases where splitting isn't worth
the combine overhead.

This PR fixes the write-back bug and re-enables num_splits > 1 for this
case, but narrows the trigger to only when the caller explicitly requests a
specific num_splits (mha_varlen_fwd already exposes num_splits as a
parameter, added in #110) — not unconditionally for every paged_KV call.
This is strictly narrower than #2448/#2542's gate and avoids the dilution
that sank #2542, while leaving the performance tradeoff where the caller
(who knows its own access pattern) can make it.

Motivating use case
Speculative-decoding verify steps (e.g. DFlash-style block/tree drafting)
reuse the same small, padded max_seqlen_q (K draft tokens + 1) every round,
with paged_KV and (per-request) cu_seqlens_q — exactly the varlen +
non-swapped (seqlenq_ngroups_swapped == false, since max_seqlen_q > 1)
case this PR targets, and exactly the regime #2542's benchmark didn't cover
(it appears to have swept kv_len at a fixed, likely larger max_seqlen_q).
At batch sizes too small to otherwise fill the SMs, splitting genuinely
helps here: in our own downstream use (DFlash verify on an RTX 3090, 3
prompt-length buckets), enabling split-KV for this path gave -13.8% to
-18.9% wall-clock latency on the long-context bucket (batch=1), measured
against the unpatched baseline across multiple runs.

Changes
csrc/flash_attn/flash_api.cpp — mha_varlen_fwd's split-KV gate:


if (seqlenq_ngroups_swapped || (paged_KV && num_splits > 1)) {
    std::tie(softmax_lse_accum, out_accum) = set_params_splitkv(...);
} else if (paged_KV) {
    STD_TORCH_CHECK(num_splits <= 1, "num_splits > 1 is not supported for varlen paged KV");
    params.num_splits = num_splits;
}
The gate is deliberately num_splits > 1, not num_splits != 1: the Python
default is num_splits=0 ("let the heuristic decide"), which almost every
existing caller relies on implicitly. Gating on != 1 would route that
default into set_params_splitkv, whose own num_splits < 1 branch then
auto-picks a split count via num_splits_heuristic -- silently changing
behavior for every caller who never opted into anything, which is exactly
the blanket-enable #2542 was closed for. With > 1, both num_splits == 0
(default) and num_splits == 1 (explicit no-split) reproduce the exact
pre-existing behavior; only an explicit num_splits > 1 request reaches
set_params_splitkv.

vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py also keeps an explicit
NotImplementedError for num_splits > 1 when block_table is None
(non-paged_KV): the C++ side only permits num_splits > 1 for paged_KV
calls, and would otherwise silently ignore the request (falls through to
params.num_splits = 0) rather than erroring -- a caller who explicitly
asked for a specific split count should be told it wasn't honored, not
have it dropped quietly.

csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_fwd_kernel.h — combine_attn_seqk_parallel:

O write-back: replaced batch_idx * params.o_batch_stride with BlockInfo's existing q_offset() helper (already used by every other write path in this file for exactly this varlen-vs-fixed-shape distinction), plus a row >= binfo.actual_seqlen_q skip for ragged batches.
LSE write-back: added a cu_seqlens_q != nullptr branch computing the true (unpadded/concatenated) address, adapted from #2542's fix for the same issue (credit: @liangel-02).
Testing
Extended the existing test_varlen_with_paged_kv (already exercises ragged
per-sequence query lengths + paged KV + causal, compared against the
file's own ref_paged_attn reference) with a num_splits parametrize
([0, 1, 2, 4]), skipped for fa_version != 2 (this fix is FA2-only,
hopper/ FA3 sources untouched):


576 passed, 1832 deselected in 5.29s
(the full non-skipped parameter space for this test function: num_heads ×
head_size × block_size × dtype × soft_cap × num_blocks × num_splits)

compute-sanitizer on representative num_splits=2/num_splits=4 cases:


memcheck:   0 errors
racecheck:  0 hazards (0 errors, 0 warnings)
Scope / limitations
FA2 (csrc/flash_attn) only; FA3 (hopper/) is untouched and has its own code path.
The measured performance benefit above is from our own downstream (DFlash-style, short multi-token, batch-small) use case; we haven't swept large-max_seqlen_q or large-batch configurations for performance (only for correctness, via the test above, which does cover a range of shapes). Whether splitting is worth it for other access patterns is left to the caller's judgment via the explicit num_splits parameter, same as the existing seqlenq_ngroups_swapped decode path already does.

items.title: Enable split-k for varlen paged KV when query lengths are uniform
items.body:
## Enable split-k for varlen paged KV when query lengths are uniform

`mha_varlen_fwd` refuses split-k on the paged path unconditionally:

```cpp
} else if (paged_KV) {
    STD_TORCH_CHECK(num_splits <= 1, "num_splits > 1 is not supported for varlen paged KV");
```

For speculative decoding this is the hot path — every verify step is a paged varlen call
with `q = num_speculative_tokens + 1` — and forcing `num_splits = 1` launches only
`batch_size * num_heads` CTAs, which serialise over the KV length.

Measured on 2× RTX 3090 (sm_86), Qwen3.8-27B shape, hd256, 12 q-heads / 2 kv-heads per
card, page size 16, identical KV bytes in both columns:

| KV len | q=1 | q=8 (verify) | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4,096 | 0.0695 ms | 0.3750 ms | ×5.40 |
| 32,768 | 0.1376 ms | 2.9393 ms | ×21.36 |
| 200,000 | 0.5795 ms | 15.7886 ms | **×27.25** |

With split-k restored:

| KV len | q=8 before | q=8 after | ratio now | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4,096 | 0.3750 ms | **0.0846 ms** | ×1.03 | 4.4× |
| 32,768 | 2.9393 ms | **0.5203 ms** | ×3.78 | 5.6× |
| 200,000 | 15.7886 ms | **3.0246 ms** | ×5.18 | **5.2×** |

Also measured at an hd128 TP=1 verify shape (32 q-heads / 8 kv-heads, q=8, 32K):
1.336 ms → 0.584 ms, **×2.29**. The gain shrinks as heads-per-GPU rises, because the
unsplit grid is already wider.

### Why it is safe when query lengths are uniform

The guard exists because the splitkv accumulators are sized
`{num_splits, b, h, max_seqlen_q}` (`set_params_splitkv`) and `flash_fwd_splitkv_combine_kernel`
indexes them — and the output — **densely**, as `b * h * seqlen_q`, where
`params.seqlen_q == max_seqlen_q` on this path. It never reads `cu_seqlens_q`. Varlen output
is packed as `total_q` rows, so dense indexing is wrong whenever query lengths differ.

When `total_q == batch_size * max_seqlen_q`, every sequence contributes exactly
`max_seqlen_q` query tokens, packed and dense coincide, and the indexing is exact. That is
always true for spec-decode verify. Ragged input keeps the original refusal.

One additional assignment is required: `params.o_batch_stride` is only set when
`cu_seqlens_q == nullptr` (`set_params_fprop`), so on the varlen path it is still 0 and the
combine kernel would write every sequence into batch 0. Under the uniform-q precondition the
correct stride is simply `max_seqlen_q * o_row_stride`. **This is invisible at `batch_size == 1`**,
which is worth knowing when reproducing.

### Precondition and contract

The branch requires `max_seqlen_q` to be **exact** and `total_q == cu_seqlens_q[b]`. This is
the same assumption the existing `seqlenq_ngroups_swapped` branch already relies on. vLLM
satisfies it (`max_seqlen_q = max_query_len`, `q = query[:num_actual_tokens]`).

If a caller under-reports `max_seqlen_q`, or passes padding rows beyond `cu_seqlens_q[b]`,
the dense indexing is wrong and results are silently incorrect — where the unsplit path
happened to tolerate it. Hence the equality test rather than a per-sequence scan.

### Blast radius

Shapes that were previously never eligible for split-k are now *eligible* (most still get
`num_splits == 1` from the heuristic): MHA `q=1` decode, sliding-window `q=1` decode (the
window disables the ngroups swap), cascade-attention prefix (`b=1`), and single-sequence
prefill.

Kernel selection for shapes the heuristic declines to split is **unchanged** —
`set_params_splitkv` normalises "no split" to `num_splits = 1`, which the dispatcher reads
as a request for the batch-invariant *align* kernel, so the caller's value is restored
afterwards. Verified: non-engaged hd128 shapes still launch
`Flash_fwd_kernel_traits<128, 64, 128, 4>`, as on `main`.

Numerics change where split-k engages, because the combine kernel reorders softmax/LSE
accumulation. Verified against an fp32 reference reading the paged KV through a permuted
block table: **max 0.909 bf16 ulp of tensor scale, LSE max abs error 4e-06**, across b=3/4/5/8,
ragged `seqused_k` (33 … 20,000), local windows, softcap, MHA, non-causal, q>64 spanning two
m-blocks, and zero-length KV. `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` passes `num_splits = 1` and so bypasses
the branch entirely.

Under full CUDA graphs the split count is baked at capture time from `max_model_len`, so short
contexts replay a count chosen for the longest — a perf consideration, not a correctness one.

### Tests

`test_varlen_paged_uniform_query_len` — uniform query lengths across b=3/4/8/2, GQA and MHA,
hd128 and hd256, both block sizes, softcap, and `return_softmax_lse=True` with the **LSE
shape and finiteness asserted** (an output-only check would miss a stride error in the
combine's LSE write). The existing `test_varlen_with_paged_kv` cases are all ragged
(`[1, 5, 129]`) and never reach this branch.

`test_varlen_paged_split_k_engages_only_when_uniform` — positive and negative control via a
profiler trace: the combine kernel is launched iff `num_splits > 1`, so its presence proves
the branch ran and its absence on ragged input proves the guard holds. **This test fails on
`main`** (split-k cannot engage there) and passes with the patch.

Run:
```
pytest tests/test_vllm_flash_attn.py -k "uniform_query_len or split_k_engages"
```

### End-to-end effect

Measured on the same rig, vLLM v0.27.1, TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B with an external drafter at
`num_spec_tokens=7`, one-shot prompts, `min_tokens=400`, tokens counted from
`usage.completion_tokens`. Six boots, arms alternated A,B,A,B,A,B; the patched `.so` is verified
per boot by checksum. **The patched arm is a probe container — this is not a shipped
configuration.**

| arm | 32K (r1/r2/r3) | median | 90K (r1/r2/r3) | median |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FA2 **+ this patch** | 112.0 / 93.3 / 111.5 | **111.5 tok/s** | 51.5 / 62.4 / 43.1 | 51.5 tok/s |
| FlashInfer (same model, same drafter) | 78.8 / 65.9 / 63.0 | 65.9 tok/s | 74.7 / 59.0 / 72.2 | 72.2 tok/s |

At 32K the two arms' ranges are **disjoint** (93.3–112.0 vs 63.0–78.8). Against the same
configuration on unpatched FA2 (54.95 tok/s, single boot) the patched arm's median is
**+103%** — the verify step stops dominating the decode loop.

At 90K FlashInfer still leads; that is expected and unrelated to this change (its decode kernel
uses a 16-row tile against FA2's 64 at head-dim 256, so FA2 does ~10× the padded MMA per tile —
a separate limitation this patch does not address).

**Measurement caveat, stated plainly:** accept-length varies 1.84–3.41 across boots on the same
arm and rung, and per-arm throughput spread is 18–37%. Medians over n=3 are reported for that
reason; a single-boot comparison of a speculative-decoding configuration cannot support a
percentage claim. The 32K conclusion holds because the ranges do not overlap, not because the
medians differ.

### Not included

While validating this I found a **pre-existing** bug unrelated to the change: the splitkv
early-exit path computes the LSE offset with the dense `(b, h, q)` formula even when
`unpadded_lse` is set, where the normal-exit path has an unpadded branch. A zero-length-KV
sequence in a varlen batch can therefore write `+inf` into a neighbouring sequence's LSE slot.
Present in Dao-AILab upstream too. Happy to file separately.

items.title: Fix LSE output error in FA2 kv-split
items.body:
### Background

During vLLM inference, some features like **Cascade Attention** require the LSE output from the attention mechanism.

When the FlashAttention-2 kernel operates with `seqlenq_ngroups_swapped = True` (the case for an inference-only batch with GQA), it performs the attention computation with an internal shape of `(b, ngroups, nheads_kv, d)`. After the computation, it restores the `softmax_lse` tensor to the expected layout using the following transformation:

```
int64_t lse_size_before[] = {num_heads, batch_size, max_seqlen_q};
int64_t lse_size_after[] = {num_heads * max_seqlen_q, batch_size};
softmax_lse = softmax_lse.reshape(lse_size_before).transpose(1, 2).reshape(lse_size_after)
```

### The Problem with split_kv

The issue arises when the split_kv path is triggered in FlashAttention-2's flash_api.cpp. The decision to use this path is made by the `num_splits_heuristic` function. When split_kv is enabled, the kernel partitions the K/V tensors, stores partial LSE results in softmax_lse_accum, and finally launches a `combine_attn_seqk_parallel` kernel to reduce these partial results into the final LSE.

The root cause of the bug lies in the memory layout defined within the combine_attn_seqk_parallel kernel. Specifically, when `seqlenq_ngroups_swapped = True` and `unpadded_lse = True`, the layout for the output tensor gLSE_unpadded is constructed as follows:

```
// Note: This code is inside the combine_attn_seqk_parallel kernel
// When seqlenq_ngroups_swapped is True, then unpadded_lse is always True as well.

auto transposed_stride = params.seqlenq_ngroups_swapped ? make_stride(params.b, params.seqlen_q * params.b, 1) : make_stride(1, params.seqlen_q * params.b, params.seqlen_q);

Layout remapped_layout = make_layout(make_shape(params.seqlen_q, params.h, params.b), transposed_stride);
Layout final_layout = cute::composition(remapped_layout, cute::composition(orig_layout, flat_layout));

Tensor gLSE_unpadded = make_tensor(make_gmem_ptr(reinterpret_cast<ElementAccum *>(params.softmax_lse_ptr)), final_layout);
```

Because of this final_layout, the physical memory layout of gLSE_unpadded is already aligned with the desired output shape and can be correctly interpreted with a simple reshape like `softmax_lse.reshape(num_heads * max_seqlen_q, batch_size)`.

**However, the original code path unconditionally applies the `.transpose(1, 2)` operation, which is incorrect for the split_kv case. This erroneous transpose corrupts the LSE layout, leading to a complete precision collapse in downstream operations.**

### Reproducibility
This bug is hard to reproduce because it only manifests under a specific combination of conditions:

- Using a feature that consumes the LSE output (e.g., Cascade Attention).
- The num_splits calculated by `num_splits_heuristic` is greater than 1. This value is sensitive to:
    - GPU architecture (e.g., number of SMs)
    - Batch size
    - Sequence length of the KV cache for the inference requests.
    - Different LLM Model

Related Issues 
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/17580
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/17652 
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/17886
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/18345
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22103

I successfully reproduced the issue using the sample program provided in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22103 on an L20 machine, and the changes in this commit fix the problem.

items.title: [FA2] Write a caller-provided out in place on the varlen decode path
items.body:
## What we fixed

`mha_varlen_fwd` accepts an optional `out` tensor. On the varlen decode path it ignores it: the
attention result is written into a temporary, and the buffer the caller passed in is never
touched. The function returns the temporary, so a caller that uses the return value sees nothing
wrong. A caller that passes a buffer and reads *that buffer* gets whatever was there before.

That is the bug. `out` is an output parameter, and on this path it does nothing.

The path in question is the decode fast path guarded by `seqlenq_ngroups_swapped`, which applies
when all of these hold:

- `max_seqlen_q == 1` — one query token per sequence, i.e. uniform decode (not prefill, not a
  mixed prefill+decode step)
- `num_heads > num_heads_k` — GQA or MQA; plain MHA has no groups to swap
- `window_size_left < 0 && window_size_right < 0` — full attention, no sliding window
- `p_dropout == 0`, no alibi

`causal=True` does not opt out. The function sets `is_causal = false` when `max_seqlen_q == 1`
(causal masking over a single query token is a no-op) before it tests the window bounds, so a
causal GQA decode still takes this path.

This is the ordinary configuration for full-attention GQA models (LLaMA/Qwen-style) served with a
preallocated output buffer. vLLM runs FA2 exactly this way — it passes `out=output`, ignores the
return value, and reads `output`. It also captures FA2 CUDA graphs with `max_query_len=1`
specifically to exploit this packed-GQA decode path.

## How we fixed it

The swap reorders the head axis, so the kernel's output layout is not the caller's:

```cpp
q = q.reshape({batch, num_heads_k, ngroups, d}).transpose(1, 2)
     .reshape({batch * ngroups, num_heads_k, d});
```

The kernel addresses the output as `(batch, row, head)` where `row` is the swapped `seqlen_q`.
Element `(row r, head h)` belongs at original head `h * ngroups + r`.

The current code sidesteps that by writing into a swapped temporary and fixing it up afterwards:

```cpp
out = out.reshape({batch, num_heads_k, ngroups, d})
         .transpose(1, 2)
         .reshape({batch * ngroups, num_heads_k, d});
```

`transpose` makes the tensor non-contiguous, so that trailing `reshape` **copies**. The kernels
write the copy; nothing copies back into `out_`. That is where the caller's buffer gets dropped.

The fix is to hand the kernels the caller's buffer and tell them its strides. Two changes:

**1.** Produce `out` in the final `[batch, num_heads_k, ngroups, head_size]` layout, for both the
`out`-provided and `out=None` cases. The `out` view is a pure view of the caller's tensor — no
copy.

**2.** After `set_params_fprop`, override the three output strides:

```cpp
if (seqlenq_ngroups_swapped) {
    params.o_batch_stride = out.stride(0);
    params.o_head_stride  = out.stride(1);
    params.o_row_stride   = out.stride(2);
}
```

The override is required rather than cosmetic. `set_params_fprop` derives the output strides
from the packed `q` layout, where head is the middle dimension — which describes a different
tensor. Reading them off the 4-D view gives row stride `d` and head stride `ngroups * d`, so
`r * o_row_stride + h * o_head_stride == (h * ngroups + r) * d`, i.e. original head
`h * ngroups + r`. That is exactly what the kernel's `(batch, row, head)` indices expect.

With the kernels writing the caller's buffer directly, the post-kernel fixup collapses to a view:

```cpp
out = out.reshape(size_after);
```

**Behavior change:** a caller-provided `out` must now be contiguous, checked explicitly with a
clear message. This is not a new requirement — the old code already called `reshape`/`view` on
the caller's tensor, which throws on a non-contiguous input, so every `out` that worked before
still works. The check only turns a confusing late failure inside `reshape` into an explicit one.

## Correctness evidence

RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, `FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=120`.

- **`out` is written, and is bitwise identical to the `out=None` result.** 108 configurations:
  paged/dense × fp16/bf16 × batch 1/8/16 × GQA (heads/heads_k) 8/2, 24/4, 32/8 × head_size
  64/128/256 × seqlen_k 2048/4096. Each case prefills `out` with NaN and asserts
  `torch.equal(out, ref)`, `torch.equal(returned, ref)`, and that no NaN survives.
- **`compute-sanitizer --tool=memcheck`: 0 errors** on the direct-write path.
- **The new test fails on current `main`** with `"out was not written; the output path made a
  copy"`, and passes with this change. No existing test passed `out=` to the varlen entry point.
- **No regressions:** `pytest tests/test_flash_attn.py -k "varlen and not determinist"` →
  **78347 passed, 23232 skipped, 0 failed**. Dense and non-swapped varlen paths, causal and
  sliding-window configs verified separately.

```bash
FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=120 MAX_JOBS=10 python setup.py build_ext --inplace
python -m pytest tests/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_varlen_swapped_gqa_honors_out -q
python -m pytest tests/test_flash_attn.py -q -k "varlen and not determinist"
compute-sanitizer --tool=memcheck python repro.py
```

## Performance

The change removes one device-to-device copy of the output and one temporary allocation per
call. Kernel-level, `seqlen_q=1`, GQA 24/4, `head_size=256`, bf16, median of 7 runs × 50
CUDA-event iterations:

| shape | before | after | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| b=1, k=4096 | 23.67 µs | 20.48 µs | −13.5% |
| b=8, k=4096 | 42.61 µs | 40.72 µs | −4.4% |
| b=16, k=2048 | 52.80 µs | 50.74 µs | −3.9% |
| b=32, k=4096 | 345.53 µs | 343.27 µs | −0.7% |

The saving is small but real and it is more API correct.

## Scope

One function, `mha_varlen_fwd`.

If you would like me to look at `mha_fwd`, and `mha_fwd_kvcache`, I can. 

## AI assistance

I used pi with DeepSeek 4.1 flash to help implement and validate the change.
I discovered the bug when validating fa2 performance improvements in vllm with Qwen 3.8 27b.

---

### Aside: nearby work

These were found when I was looking to see if someone had already submitted the fix. These are not prerequisites for this PR. 

- **`vllm-project/flash-attention` `04325b6`** (vllm#32, Woosuk Kwon, 2024-12) is a downstream
  workaround for this exact bug: allocate an `empty_like` temporary and `copy_` it back into
  `out_`, noting that `out.reshape(size_after)` "causes a redundant clone operation". Correct,
  but pays a full copy per call. Landing this upstream lets that fork drop the workaround instead
  of replaying it at each sync.
- **#708** (open since 2023-12) saves `ori_seqlen_q` in `mha_fwd_kvcache` to avoid a spurious
  `TORCH_CHECK`. Different function, different defect, not touched here.
- **#848** (open since 2024-02) reports passing `out` to `mha_fwd` failing when `seqlen_q == 1`.
  Different entry point, not addressed here. This PR does not close it.
- **#976** (merged) fixed the `CHECK_SHAPE` on a caller-provided `out` after `seqlen_q` is
  overwritten. This PR keeps that validation. #976 stopped this path from *throwing*; it did not
  make it *work* — the reshape chain still copied, so the caller's buffer stayed empty.
- **#2573** (open) fixes a SplitKV early-exit LSE offset in `flash_fwd_kernel.h`. Kernel-side, no
  overlap.

items.title: Fix FA2 varlen SplitKV early-exit LSE offset
items.body:
## Summary

Fix the LSE write offset used by the FA2 SplitKV early-exit path when writing directly to unpadded `softmax_lse`.

Upstream varlen forward stores LSE in the packed unpadded layout by setting `params.unpadded_lse = true`. The normal epilogue path already handles this layout, but the SplitKV early-exit path still uses the padded `(batch, head, seqlen_q)` offset.

## Problem

When running a Qwen 235B model on a single node with 8x L40S GPUs after enabling DCP, execution can hang and eventually report:

`torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`

The issue is in the FA2 SplitKV early-exit path. It always computes `row_offset_lseaccum` with the padded SplitKV-style layout:

`((n_split_idx * b + bidb) * h + bidh) * seqlen_q + m_block * kBlockM`

That layout is correct for SplitKV/LSE accumulation buffers, but not for direct unpadded LSE output in varlen mode.

For varlen forward, `softmax_lse` is allocated as `{num_heads, total_q}` and `params.unpadded_lse` is set to `true`. In this case, the early-exit path must use the same packed varlen LSE layout as the normal epilogue path.

## Fix

Use the packed varlen LSE offset when writing directly to unpadded `softmax_lse`:

`bidh * params.total_q + binfo.q_offset(params.seqlen_q, 1, bidb) + m_block * kBlockM`

Keep the existing padded offset for SplitKV accumulation buffers and padded LSE output.

items.title: Why split_kv is only enabled on n_heads > n_heads_k
items.body:
The precondition of `split_kv` on varied length forward is `seqlenq_ngroups_swapped=True`
https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/6df7e0a02edcee851744168079377a039f6d728d/csrc/flash_attn/flash_api.cpp#L702
However, that condition requires `num_heads > num_heads_k`, meaning splitkv only works for grouped-head attention. However, when the batch size is small, it is still more efficient to run parallel on kv dimension. 
Why is this condition required for split_kv? I suppose only `max_seqlen_q == 1` is necessary.

items.title: Issue with output tensor shapes in mha_fwd_kvcache
[Bug][FA2] Incorrect `softmax_lse` from `flash_attn_varlen_func` in GQA decoding with paged KV
items.body:
## Summary

`flash_attn_varlen_func` with a paged KV cache (`block_table`) silently returns `softmax_lse` with heads and sequences mixed up when

```
max_seqlen_q == 1 and num_heads > num_heads_k   # GQA decoding, without window, ALiBi or dropout
num_splits == 1                                 # the heuristic's choice for short keys or large batches
```

The kernel stores `softmax_lse` as `(num_heads_k, b, ngroups)`, while the host reads it as `(num_heads_k, ngroups, b)`. `out` is correct. The tests miss it because no test compares `softmax_lse` with a reference ([L669](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/965c9212e6be33c821ee9f2b461564c5c91a2503/tests/test_flash_attn.py#L669), [L2082](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/965c9212e6be33c821ee9f2b461564c5c91a2503/tests/test_flash_attn.py#L2082)), and the paged GQA decoding test sets `window_size_right=0`, which turns the swap off ([L2571](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/965c9212e6be33c821ee9f2b461564c5c91a2503/tests/test_flash_attn.py#L2571)).

## Environment

- RTX 5070 Ti (sm_120), driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.10.0, flash-attention `main` 965c921.
- `flash_attn_2_cuda` is built for sm_120 with only the hdim 64 and 128 FP16 kernels.

## Root Cause

In GQA decoding, `mha_varlen_fwd` reshapes `q` from `(b, num_heads, d)` to `(b * ngroups, num_heads_k, d)`, with `ngroups = num_heads / num_heads_k` ([flash_api.cpp L623–L631](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/965c9212e6be33c821ee9f2b461564c5c91a2503/csrc/flash_attn/flash_api.cpp#L623-L631)). So the kernel computes `softmax_lse` as `(num_heads_k, b, ngroups)`. After the kernel, the host reshapes it to `(num_heads_k * ngroups, b)` without moving any data ([L785](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/965c9212e6be33c821ee9f2b461564c5c91a2503/csrc/flash_attn/flash_api.cpp#L785)), so it expects the kernel to store `(num_heads_k, ngroups, b)`. The helper function `get_lse_tile` ([flash_fwd_kernel.h L43–L45](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/965c9212e6be33c821ee9f2b461564c5c91a2503/csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_fwd_kernel.h#L43-L45)) and the combine kernel ([L1153](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/965c9212e6be33c821ee9f2b461564c5c91a2503/csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_fwd_kernel.h#L1153)) store it this way.

With paged KV and one split, `flash_fwd_splitkv_kernel` stores the final `softmax_lse` at an offset of its own and forgets the transpose ([L1030–L1032](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/965c9212e6be33c821ee9f2b461564c5c91a2503/csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_fwd_kernel.h#L1030-L1032)):

```cpp
// Bug: no case for seqlenq_ngroups_swapped. It takes the varlen case (h, total_q),
// so softmax_lse is stored as (num_heads_k, b, ngroups) instead of (num_heads_k, ngroups, b).
const index_t row_offset_lseaccum = (Split || !params.unpadded_lse ?
        ((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q : bidh * params.total_q + binfo.q_offset(params.seqlen_q, 1, bidb)
    ) + m_block * kBlockM;
```

## Reproduction

`repro.py` decodes one query for each of 3 sequences with 16, 64 and 256 keys, with 4 query heads on one KV head. With at most 256 keys, the split heuristic picks one split on any GPU.

```python
import torch
from flash_attn import flash_attn_varlen_func

torch.manual_seed(1)
b, h, d, lens = 3, 4, 64, [16, 64, 256]  # 3 sequences decoding one query each; 4 query heads share 1 KV head
q = torch.randn(b, h, d, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
k, v = torch.randn(2, b, 256, 1, d, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)  # one page of 256 keys per sequence
cu_q = torch.arange(b + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
cu_k = torch.tensor([0, 16, 80, 336], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")  # 16, 64 and 256 keys
block_table = torch.arange(b, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")[:, None]
_, lse, _ = flash_attn_varlen_func(q, k, v, cu_q, cu_k, 1, 256, return_attn_probs=True, block_table=block_table)
lse_ref = torch.stack([(q[i].float() @ k[i, :n, 0].float().T / d**0.5).logsumexp(-1) for i, n in enumerate(lens)], 1)
print("reference [head][seq]:", lse_ref.double().round(decimals=2).tolist())
print("returned  [head][seq]:", lse.double().round(decimals=2).tolist())
```

## Result

```
$ python repro.py
reference [head][seq]: [[2.65, 4.66, 5.97], [3.16, 5.07, 5.99], [2.99, 4.9, 5.88], [3.46, 4.42, 6.05]]
returned  [head][seq]: [[2.65, 3.16, 2.99], [3.46, 4.66, 5.07], [4.9, 4.42, 5.97], [5.99, 5.88, 6.05]]
```

Heads 0, 1 and 2 of sequence 0 come back as head 0 of sequences 0, 1 and 2. `out` is correct, and so is `softmax_lse` with two splits, which the combine kernel stores.

## Suggested Fix

Store the one-split `softmax_lse` through `get_lse_tile`:

```diff
     const index_t row_offset_oaccum = (((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q
                                          + m_block * kBlockM) * params.d_rounded;
-    const index_t row_offset_lseaccum = (Split || !params.unpadded_lse ?
-            ((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q : bidh * params.total_q + binfo.q_offset(params.seqlen_q, 1, bidb)
-        ) + m_block * kBlockM;
+    const index_t row_offset_lseaccum = ((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q + m_block * kBlockM;
 
     Tensor gOaccum = make_tensor(make_gmem_ptr(reinterpret_cast<ElementO *>(Split ? params.oaccum_ptr : params.o_ptr) + (Split ? row_offset_oaccum : row_offset_o)),
                                  Shape<Int<kBlockM>, Int<kHeadDim>>{},
                                  make_stride(Split ? kHeadDim : params.o_row_stride, _1{}));
-    Tensor gLSEaccum = make_tensor(make_gmem_ptr(reinterpret_cast<ElementAccum *>(Split ? params.softmax_lseaccum_ptr : params.softmax_lse_ptr) + row_offset_lseaccum),
-                                   Shape<Int<kBlockM>>{}, Stride<_1>{});
+    auto gLSEaccum = [&] {
+        if constexpr (Split) {
+            return make_tensor(make_gmem_ptr(reinterpret_cast<ElementAccum *>(params.softmax_lseaccum_ptr) + row_offset_lseaccum),
+                               Shape<Int<kBlockM>>{}, Stride<_1>{});
+        } else {
+            return get_lse_tile<ElementAccum, Params, kBlockM, Is_even_MN>(params, bidb, bidh, m_block, binfo);
+        }
+    }();
```

With the fix, `repro.py` prints the reference values:

```
reference [head][seq]: [[2.65, 4.66, 5.97], [3.16, 5.07, 5.99], [2.99, 4.9, 5.88], [3.46, 4.42, 6.05]]
returned  [head][seq]: [[2.65, 4.66, 5.97], [3.16, 5.07, 5.99], [2.99, 4.9, 5.88], [3.46, 4.42, 6.05]]
```

The early exit ([L552](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/965c9212e6be33c821ee9f2b461564c5c91a2503/csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_fwd_kernel.h#L552)) also stores `softmax_lse` without the transpose; #3004 changes that line. I can open a PR with this fix and a regression test.

items.title: Fully enable varlen split KV
items.body: **Context** today, for split KV varlen with paging, the input gets reshaped to include batch dimension before it hits the split KV kernel, so it's not actually varlen. this PR fully enables varlen split KV by keeping the ragged sequences. we need to modify the way we compute address indices to convert between rectangular and padded layouts. **What changed** in the combine kernel for split KV, the partial results for oaccum (partial weight output) + lseaccum (partial lse) get merged. first it reads the partial results from all splits and then writes the global result to the output lse/output tensors. but for varlen, we need to make sure that that the correct addresses are computed. we do this by using `cu_seqlens_q` to properly calculate the boundaries of the tensors to skip the padding rows. (the padding comes from here where the rectangular buffers get allocated) https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/8a8b2f10ddca88fd46db406c3e143e1ab0af977f/csrc/flash_attn/flash_api.cpp#L320-L321 **Testing**

items.title: New FA 2.7.4.post1 has much slower  flash_attn_with_kvcache
items.body:
I am using flash_attn_with_kvcache but when I upgrade to a new FA version it's much slower. You can see below my results from upgrading 2.4 to 2.7. It seems like the launch grid shapes have changed.  This is on H100 system.

Newer slower version:
```
Flash Attention version: 2.7.4.post1
Warming up...

Running 100 iterations...
Run: 0.668 ms/iter
Run: 0.667 ms/iter
Run: 0.666 ms/iter
Run: 0.668 ms/iter
Run: 0.667 ms/iter

Average: 0.667 ms/iter
Std dev: 0.001 ms
```

Older faster version:
```
Flash Attention version: 2.4.2.dev3
Warming up...

Running 100 iterations...
Run: 0.145 ms/iter
Run: 0.145 ms/iter
Run: 0.145 ms/iter
Run: 0.145 ms/iter
Run: 0.145 ms/iter

Average: 0.145 ms/iter
Std dev: 0.000 ms
```


here is my script to reproduce:
```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Simple benchmark script for flash_attn_with_kvcache with specific shapes.
"""

import torch
import time
import numpy as np

try:
    from flash_attn import flash_attn_with_kvcache
    import flash_attn
    print(f"Flash Attention version: {getattr(flash_attn, '__version__', 'Unknown')}")
except ImportError:
    print("Error: flash_attn not installed")
    exit(1)

device = 'cuda'
dtype = torch.bfloat16

q = torch.randn(64, 1, 16, 128, device=device, dtype=dtype)
k_cache = torch.randn(64, 8191, 2, 128, device=device, dtype=dtype)
v_cache = torch.randn(64, 8191, 2, 128, device=device, dtype=dtype)
k = torch.randn(64, 1, 2, 128, device=device, dtype=dtype)
v = torch.randn(64, 1, 2, 128, device=device, dtype=dtype)
rotary_cos = torch.randn(8191, 64, device=device, dtype=dtype)
rotary_sin = torch.randn(8191, 64, device=device, dtype=dtype)
cache_seqlens = torch.randint(1, 8191, (64,), device=device, dtype=torch.int32)

# Warmup
print("Warming up...")
for _ in range(10):
    out = flash_attn_with_kvcache(
        q=q,
        k_cache=k_cache,
        v_cache=v_cache,
        k=k,
        v=v,
        rotary_cos=rotary_cos,
        rotary_sin=rotary_sin,
        cache_seqlens=cache_seqlens,
        rotary_interleaved=False
    )
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

# Benchmark
num_iterations = 100
times = []

print(f"\nRunning {num_iterations} iterations...")
for _ in range(5):  # 5 runs
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    start = time.time()
    
    for _ in range(num_iterations):
        out = flash_attn_with_kvcache(
            q=q,
            k_cache=k_cache,
            v_cache=v_cache,
            k=k,
            v=v,
            rotary_cos=rotary_cos,
            rotary_sin=rotary_sin,
            cache_seqlens=cache_seqlens,
            rotary_interleaved=False
        )
    
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    elapsed = (time.time() - start) / num_iterations * 1000  # ms per iteration
    times.append(elapsed)
    print(f"Run: {elapsed:.3f} ms/iter")

print(f"\nAverage: {np.mean(times):.3f} ms/iter")
print(f"Std dev: {np.std(times):.3f} ms")

```
