items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Backward 2CTA: store the exchanged dS half in place, and sync_warp before the S_P / LSE arrivals
items.body:
Work done at Meshy by Yang Liu (@liuyang-05), authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).

1. `[CuTe, SM100] Backward 2CTA: store the exchanged dS half to sdS_xchg inside the stage loop`
2. `[CuTe, SM100] Backward 2CTA pipelined: sync_warp before the per-warp S_P / LSE arrivals`

Both apply to the pipelined 2CTA schedule (hdim <= 128, i.e. the default hdim 128 backward on SM100, dense
or block-sparse with 256-wide sparse KV blocks). The serial schedule (hdim 192) and the M=64 layout are
unchanged.

## Problem / root cause (commit 1)

In the pipelined 2CTA schedule each compute thread converts its dS row in two stages. The stage the peer CTA
needs (`exchange_stage = cta_rank ^ 1`, a run-time value) is copied into a 16-register fragment
(`tdPrdS_xchg`) and written to `sdS_xchg` only after the stage loop. Because the selecting value is only known
at run time, the fragment is live across the whole stage loop and the compiler carries it around the trip:

| compute loop per trip (SASS) | main | commit 1 |
|---|---|---|
| dense hdim 128 non-causal 8k | 548 instr, 51 MOV | 495 instr, 2 MOV |
| dense hdim 128 causal 8k | 583 instr, 52 MOV | 530 instr, 3 MOV |
| block-sparse causal mask_mod 8k, sparse block 256x256 | 1865 instr, 264 MOV, 34 STL / 35 LDL, STACK 144 | 1501 instr, 252 MOV, 14 STL / 15 LDL, STACK 56 |
| dense hdim 192 (serial schedule) | 547 instr | identical SASS |

(In a block-sparse kernel, where the compute warps are already short of registers, the extra 16 live
registers turn into spills.)

## Fix (commit 1)

Store the exchange stage straight to `sdS_xchg` where it is produced. `sdS_xchg` is free at that point for
the same reason it was free for the old post-loop store: both happen after the stage-0
`pipeline_dS.producer_acquire`, whose release follows the previous dQ MMA, which waited (through the relay
warp and the cluster-leader barrier) for both CTAs' exchange copies. Same bytes, same addresses, same ordering
w.r.t. the fence / barrier / DSMEM copy that follows. The serial schedule keeps the fragment because there
`sdS_xchg` aliases `sdQaccum` and the store has to wait for `dQaccum_empty`.

## Commit 2

After the P store, the compute warps hit a compute-wide barrier that only precedes the S_P release and the LSE
release. Both mbarriers count one arrival per compute warp (S_P: 8 warps x 2 CTAs, LSE: 8), so the mbarrier is
already the cross-warp join, exactly the argument NOTE [hdim64 dedicated P/dS TMEM slots] makes for
`split_P_dS`. In the pipelined 2CTA schedule P was already stored after its own P-over-S barrier (or to SMEM
with the M=64 layout), so there is nothing else to order: use `sync_warp`. The barrier before the dS commit
stays (it orders the `sdS_xchg` writes ahead of the single-thread DSMEM copy), and the serial schedule is
unchanged. SASS: BAR.SYNC per compute-loop trip 5 -> 4 (hdim 128); hdim 192 unchanged.

## Numbers

B200 (1000 W), bf16, hdim 128, backward only, one process with main (renamed copy), commit 1 and commit 1+2
interleaved, CUDA-event medians. Dense: 200 cycles, A/A control (main vs main, same job) within +-0.2%
(job 366794). Block-sparse: batch 1, 16 heads, sparse block 256x256 (2CTA), 30 cycles (job 366788).

| case | main ms | commit 1 | commit 1+2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| dense non-causal 8k (B=2, H=16) | 2.266 | 2.264 (-0.1%) | 2.251 (-0.7%) |
| dense non-causal 16k (B=1, H=16) | 4.368 | 4.335 (-0.8%) | 4.314 (-1.2%) |
| dense non-causal 32k (B=1, H=16) | 17.055 | 17.064 (+0.1%) | 16.996 (-0.3%) |
| dense causal 8k | 1.316 | 1.279 (-2.8%) | 1.269 (-3.6%) |
| dense causal 16k | 2.403 | 2.318 (-3.5%) | 2.303 (-4.2%) |
| dense GQA 16/4 heads 4k | 0.666 | 0.644 (-3.3%) | 0.643 (-3.5%) |
| dense unaligned 8000 | 2.232 | 2.231 (-0.0%) | 2.219 (-0.6%) |
| block-sparse causal mask_mod 32k | 11.619 | 9.567 (-17.7%) | 9.481 (-18.4%) |
| block-sparse prefix 4k + block-causal 2k 32k | 13.331 | 11.811 (-11.4%) | 11.761 (-11.8%) |
| block-sparse sliding window 2k 32k | 1.894 | 1.665 (-12.1%) | 1.656 (-12.6%) |
| block-sparse document 32k | 4.796 | 4.727 (-1.4%) | 4.716 (-1.7%) |
| dense hdim 192 4k (serial) | 0.887 | 0.889 (+0.1%) | 0.886 (-0.1%) |
| dense hdim 64 8k (1CTA) | 1.647 | 1.648 (+0.1%) | 1.653 (+0.3%) |

A repeat on another node (job 366745, n=30) gives the same picture (causal 8k -2.9% / -3.6%, GQA -3.3% /
-3.3%, block-sparse causal -17.5% / -18.1%).

## Tests

B200, cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, both commits applied (and commit 1 alone, same results); per-test
outcomes compared with main on the same selection:

| selection | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_flash_attn_output`: hdim 64/128/192, MHA+GQA, causal, local_enum 0/1, deterministic on/off, softcap 0 (+15 for hdim 128 MHA), all 26 seqlen pairs (1456 ids) | 1092 passed, 364 skipped | identical |
| `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` (hdim 64/128/192, MHA, random varlen, det on/off; 252 ids) + `test_flash_attn_bwd_tile_n.py` (M=64 layout, 2CTA) | 344 passed, 24 skipped | identical |
| `tests/cute/test_mask_mod.py` | 835 passed, 748 skipped | identical |

Bitwise check against main in one process (`fa4pr.py check all-check`, 39 cases, final job 366881; earlier
366712, 366739, 366805): `out` / `lse` / `dk` / `dv` bitwise and `dq` (and GQA `dk` / `dv`, which are accumulated with fp32 atomics) within main's own run-to-run variation: every element within one bf16 ulp of its magnitude (2^-14 absolute near zero), with the same max difference and fraction of differing elements (1e-5 to 1e-4) as main against itself over 6 repeats, on dense hdim 128 (aligned,
unaligned 8000 / 1000, causal, GQA, deterministic incl. dq bitwise, varlen), hdim 192 (serial, unchanged
binary), hdim 64, and block-sparse 2CTA causal / document / prefix-block-causal mask_mods incl. GQA. GQA
dK / dV are accumulated with fp32 atomics and differ run to run by up to 1 bf16 ulp on main itself; they
are compared at that granularity.

Commands:

```
python fa4pr.py check all-check
python fa4pr.py bench d128_8k,d128_16k,d128_32k,d128_8k_causal,d128_16k_causal,d128_4k_gqa,d128_8000 --what bwd --cycles 200 --pkgs base,test,alt
python fa4pr.py bench bs2_causal_32k,bs2_doc_32k,bs2_pbc_32k,bs2_swa2k_32k,d192_4k,d64_8k --what bwd --cycles 30 --pkgs base,test,alt
pytest -n 8 @sel_fa_output.txt
pytest -n 8 @sel_fa_varlen.txt tests/cute/test_flash_attn_bwd_tile_n.py
pytest -n 8 tests/cute/test_mask_mod.py
```

The detailed tables above were measured on e9d8944c. After the rebase:

the `test_flash_attn_output` bwd selection (1456 ids, re-collected on 98c1cee0) + `test_flash_attn_bwd_tile_n.py`
1184 / 388 (jobs 425826 / 425830); `test_flash_attn_hd256_bwd.py` 88 / 8 both with the dedicated hd256

Not re-measured on 98c1cee0: SASS and perf (the patch is unchanged and applied without conflicts; the latest
SASS / perf numbers are the e7a6402a ones above). #2967 and #3012 do edit flash_bwd_sm100.py elsewhere, so the
test and bitwise results above are the evidence that they do not interact.

- Not included: letting the relay warp issue the DSMEM copy so that the last compute-wide barrier (before

items.title: [CuTe, Bwd, SM100] hdim128 2CTA: issue Q before Qt, start dQ reduce-adds after the dS exchange
items.body:
Stacked PRs:
 * __->__#3099
 * #3098
 * #3087
 * #3086

--- --- ---

## Human Note

## Agent Notes

**Summary:** in the hdim128 2-CTA backward, the Q(m) fill and the dS(m) exchange copy queue in the TMA unit behind the dQ(m-1) reduce-adds. This change issues Q(m) before Qt(m-1) and starts the dQ reduce-adds only after the next dS exchange copy is issued (`BwdConfig.dQ_after_dS_xchg`). GB300 1.014x geomean (1.006-1.023), B300 1.014x, B200 1.008x; dK/dV bitwise unchanged.

Issue order on one CTA for M block m (TMA serves bulk copies roughly in issue order):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    title Before
    participant L as Load warp
    participant C as Compute (dS)
    participant R as Reduce warp
    participant T as TMA unit
    participant M as MMA warp
    M->>L: dK(m-2) done, frees the Qt stage
    L->>T: Qt(m-1)
    R->>T: dQ(m-1) reduce-adds
    L->>T: Q(m), queued behind the reduce-adds
    C->>T: dS(m) exchange copy, queued behind the reduce-adds
    T-->>M: Q(m) late, so S(m) starts late
    T-->>M: dS(m) late, so dQ(m) starts late
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    title After (dQ_after_dS_xchg)
    participant L as Load warp
    participant C as Compute (dS)
    participant R as Reduce warp
    participant T as TMA unit
    participant M as MMA warp
    L->>T: Q(m), no wait on the Qt acquire
    C->>T: dS(m) exchange copy
    C->>R: dS_xchg_issued = m (SMEM counter)
    R->>T: dQ(m-1) reduce-adds, after the counter reaches m
    M->>L: dK(m-2) done
    L->>T: Qt(m-1)
    T-->>M: Q(m) and dS(m) arrive ahead of the reduce-adds
```


In the pipelined 2-CTA schedule (hdim128), the MMA warp spends most of its time in mbarrier
waits. Clock64 timelines on B300 show the critical chain:
1. The load warp issues the Q(m) fill for S(m) only after the Qt(m-1) acquire, which waits for
   dK(m-2).
2. The fill then queues in the per-SM TMA unit behind the dQ(m-1) bulk reduce-adds. The TMA
   unit serves bulk copies roughly in issue order.
3. Those reduce-adds also run ahead of the dS(m) DSMEM exchange copy, which sits on the
   dS -> dQ MMA path.

A timing-only probe that removes the reduce-adds (wrong output) makes the step 1.08x faster.

This change makes two ordering changes and adds no bulk tensor traffic (only a 32-bit SMEM counter) and no registers:
- **Load warp:** Q(m) is issued before Qt(m-1), so the Q fill no longer waits for the Qt acquire.
- **Reduce warp:** the first reduce-add of dQ(i) waits until the compute thread has issued the
  dS(i+1) exchange copy. A monotonic SMEM counter `dS_xchg_issued`, written with
  `st.volatile.shared` and polled with `ld.volatile.shared`, carries the signal. The last tile is
  not gated.

The counter is a timing hint only. The reduce warp reads no dS data, so relaxed volatile
accesses are enough.

The gate is config policy: `BwdConfig.dQ_after_dS_xchg`, chosen by `select_bwd_config` through
`can_use_dQ_after_dS_xchg`. It is on for the SM100 / SM110 generic kernel's pipelined 2CTA schedule
(2CTA, head_dim not padded to 192 or 256, i.e. hdim128) in non-deterministic runs: in
deterministic mode the serialized dQ adds across CTAs bind and both orderings measured slower.
`validate_bwd_config` rejects it anywhere else, and it holds False on SM90 / SM120. The kernel
takes the field as a constructor argument and asserts the pipelined schedule; the config is in the
compile key. When off, the counter is a zero-size struct member and the SASS is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- **Liveness:** every compute iteration issues the exchange copy and bumps the counter, including
  for out-of-bounds m_blocks. Both loops take `loop_count` from the same function, with or
  without block sparsity. The dQ TMEM release happens before the gate, and in the pipelined
  schedule `sdS_xchg` does not alias `sdQaccum`, so the reduce warp cannot block its own producer.
- **compute-sanitizer racecheck:** it reports one extra hazard, on the counter itself: the
  compute thread's STS against the reduce warp's polling LDS. The race is intended, since the
  value only gates timing. The two pre-existing hdim128 hazards are unchanged.
- **Rejected alternatives:**
  - a fixed-delay reducer deferral: it has a cliff, from 1.01x at 1024 clk to 0.87x at 2048;
  - gating on the dO issue: 1.00x;
  - a second Q stage: it fits, but measured 0.97x.

</details>

## Performance

hdim128, non-deterministic, 24 cells per GPU: bf16 and fp16 x MHA 32/32 and GQA 32/8 x causal on
and off x S 4k/8k/16k at B 4/2/1. Speedup = time without the change / time with it (higher is
better).
- **duty** = CUDA-graph replays with 50 ms idle (per clock); median of 3 interleaved
  fresh-process trials.
- **sustained** = 1.5 s of back-to-back replays at the power cap; median of 5 trials.

B200 / B300 were measured with the same kernel change on main (`4616f511`); GB300 on this stack.

| GPU | duty geomean | duty per-cell range | sustained geomean | sustained per-cell range |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| B200 | 1.008 | 1.002-1.013 | 1.006 | 1.000-1.012 |
| B300 | 1.014 | 1.005-1.026 | 1.006 | 0.997-1.013 |
| GB300 | 1.014 | 1.006-1.023 | — | — |

GB300 ran duty only (this stack); 20 back-to-back replays give geomean 1.016 (1.008-1.037). The
largest gains are on GQA and non-causal cells: bf16 GQA non-causal is 1.023-1.025 duty on B300 and
1.018-1.023 on GB300.
At the power cap the sustained gain is smaller, because the arm draws the same power and runs a
few MHz lower. The deterministic cells and all hdim64 cells run unchanged SASS.

## Validation

- **Codegen:** compile-only capture over ~1100 SM100 / SM103 backward call specs: the
  `dQ_after_dS_xchg` decision equals the kernel-internal rule it replaces in every spec.
- **Cubins:** the same 22 configs as the parent commit. With the change on (6: bf16 / fp16, MHA /
  GQA, causal / none, varlen, tile_n=64, SM103), the main backward cubin is byte-identical to the
  same kernel change on main with its kernel-internal gate; the 5 fold configs are unchanged, and
  the 11 configs with both levers off (fp16, GQA, deterministic, softcap, hdim 192 / 256, 1-CTA
  hdim128) are byte-identical to `2a11f3ed`.
- **SASS (B200 / B300, same kernel change on main):** 32 configs. The backward kernel's SASS
  differs from the parent commit only at hdim128 non-deterministic, and is unchanged in
  deterministic mode.
- **Bitwise (B200 / B300):** dK / dV are bitwise equal with and without the change in every
  hdim128 cell. Deterministic dQ is bitwise equal. Non-deterministic dQ order-dependent bits
  differ, as between any two runs.
- **Tests (GB300, at the tip of this two-commit change and at its parent `2a11f3ed`, same
  selection, xdist 24 workers on 2 GPUs):** `test_flash_attn_output` at d 64/128 (9984 ids), a 1/64
  sample of `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` at d 64/128 (3024), the other test_flash_attn.py
  backward tests (122), `test_flash_attn_varlen.py` at D 64/128 (3888), the race-condition
  (deterministic) tests at d 64/128 (1248), bwd pack_gqa / tile_n (717), score_mod backward (331),
  hd256 backward (96), and test_bwd_config. The first pass hit OOM / reference-kernel errors at
  12 workers per GPU on both trees; rerunning the union of those ids (1048) at 2 workers per GPU,
  both trees fail only the same 8 learnable-sink dSink tolerance ids.

items.title: [FA2] Write a caller-provided out in place on the varlen decode path
items.body:
## What we fixed

`mha_varlen_fwd` accepts an optional `out` tensor. On the varlen decode path it ignores it: the
attention result is written into a temporary, and the buffer the caller passed in is never
touched. The function returns the temporary, so a caller that uses the return value sees nothing
wrong. A caller that passes a buffer and reads *that buffer* gets whatever was there before.

That is the bug. `out` is an output parameter, and on this path it does nothing.

The path in question is the decode fast path guarded by `seqlenq_ngroups_swapped`, which applies
when all of these hold:

- `max_seqlen_q == 1` — one query token per sequence, i.e. uniform decode (not prefill, not a
  mixed prefill+decode step)
- `num_heads > num_heads_k` — GQA or MQA; plain MHA has no groups to swap
- `window_size_left < 0 && window_size_right < 0` — full attention, no sliding window
- `p_dropout == 0`, no alibi

`causal=True` does not opt out. The function sets `is_causal = false` when `max_seqlen_q == 1`
(causal masking over a single query token is a no-op) before it tests the window bounds, so a
causal GQA decode still takes this path.

This is the ordinary configuration for full-attention GQA models (LLaMA/Qwen-style) served with a
preallocated output buffer. vLLM runs FA2 exactly this way — it passes `out=output`, ignores the
return value, and reads `output`. It also captures FA2 CUDA graphs with `max_query_len=1`
specifically to exploit this packed-GQA decode path.

## How we fixed it

The swap reorders the head axis, so the kernel's output layout is not the caller's:

```cpp
q = q.reshape({batch, num_heads_k, ngroups, d}).transpose(1, 2)
     .reshape({batch * ngroups, num_heads_k, d});
```

The kernel addresses the output as `(batch, row, head)` where `row` is the swapped `seqlen_q`.
Element `(row r, head h)` belongs at original head `h * ngroups + r`.

The current code sidesteps that by writing into a swapped temporary and fixing it up afterwards:

```cpp
out = out.reshape({batch, num_heads_k, ngroups, d})
         .transpose(1, 2)
         .reshape({batch * ngroups, num_heads_k, d});
```

`transpose` makes the tensor non-contiguous, so that trailing `reshape` **copies**. The kernels
write the copy; nothing copies back into `out_`. That is where the caller's buffer gets dropped.

The fix is to hand the kernels the caller's buffer and tell them its strides. Two changes:

**1.** Produce `out` in the final `[batch, num_heads_k, ngroups, head_size]` layout, for both the
`out`-provided and `out=None` cases. The `out` view is a pure view of the caller's tensor — no
copy.

**2.** After `set_params_fprop`, override the three output strides:

```cpp
if (seqlenq_ngroups_swapped) {
    params.o_batch_stride = out.stride(0);
    params.o_head_stride  = out.stride(1);
    params.o_row_stride   = out.stride(2);
}
```

The override is required rather than cosmetic. `set_params_fprop` derives the output strides
from the packed `q` layout, where head is the middle dimension — which describes a different
tensor. Reading them off the 4-D view gives row stride `d` and head stride `ngroups * d`, so
`r * o_row_stride + h * o_head_stride == (h * ngroups + r) * d`, i.e. original head
`h * ngroups + r`. That is exactly what the kernel's `(batch, row, head)` indices expect.

With the kernels writing the caller's buffer directly, the post-kernel fixup collapses to a view:

```cpp
out = out.reshape(size_after);
```

**Behavior change:** a caller-provided `out` must now be contiguous, checked explicitly with a
clear message. This is not a new requirement — the old code already called `reshape`/`view` on
the caller's tensor, which throws on a non-contiguous input, so every `out` that worked before
still works. The check only turns a confusing late failure inside `reshape` into an explicit one.

## Correctness evidence

RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, `FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=120`.

- **`out` is written, and is bitwise identical to the `out=None` result.** 108 configurations:
  paged/dense × fp16/bf16 × batch 1/8/16 × GQA (heads/heads_k) 8/2, 24/4, 32/8 × head_size
  64/128/256 × seqlen_k 2048/4096. Each case prefills `out` with NaN and asserts
  `torch.equal(out, ref)`, `torch.equal(returned, ref)`, and that no NaN survives.
- **`compute-sanitizer --tool=memcheck`: 0 errors** on the direct-write path.
- **The new test fails on current `main`** with `"out was not written; the output path made a
  copy"`, and passes with this change. No existing test passed `out=` to the varlen entry point.
- **No regressions:** `pytest tests/test_flash_attn.py -k "varlen and not determinist"` →
  **78347 passed, 23232 skipped, 0 failed**. Dense and non-swapped varlen paths, causal and
  sliding-window configs verified separately.

```bash
FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=120 MAX_JOBS=10 python setup.py build_ext --inplace
python -m pytest tests/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_varlen_swapped_gqa_honors_out -q
python -m pytest tests/test_flash_attn.py -q -k "varlen and not determinist"
compute-sanitizer --tool=memcheck python repro.py
```

## Performance

The change removes one device-to-device copy of the output and one temporary allocation per
call. Kernel-level, `seqlen_q=1`, GQA 24/4, `head_size=256`, bf16, median of 7 runs × 50
CUDA-event iterations:

| shape | before | after | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| b=1, k=4096 | 23.67 µs | 20.48 µs | −13.5% |
| b=8, k=4096 | 42.61 µs | 40.72 µs | −4.4% |
| b=16, k=2048 | 52.80 µs | 50.74 µs | −3.9% |
| b=32, k=4096 | 345.53 µs | 343.27 µs | −0.7% |

The saving is small but real and it is more API correct.

## Scope

One function, `mha_varlen_fwd`.

If you would like me to look at `mha_fwd`, and `mha_fwd_kvcache`, I can. 

## AI assistance

I used pi with DeepSeek 4.1 flash to help implement and validate the change.
I discovered the bug when validating fa2 performance improvements in vllm with Qwen 3.8 27b.

---

### Aside: nearby work

These were found when I was looking to see if someone had already submitted the fix. These are not prerequisites for this PR. 

- **`vllm-project/flash-attention` `04325b6`** (vllm#32, Woosuk Kwon, 2024-12) is a downstream
  workaround for this exact bug: allocate an `empty_like` temporary and `copy_` it back into
  `out_`, noting that `out.reshape(size_after)` "causes a redundant clone operation". Correct,
  but pays a full copy per call. Landing this upstream lets that fork drop the workaround instead
  of replaying it at each sync.
- **#708** (open since 2023-12) saves `ori_seqlen_q` in `mha_fwd_kvcache` to avoid a spurious
  `TORCH_CHECK`. Different function, different defect, not touched here.
- **#848** (open since 2024-02) reports passing `out` to `mha_fwd` failing when `seqlen_q == 1`.
  Different entry point, not addressed here. This PR does not close it.
- **#976** (merged) fixed the `CHECK_SHAPE` on a caller-provided `out` after `seqlen_q` is
  overwritten. This PR keeps that validation. #976 stopped this path from *throwing*; it did not
  make it *work* — the reshape chain still copied, so the caller's buffer stayed empty.
- **#2573** (open) fixes a SplitKV early-exit LSE offset in `flash_fwd_kernel.h`. Kernel-side, no
  overlap.

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Backward: condition mask_seqlen on tile-aligned sequence lengths
items.body:
Work done at Meshy by Yang Liu (@liuyang-05), authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).

## Problem

`FlashAttentionBackwardSm100.compute_loop` masks every S tile with `mask_seqlen=True`
(`# TODO: condition mask_seqlen`). The sequence-bound code in `apply_mask_sm100_transposed` is per element
and is compiled into every trip of the compute loop, even for shapes where no tile can ever reach past
`seqlen_q` / `seqlen_k`:

- block-sparse with a mask_mod: on full blocks, the per-element Q / K bound checks under the run-time
  `check_m_boundary`, which ptxas if-converts into SEL / ISETP for every element of every tile; on partial
  blocks, the bound checks after mask_mod plus the fastdiv wrap of the aux-tensor indices;
- dense non-causal: the per-KV-row bound check (64 SEL per trip);
- dense causal / local: the `seqlenk_col_limit <= 0` row-limit override.

For block-sparse mask_mod backward this is the largest single cost in the compute warps: the loop does not
fit the 128-register budget and spills.

## Root cause (SASS)

cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, B200, `cuobjdump -sass` + `sass_loops.py` (per-trip counts of the compute-warp loop):

| config | main: instr / STL / LDL / SEL / ISETP | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| block-sparse causal mask_mod, 1CTA (sparse block 256x128), 8k | 1855 / 47 / 38 / 384 / 207 | 706 / 0 / 0 / 64 / 64 |
| block-sparse causal mask_mod, 2CTA (256x256), 8k | 1865 / 34 / 35 / 384 / 201 | 793 / 0 / 0 / 64 / 65 |
| dense hdim 128 non-causal (2CTA), 8k | 548 / 0 / 0 / 64 / 0 | 480 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| dense hdim 64 non-causal (1CTA), 8k | 449 / 0 / 0 / 64 / 1 | 380 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| dense hdim 192 non-causal (2CTA serial), 4k | 547 / 0 / 0 / 64 / 0 | 479 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| dense hdim 128 causal, 8k | 583 / 0 / 0 / 65 / 5 | 573 / 0 / 0 / 64 / 2 |

Kernel-wide: block-sparse 1CTA STACK 168 -> 0, 2CTA STACK 144 -> 8 (one spill outside the loop).

## Fix

`_flash_attn_bwd` knows the sequence lengths of fixed-length inputs. When there is no `cu_seqlens_*` /
`seqused_*`, `seqlen_q` is a multiple of the Q tile (of the sparse Q block, `m_block_size *
q_subtile_factor`, with block sparsity) and `seqlen_k` is a multiple of the KV tile times the cluster size
(`n_block_size * cluster_size`, so the extra KV tile a 2CTA cluster pads to does not exist either), then no
tile has an out-of-bounds row or column. In that case the kernel is built with `mask_seqlen=False`, a new
`FlashAttentionBackwardSm100` constructor argument that is part of the compile key. Every other case
(varlen, seqused, unaligned) passes `mask_seqlen=True` and traces exactly the same code as before.

Alternative considered: deciding at run time and masking only the last m / n block. That would also
help unaligned shapes, but keeping the code out of the other trips needs a second copy of the compute loop
(a run-time branch inside the loop is if-converted back into every trip, which is how the full-block
`check_m_boundary` branch ends up as SELs today). The compile-time condition is a three-line host check, keeps
one loop, and costs one more compiled variant per configuration (aligned vs. not).

## Numbers

B200 (1000 W), bf16, backward only, one process with main (imported as a renamed copy) and this PR
interleaved, CUDA-event medians. Block-sparse: hdim 128, batch 1, 16 heads, 30 cycles (job 366786). Dense:
200 cycles plus a same-process A/A control (main vs main) on three of the shapes, within +-0.1% (job 366795).

| case | main ms | this PR ms | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| block-sparse causal mask_mod 32k, 1CTA | 11.935 | 9.676 | -18.9% |
| block-sparse document mask_mod 32k, 1CTA | 4.945 | 3.528 | -28.7% |
| block-sparse prefix 4k + block-causal 2k 32k, 1CTA | 12.524 | 10.515 | -16.1% |
| block-sparse sliding window 2k 32k, 1CTA | 1.909 | 1.603 | -16.0% |
| block-sparse causal mask_mod 32k, 2CTA | 11.605 | 9.239 | -20.4% |
| block-sparse document mask_mod 32k, 2CTA | 4.934 | 3.547 | -28.1% |
| block-sparse prefix + block-causal 32k, 2CTA | 13.738 | 9.791 | -28.7% |
| block-sparse sliding window 2k 32k, 2CTA | 1.711 | 1.459 | -14.8% |
| dense hdim 128 causal 8k (B=2) / 16k (B=1) | 1.341 / 2.494 | 1.295 / 2.392 | -3.4% / -4.1% |
| dense hdim 64 non-causal 8k / 16k | 1.693 / 3.346 | 1.643 / 3.204 | -3.0% / -4.2% |
| dense hdim 64 causal 16k | 1.743 | 1.733 | -0.6% |
| dense hdim 128 GQA 16/4 heads 4k | 0.686 | 0.666 | -2.9% |
| dense hdim 128 non-causal 8k / 16k | 2.330 / 4.487 | 2.319 / 4.479 | -0.5% / -0.2% |
| dense hdim 96 non-causal 8k | 2.065 | 2.062 | -0.1% |
| dense hdim 128 unaligned 8000 (unchanged kernel) | 2.284 | 2.283 | -0.0% |

So dense backward also benefits on aligned shapes, most visibly causal hdim 128, hdim 64 and GQA (on main 98c1cee0, whose backward packs the query heads for that GQA shape, the GQA gain is now within noise; see the re-validation below); hdim 128
non-causal is within noise even though its loop loses its 64 SELs. Earlier runs on other nodes (jobs 366750,
366786; n=30) agree: dense causal 8k -2.5% / -2.4%, hdim 64 8k -2.6% / -4.3%, GQA -2.2% / -2.2%.

Combined with the two other block-sparse backward PRs of this series (split partial/full loops, 2CTA dS
exchange) the block-sparse 2CTA backward at 32k goes from 13.75 / 11.70 / 4.88 ms to 8.52 / 8.23 / 3.06 ms
(prefix-block-causal / causal / document; job 366813), see the series summary.

## Tests

B200, cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130; per-test outcomes compared with main run on the same selection:

| selection | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_flash_attn_output`: hdim 64/128/192, MHA+GQA, causal, local_enum 0/1, deterministic on/off, softcap 0 (+15 for hdim 128 MHA), all 26 seqlen pairs (1456 ids) | 1092 passed, 364 skipped | identical |
| `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` (hdim 64/128/192, MHA, random varlen, det on/off; 252 ids) + `test_flash_attn_bwd_tile_n.py` | 344 passed, 24 skipped | identical |
| `tests/cute/test_mask_mod.py` | 835 passed, 748 skipped | identical |
| `tests/cute/test_block_sparsity.py` | 4883 passed, 40 skipped | identical |

Bitwise check against main in one process (`fa4pr.py check all-check`, 39 cases, final job 366878; earlier
366711, 366738): `out` / `lse` / `dk` / `dv` bitwise equal and `dq` (and GQA `dk` / `dv`, which are accumulated with fp32 atomics) within main's own run-to-run variation: every element within one bf16 ulp of its magnitude (2^-14 absolute near zero), with the same max difference and fraction of differing elements (1e-5 to 1e-4) as main against itself over 6 repeats, on dense hdim 64 /
96 / 128 / 192, causal and not, aligned (8k, 4k) and unaligned (8000, 1000) lengths, GQA, deterministic
(dq bitwise too), varlen, and block-sparse causal / document / sliding-window / prefix-block-causal
mask_mods on 1CTA and 2CTA tables at 8k and 8000.

Commands:

```
python fa4pr.py check all-check
```

items.title: [CuTe, Bwd, SM100] Fix dV epilogue for asymmetric head dimensions
items.body:
Fixes #2552.

## Summary

Public API accepts asymmetric head dims such as `(Dqk, Dv) = (128, 96)`, but SM100 backward can return wrong **dV** while forward stays correct. Training with supported shapes can fail silently ([#2552](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/issues/2552)).

**Root cause.** In `epilogue_dK_or_dV_tma` each compute warpgroup owns `tile_hdimv // 2` TMEM columns (48 when `Dv = 96`). GMEM layout already uses 16-column epilogue subtiles (`sdV_epi_tile[1] = gcd(64, 48) = 16`, so `num_epi_stages_v = 3`), but the TMEM load atom reused the Q/K width (`dK_reduce_ncol = 32`). Each epilogue stage issues one `Ld32x32b` transfer indexed by stage id, so stage *i* reads TMEM columns `[32i, 32i+32)` instead of `[16i, 16i+16)`. Stages 1–2 therefore pull the wrong columns; stage 2 also reads past the warpgroup’s 48 columns. **dV** is wrong on both MHA (TMA store path) and GQA (FP32 `cpasync_reduce_bulk_add` path). dK stays correct when `Dqk = 128` because 64 columns per warpgroup remain aligned with 32-column loads.

**Fix.** Derive `dV_reduce_ncol = gcd(32, tile_hdimv // 2)` independently (16 for `Dv = 96`). Update dV FP32 staging layout, TMEM load atom, and `tma_copy_bytes["dVacc"]` together. Separately, on **2CTA** only, widen `sV` allocation when narrow `Dv` makes FP32 GQA staging larger than the BF16 `V` tile (`sV_alloc_bytes = max(sV_bytes, sdV_bytes)`).

**GQA shared-memory** (`tile_n = 128`; FP32 staging `tile_n × reduce_ncol × 2 × 4` vs BF16 `tile_n × Dv × 2`):

| `Dv` | `reduce_ncol` (before → after) | sdV | sV | Outcome |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 96 | 32 → 16 | 32 KiB → 16 KiB | 24 KiB | smem assertion fixed by width alone |
| 32 | 32 → 16 | 32 KiB → 16 KiB | 8 KiB | needs `max()` (+8 KiB smem, 2CTA GQA narrow-V only) |

Public APIs and return types are unchanged.

Adapts @guoriyue's independent-width approach from [#2780](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2780) (closed pending B200/B300 validation; see [comment](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2780#issuecomment-5249935357)).

## Correctness

B200, baseline [3451a2a](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/commit/3451a2a67a24eeed8af54d3c5b8d219577113797).

BF16, causal, `(Dqk, Dv) = (128, 96)`. Max abs error vs FP64 reference.

| `(B, Sq, Sk, Hq, Hkv)` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(1,129,257,4,4)` MHA | dV **1.107** | **0.00293** |
| `(1,129,257,4,2)` GQA | smem assertion | dV **0.00303** |
| `(2,1024,1024,16,16)` MHA (issue shape) | dV **7.542** | **0.0175** |
| `(2,1024,1024,16,8)` GQA | smem assertion | dV **0.0182** |

10/10 fail baseline, 10/10 pass patched per config. Full protocol, SASS diff, neutral control, and provenance: [issue-2552 data index](https://github.com/fusheng-ji/flash-attention/blob/64a0241e3abbaac251afd9beb354b974f4ec5c26/issue-2552/README.md) (pinned `pr_asset` commit).

## Tests

```bash
pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k sm100_asymmetric_backward
pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn_fast.py \
  -k '(test_flash_attn_output or test_flash_attn_varlen_output) and 256 and not -3-'
```

- **50** `sm100_asymmetric_backward` GPU cases (24 main-matrix BF16 + 26 edges).
- **24** existing backward cases from `test_flash_attn_fast.py`.

The published data index records the earlier 74-case FP16/BF16 campaign; the current PR contains the 50-case selection listed above.

New cases support FakeTensor compile pass. Ruff check/format clean on touched `flash_attn/cute` files.

## Performance

14 working BF16 controls (`B=2`, `Sq=Sk=2048`, `Hq=8`): complete-backward median **−0.79% to +1.16%**, none above 5% threshold. Measured at kernel commit [`259d0ae`](https://github.com/fusheng-ji/flash-attention/commit/259d0ae21021f335a775e5e91cbabbbd249cb54e); later test-only edits do not change codegen. Details: [benchmark CSV + protocol](https://github.com/fusheng-ji/flash-attention/blob/64a0241e3abbaac251afd9beb354b974f4ec5c26/issue-2552/README.md#performance-protocol).

## Limitations

Validation covers B200/SM100. B300 (SM103), SM110, and the full parameterized suite were not exercised. Performance conclusions cover only the 14 listed controls.

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Block-sparse backward: separate loops for partial and full Q blocks (+ 1CTA sync_warp)
items.body:
Work done at Meshy by Yang Liu (@liuyang-05), authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).

1. `[CuTe, SM100] Block-sparse backward: walk partial and full Q blocks in separate loops`
2. `[CuTe, SM100] Backward 1CTA: sync_warp before the per-warp S_P / LSE and dS / dPsum arrivals`

Commit 1 is best reviewed with whitespace changes hidden (`git show -w`, `?w=1`): the loop body is only
re-indented under a two-iteration `range_constexpr`; the real change is ~35 lines at the loop head.

## Problem / root cause (commit 1)

With a mask_mod, the block-sparse backward compute warps walk a KV tile's partial Q blocks and then its full
ones in one loop. `get_m_block_from_iter_bwd` returns a run-time `is_full_block`, and
`apply_mask_sm100_transposed` branches on it inside every trip, so both the mask_mod path and the full-block
path are compiled into the loop body. The full blocks, typically the majority, carry the mask_mod code (aux
tensor loads, per-element mask_mod calls) through register allocation, and the loop spills:

| compute loop(s) per trip (SASS), document mask_mod 8k | main | commit 1 |
|---|---|---|
| 1CTA (sparse block 256x128) | one loop: 2879 instr, 48 STL / 42 LDL, 449 MOV | partial loop 1962 instr, 16 / 15, 10 MOV; full loop 739 instr, 0 / 0, 14 MOV |
| 2CTA (sparse block 256x256) | one loop: 2849 instr, 35 STL / 36 LDL, 307 MOV | partial 2127 instr, 8 / 8; full 813 instr, 0 / 0 |
| 1CTA causal mask_mod (with commit 2) | one loop: 1855 instr, 47 / 38 | partial 777 instr, 0 / 0; full 740 instr, 0 / 0 |

## Fix (commit 1)

Run the same iteration space as two loops, `[0, num_partial)` and `[num_partial, total)`, under a
`range_constexpr` over the two phases, with `is_full_block` a compile-time constant in each, so the full-block
loop has no mask_mod code at all. The m_block of each iteration is read directly from the partial or the full
index list. Iteration order, m_block values, and the per-tile pipeline protocol are unchanged (the load, MMA
and dQ reduce warps walk the same lists in the same order), so `out` / `lse` / `dk` / `dv` stay bitwise
identical and `dq` stays within its run-to-run spread. Only the block-sparse backward with a mask_mod, no
causal / local, and full-block lists takes the split; every other configuration traces the original single
loop (dense SASS identical to main, verified for hdim 128).

## Commit 2

Two compute-wide barriers per trip only precede mbarrier arrivals that already count one arrival per
compute warp: before the S_P / LSE release and before the dS commit / dPsum release. NOTE [hdim64 dedicated
P/dS TMEM slots] already turned them into `sync_warp` for `split_P_dS`; the same argument holds for every 1CTA
configuration, because the aliased layout keeps its own P-over-S and dS-over-dP barriers and only 2CTA needs
the barrier before the dS commit (sdS_xchg / DSMEM copy ordering). The NOTE is updated accordingly.
SASS: BAR.SYNC per compute-loop trip 5 -> 3 on 1CTA loops (block-sparse with 128-wide sparse KV blocks,
dense hdim 96); 2CTA loops unchanged.

## Numbers

B200 (1000 W), bf16, hdim 128, batch 1, 16 heads, backward only, one process with main (renamed copy),
commit 1 and commit 1+2 interleaved, 30 cycles, CUDA-event medians (job 366787); same-process A/A control
(main vs main) +0.0% / +0.2%.

| case (32k) | main ms | commit 1 | commit 1+2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| causal mask_mod, 1CTA | 11.812 | 9.814 (-16.9%) | 9.645 (-18.3%) |
| document mask_mod, 1CTA | 4.813 | 3.761 (-21.9%) | 3.697 (-23.2%) |
| prefix 4k + block-causal 2k, 1CTA | 12.476 | 10.381 (-16.8%) | 10.274 (-17.7%) |
| sliding window 2k, 1CTA | 1.775 | 1.527 (-14.0%) | 1.503 (-15.3%) |
| causal mask_mod, 2CTA | 11.438 | 9.232 (-19.3%) | 9.171 (-19.8%) |
| document mask_mod, 2CTA | 4.818 | 3.923 (-18.6%) | 3.908 (-18.9%) |
| prefix + block-causal, 2CTA | 13.514 | 9.706 (-28.2%) | 9.643 (-28.6%) |
| sliding window 2k, 2CTA | 1.838 | 1.518 (-17.4%) | 1.511 (-17.8%) |
| causal mask_mod 4k GQA 16/4, 1CTA | 0.358 | 0.317 (-11.6%) | 0.318 (-11.2%) |
| dense hdim 128 8k | 2.221 | 2.217 (-0.2%) | 2.222 (+0.0%) |
| dense hdim 96 8k (1CTA) | 1.961 | 1.941 (-1.0%) | 1.942 (-1.0%) |

(2CTA rows are unaffected by commit 2, as expected; the dense rows are noise, n=30.) A first run on another
node (job 366749) agrees: causal 1CTA -17.1% / -18.8%.

The full-block loop still carries the sequence-bound mask (SEL 192 / ISETP 66 per trip in the table above);
the companion PR `sm100-bwd-condition-mask-seqlen` removes that for tile-aligned shapes. With both, plus the
2CTA dS-exchange PR, the 2CTA document-mask backward at 32k goes 4.88 -> 3.06 ms (-37%), prefix-block-causal
13.75 -> 8.52 ms (-38%) (job 366813).

## Tests

B200, cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, both commits; per-test outcomes compared with main:

| selection | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/cute/test_mask_mod.py` | 835 passed, 748 skipped (x3 runs) | 834 passed + 1 failed (first run), then 835 passed x2; see note |
| `tests/cute/test_block_sparsity.py` | 4883 passed, 40 skipped | identical |
| `test_flash_attn_output` hdim 96 (MHA+GQA, causal, local 0/1, det on/off; 416 ids) + hdim 128 MHA subset (104 ids) | 390 passed, 130 skipped | identical |
| `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` subset (252 ids) + `test_flash_attn_bwd_tile_n.py` | 344 passed, 24 skipped | identical |

Note on `test_mask_mod.py`: the first full run on this branch (job 366791) had one failure,
`test_parameterized_masks[True-128-128-document-None-False-dtype0-128-mha-16-1024-1024]` (dK error 3.1e-2 vs a
tolerance of 1.6e-2). That case runs a document mask_mod *without* block sparsity on the hdim 128 2CTA kernel,
which this PR does not change: its backward SASS is identical to main's (normalized-SASS md5
`a47de3eb664c77cdb6e92bbd9fd3f0b6` for both, job 366815), and its document layout comes from Python's unseeded
`random` module, so it differs from run to run. Not reproduced afterwards: two more full runs of the file on
this branch and two on main gave 835 passed / 748 skipped each (jobs 366847, 366848), and the case alone over
Python seeds 0-399 and 0-39 failed 0 times on main and on this branch (jobs 366814, 366820). We count it as a
pre-existing flaky test, not caused by this PR, but did not find its trigger.

Bitwise check against main in one process (`fa4pr.py check all-check`, 39 cases, final job 366880; earlier

sliding-window / prefix-block-causal mask_mods (1CTA and 2CTA tables, 8k and 8000, GQA), mask_mod without
block sparsity, dense hdim 64 / 96 / 128 (incl. deterministic: dq bitwise too).

Commands:

```
python fa4pr.py bench bs_causal_32k,bs_doc_32k,bs_pbc_32k,bs_swa2k_32k,bs2_causal_32k,bs2_doc_32k,bs2_pbc_32k,bs2_swa2k_32k,d96_8k,d128_8k,bs_causal_4k_gqa --what bwd --cycles 30 --pkgs base,test,alt

pytest -n 8 tests/cute/test_block_sparsity.py
pytest -n 8 @sel_fa_output_d96.txt @sel_fa_output_small.txt
pytest -n 8 @sel_fa_varlen.txt tests/cute/test_flash_attn_bwd_tile_n.py
```

## Re-validation after rebasing onto main e7a6402a (#2966, #2732), 2026-10-19

`FLASH_ATTENTION_HD256_GENERIC_BWD=1` (MHA, causal, unaligned 4000, GQA, deterministic): out / lse / dk / dv

- Ported by hand onto main after #2966 (which edits lines inside the loop body): the two-phase header is
  the same and the body is #2966's body re-indented; the change lines are identical to the pre-#2966
  version modulo whitespace. Applies cleanly on top of the still-open #2967 / #2968.
- Commit 2 and the 2CTA PR's second commit edit the same `if const_expr(...)` line (barrier before the S_P /
  LSE release); merged, the condition is `not self.use_2cta_instrs or self.cta_schedule ==
  CtaSchedule.TWO_CTA_PIPELINED`.

items.title: [CuTe, Bwd, SM100] Fold the hdim64 LSE / dPsum subtractions into the S / dP MMA
items.body:
Stacked PRs:
 * #3099
 * __->__#3098
 * #3087
 * #3086

--- --- ---

## Human Note

## Agent Notes

With `split_P_dS` (1-CTA hdim64), every compute thread reads the per-row LSE and dPsum with
broadcast LDS and subtracts them in FFMA2 / FADD2: P = exp2(S * scale_log2 - LSE) and
dS = P * (dP - dPsum). The LDS share the MIO queue with MUFU, and their consumers stall on the
short scoreboard. On B300, ncu warp-state samples put 360-400 clk per CTA-step per compute warp on
these LDS in each of the P and dS phases. A timing-only probe that drops the loads (wrong output)
makes the step 1.12x faster.

This change folds both subtractions into the MMAs, as one extra K=16 block per MMA:
- A_x = [1, 1, 1, 0, ...] in every key row.
- B_x holds, per Q row, the bf16 3-way split [hi, mid, lo, 0, ...] of -LSE / scale_log2
  (added to S) or of -dPsum (added to dP). The fp32 accumulators then hold S - LSE / scale_log2
  and dP - dPsum directly.

Warps 14 and 15 are idle at 1-CTA. They now own the LSE / dPsum bulk loads and build B_x per Q
tile, publishing it on `pipeline_Lx` / `pipeline_Dx`. The MMA warp waits on those pipelines
before the extra block. The P phase no longer touches SMEM, so its `fence.proxy.async` is
dropped.

The gate is config policy: `BwdConfig.fold_LSE_dPsum`, chosen by `select_bwd_config` through
`can_fold_LSE_dPsum`. It is on for SM100 / SM110 split_P_dS tiles (1-CTA, 128 x 128, both head dims
padded to 64) with bf16, MHA, non-deterministic runs, a nonzero softmax_scale, and no block sparsity, score_mod,
score_mod_bwd, or softcap. `validate_bwd_config` rejects an explicit config that turns it on
anywhere else, and it holds False on SM90 / SM120 like the other SM100-only fields. To decide,
`BwdHeuristicInputs` now carries `dtype`, `has_score_mod_bwd`, `has_softcap`, and
`zero_softmax_scale` (the fold divides by the softmax scale, so `softmax_scale=0` keeps the subtractions). The kernel takes
the field as a constructor argument and only asserts what the fold needs to be correct
(split_P_dS, bf16, unpacked rows, no block sparsity or score_mod); the config is in the compile
key. Gradients are not bitwise equal to the unfolded kernel, because the MMA rounds the folded
sum. Every configuration with the field off generates the same SASS as before.

Review order:
1. `can_fold_LSE_dPsum` and its use in `select_bwd_config` / `validate_bwd_config`;
2. NOTE [hdim64 LSE / dPsum fold into the S / dP MMA];
3. `fold_stats` / `_zero_smem`;
4. the extra MMA blocks in the MMA warp;
5. the compute-loop changes.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- **SMEM:** A_x is 4 KiB; B_L and B_D are 2 stages x 4 KiB each. dPsum gets its own 2-stage
  buffer, so warp 15 can build B_D(t+1) during dP(t). The new struct members are zero-sized and
  placed last when the fold is off, so the layout of every other configuration is unchanged.
- **Load ownership:** the builder warps are the only consumers of sLSE / sdPsum. They issue the
  stat loads up to two tiles ahead, independent of the load warp's Q / dO order.
- **Zero-fill order:** the operand buffers are zeroed once per work tile with 16 B stores, after
  the first stat loads are issued. The first version zeroed them with scalar stores through the
  swizzled layout before issuing any load. That put several thousand clk at the head of every CTA
  and made the fold 3-5% slower than the unfolded kernel at S = 4k on B300.
- **Why each case stays off:**
  - fp16: the split needs the fp32 exponent range. |dPsum| > 65504 overflows hi to inf and
    produces NaN, and small values lose mid / lo to subnormals.
  - GQA and deterministic mode: measured slower. In deterministic mode the serialized dQ adds
    bind instead of the compute warps. On GB300, an explicit config forcing the fold on for
    unpacked GQA 32/8 (bf16 hdim64, validation bypassed) measured 0.983-0.985x at non-causal and
    1.006-1.018x at causal against the same unpacked config without the fold. These two are
    policy only: the kernel runs them correctly, so `can_fold_LSE_dPsum` is the one place to widen
    the scope.
  - pack_gqa: the builder warps index the stats by query head.
  - Block sparsity: that load path issues the stat loads itself.
  - score_mod / score_mod_bwd / softcap: score_mod sits between S and the LSE subtraction, and
    score_mod_bwd reads the raw S.
- **Sanitizer side effect:** compute-sanitizer racecheck reported 2 hazards on the unfolded
  hdim64 kernel, between the stats bulk copy and the compute-warp broadcast LDS. With the fold it
  reports 0, because those reads are gone.

</details>

## Performance

bf16 hdim64 MHA (32/32 heads), non-deterministic; S 4k/8k/16k at B 4/2/1. Speedup = time
without the fold / time with it (higher is better).
- **duty** = one backward captured in a CUDA graph and replayed with 50 ms idle between replays,
  so the SM clock stays at its maximum; median of 3 interleaved fresh-process trials.
- **sustained** = back-to-back replays for 1.5 s after a 0.5 s warmup, at the power cap; median
  of 5 trials.

B200 / B300 were measured with the same kernel change on main (`4616f511`); GB300 on this stack.

| GPU | causal | S=4k duty / sustained | S=8k | S=16k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B200 | no | 1.065 / 1.046 | 1.089 / 1.058 | 1.086 / 1.076 |
| B200 | yes | 1.116 / 1.077 | 1.137 / 1.095 | 1.139 / 1.096 |
| B300 | no | 1.040 / 1.023 | 1.040 / 1.018 | 1.036 / 1.016 |
| B300 | yes | 1.076 / 1.050 | 1.100 / 1.039 | 1.114 / 1.047 |
| GB300 | no | 1.034 / — | 1.053 / — | 1.038 / — |
| GB300 | yes | 1.081 / — | 1.112 / — | 1.122 / — |

GB300 (2070 MHz duty clock) ran duty only; 20 back-to-back replays give geomean 1.075
(1.033-1.127). The other cells of the matrix (fp16, hdim128, GQA 32/8, deterministic) run the same
SASS as without the fold. On B200 / B300 their per-cell duty medians fall within 0.995-1.008; on
GB300 the 66 cells where neither this nor the next commit applies fall within 0.990-1.014
(geomean 1.000).

## Validation

- **Codegen:** compile-only capture over ~1100 SM100 / SM103 backward call specs (bf16 / fp16,
  hdim 64-256, MHA / GQA, causal / local / none, deterministic, varlen, block sparsity, softcap /
  score_mod, 2CTA / tile_n env knobs): the fold decision equals the kernel-internal rule it
  replaces in every spec.
- **Cubins:** 22 SM100 / SM103 backward configs compiled under FakeTensorMode with
  `CUTE_DSL_KEEP=cubin`. With the fold on (5: bf16 hdim64 MHA causal / local / none, varlen,
  SM103), the main backward cubin is byte-identical to the same kernel change on main with its
  kernel-internal gate. With it off (17: fp16, GQA, deterministic, softcap, hdim 128 / 192 / 256,
  1-CTA hdim128), it is byte-identical to the parent commit.
- **SASS (B200 / B300, same kernel change on main):** 32 configs (bf16/fp16 x hdim 64/128 x
  MHA/GQA x causal x deterministic). The backward kernel's SASS is unchanged everywhere except
  bf16 hdim64 MHA non-deterministic. No new LDL / STL.
- **Bitwise (B200 / B300):** in the 96-cell A/B, every cell where the fold is off had dK / dV
  bitwise equal to the unfolded kernel in all trials, and dQ too in the deterministic cells.
- **Tests (GB300, at the tip of this two-commit change and at its parent `2a11f3ed`, same
  selection, xdist 24 workers on 2 GPUs):** `test_flash_attn_output` at d 64/128 (9984 ids), a 1/64
  sample of `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` at d 64/128 (3024), the other test_flash_attn.py
  backward tests (122), `test_flash_attn_varlen.py` at D 64/128 (3888), the race-condition
  (deterministic) tests at d 64/128 (1248), bwd pack_gqa / tile_n (717), score_mod backward (331),
  hd256 backward (96), and test_bwd_config. The first pass hit OOM / reference-kernel errors at
  12 workers per GPU on both trees; rerunning the union of those ids (1048) at 2 workers per GPU,
  both trees fail only the same 8 learnable-sink dSink tolerance ids.
- **compute-sanitizer (B200, B1 S1024 H8):** racecheck reports 0 hazards with the fold (2
  without). memcheck finds no kernel errors. synccheck reports the same divergent-barrier class
  as without.

items.title: [CuTe, SM120] SM12x-owned forward and backward (flash_attn.cute.sm120)
items.body:
**Builds on #3108, which should be reviewed first.** This branch contains its 5 commits; the 3 commits specific to this PR are the last ones:
- `[CuTe, SM120] SM12x forward owned by flash_attn.cute.sm120`
- `[CuTe, SM120] SM12x backward owned by flash_attn.cute.sm120`
- `[CuTe, SM120] Keep unused V cache rows out of the SM12x forward`

> **Disclaimer:** I am the author of the SGLang SM12x FlashAttention-4 forward ([sgl-project/sglang#32991](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32991)). The forward here is that implementation, ported to this repository's layout and conventions and extended (block sparsity, per-batch SplitKV, scheduler metadata). The backward is new work on the same base.

## What this does
Today SM12x (RTX PRO Blackwell, GeForce RTX 50xx, DGX Spark / GB10) runs FA4 through SM80 subclasses (`flash_fwd_sm120.py`, `flash_bwd_sm120.py`). Those use fixed 64 x 64 tiles and 128 threads, and they reject paged KV, SplitKV, deterministic backward, score/mask_mod backward, block sparsity and head dims above 128 in the backward.

This PR replaces both with kernels and launch planning owned by SM12x, under `flash_attn/cute/sm120/`:
- `interface.py` reaches them through `sm120/dispatch.py` (`get_forward_host` / `get_backward_host`) and passes the host's arguments through without interpreting them.
- `select_fwd_config` / `select_bwd_config` reject SM12x with a pointer to the host. The host's `fwd_config` / `bwd_config` give the shared code its tiles.

**Forward** (`sm120/flash_fwd.py`, `flash_fwd_decode.py`, `runtime.py`, `scheduler.py`, `paged_kv.py`, `policy.py`):
- **Kernel and features:** warp-MMA kernel with TMA K/V. It covers:
  - head dims up to 256, including head_dim != head_dim_v
  - causal, local, softcap
  - score_mod / mask_mod with aux tensors
  - learnable sink, pack_gqa
  - varlen Q/K and seqused
  - paged KV, block sparsity, SplitKV
- **Tile choice:** per call, from a schedule model of the grid: wave quantization, LPT order and L2 head groups, using the SM count of the current stream's context.
- **Decode:** a transposed paged-decode kernel with the packed query heads on the MMA N dimension, plus a split policy for low head dims.
- **Per-batch SplitKV:**
  - The prepare kernel's per-batch counts, built from the generic pieces in #3108, with a compact split grid.
  - One-split batches write their output directly, and the combine skips them.
  - A gate takes per-batch splits only when the KV tail they remove outweighs their fixed cost.
- **`get_scheduler_metadata`:** plans SM12x calls with the same host and tags the tensors with the plan and the call shapes. The forward rebuilds them (with a warning) when its own differ.
- **Unused V cache rows:** TMA loads the whole last K/V block, so V rows past `seqused_k` (which may hold NaN) would reach O through 0 x NaN. The forward zeroes those rows in shared memory on the first block it processes, which is the only block that holds the sequence end. The five `unused_v_cache` tests now also run on SM12x.

**Backward** (`sm120/flash_bwd.py`, `bwd_runtime.py`):
- **Kernels:** a dK/dV kernel that can also reduce dQ, and a dQ kernel, both warp MMA. They cover:
  - head dims up to 256, including head_dim != head_dim_v
  - causal, local, softcap
  - score_mod / mask_mod with aux tensors
  - learnable sink, GQA/MQA, varlen and seqused
  - block sparsity and deterministic dQ
- **TMA producer:** a TMA producer warp group with two-stage ping-pong feeds hd 64/96/128.
- **Host policy:**
  - fused or split dQ
  - tiles per head dim and head splits
  - a KV sweep for short K
  - a split of the last wave's work
  - LPT head groups sized to L2
- **Fixes:** the varlen GQA backward is fixed on SM12x. `test_flash_attn_varlen_cumsum_metadata_paths` with GQA fails on `main` (wrong dK) and passes here.

**Shared kernels:**
- The postprocess reads SM12x accumulators in their declared tile order.
- The pre- and postprocess handle 96-column tiles (`utils.fit_row_copy`).
- The LPT backward scheduler can cap its L2 group at one wave.

## Performance
**Method:**
- CUDA-graph replay, implementation order shuffled per round, median per call.
- `main` vs this branch as separate processes in ABAB order on the same GPU. Each ratio is the geomean of the two pairings; their median disagreement is 0.5%.
- Decode is measured with L2 flushed before each call.
- Baseline: `main` at 4616f511; this branch was measured before its rebase onto current `main`. Later `main` commits do not change the SM120 kernels, and the rebase is performance-neutral (ABAB, 111 training and 35 decode cases: geomean 1.000).
- FA2 (2.8.4, built from this repository) and cuDNN SDPA run in the same process as this branch.

**Training: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, 188 SMs.**
- Grid of 165 cases: bf16 hd 64/96/128/192/256 x MHA/GQA/MQA x S 512/2048/8192 x noncausal/causal/local, plus fp16 hd128 and an 8-length varlen batch; 16K tokens.
- `main` cannot run hd192 or hd256 (54 cases). The comparison below covers the other 111.

| | forward | backward | forward + backward |
|---|---|---|---|
| vs `main` (geomean, 111 cases) | **1.34x** | **1.15x** | **1.21x** |
| cases slower than `main` (>1%) | 0 | 10 | 3 |
| vs FA2 (165 cases) | 1.13x | 1.07x | 1.08x |
| vs cuDNN SDPA (72 dense, non-local cases) | 1.23x | 1.41x | 1.37x |

**Decode: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.**
- 89 cases: q=1, hd 64/128/256, batch 1/8/32/128.
- Lengths: uniform 512 / 4K / 32K, one long request among short ones, and log-uniform 64..32K.
- Cache layouts: dense KV cache with `seqused_k`, and paged (page 256).

| | dense cache | paged |
|---|---|---|
| vs `main` (`main` runs dense non-hd256 only: 40 cases) | **2.54x**, never slower, up to 12.3x | (`main` has no paged KV on SM120) |
| vs FA2 `flash_attn_with_kvcache` | 1.15x | 1.12x |
| per-batch SplitKV vs the static plan | 1.29x | 1.21x |

**Key cases on other SM12x boards** (no overall geomean), speedup vs `main`:

| case | RTX PRO 5000 (110 SMs) fwd / bwd / fwd+bwd | GB10 (48 SMs) fwd / bwd / fwd+bwd |
|---|---|---|
| hd128 GQA S8192 local (1024, 0) | 4.85x / 1.03x / 1.81x | 4.17x / 1.27x / 1.85x |
| hd128 GQA S8192 causal | 1.26x / 1.22x / 1.23x | 1.16x / 1.16x / 1.16x |
| hd128 MHA S2048 causal | 1.25x / 1.29x / 1.28x | 1.14x / 1.14x / 1.14x |
| varlen hd128 GQA causal | 1.34x / 1.13x / 1.18x | 1.16x / 1.13x / 1.14x |
| hd64 MHA S8192 noncausal | 1.04x / 1.19x / 1.15x | 1.04x / 1.14x / 1.11x |
| decode, one 32K request in B8 / B32 | 8.5-10.5x / 6.6-7.8x | 1.7-2.0x |
| decode, log-uniform B32 | 1.8-3.3x | 1.07x |

`main` cannot run hd256 on either board.

**Known gaps:**
- **Backward at S512 MHA, and hd96 MQA S2048 causal:** 1.5-5.5% and 3.5% slower than `main`. At S512 each CTA covers only a few Q tiles, and the old SM80 kernel has less fixed per-CTA work; our other tile and route choices are all slower there. The hd96 MQA case is not yet analyzed.
- **hd96 MHA local "backward":** the S512-S8192 cells show 4-6% slower, but this is mostly an artifact of measuring backward as (fwd+bwd) - fwd. The forward that returns LSE takes 171 instead of 168 registers there, which lowers occupancy. The backward kernels themselves are faster than `main`, and so is the training step.
- **Per-batch SplitKV on uniform batches:** a call with uniform lengths can pay the fixed prepare and combine cost (a few us) for no gain, since the host does not see the lengths. The worst case measured is 7% on a 25 us hd256 call.

## Tests
New:
- `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_sm120.py` (forward: dense, varlen, paged, decode, per-batch splits, scheduler metadata, block sparsity, sinks, score_mod)
- `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_bwd_sm120.py` (backward: the head-dim / mask / layout matrix, deterministic, TMA routes, splits, L2 groups, block sparsity, mods, sinks)

Shared suites are extended to SM12x where they were skipped: SplitKV, hd256 backward, block-sparse granularity, mask_mod varlen.

RTX PRO 6000 results: SM12x forward + fast 311 passed; SM12x backward 181 passed. Shared suites:

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| varlen sample | 195 passed |
| kv-cache sample | 647 passed |
| `test_cuda_graph.py` + `test_flash_attn_varlen.py` | 3895 passed |
| mask_mod / score_mod_varlen backward + sparse | 1609 passed |
| combine + fwd / bwd / swapab / MLA config + autotune | all passed |

## Overlap with open PRs
Several open PRs extend the SM80-subclass SM120 path that this PR replaces:
- #2336 split-KV
- #2348 and #3060 paged KV
- #2389 block-sparse forward
- #2752 learnable sink
- #2654 score_mod backward
- #2998 tile tuning
- #2902 shared-memory rejects
- #2474 Spark regressions

#2634 is a separate SM120 integration. I have not reviewed their designs in depth. If this PR lands, they would need to target `flash_attn/cute/sm120/` instead.

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Block-sparse forward: run empty tiles through the one correction epilogue
items.body:
Work done at Meshy by Yang Liu (@liuyang-05), authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).

## Problem

On B200 the block-sparse forward is 11-21% slower than it needs to be, even when every Q tile has KV blocks
and no tile is ever empty. With all tiles in the full lists and no mask_mod, a 256x128 tile runs at
1101 TF/s against 1361 TF/s for the dense kernel at the same size.

## Root cause

`correction_loop` handles a work tile with no KV block (`total_block_count == 0`) in its own `else` branch,
`handle_block_sparse_empty_tile_correction_sm100`, which inlines a second copy of `correction_epilogue`
(`zero_fill=True`) next to the regular one. The branch is never taken when every tile has work, but its
code still changes the register allocation of the kernel. SASS of the all-full block-sparse forward
(cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, `cuobjdump -sass`, per-loop counts from `sass_loops.py`):

| | main | this PR | main with the empty branch deleted by hand (diagnostic only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| kernel STACK / STL / LDL | 32 / 9 / 11 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| softmax tile loop (MUFU 564): STL / LDL / MOV | 2 / 4 / 48 | 0 / 0 / 25 | 0 / 0 / 25 |
| softmax KV loops (x2): LDL per trip | 1 each | 0 | 0 |
| correction tile loop: instr / LDL / BAR.SYNC | 875 / 7 / 8 | 816 / 0 / 6 | 761 / 0 / 6 |
| correction rescale loop (per KV block): instr | 224 | 187 | 187 |

In the rescale loop main rematerializes the TMEM address of every 16-column chunk on each KV block
(30 `R2UR` instead of 4, 2 `S2R SR_TID.X`, `LOP3`/`SHF`, loop counter in a vector register) instead of
using hoisted uniform addresses with immediate offsets (`sass/correction_rescale_loop_main_vs_pr2.txt`).
We did not isolate which of these costs the time (softmax LDL per trip vs. the longer correction loop);
what we did establish is that the binary without the second epilogue copy runs at the same speed as the
hand-made diagnostic binary that cannot handle empty tiles at all (table below).

## Fix

Empty tiles go through the regular per-stage epilogue:

- the KV loop part (first stats handshake, rescale loop, final release) is skipped;
- the row stats are the fully-masked ones (`row_sum = 1`, `row_max = -inf`, then the learnable sink
  exactly as before);
- the O-accumulator wait and the `mbar_P_full_O_rescaled` release, which only exist for a tile the MMA
  warp worked on, are skipped;
- `zero_fill` is passed at run time: `correction_epilogue` already has the run-time `zero_fill` branch for
  `seqlen_k == 0` with TMA KV (now also for the empty tile), so there is exactly one inlined epilogue.

The softmax <-> correction <-> epilogue mbarrier handshake is unchanged (same waits / arrivals per stage
as the old helper; NOTE [SM100 block-sparse empty tiles: mbarrier contract] updated), empty tiles still
write real zeros and LSE = -inf (#2906), and `handle_block_sparse_empty_tile_correction_sm100` is removed.
The helper also wrote the default stats into `sScale`; nothing reads `sScale` for an empty tile (the
correction warps use the values directly), so that store is gone too. Dense kernels trace exactly the same
code as before: the new branches are `const_expr(self.use_block_sparsity)`-guarded, and the dense forward
SASS is instruction-for-instruction identical to main.

No caller guarantee or opt-in hint is needed.

## Numbers

B200 (1000 W), bf16, hdim 128, batch 1, 16 heads, forward, one process, the main kernel (imported as a
renamed copy of main) and this PR interleaved, 30 cycles, CUDA-event medians (job 366785; TF/s count
visible pairs only):

| case | main ms | this PR ms | delta | TF/s main -> PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all-full block-sparse 16k, no mask_mod | 1.874 | 1.578 | -15.8% | 1173 -> 1393 |
| all-full block-sparse 32k, no mask_mod | 7.986 | 6.359 | -20.4% | 1101 -> 1383 |
| causal mask_mod 32k | 4.273 | 3.373 | -21.1% | 1029 -> 1304 |
| document mask_mod 32k | 1.977 | 1.660 | -16.0% | 696 -> 828 |
| prefix 4k + block-causal 2k mask_mod 32k | 4.388 | 3.437 | -21.7% | 1073 -> 1369 |
| sliding window 2k mask_mod 32k | 0.769 | 0.662 | -13.9% | 693 -> 805 |
| causal mask_mod 8k, 25% of Q tiles empty | 0.421 | 0.350 | -16.7% | 654 -> 785 |
| dense 16k | 1.598 | 1.596 | -0.1% | 1376 -> 1378 |
| dense 32k | 6.467 | 6.465 | -0.0% | 1360 -> 1361 |

- Diagnostic binary (empty-tile branch deleted by hand, only valid without empty tiles), same job:
  1.559 ms (16k) / 6.326 ms (32k), i.e. within 1.2% / 0.5% of this PR.
- Same-process A/A control (main vs main) in the same job: +0.04% to +0.65%.
- Repeat run on another node (job 366737): all-full 16k -11.0%, 32k -19.8%, causal 32k -21.9%,
  document 32k -15.5%.

## Tests

B200, cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130:

| selection | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/cute/test_mask_mod.py` (whole file) | 835 passed, 748 skipped | 835 passed, 748 skipped (per-test outcomes identical) |
| `tests/cute/test_block_sparsity.py` (whole file) | 4883 passed, 40 skipped | 4883 passed, 40 skipped (identical) |
| `test_flash_attn_output`, hdim 128 MHA subset (104 ids) | 78 passed, 26 skipped | identical |

including `test_sm100_block_sparse_empty_tile_writes_real_zeros`, `test_sm100_block_sparse_sink_all_masked`,
`test_persistent_blocksparse_empty_tiles` and the split-KV block-sparse tests.

Bitwise check against main in one process (`fa4pr.py check`, job 366710; full 39-case sweep `check all-check`, job
366879): `out` and `lse` bitwise equal on block-sparse causal / document / sliding-window / prefix-block-causal mask_mods (8k and 8000), the
all-full table, two empty-tile tables (25% of the Q tiles without any KV block, 8k causal and 8000
document), GQA, and dense / varlen cases; the backward of those cases is unchanged (dk / dv bitwise,
dq within main's own run-to-run spread).

Commands (one B200, `PYTHONPATH` = this tree + a renamed copy of main as `fa_base.cute`):


items.title: [CuTe, SM80] For FlashAttention 4, extend paged KV support from SM90 to SM80/SM120
items.body: The current FA4 supports paged attention on both Hopper and Blackwell. With a few lines of patch, we can extend Hopper's support to cover Ampere and RTX Blackwell

items.title: [Hopper] PackGQA fwd: fence the cp.async Q/Qv writes before the wgmma reads them
items.body:
**Summary.** In every SM90 PackGQA forward, the producer warpgroup writes Q (and `Qv`) to shared memory with `cp.async`, and nothing executes `fence.proxy.async` between those writes and the `wgmma` reads, except for `sQ` on the AppendKV rotary path, although PTX requires one. This PR makes each producer thread wait for its own copies and execute `fence_view_async_shared()` before arriving on `barrier_Q`, and the same for `barrier_Qv`.

#### Problem

- With PackGQA, Q is not loaded with TMA (`Use_TMA_Q = !PackGQA`); `PackGQAManager::load_Q` loads it with `cp.async`.
- The producer then arrives on `barrier_Q` (`cpasync_barrier_arrive` and `barrier_Q.arrive()`), and the QK `wgmma` reads `sQ` after `barrier_Q.wait`.
- The only fence is on the AppendKV rotary path, where the MMA threads rewrite `sQ` and fence.
- The `Qv` load right below has the same pattern.
- `run_mha_fwd` in `hopper/flash_api.cpp` forces PackGQA for split-KV and paged non-TMA KV, and `get_pack_gqa` enables it by default for some GQA shapes.

We reported the same pattern in CUTLASS's SM90 `cp.async` GMMA collectives as NVIDIA/cutlass#3721.

#### Change

- The wait is `cute::cp_async_wait<0>()`, which is `cp.async.wait_all`, because `load_Q` does not commit a group. FA3's own `flash::cp_async_wait<0>` emits `cp.async.wait_group 0` and would not wait for these copies; the code comment says so.
- The writing threads fence before they signal, as FA3 already does for rotary Q, transposed V and P.
- The arrive calls and `barrier_Q`'s count are unchanged.

**Not changed:** the paged non-TMA K/V loads (`PagedKVNonTMA`, `load_K`/`load_V` with `producer_commit(..., cpasync_barrier_arrive)`; V only without `Transpose_V`) publish to the `wgmma` in the same way. We have only read that path in the source and did not change it here; we're happy to extend the PR if you'd like.

#### Why the fence is needed

- `cp.async` writes shared memory in the generic proxy (PTX ISA 9.4 §9.7.10.28.3.1: "cp.async is treated as a weak memory operation performed in the generic proxy").
- `wgmma` reads its shared-memory operands in the async proxy (§9.7.17.4, Async Proxy).
- §9.7.17.7.1 (`wgmma.fence`): "An async proxy fence must be used to establish an ordering between prior writes to shared memory matrices and subsequent reads of the same matrices in a wgmma.mma_async instruction."

#### Cost and alternatives

- The producer now waits for its copies once per tile before going on to later loads. `wait_all` waits for all of the thread's outstanding `cp.async`, so under paged non-TMA KV it also waits for the first K block issued just before Q (and V with `Transpose_V`). With Qv, the Q and Qv loads are now serialized. We have not measured this.
- A cheaper alternative is one `fence_view_async_shared()` by the MMA threads after `barrier_Q.wait`. But then the fence is executed by threads that only observed the writes, and PTX says bi-directional proxy fences take effect within a single thread and compose with other synchronization (§9.7.15.4); it does not clearly say that this covers other threads' writes.

#### Testing

- Evidence: found by reading FA3's PTX against the ISA; we have not seen wrong output.
- Not run: we have not yet run this change on a GPU.

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] hd256 GQA/MQA dK/dV split and forward launch-plan cache
items.body:
Two SM100 changes, each in its own commit, plus a test commit. I can split them into separate PRs if you prefer.

## 1. hd256 GQA/MQA: split the dK/dV head loop

**Problem.** The hd256 2-CTA dK/dV kernel runs one cluster per KV tile. Each cluster loops in series over `h_r × Q blocks` (`h_r` = q heads per KV head). With MQA and one long sequence in a varlen pack, a few clusters run very long loops. Example: 16 q heads / 1 KV head, full Q × half KV, 26 CTAs × 416 iterations. On a 152-SM GB300, spreading the same work evenly would take about a fifth of the time.

**Change.**
- The flattened `(head × Q block)` range of a KV tile is cut into up to 4 contiguous chunks. The split count is chosen per tile on the GPU from that tile's iteration count.
- Each chunk writes fp32 dK/dV partials to a workspace and increments a per-tile arrival counter (acq_rel).
- The last chunk to arrive sums the partials in split order, scales, converts to the output dtype, stores the result and resets the counter. There is no extra kernel and no memset.
- Workspace and counters are cached per (device, stream). The workspace is `4 × tiles × 2 × 64 × 256` fp32.

**When it is on.** It is on by default for SM100/SM110 hd256 with `h_r ≥ 2`, when `h_r · ceil(seqlen_q / 128)` exceeds one chunk (40 iterations). MHA is never split.
- Opt out with `FLASH_ATTENTION_HD256_DKDV_SPLITS=1` or `dkdv_num_splits=1` in `_flash_attn_bwd`.
- Tune with `FLASH_ATTENTION_HD256_DKDV_CHUNK_ITERS` and `FLASH_ATTENTION_HD256_DKDV_SLOTS`.

**Numerics.**
- O, LSE and dQ are bitwise unchanged.
- dK/dV change only in fp32 summation order: relative L2 against the unsplit kernel is 3.5e-5 to 1.1e-4. Their error against FP64 eager is unchanged (dK rel. L2 2.41e-3 split and unsplit).
- The split is deterministic: repeated runs are bitwise identical.
- With the split off, outputs are bitwise identical to `main`.

**Performance.** GB300, bf16, 16 q / 1 KV heads, hd256. The input is a varlen pack with one long sequence and many short ones; the step names are the context-parallel ring cases.

| Step | dK/dV `main` → split (µs) | Whole backward (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| full Q × half KV | 699.5 → 227.5 | 1048.6 → 578.4 |
| half Q × full KV | 375.8 → 227.4 | 704.2 → 555.8 |
| diagonal (causal) | 830.7 → 276.5 | 1221.9 → 668.5 |

dQ time is unchanged. Host time per backward call rises by about 2–20 µs. In an end-to-end MQA hd256 training run with context parallelism 64 on GB300, the training step went from 11.08 s to 9.85 s (−11%).

## 2. Forward launch-plan cache

**Problem.** `_flash_attn_fwd` re-derives the compile key, tile choice and argument list in Python on every call. In loops that repeat the same shapes, such as context-parallel ring steps, this host time is on the critical path.

**Change.**
- After a launch, `_flash_attn_fwd` stores a plan: the compiled function plus its argument template, with the tensor slots left empty.
- A later call with the same key fills in only the tensors and launches.
- The key holds everything the host path reads for an eligible call: shapes, strides, dtypes, devices and `requires_grad` of q/k/v; the metadata of `cu_seqlens`/`seqused`; `max_seqlen`, scale, causal, window and `return_lse`; and the global scheduler, 2-CTA, ping-pong and SM-count switches.
- **Limits.** Only plain calls are recorded: no `qv`, paged KV, softcap, sink or tile overrides. A call is recorded only when no input copy was needed and the replay would reproduce the launch exactly. The cache holds at most 4096 entries and stores no tensor data.
- Opt out with `FLASH_ATTENTION_FWD_PLAN_CACHE=0`.

**Numerics.** Bitwise identical, both through `flash_attn_varlen_func` and through direct `_flash_attn_fwd` calls (42/42 varlen ring-step cases).

**Performance.** About 40–48 µs less host time per forward call (GB300, varlen hd256).

## Tests
- New `tests/cute/test_hd256_dkdv_split.py` (48 cases): MQA 16/1 and GQA 24/4 packs with one long sequence; causal and non-causal; bf16 and fp16; with a host `max_seqlen` and with `max_seqlen=None`. It checks that O/dQ are bitwise equal to the unsplit kernel, that all outputs are bitwise equal across runs, and that O/dQ/dK/dV stay within the FP64 tolerance of `eager_reference`.
- GB300, FA4 4.0.0b34 environment (torch 2.13, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.2):
  - `test_hd256_dkdv_split.py`: 48 passed.
  - `test_flash_attn_hd256_bwd.py`: 88 passed, 8 skipped.
  - `test_hd256_varlen_scheduler.py`: 101 passed, 48 skipped, 4 failed (paged-KV cases). The same 4 fail on `main` in this environment.
  - `test_flash_attn_hd256_features.py`: 8 passed, 38 failed (softcap and other forward features). The same 38 fail on `main` in this environment.
  - `test_flash_attn_fast.py`, `test_flash_attn_varlen.py`: still running; results will follow in a comment.
- `ruff check` is clean on all changed files.
