items.title: [CuTe, SM90] hdim256 backward: C++ FA3 dQ path and 2-CTA DSMEM dS exchange (373 → 530 TFLOP/s)
items.body:
## Summary

This PR takes the CuTe SM90 backward at head_dim 256 from 373 to 530 TFLOP/s (dense bf16, S=16k, H200), 1.42x, past the C++ FA3 kernel (480 TFLOP/s on the same GPU), with unchanged numerics. It is the follow-up to #2888, which fixed the swapped postprocess layout and moved hdim 256 to a 2-stage 64x48 config (302 → 373 TFLOP/s). The two optimization commits are independently useful:

1. **C++ FA3's hdim256 dQ path** (`BwdConfig.dQacc_use_TMA=False`). No smem staging of dQ: the MMA warp groups reduce the dQ accumulator straight into `dQaccum` with `red.global.add.v4.f32`, partitioned by the same R2S tiled copy as the smem path, so the gmem layout and the postprocess are unchanged. dQ is computed in two hdim halves into the same registers (C++ `Slice_dQKV_Mma`; with two accumulators ptxas hoists the second WGMMA above the atomics and dV spills at tile_n=80). The freed 64 KB is what lets the C++ tile (64x80, 2-stage Q) fit. 373 → 471 TFLOP/s, C++ FA3 is 480 on the same GPU.
2. **FA4's 2-CTA dS exchange, on Hopper via DSMEM** (`BwdConfig.cluster_size=2`). With the atomics compiled out the 1-CTA kernel runs at 747 TFLOP/s, so what remains is the fp32 reduce traffic into dQaccum (`S² · d · 4 B / tile_n` per head; a single SM sustains only ~30 GB/s of `red.add`). The two CTAs of a cluster take KV blocks n and n^1 of one head, walk the union of their m-block ranges in lockstep and exchange their dS tiles through distributed shared memory (`cp.async.bulk.shared::cluster`, mbarrier full/empty handshake with remote arrive/expect_tx). CTA r then computes `dQ[:, 128r:128r+128] = dS_own @ K_own[:, half] + dS_peer @ K_peer[:, half]` (K = 2·tile_n) and reduces only its half: half the atomics and half the dQ registers at the same tile_n. Splitting by head-dim halves rather than query rows (FA4's Blackwell variant) needs only the peer's K half (20 KB) in smem, which is what makes 64x80 fit exactly (232,448 B). Q and dO are TMA-multicast to the pair. Odd block counts use a "ghost" partner that participates in every barrier with fully masked columns (dS = 0), flushes its dQ half, and skips the dK/dV epilogue. 471 → 530 TFLOP/s.

The pair's fixed cost only pays off once the m-block loop is long enough, so `_tile_size_bwd_sm90` selects the 2-CTA kernel for `seqlen_q >= 2048` (max_seqlen_q for varlen) and keeps the 1-CTA 64x80 config below (measured crossover, table below). Deterministic and block-sparse backward keep the semaphore-ordered smem-staged path, matching the C++ restriction `Deterministic && kHeadDim < 256`. Forward and hdim ≤ 192 are untouched.

A third commit rounds `seqlen_k_rounded` straight to `n_block_size * cluster_size` instead of fixing up the parity of the n-block count. The old form branched on `max_seqlen_k`, which callers may pass as a device tensor (HF/TE varlen): that synced, and raised `DataDependentOutputException` in the FakeTensorMode compile pass. The rounding is the same value and does not branch. The SM100 2-CTA backward has the same issue; the SM90 cluster config added here reaches it from the varlen path.

New surface: two `BwdConfig` fields (`dQacc_use_TMA`, `cluster_size`) and two `FlashAttentionBackwardSm90` constructor arguments of the same names, both selected in `_tile_size_bwd_sm90` (which gains `deterministic` and `seqlen_q` keyword arguments). No public API change.

## Results

H200 (132 SMs, 227 KB smem; CUDA 12.8, torch 2.10, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1), bf16, backward, ms · TFLOP/s:

| | `main` (before #2888) | #2888 | commit 1 (1-CTA) | commit 2 (2-CTA) | C++ FA3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dense S=16384 H=16 D=256 | 36.5 · 302 | 29.5 · 373 | 23.3 · 471 | **20.8 · 530** | 22.9 · 480 |
| dense causal S=16384 | 17.2 · 320 | 14.8 · 370 | 11.9 · 464 | **10.5 · 522** | 11.7 · 471 |
| varlen S=86000 H=32 (#2878) | 1931 · 314 | 1672 · 362 | 1314 · 461 | **1250 · 485** | 1277 · 474 |
| varlen causal S=86000 H=32 | — | 790 · 383 | 659 · 460 | **568 · 534** | 645 · 470 |
| dense S=65536 H=16 | 567 · 310 | 480 · 367 | 383 · 459 | **364 · 483** | 371 · 475 |

Other head dims are untouched (the same kernels compile; hdim 192 GQA works because of #2888). Same GPU, `main` and this branch back to back, S=16384 H=16, dense / causal:

| D | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 128 | 8.86 / 4.48 ms · 620 / 614 TFLOP/s | 8.53 / 4.36 ms · 645 / 631 |
| 192 | 15.72 / 7.93 ms · 525 / 520 | 15.46 / 7.73 ms · 533 / 534 |
| 64 | 4.84 / 2.36 ms · 568 / 583 | 4.70 / 2.36 ms · 584 / 583 |

2-CTA vs 1-CTA (same 64x80 tile, H=16, ms ratio; `bench/crossover_*.log`):

| seqlen | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 | 8192 | 16384 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dense | 1.02 | 1.03 | 0.91 | 0.91 | 0.92 | 0.83 |
| causal | 1.02 | 1.02 | 0.95 | 0.92 | 0.93 | 0.88 |
| local (1024,1024) | 1.00 | 0.97 | 0.90 | 0.89 | 0.89 | 0.91 |
| local (256,0) | 1.02 | 1.01 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.01 |

## Correctness

- Max error vs an fp32 reference is unchanged from `main` on every path (S=2048: dq/dk/dv 1.33e-3 / 1.16e-3 / 9.14e-4 non-causal, 1.20e-2 / 1.21e-2 / 1.58e-2 causal). dQ stays fp32-accumulated; only the reduction order changes, as in the C++ kernel.
- Checked vs the fp32 reference on both the 1-CTA and the 2-CTA kernel: dense, causal, GQA 16/4 and 16/2, MQA, local (200,0)/(100,50)/(256,0)/(1024,1024), softcap, deterministic (bitwise-identical repeat, MHA and GQA; smem path), hdim_v=128, hdim 200/224/240 (MHA and GQA, per kv head), odd n-block counts (ghost CTA), ragged S=1000, S=4096, varlen S=86000.
- Varlen with the 2-CTA kernel, per batch vs the fp32 reference (`bench/varlen_gqa_cluster.py`): GQA/MQA/MHA with batches of 0, 1, odd and many KV blocks, causal and not, identical errors to the 1-CTA kernel (this caught a padded-offset mismatch between the kernel and the dK/dV accumulator layout during review; fixed in commit 2).
- Varlen callers that pass `max_seqlen` as a device tensor: same gradients as the host-int call, and the FakeTensorMode compile pass goes through (commit 3).
- `tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_output -k -256-` (8560 ids: every head_dim 256 case and every seqlen 256 case, mha/mqa/gqa × causal × local × softcap × deterministic × sink): 5246 passed, 3312 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures are the `dSink` tolerance check at `[256-256-128-...-mqa]` (diff 0.0018 vs tolerance 0.0011, head_dim 128) and fail identically with `main`'s `flash_bwd_sm90.py` / `interface.py` on this GPU. `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` d=256 random sample (320 ids): 196 passed, 124 skipped, 0 failed. `test_flash_attn_sm90_hdim_padding*` and the empty-workload backward tests: 170 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (0.11.13) clean on `flash_bwd_sm90.py`.

Related: #2878, #2888.

items.title: FA4 SM103 backward preprocess predicate shape mismatch for padded head dimensions
items.body:
### Summary

On B300/SM103, FA4 beta27's backward preprocess reuses a predicate covering all per-thread row modes after slicing the O/dO source and destination tensors to a single row. CuTe rejects the resulting copy because the predicate has shape `(1,(2,3))` while the data expects `(1,(3))`.

The same `flash_bwd_preprocess.py` code is present in beta29 and current `main` (`4fd8d758c1fb7d93ef2e9a316ba4db1ab7fc05fe` as fetched on 2026-09-03).

### Environment

- NVIDIA B300 / SM103
- CUDA 13.2 base image
- PyTorch 2.10.0a0+3a035ad5.nv25.12
- Python 3.13
- `flash-attn-4==4.0.0b27`
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2`
- BF16, varlen causal attention
- `CUTE_DSL_SHOW_STACKTRACE=1`

### Sanitized reproducer

```python
import torch
from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_varlen_func

torch.manual_seed(42)
q = torch.randn(256, 16, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
k = torch.randn(256, 4, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
v = torch.randn(256, 4, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
cu = torch.tensor([0, 256], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
result = flash_attn_varlen_func(
    q,
    k,
    v,
    cu_seqlens_q=cu,
    cu_seqlens_k=cu,
    max_seqlen_q=256,
    max_seqlen_k=256,
    causal=True,
)
out = result[0] if isinstance(result, tuple) else result
out.float().square().mean().backward()
```

Backward-preprocess compile key:

```text
dtype=BFloat16, head_dim=80, head_dim_v=80, m_block_size=128,
has_cuseqlens_q=True, has_seqused_q=False, has_dlse=False,
has_dq_accum=True, has_scale_p=False, use_padded_offsets=True,
nheads_major=False, pack_gqa=False, qhead_per_kvhead=1,
nheads_kv=1, has_cu_total_m_blocks=False
```

Compiler diagnostic:

```text
error: unknown: 'cute.copy' op expects pred to have compatible shape with: (1,(3)) but got actual predShape: (1,(2,3))
note: unknown: see current operation: "cute.copy"(...) :
  (!cute_nvgpu.atom.universal_copy<bf16, 128 b>,
   !cute.memref<bf16, gmem, align<16>, "((8,1),(3)):((1,0),(32))">,
   !cute.memref<bf16, rmem, align<16>, "((8,1),(3)):((1,0),(8))">,
   !cute.memref<i8, rmem, align<32>, "(1,(2,3)):(3,(0,1))">) -> ()
```

### Source mapping and proposed correction

`flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd_preprocess.py` constructs `tOpO` from unsliced `tOcO`, then captures it in a `partial`. Inside the `m` loop it slices both data tensors with `[None, m, None]` but does not slice the predicate.

Slicing the predicate over the same row mode makes the preprocess compile and run:

```diff
-copy = partial(copy_utils.copy, pred=tOpO)
 ...
-copy(tOgO[None, m, None], tOrO[None, m, None])
-copy(tOgdO[None, m, None], tOrdO[None, m, None])
+row_predicate = tOpO[None, m, None] if const_expr(tOpO is not None) else None
+copy_utils.copy(tOgO[None, m, None], tOrO[None, m, None], pred=row_predicate)
+copy_utils.copy(tOgdO[None, m, None], tOrdO[None, m, None], pred=row_predicate)
```

This report is limited to the backward-preprocess predicate mismatch; the reproducer may encounter other constraints later in the general SM100 backward kernel once preprocess is repaired.

items.title: [CuTe, Bwd, SM100] Bound the Q/dO TMA loads by seqlen_q so unused rows cannot poison dK/dV (packed varlen and seqused_q)
items.body:
_AI-assisted (OpenAI Codex, Claude Code)._

Related: #2374, #2999, #3012, #3071.

## Problem

#3012 / #3071 bound the SM100 backward's K/V loads by `seqlen_k`. The query side has the same hazard. The Q, dO and 2-CTA Qt, dOt descriptors span the whole buffer, so a partial query tile loads its rows past `seqlen_q` from the next packed sequence or from unused `seqused_q` storage. P and dS are masked there, but `dK = dS^T @ Q` and `dV = P^T @ dO` still reduce over those rows, and `0 * NaN = NaN`. A NaN/Inf in one sequence's Q or dO therefore poisons dK/dV of the sequence before it. If the memory after Q or dO is unmapped, the load faults.

Reproducer: bf16, D256 with `FLASH_ATTENTION_HD256_GENERIC_BWD=1`, 16 Q / 8 KV heads, packed lengths 129/257/511, causal, window (1023, 0), deterministic. NaN or +Inf in the last sequence's Q or dO makes all of the middle sequence's dK/dV NaN (526,336 = 257 × 8 × 256 per tensor). The same values in K or V, or a finite 317 anywhere, change nothing. Before fixing, we predicted that a tile-aligned middle length of 256 would be clean and 255 would not. Both held on SM103 (255: all 255 dK/dV rows NaN, 522,240 per tensor).

## Fix

When `cu_seqlens_q` or `seqused_q` is given, #3071's per-CTA descriptor rewrite now also sets the row extent of Q, dO, Qt and dOt. The extent is `offset_q + seqlen_q` for packed layouts and `seqused_q[b]` for dense ones; under packed GQA only the sequence axis changes. It runs in the same per-batch update and fence as K/V, and TMA zero-fills the tail. The SM100 workspace grows from 3 to 7 descriptors per CTA (384 → 896 B) and is also allocated when only query metadata is given. SM90, calls without metadata and the dedicated hd256 kernel are untouched.

The first commit fixes a pre-existing host bug that the new workspace test hit. Above 256 sequences, the backward builds a tile prefix sum for both Q and K whenever any metadata is passed. With one-sided metadata (e.g. only `seqused_q`) it fails with `_compute_tile_cumsum requires num_m_blocks, cu_seqlens, or seqused`. SM100 now builds each side's prefix sum only when that side is ragged.

**Cost, on the shapes timed below:** whole-call backward time up to 1.14× on packs of 1–64-row sequences, 1.01–1.02× on long ones. Calls with query-side metadata only were not timed.

## Validation

B200 (SM100) and B300 (SM103), driver 580.173.02, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, main `98c1cee`.

- **Controls.** Each build ran the reproducer 10 × {Q, K, V, dO} × {317, NaN, +Inf}, with the compile cache cleared per build. Builds: main, this PR, and a neutral edit (a no-op source change forcing a fresh compile).
  - Q/dO NaN/Inf poisoned dK/dV in 40/40 trials on main and on the neutral edit (526,336 NaN per tensor). With this PR, all 40 trials were bit-identical.
  - K/V NaN/Inf and the finite 317 were bit-identical on all three builds.
  - These are B200 counts; B300 matched them with the same kernel source. On SM103 the neutral edit compiled to main's normalized SASS, so it only shows that a fresh compile reproduces the failure.
- **PTX/SASS** (SM103, D256 2-CTA): PTX `tensormap.replace` 3 → 7 and acquires 3 → 7; SASS `UTMACCTL.IV` 3 → 7. The PTX feeds the per-sequence query end into dimension 1 of the Q/dO/Qt/dOt descriptors their TMA loads use.
- **New tests** (402), all passing on B200 and B300 (B300's 6 boundary cases ran on an earlier interface revision, same kernel).
  - `test_flash_attn_sm100_bwd_unused_query_tail` (384) poisons Q, dO or both across packed / packed + seqused / dense + seqused layouts, D64/128/256, 1-/2-CTA and GQA packing. On main it fails at its first case with `Q=nan: dK has NaN/Inf`.
  - `..._query_tma_allocation_boundary` (6) ends Q/dO at an unmapped VMM range. On main, a standalone copy of its script faults with an illegal address (checked at D64, for Q and for dO).
  - `..._query_tensormap_workspace_padding` (12) uses 301 `seqused_q` sequences. On main (B300) its first dense-K/V case, the only one run, hits the host assertion. The packed-K/V cases pass `cu_seqlens_k` and can't hit it.
- **Existing tests:** `-k "unused or seqused"` (new tail test deselected) gives 226 passed and 64 SM90-only skips on both GPUs.
- **Finite inputs:** O, LSE, dQ, dK and dV are bit-identical to main in every deterministic timing case below. Non-deterministic cases are identical except dQ in 5 cases per GPU, and in each of those main's own dQ also differs between two runs (atomic accumulation).
- **SM90:** not executed; behaviour unchanged (both prefix sums still built, same 2-descriptor workspace).
- **#3048:** applies cleanly in either order. It changes only calls without `cu_seqlens_*` / `seqused_*` (it keeps `mask_seqlen=True` when `is_varlen`), and this PR changes only calls with them. Not run together.

## Overhead

B200 backward time. Each sample is one whole `_flash_attn_bwd` call bracketed by CUDA events and a sync: preprocess, main kernel, postprocess and launch gaps, with O/LSE precomputed. Rows: bf16, 16 Q / 8 KV heads, packed, deterministic. µs are medians of 15 alternating rounds × 30 calls; PR/main is the median per-round ratio.

| shape | D | main µs | PR µs | PR/main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 384 seqs of 1–64, causal | 64 | 385.3 | 416.4 | 1.081 |
| 384 seqs of 1–64, non-causal | 64 | 383.1 | 412.0 | 1.077 |
| 384 seqs of 1–64, causal | 128 | 875.4 | 994.9 | 1.137 |
| 300 of 1–64 + 4093 + 8191, causal | 64 / 128 | 1366.7 / 2524.4 | 1417.9 / 2709.3 | 1.037 / 1.073 |
| 4093 + 8191, causal | 64 / 128 | 773.8 / 943.7 | 784.2 / 951.0 | 1.012 / 1.007 |
| 1 × 8192, causal | 128 | 808.0 | 818.0 | 1.014 |

More results:
- B200, non-deterministic, 384-sequence causal pack: 1.087 (D64) and 1.127 (D128).
- B300, deterministic: 1.088 / 1.129 on that pack, 1.005 / 1.007 on 4093 + 8191, and 1.022 on 1 × 8192.

Profiles (B200, row 2 and D128 1 × 8192):
- In nsys, the main kernel alone grows 1.111× (258.0 → 286.6 µs) against 1.077× for the whole call, and 1.018× (656.2 → 668.2 µs) against 1.014×.
- ncu replay durations differ: 411.6 → 455.7 µs and 1157.7 → 1181.7 µs.
- Preprocess and postprocess stay within 2%, and host dispatch got faster.
- The worst row (D128, 1.137×) was not profiled, so its kernel-only ratio is unknown.

The profiles are consistent with added per-CTA descriptor setup in the load warp, with no added math. Under the single-tile scheduler, each CTA's load warp now initializes, rewrites and fences 4 descriptors instead of 2 (D64, 1-CTA) before its first load. Descriptor-update instructions double (334,848 → 669,696). Compute-warp long-scoreboard samples at the LSE pipeline wait rise 1,180 → 2,255, and tensor-pipe activity falls 5.7% → 5.2%. No exact critical-path attribution is established.

We found no cheap fence-only fix. `TensorMapManager` already batches the updates behind one release fence. A tensormap acquire covers a fixed 128 bytes, so the seven acquires can't be merged. Membar stalls are unchanged, and overlapping the rewrite with a previous tile needs a persistent schedule. Happy to iterate if you'd prefer a different approach.

## Not covered

- **Untimed: calls with query-side metadata only** (e.g. dense Q + `seqused_q`, dense K/V). Main does no descriptor rewrites there; this PR allocates the workspace and rewrites 2 (1-CTA) or 4 (2-CTA) descriptors per CTA. The one dense layout we timed (B300, D64, 384 × 1–64, `seqused_q` + `seqused_k`, non-causal, non-deterministic) gave 1.083.
- **Not run: `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_varlen.py`** (#3071 ran 3,887 of its cases); this PR changes every SM100 varlen backward call. Also not run: `test_flash_attn_hd256_bwd.py`, #3071's packed-varlen set, MLA backward.
- **Dedicated hd256 backward** (the D256 default): it has its own load path and, from the source, likely the same hazard. Not fixed or tested here.
- **SM90 query loads** look equally unbounded from the source; unchanged and not run.
- **SM90/SM80/SM120 keep the one-sided-metadata host assertion.** Their main kernels also pick the varlen scheduler from K-side metadata only (`flash_bwd_sm90.py:542`, `flash_bwd.py:417`), so dropping the `arch // 10 not in [10, 11]` guard should generalise the first commit. Left out as untested on those archs; happy to follow up.


## Update: rebased onto `main` (54b044c)

Rebased onto the typed backward configuration API (#3044). The kernel commits are unchanged apart from one conflict in `interface.py`; both per-side ragged guards and the typed-config tile sizes are kept. Upstream now caches the pack-GQA, tile-N and hd256-generic backward overrides, so the new tests patch those getters per parametrized case instead of setting environment variables (third commit, test-only; assertions, inputs and tolerances unchanged).

On B200, all 402 new cases pass both the compile-only pass and real execution, with no skips; both passes use the same 568 unique compilation keys, which confirm the intended generic-D256 and packed/unpacked GQA variants ran. Eight representative poison cases fail on `main` with NaN/Inf gradients. The existing unused-K/V-tail (64) and packed unaligned-head-dim (4) cases pass. Performance was not remeasured after the rebase; the overhead numbers above are from the earlier base.

items.title: [CuTe] Add E4M3 forward attention on SM120
items.body:
Add an E4M3 `mma.sync.m16n8k32` path to the SM80-derived SM120 forward
implementation, returning BF16 output, add SplitKV forward (BF16 and FP8) on SM120, and add FP8 paged KV forward on SM120.

## Numerical contract

- Optional per-batch/KV-head Q/K descales enter the softmax scale; V descale
  enters output normalization.
- Multiply unnormalized probabilities by `2**8` before E4M3 conversion; keep
  the unrounded FP32 denominator and unchanged online rescaling factor.
- Return natural-log FP32 LSE. Like SM100, subtract the offset inside
  `log2(row_sum) - 8` before conversion to natural-log units; the adjustment
  removes `8*ln(2)` from the offset denominator's log.
- Return BF16 O; fully masked rows produce exactly O=0 and LSE=-inf.

This follows the SM100 FP8 convention, not bitwise equivalence across GPU
architectures. V is read row-major (native transposed byte ldmatrix); there is no V repack.

## Scope

Dense and varlen forward, MHA/GQA/MQA, causal/noncausal/local attention,
bottom-right causal alignment for unequal lengths. Qualification covers
D64/D128/D256 with Dv=D; other admitted multiples of 16 are not claimed tested.

SplitKV (`num_splits > 1`, and automatic `0`/negative) is supported for BF16 and FP8; see below.

Not included: FP8 backward, E5M2 inputs, D72, BF16/FP16 paged KV (paged KV here is FP8 only), Qv/MLA,
learnable sinks, softcap, custom score/mask modifiers, block sparsity or
precomputed scheduler metadata. No BF16 fallback is presented as FP8.

## Tests


RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120). Originally qualified on `1fc0221` (#2758, automatic `num_splits` on
SM120); now ported onto `819ef26` (#2733, typed forward configs, main 2026-10-29) and requalified
2026-11-02 (see "Rebase onto current main" below). With SplitKV, `test_flash_attn_sm120_num_splits` and
`test_flash_attn_sm120_fp8_num_splits` now check `num_splits=3` against `num_splits=1` instead of
expecting a rejection:

- 522 selected upstream dense FP8 cases and 369 selected varlen FP8 cases pass,
  with the upstream numerical assertions unchanged. These are bounded
  selections, not the entire upstream parameter product.
- 146 additional O/LSE cases against independent FP64 attention pass (run on base `76d9331`,
  2026-10-07; the kernel code is unchanged since), including
  nonunit descales, unequal/empty sequences, exact repeats and unchanged inputs.
  O uses FA's error criterion. LSE uses twice an independent FP32 blockwise
  comparator's error plus four FP32 ULPs at the reference's maximum magnitude.

Six representative upstream smoke tests from the passing selection, on SM120
with the FP8 test enablement applied (`dtype1` is E4M3 at this pin):

```bash
for d in 64 128 256; do
  pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_output \
    -k "1-1-${d}-False-0-0.0-False-False-False-mha-dtype1"
  pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_varlen_output \
    -k "True-True-True-True-random-511-1-${d}-False-False-0-0.0-False-False-False-mha-dtype1"
done
```

## SM120 FP8 forward performance

Use 64x64 default tiles for E4M3 forward and load row-major V directly with
SM120 `ldmatrix.m16n16.trans.b8`. This removes the per-call V pack allocation
and kernel while retaining E4M3 QK/PV MMA, offset-eight probability scaling,
FP32 accumulation, caller descales, BF16 output and optional FP32 LSE.
Explicit tile overrides and FP16/BF16 dispatch are unchanged. There is no
cross-call input/output caching. Dense/varlen, causal/noncausal/local and GQA/MQA
forward remain covered; SplitKV and FP8 paged KV are added in later sections; FP8 backward is future work.

The commit sequence first introduces smaller tiles for wide heads/small grids,
then makes 64x64 the general FP8 default, then removes the V pack. These are
measured SM120 changes, not a transfer of performance claims from another GPU.
SGLang's SM12x work informed the tile-selection study; the implementation uses
FA4 idioms and copies no SGLang code.

Measured on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), torch 2.13.0+cu130, paired CUDA
Graph replay, 100 iterations, three balanced cycles, ten warmups and five seconds
GPU warmup. Request 1550 MHz under exclusive GPU ownership; every scored pair
passes the unchanged +/-75 MHz and 30 MHz maximum-spread checks. Observed scored
operator clocks span 1477–1552 MHz; largest within-operator spread is 15 MHz.
Input layout is separate contiguous BSHD Q/K/V, equal Q/K sequence length,
unit descales; BF16 comparisons use the same representable input values as the
FP8 codes. All device work in each fresh public forward call is captured;
Python dispatch, input generation/quantization, JIT and host allocation latency
are not measured by graph replay. This is a steady-state forward result, not
an eager latency or training/backward claim.

Classic FA2 BF16 is pinned at `ce088ab9ce0fc0434dcd8afa0a791da9fcc3a820`;
FA4 BF16 uses upstream default tiles from `1fc0221`, with no BF16 changes in
these commits. Upstream FA4 BF16 cannot launch the two D256 rows under the
SM120 shared-memory limit: both remain in the table, with FA2 comparisons,
and are labelled unsupported for FA4 BF16. No alternate BF16 tile is substituted.
DSL 4.8.0 is scored. Released DSL 4.7.1 is a separate, unscored diagnostic of
the same final source. Dependency layering retains each isolated DSL ahead of
the project torch installation; quack 0.6.5, TVM FFI 0.1.11 and dlpack-ext 0.1.4
are pinned on both stacks.

| Stack | Geomean vs FA2 BF16 (49 rows) | Wins | Geomean vs upstream FA4 BF16 (47 supported rows) | Wins |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DSL 4.8.0 — scored | 1.312259x | 49/49 | 1.398582x | 47/47 |
| DSL 4.7.1 — diagnostic | 1.302672x | 49/49 | 1.370242x | 47/47 |

The three accepted steps improve the FA2-normalized geomean by 29.904%
relative to the original FP8 PR tree on the same declared 49-row matrix.
The final V-load step adds 5.085% relative to the
64x64 parent. These parent comparisons normalize separate runs to the pinned
FA2 comparator; they are not direct candidate-versus-parent paired timings.

Every row is included below. The final step has 3 scored normalized
regressions relative to its parent: `fa_std_d64_b4_s4096_nc` (-0.523%), `fa_std_d64_b2_s8192_nc` (-0.954%), `fa_std_d64_b1_s16384_nc` (-1.240%).

Validation on the exact final source: 525 CPU checks, 522 upstream dense FP8
cases, 369 upstream varlen FP8 cases, 146 independent full-key FP64 O/LSE cases,
and four num_splits contract cases passed with unchanged references/tolerances.
Each earlier accepted commit passed the same gates. Device SASS from all seven
predeclared NCU samples contains real E4M3 QMMA, zero HMMA and native
`LDSM.8.MT1616`. Each captured public call contains exactly one forward kernel
and no V pack. Captured D64/D128/D256 QMMA counts are 64/128/512; native byte
transpose counts are 16/32/128 (static instructions, not dynamic counts).

Complete evidence, including slower rows and unsupported comparisons, is retained with source, test and toolchain hashes.



## SM120 SplitKV forward (BF16 and FP8)

Adds SplitKV forward on SM120 for BF16 and E4M3 FP8: explicit `num_splits > 1` and automatic
selection (`0`/negative). Split partials write normalized FP32 O and natural-log FP32 LSE directly to
global memory and reuse FA4's existing combine kernel; empty splits contribute O=0 and LSE=-inf.
Works with packed GQA/MQA, ragged lengths, `seqused_k`, causal and local attention. The split
plumbing and direct FP32 partial epilogue adapt @blake-snc's #2336 (co-authored commit).

The FP8 call contract matches SM100/SGLang: E4M3 Q/K/V supplied by the caller, optional FP32
descales shaped `(batch, kv_heads)` (`q_descale=None` means 1), BF16 output, optional FP32 LSE.

**Tests** (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, CUTLASS DSL 4.8.0): all selected upstream SM120 calls in
`tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py` / `test_flash_attn_combine.py` (5,333 calls: dense, varlen, contiguous
KV cache, combine, varlen/virtual-batch combine, split regressions) pass, except 72 pre-existing
backward dK/dV assertions in varlen GQA/MQA with unpadded KV that fail identically on `main`
(#2997, fixed by #2771). Plus 4,086 forward cases against independent FP64 references (incl. empty
splits, ragged metadata refresh, same-pointer/changed-content and CUDA-graph replay), 1,080
compute-sanitizer memcheck cases (no device memory errors), and an SASS check that FP8 executes E4M3
`mma.sync` (QMMA) with no HMMA. `test_splitkv_forwards_explicit_arch` now sets
`FLASH_ATTENTION_NUM_SMS` itself, since it requests `_arch=100` and otherwise only passes on an SM100 host.

**Decode performance** (216 decode shapes, Q length 1, K length 128-8192, batch 1/8/32, D64/128/256,
MHA/GQA/MQA; automatic splits; CUDA-graph, paired and interleaved against FA2 `ce088ab` with its
own SplitKV; clock requested at 1400 MHz, both sides at matched clocks):

| | Shapes | Geomean vs FA2 | Faster than FA2 | Worst row |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| FP8 (E4M3 inputs) | 108 | **1.70x** | 103/108 | 0.85x |
| BF16 | 108 | **1.17x** | 61/108 | 0.43x (`b32, k8192, MQA, D64`) |

FP8 is compared against FA2 BF16 on the same logical inputs. BF16 still trails FA2 on long-context,
large-batch decode with narrow heads (the 8192-length, batch-32 MQA/GQA rows); that is a known gap and
a follow-up. Prefill is unchanged: 96 prefill shapes vs the preceding commit, geomean 1.000x, every
row within 2%.

## SM120 FP8 paged KV forward

Adds a paged KV cache (`page_table`) to the SM120 E4M3 forward, including with SplitKV. The per-row
page lookup and predicated `cp.async` K/V loads adapt @blake-snc's #2348 (co-authored commit). Any
positive `page_size` works (no tile-divisibility requirement). BF16/FP16 paged calls are rejected
explicitly rather than silently falling back. Paged-only setup is gated at compile time, so non-paged
kernels are unchanged: on CPU, 44 non-paged calls (48 kernels) compile to SASS identical to the
preceding commit.

**Tests** (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, CUTLASS DSL 4.8.0): 243 upstream `test_flash_attn_kvcache` FP8
paged cases; 768 forward cases against independent FP64 references (page sizes 1/16/64/128, shuffled
and unused pages, empty and ragged sequences, descales, explicit and automatic splits); 72
changed-content/CUDA-graph replay cases; 24 compute-sanitizer memcheck cases (no device memory
errors); and a SASS check on 180 paged kernels (E4M3 QMMA, no HMMA). All earlier dense, varlen,
SplitKV and FP64 tests were rerun on this commit and pass.

**Performance.** Non-paged speed is unchanged: 216 decode shapes 1.000x and the prefill matrix
1.000x vs the preceding commit, no row outside its regression floor. Paging itself has a cost. I
timed 144 causal decode/short-prefill shapes (page size 1/16/64/128, D64/128/256, Hq=8 with
Hkv=8/2/1, batch 1/8, Q length 1/8, K length 513/2048, automatic splits). Each was a paired
CUDA-graph timing against the same FP8 kernel on contiguous KV, with the clock requested at 1400 MHz.

| | Shapes | Paged vs contiguous FP8 (geomean) | Within 5% | Worst row |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| All | 144 | 0.883x | 33/144 | 0.71x (`D256, MHA, b8, q1, k2048`) |
| D64 / D128 / D256 | 48 each | 0.927x / 0.899x / 0.826x | | |
| Page size 1 / 16 / 64 / 128 | 36 each | 0.875x / 0.883x / 0.886x / 0.887x | | |

So a paged call takes about 13% longer than the same call on contiguous KV (geomean), and up to
about 41% longer for D256 MHA at batch 8. Page size barely matters. The paged K/V load path is not
yet tuned; two-stage K/V loads and a paged-specific tile/split policy are the follow-up.

## Long-context FP8 precision (automatic splits)

At 1M keys, an unsplit FP8 call adds every probability into one FP32 softmax denominator. On a 1M-key
chunked prefill this pushed LSE error past our bound (1.96e-5 against 1.77e-5; O was fine). The fix is
host dispatch only. Automatic SM120 E4M3 calls with more than 262,144 keys use at least
`ceil(K / 65536)` splits, keeping the heuristic count when it is larger, with each split's length
tile-aligned. Explicit `num_splits` / `seqlen_k_per_split` / scheduler metadata stay the caller's
choice. Nothing changes at or below 262,144 keys: all 312 earlier timed rows dispatch identically,
and the compiled kernels are byte-identical. Asking for more than 256 splits raises an error rather
than silently exceeding the bound.

Both 1M prefill cases now pass the unchanged LSE bound. Automatic long decode keeps its parallelism:
paged FP8, page size 64, D128 at b1 runs GQA-4 in 846 us at 512K and 1,668 us at 1M, and MQA in
167 us at 512K and 319 us at 1M (CUDA graph, clock requested at 1400 MHz).

Paged vs contiguous FP8 at long context (paired, same kernel; automatic splits only): decode
geomean 0.86x across 18 shapes (worst 0.74x) (131K-1M keys, D64/128/256, GQA/MQA, b1/b8, page 16/64/128); chunked
prefill geomean 0.94x across 5 shapes (32K-1M keys). The paged-KV policy is still a follow-up.

## Rebase onto current main

Rebased onto `98c1cee`. There were five conflict hunks, all next to SM90/SM100 changes and none in
FP8 code: #3071's SM90 `tensormap_workspace` argument sits beside the SM120 descale/split arguments,
and the tests added by #3034/#3071 are kept. One extra commit only runs `ruff format` on
`flash_fwd_sm120.py`, `paged_kv.py` and `softmax.py`, which 4be17b0 already failed under the
`pre-commit` lint; the AST is unchanged. All earlier gates were rerun on the rebased head and pass.
Decode, prefill and long-context timing match the pre-rebase head: geomean 0.999x / 1.000x /
1.000x, no row below 0.96x.

On SM120 the new `tests/cute/test_cuda_graph.py` (#3007) passes both dense cases. All four varlen
cases fail dK identically on unpatched main, in eager mode too. That is the existing backward bug in
#2997, outside this PR. `test_paged_decode_cuda_graph_replay[splits1]` uses BF16 paged KV, which this
PR does not add (#3060 does), so it also fails on main.

### Port onto #2733 (typed forward configs)

The branch is now based on `819ef26`. The SM120 FP8 tile choice, SplitKV (explicit and automatic), paged-KV geometry and the long-context split grain live in `config.py`'s typed-config path, replacing its two SM120 rejections, not as separate dispatch in `interface.py`. On CPU, every SM120 call in our historical census (1,966 calls) picks the same tiles, splits, grain and kernel as before the port. The 159 compiled kernels for the representative calls have identical SASS, and non-SM120 config selection is unchanged (14,580 cases).

One new commit, "Update typed-config SplitKV validation for SM120", changes a test from #2733: `test_explicit_config_validation` asserted that SM120 rejects `num_splits=3`, the feature this PR adds. It now checks that the explicit split count is kept for BF16 and E4M3 at 1, 3 and 16 splits, like the earlier "Update SplitKV tests for SM120" commit. The paged-BF16 rejection check is unchanged.

All correctness gates were rerun from scratch on the ported head and pass: 30/30, including the full upstream suite (dense, varlen, KV cache, combine, paged), the FP64 FP8 and paged references, compute-sanitizer, SASS checks and all of `test_fwd_config.py`. The varlen CUDA-graph cases and BF16 paged `splits1` are excluded for the reasons above. Timing on all 762 pairs at a locked 1400 MHz matches the pre-port head: geomean 0.999x decode (worst 0.96x), 1.000x prefill, 1.000x long-context and 1.003x long contiguous.

#2973 landed after this port and conflicts in 5 small hunks: `use_swapab` next to the split grain in `config.py`, and in `interface.py` three call-site formatting overlaps plus the split-metadata condition. I'll rebase as soon as you're ready to review, so it doesn't go stale again in the meantime.

items.title: [CuTe, SM90] Persistent forward: overlap the next tile's loads with the epilogue
items.body:
The SM90 forward launches one CTA per tile. Every tile pays the CTA prologue (barrier init, Q and first K load) and its O store back to back, with nothing to overlap them. C++ FA3 runs persistent CTAs instead. The cost is largest where tiles are short: on main, FA4 runs at 0.65x of FA3 for hdim 192 causal at seqlen 512 and at 0.79-0.95x for most other configurations at seqlen 512-2k.

### Change

- **Dynamic persistent scheduling.** `SingleTileLPTScheduler` gets a `DYNAMIC` mode: the grid is one CTA per SM, and the producer warp claims the next tile with an atomic counter and broadcasts it to the consumers through smem (`DynamicPersistentSchedulerState`, as the varlen scheduler already does). Causal/local keep the LPT, L2-sectioned order. Non-causal walks the m blocks of one head before moving to the next, so concurrent tiles share K/V in L2. A static round-robin assignment measured up to 3% slower than this, and the LPT section order up to 40% slower for non-causal.
- **sO aliases sV instead of sQ, as in FA3.** With sO in sQ, a persistent kernel cannot release Q until the O store has read sO, so the next tile's Q load cannot overlap the epilogue. With sO in sV, Q is still released before the last PV GEMM, so the next tile's Q and first K load during the epilogue. Only the first V load of the next tile waits, on an mbarrier that the epilogue arrives on once the O store has read sO (after the TMA store's `wait_group.read`, or after the smem-to-register copy on the non-TMA path). sO fits in the two V stages for every SM90 tile config; the interface falls back to single-tile when it would not (`tile_m > 2 * tile_n`).
- **Interface.** Persistent for non-varlen, non-block-sparse calls with more than one wave of tiles, except non-causal calls with seqlen_k > 8192. Those already amortize the per-tile cost, and there the persistent kernel's mainloop measured up to 2% slower at hdim 128: it compiles to a slightly different schedule (launching the persistent kernel with one CTA per tile is just as slow, so the cause is the code, not the scheduling). The counter is a `torch.zeros(1)` per call, as in FA3. `FA_DISABLE_SM90_PERSISTENT=1` turns persistence off.

Varlen keeps `SingleTileVarlenScheduler`; this PR does not overlap with #2754 functionally, but the two add the same scheduler plumbing to `flash_fwd_sm90.py`. Whichever lands second can reuse the other's setup. On top of this PR, #2754 would only need to select `DynamicPersistentVarlenScheduler` for varlen and could rely on the sV aliasing instead of deferring the Q release.

### Performance (H100 SXM, bf16, 32k total tokens, nheads = 2048 / hdim)

FA4 / FA3 throughput. Each ratio is paired within one process (FA3 and FA4 interleaved ABBA over CUDA-graph replays) and is the median over two processes per variant (run in the order main, this PR, this PR, main). The last column is this PR together with #A, measured the same way in an earlier run.

| | main | this PR | this PR + #A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-causal geomean (hdim 64-256 x seqlen 512-16k) | 0.967 | 1.019 | 1.021 |
| Causal geomean | 0.900 | 0.982 | 1.021 |

| hdim | causal | seqlen | main | this PR | this PR + #2989 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | no | 512 | 0.954 | 1.168 | 1.168 |
| 96 | no | 1024 | 0.913 | 1.021 | 1.023 |
| 128 | no | 2048 | 0.941 | 0.985 | 0.990 |
| 192 | no | 2048 | 0.934 | 0.998 | 1.003 |
| 64 | yes | 512 | 0.808 | 0.986 | 1.020 |
| 96 | yes | 512 | 0.891 | 0.995 | 1.182 |
| 128 | yes | 1024 | 0.836 | 1.007 | 1.050 |
| 128 | yes | 16384 | 0.927 | 0.954 | 0.956 |
| 192 | yes | 512 | 0.649 | 0.685 | 1.040 |
| 192 | yes | 1024 | 0.794 | 0.913 | 1.023 |
| 256 | yes | 1024 | 0.869 | 0.996 | 1.028 |

No configuration measured slower than main beyond noise. The causal configurations where the LPT scheduler's L2 sections thrash (hdim 192 at seqlen 512-1k, hdim 96 at 1k) only recover with #2989. hdim 128 causal at 2k-16k (0.95-0.97x) remains behind FA3; that gap is in the mainloop, not the scheduling.

### Correctness

Validated on top of #2989; the same build without #2989 gives bitwise identical out and LSE for every case below (only the tile order differs).

- Forward out and LSE are bitwise identical with and without persistence for 4,875 cases: hdim 64/96/128/192/256, (192,128), (128,64); none, causal and local windows; softcap; learnable sink; MHA/GQA/MQA; dense, TMA-paged and cp.async-paged KV; seqlens from (1,1) to (4224,4224), sized so each CTA runs several tiles. The only mismatches, hdim 96 non-causal paged KV, are wrong on main in both variants (fixed in #2988).
- `test_flash_attn.py -k test_flash_attn_output` (deterministic=False) two-pass: 7,008 passed, 8 failed. The same 8 fail with persistence off (`dSink` tolerance in the backward).
- `test_flash_attn_fast.py`: same result with persistence on and off (192 passed; 1 failure that also fails on main).
- SM90 edge-case selection of `test_flash_attn.py` (seqlen_k zero, empty Q, hdim padding, pack_gqa padding, kvcache/paged, learnable sink, lse grad): 2,703 passed.
- `test_mask_mod.py`: 1,383 passed. `test_score_mod.py`: 1,683 passed (16 xfailed).

items.title: [CuTe, SM90] Fit backward tile to the block-sparse block size
items.body:
### Motivation

Follow-up to #2903, which fits the SM90 **forward** tile to `BlockSparseTensorsTorch.block_size`. That PR left this open: "The remaining backward rejections come from the SM90 backward's own tile_n (128 for hdim <= 128, 96 for 192, 64 for 256). That is a separate heuristic and is left for a follow-up."

`_tile_size_bwd_sm90` only looks at the sparse Q block, and only for hdim 128 (non-causal `tile_m=80` drops to 64). It never looks at the sparse KV block. SM90 has no KV subtiling (`kv_subtile_factor` must be 1), so every sparse KV block other than the heuristic `tile_n` raises a `ValueError` in `normalize_block_sparse_config_bwd`. Its `tile_m=128` for hdim 64 also rejects 64-row Q blocks. Some examples through `flash_attn_func` / autograd:

- hdim 64: `(64, 128)` fails (`tile_m=128`), and so do `(128, 64)` and `(64, 64)`.
- hdim 96 / 128: every KV block other than 128 fails, e.g. `(128, 64)`, `(64, 64)`, `(128, 96)`.
- hdim 192: everything except `(128, 96)` fails, e.g. `(128, 64)` and `(64, 64)`.
- hdim 256: anything below 64 fails, e.g. `(128, 48)` and `(64, 32)`.

### Root cause

A smaller `tile_n` is not just a number change. The SM90 backward runs five WGMMAs whose 64-row M axis has to land on a dimension that is a multiple of 64 per warp group. The hdim <= 128 configs put `tile_n` on M of the swapped S/dP GEMM and the unswapped dK/dV GEMM, with two warp groups, so they only work at `tile_n = 128`. Fitting `tile_n` means choosing the swap and atom-layout flags again.

One constraint only showed up on hardware. With swapped dK/dV and `tile_n` split across the two warp groups (`AtomLayoutNdKV=2`, the hdim-192 layout), each warp group's `tile_n / 2` slice must be a multiple of 16. `tile_n` 48, 80 and 112 compile, but dK/dV come out wrong (max error ~1.0 vs fp32 flex; dQ and the forward are fine). No config accepted today hits this: hdim 192 uses 96 (48 per warp group), and hdim 256 dense uses 48 with `AtomLayoutNdKV=1`.

### Change

`_fit_sm90_bwd_tile_to_block_sparsity` runs after `_tile_size_bwd_sm90` when the caller supplies `block_size`. It returns the heuristic config unchanged unless `normalize_block_sparse_config_bwd` would reject it:

- `tile_m -> 64` if the sparse Q block is a multiple of 64 but not of `tile_m`. Larger Q blocks still use `q_subtile_factor`.
- `tile_n -> sparse KV block` if that block is smaller than `tile_n`, at least 32, and a multiple of 16.
- When `tile_n` changes, the MMA layout follows. All of these use the existing kernel parameters; `flash_bwd_sm90.py` is not touched:
  - Head dims that round to a multiple of 128 (96, 128, 256): S/dP unswapped and dK/dV swapped, with head_dim split across the two warp groups (`AtomLayoutNdKV=1`). Each warp group then covers all of `tile_n`, so any multiple of 16 works. This was the fastest layout in an interleaved sweep, e.g. hdim 128, block 128x64: 1.69 ms vs 1.78 / 1.82 ms for the other two layouts.
  - Otherwise, `tile_n=64` with swapped S/dP (hdim 64, `tile_m` kept at 128), or swapped dK/dV with `tile_n` split across the warp groups when each slice is a multiple of 16 (hdim 64 and 192, `tile_n` 32 / 64 / 96).
  - Anything else is left to the existing rejection: hdim 64 / 192 with KV block 48 / 80 / 112, a KV block of 16 (it trips an assertion in the kernel), and KV blocks larger than the heuristic `tile_n`. The larger blocks are hdim-192 KV 128, which is #2757's case, and hdim-256 KV 80, which does not fit in smem.

Tiles only shrink, so smem and registers never grow. Every configuration accepted today keeps the identical tile, flags and compile key. The kernel set recorded with `FLASH_ATTENTION_TEST_RECORD_KEYS` is identical to main's on `test_flash_attn.py -k test_flash_attn_output` (1929 keys), and a superset on `test_mask_mod.py` (all 270 of main's keys, plus 48 from the new test).

### Results (H200, bf16)

(head_dim x block size) combinations accepted by `flash_attn_func` forward + autograd backward, using #2903's grid: B=2 H=4 S=1024, block-aligned causal BlockMask, compared against fp32 flex. Each cell shows main -> this PR. `F` = forward only (backward raises), `F+B` = forward and backward, `-` = forward rejected.

| hdim | 128x128 | 64x128 | 128x64 | 64x64 | 128x112 | 128x96 | 128x80 | 256x128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | F+B | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F | F -> **F+B** | F | F+B |
| 96 | F+B | F+B | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F+B |
| 128 | F+B | F+B | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F+B |
| 192 | - | - | F -> **F+B** | F -> **F+B** | F | F+B | F | - |
| 256 | - | - | F+B | F+B | - | - | F | - |

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| forward | 32 / 40 | 32 / 40 |
| forward + backward | 11 / 40 | **27 / 40** |

Smaller KV blocks (q 64/128 x kv 48/32/16, 30 combinations): forward + backward goes from 0 to 16 / 30. Accepted: kv 32 for every hdim, and kv 48 for hdim 96 / 128 / 256.

Correctness of the newly accepted configurations (32 (hdim, block size) points), with real `mask_mod`s on partial blocks:
- Causal, sliding window 256 and document masks, MHA and GQA (4:1). 180 / 180 match the fp32 flex reference within the `test_mask_mod` tolerance (`err <= 2 * bf16-flex err + atol`). The worst kernel/bf16-flex error ratio is 1.31 (dK).
- On the block-aligned grid above: 32 / 32 pass, with a worst ratio of 1.15.

Previously accepted configurations, same inputs, branch vs main in one process (63 cases, all pass):
- Forward out / lse are bitwise equal.
- MHA dK / dV are bitwise equal.
- dQ, and GQA dK / dV (fp32 atomics), stay within main's own run-to-run spread.

### Performance (supporting only; this is a functionality fix)

Backward time, B=1 H=16 S=8192, same mask with a finer block vs the block size main accepts. This PR is the only way to run the finer blocks:

| hdim | mask | main's block | 128x64 | 64x64 | 128x32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | causal | 128x128: 1.284 ms | +31% | +28% | +162% |
| 128 | document | 128x128: 0.919 ms | **-16%** | **-18%** | +44% |
| 128 | sliding window 256 | 128x128: 0.258 ms | +25% | +14% | +87% |
| 64 | document | 128x128: 0.713 ms | **-15%** | **-8%** | +27% |
| 192 | document | 128x96: 1.022 ms | +10% | +5% | +94% |
| 256 | document | 64x64: 1.849 ms | (128x48) +23% | | (64x32) +58% |

Smaller tiles cost per-tile efficiency, so finer blocks only pay off when they skip enough extra work. Here that is the document mask with 64-wide blocks at hdim 64 / 128. Causal and sliding-window masks gain little sparsity from finer blocks and are slower. The main gain is that these block sizes work at all, for example a BlockMask shared with the forward or built by another backend.

### Tests

- New `test_sm90_block_sparse_bwd_tile_fits_block_size`: 10 block sizes x {block-aligned, causal `mask_mod`}, forward + autograd backward vs fp32 flex. Main: **20 / 20 fail**. This PR: 20 / 20 pass. It shares its body with `test_sm90_block_sparse_fwd_tile_fits_block_size`, whose 7 cases are unchanged and still pass.
- Per test id vs main (H200, one GPU, `-n 8`):

items.title: [CuTe] Route backward through typed configs
items.body:
Stacked PRs:
 * #3099
 * #3098
 * #3087
 * #3086
 * #2743
 * #2738
 * #2735
 * #3056
 * #3054
 * __->__#3044
 * #3062

--- --- ---

## Human Note

## Agent Notes

This routes FA4 backward through a typed config, mirroring the forward design in #2732/#2733. Policy has one
owner: `select_bwd_config` builds a fully resolved `BwdConfig` from host-only `BwdHeuristicInputs`, or an explicit
config (new keyword-only `config=` on `_flash_attn_bwd`) is checked by `validate_bwd_config`. The kernels take the
result instead of deriving it. Public wrappers and autograd are unchanged; backward still selects independently
of the forward config.

```python
inputs = _get_bwd_inputs(arch=arch, device_index=device_index, block_sparse_tensors=block_sparse_tensors, V_in_regs=V_in_regs, **host_fields)  # keyword-only host metadata
config = select_bwd_config(inputs)   # or validate_bwd_config(config, inputs)
FlashAttentionBackwardSm100(..., registers=config.registers, Q_stage=config.num_stages_Q, ...)
```

- `config.py`: `BwdHeuristicInputs` (shapes, masking, determinism, varlen bits, block-sparse block sizes, mods,
  env knobs), `BwdConfig` (tiles, Q/dO/PdS stages, swapAB and atom layouts, `num_threads`, `dQ_single_wg`,
  `V_in_regs`, 2CTA/cluster/`spt`, dedicated hd256 kernel, `registers`), and the register types
  `Sm100BwdRegisters(reduce, compute, load, mma, empty)` and `Sm90BwdRegisters(mma, mma_no_dq, producer)`.
  Shared predicates (`can_use_bwd_2cta`, `can_use_bwd_tile_n_64`, `bwd_needs_2cta`) serve selection and
  validation. The SM90 tile table moves unchanged as `select_sm90_bwd_tile`; the kv-subtile/2CTA helpers move
  from `block_sparsity.py`.
- `interface.py`: the SM90 `BwdConfig` record, `_tile_size_bwd_sm90`, and the inline SM100/SM120 branches are
  replaced by one select-or-validate call. `_get_bwd_inputs` reads shapes, host block sizes, and env knobs
  only, never tensor data. The compile key includes the config.
- `flash_bwd_sm100.py` / `flash_bwd_sm90.py` take `registers=` (and SM100 Q/dO stages) from the config. Schedule
  facts that follow from tiles and head dims (`cta_schedule`, `acc_m64`, `split_P_dS`) stay in the kernel.
- SM120 supports exactly one configuration (`sm120_bwd_fields`); validation rejects any explicit config that
  differs from it.

Behavior changes:

- Dense hd192 with `FA_DISABLE_2CTA=1` raises `ValueError("... requires 2CTA ...")` from validation instead of the
  kernel's `AssertionError`. Everything else selects the same kernel as before.
- Disk compile-cache keys change once (the key now holds the config).

Also in this PR:

- Backward `pack_gqa` (from #2967, which landed on main during review) is a `BwdConfig` field. `select_bwd_config`
  chooses it with #2967's heuristic (`bwd_pack_gqa_heuristic`, moved to `config.py` with the same arithmetic, now
  reading `BwdHeuristicInputs`) behind one shared gate
  (`can_use_bwd_pack_gqa`: SM100 family, GQA, `qhead_per_kvhead | tile_m`, no block sparsity, no score/mask mod or
  sink); the tile_n test knob leaves it off and the env override becomes `requested_pack_gqa`. Validation rejects
  `pack_gqa=True` where the gate fails. The kernel, preprocess, postprocess and tile cumsum take `config.pack_gqa`.
  Compile-only capture vs main: 3,852/3,852 GQA cases identical on SM100/SM103 (862 packed).
- SM100 and SM90 backward take a required `spt` from the config (the kernel no longer derives it); validation requires it to equal
  the derived value.
- SM90 validation mirrors the kernel's asserts (dO/PdS stages are 1 or `num_stages_Q`, WGMMA tiling divisibility,
  GQA `head_dim == head_dim_v`), so an explicit config fails with `ValueError` instead of a compile-time assert. Validation also rejects explicit SM90 configs whose shared memory exceeds the 227 KB per-CTA limit (e.g. hd128 MHA with 3 Q/dO/PdS stages needs 294,912 bytes).
  SM90 GQA with d=192/dv=128 now raises that `ValueError` earlier than the old kernel assert.
- `BwdHeuristicInputs` holds only fields the selector reads; the `pack_gqa` heuristic reads sequence bounds, batch and
  the SM count, so the backward selection cache keys on them (selection is cheap; compile keys are unaffected).

Review order: `BwdHeuristicInputs` and `BwdConfig`, `select_bwd_config` and `validate_bwd_config` in `config.py`,
then `_get_bwd_inputs` and the selection block in `_flash_attn_bwd`, then the kernel constructors, then
`tests/cute/test_bwd_config.py`.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- The legacy `m_block_size`/`n_block_size`/`num_threads`/stage/swap/atom arguments of `_flash_attn_bwd` stay in
  the signature and remain ignored, as before (now stated in the docstring). Removing them touches
  `test_mask_mod` and `benchmarks/bench_sm90.py`; left for a follow-up.
- `num_threads` is the field and `num_wg` a property, because SM120 (128 threads) does not fit the `num_wg`
  formula. SM100 records its real launch size, 512.
- `num_sms` is read only when the `pack_gqa` heuristic will run (`bwd_selection_reads_num_sms`), so a
  cross-compiled GQA backward with score_mod, block sparsity, or hd256 still works without
  `FLASH_ATTENTION_NUM_SMS`.
- The backward env knobs are read once per process, and the compiled-kernel lookup hashes its key once.
  Host cost per call vs main (GB300, enqueue only): +3.5 to +6.6 µs, down from +5.7 to +13.8 µs.
- `spt` must equal the derived value, so it is not tunable. The dedicated hd256 kernel keeps its own fixed
  register and tile constants (`registers=None`).
- SM120 "not supported" feature checks stay as interface asserts, so their error types are unchanged.

</details>

## Validation

- Policy parity: a frozen copy of the previous inline policy matches `select_bwd_config` on 6,000 cases per arch
  (SM90/100/103/110/120) over dtype, head dims (64, 96, 128, 192/128, 256), none/causal/local, deterministic,
  8 block-sparse cases, 5 env-knob combinations, and `V_in_regs`; previous error cases raise the same messages.
- Codegen parity: compile-only FakeTensor capture of kernel state after `_setup_attributes` (registers, stages,
  schedule, tiles) plus pre/postprocess arguments matches the parent commit on 1,440 cases per arch; the only
  differences are the 30 hd192 error-type cases per SM10x/SM110 arch above.
- `tests/cute/test_bwd_config.py`: oracle parity (the backward `pack_gqa` copy was checked once and not kept;
  #2967's own heuristic test covers it), register parity against the kernels' former inline code, and
  rejection cases, including SM120 field mutations.
- GPU (GB300, after rebasing onto #2967): `test_flash_attn_bwd_pack_gqa.py` + `test_flash_attn_bwd_tile_n.py` +
  `test_flash_attn_hd256_bwd.py` 517 passed, `test_flash_attn.py` backward 100 passed, `test_mask_mod.py` backward 74 passed.
- GPU (GB300, full stack, before #2967): `test_flash_attn.py` backward subset, `test_flash_attn_bwd_tile_n.py` +
  `test_flash_attn_hd256_bwd.py` (180 passed), `test_mask_mod.py` backward/kv-subtile (276 passed),
  `test_score_mod.py` backward (330 passed).

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Unify hd256 backward (3/5): hdim 256 on FlashAttentionBackwardSm100 (opt-in)
items.body:
> Stacked on #2964 (merged as 76d93310) and #2965 (merged as 2b00d76f). Merged as 965c9212, squashing the hdim 256 commit and the four review follow-ups (softcap in the race test, deterministic dQ drain on every schedule, dS-exchange handles, shared accumulate tile layout `bwd_accum_tile.py`).

Runs the hdim 256 backward on `FlashAttentionBackwardSm100` behind `FLASH_ATTENTION_HD256_GENERIC_BWD=1`; the dedicated kernels stay the default until step 5.

**Series**
1. Tests first, named 2CTA schedules and TMEM widths (#2964)
2. 64-row KV tile per CTA (M=64 TMEM layout) with GQA, varlen and deterministic support (#2965)
3. **hdim 256 on the general kernel (opt-in)** ← this PR
4. Pack the query heads of a KV head into the Q tile (GQA) (#2967)
5. Make it the default and delete the dedicated kernels (#2968)

**One kernel with 5 GEMMs instead of a dQ / dKdV pair with 7: as fast or faster than the dedicated pair on MHA and varlen, at parity on GQA from 8k** (GQA at 2k is fixed by step 4); hdim 256 gains softcap, learnable_sink, local, deterministic, score_mod, mask_mod and block sparsity.

**Changes**

Kernel (`flash_bwd_sm100.py`)
- `(256, 256)` admitted with 2CTA + `tile_n` 64; `two_cta_serial` covers hdim 256.
- dQ staging, epilogue stage counts and chunk loops follow `tile_hdim` (two 32-column chunks per thread at hdim 256).
- score_mod coordinates take the per-warpgroup split of the M=64 layout (warpgroup 1 was using warpgroup 0's columns).

Performance fix (M=64 layout, the one that matters)
- The dS half the peer needs for its dQ MMA is read straight from `sdS_dK`: its peer-Q-column half already has the peer's dQ A-operand layout (`q + 64·kv`, same 128 B swizzle).
- That removes the exchange staging buffer and, in the serial schedule, its alias into `sdQaccum` together with the `dQaccum_empty` wait before every exchange write, which had put the whole dQ reduce chain (TMEM → SMEM → `cp.reduce.async.bulk`) on the critical path: −17% at 8k, and two-stage dQ staging another −4%.

Interface / tests
- hdim 256 under the flag picks `n_block_size` 64 before the 2CTA / block-sparse decisions (a 128-row sparse block covers one CTA pair), the serial schedule and the row-major GQA accumulate; raises like hdim 192 without 2CTA.
- `test_flash_attn.py` / `test_flash_attn_race_condition.py`: d=256 feature skips lifted under the flag.

**Correctness** (B200, `FLASH_ATTENTION_HD256_GENERIC_BWD=1`)

- d=256 selection of `test_flash_attn.py` (incl. formerly skipped sink / local / softcap / deterministic) + `test_flash_attn_hd256_bwd.py` + `test_hd256_varlen_scheduler.py`: **5489 / 34 / 1938**. The 34 are expected: 32 scheduler tests assert bit-equal repeats of *non-deterministic* calls (true for direct stores, not for fp32 reduce-add; #2968 runs them deterministic) + 2 d=256 learnable_sink `dSink` tolerance cases of the class already failing on main for d=64/96/128 (#2969).
- `test_score_mod.py` / `test_mask_mod.py` d=256 backward: 112 / 0 and 242 / 0. A/B vs the dedicated kernels: dK, dV bit-identical for MHA, GQA within bf16 rounding, dQ ≤ 1e-3, deterministic repeats bit-exact.

**Performance** (B200 @ 1400 MHz locked, two alternating rounds, `benchmark_attn.py --backend fa4 --bwd`, 32k tokens per shape, ms / TFLOPS, `--headdim 256`)

| shape | causal | batch | seqlen | dedicated ms / TFLOPS | general ms / TFLOPS | general / dedicated |

| GQA 24/4 | False | 16 | 2048 | 6.05 / 682 | 7.39 / 558 | 1.22x slower

items.title: Add forward and backward support for FA4 hdim=256 on SM100
items.body:
## Summary

This PR enables `head_dim=256` forward and backward attention kernels on SM100 (Blackwell) via the **Split-D** technique. SM100's TMEM is limited to 512 FP32 columns, which is insufficient to hold all accumulators for `d=256` in a single GEMM pass. Split-D decomposes each 256-dim GEMM into two 128-dim sub-GEMMs, keeping each sub-GEMM fully compatible with the existing `d=128` datapath while achieving 100% TMEM utilization.

All Split-D logic is guarded by a compile-time `is_split_d` flag derived from `head_dim > 128 && head_dim == head_dim_v && head_dim != 192`, ensuring **zero impact** on existing `d=64/128/192` paths.

## Motivation

- Many emerging model architectures (e.g., large vision transformers, certain LLM variants) use `head_dim=256`.
- SM100 TMEM has exactly 512 FP32 columns. For `d=256`, output accumulators alone (e.g., `O_low(256) + O_high(256)` in FWD, `dV(256) + dK(256)` in BWD) exhaust the budget, leaving no room for intermediate accumulators (S, P, dP, dS).
- Split-D resolves this by splitting the head dimension: **contraction-dimension split** for QK/S GEMMs (S remains `[M, N]` — softmax and masks are unaffected), and **output-dimension split** for PV/O GEMMs.

## Technical Approach

### FWD Kernel: 2 GEMMs → 4 sub-GEMMs per N-block

**TMEM layout (512 cols, 100% utilization):**
```
|--- S0 ---|--- S1/P ---|--- O_low ---|--- O_high ---|
  [0, 128)   [128, 256)    [256, 384)    [384, 512)
```

**MMA main loop (per N-block):**
1. `S  = Q_low @ K_low^T` (zero_init)
2. `S += Q_high @ K_high^T` (accumulate) → softmax
3. `O_low  += P @ V_low`
4. `O_high += P @ V_high`

**Key techniques:**
- PTX SMEM descriptor pre-set to Q_high address; `gemm_Si_low` uses negative offset (`-sQ_stage_stride`) to access Q_low, avoiding descriptor updates in the main loop.
- 5 KV pipeline stages (each 128×128×2B = 32 KB): 4 consumed per N-block (K_low, K_high, V_low, V_high), 1 for prefetch overlap.
- `overlap_sO_sQ = True`: sQ (2 physical stages for Q_low/Q_high) and sO share SMEM.
- O_low and O_high are physically contiguous in TMEM [256, 512); correction/epilogue traverses all 256 columns via manual iterator arithmetic (`tOtO_t2r.iterator + i * corr_tile_size`).

### BWD Kernel: 5 GEMMs → 10 sub-GEMMs per M-block

**Core design decision:** dK moved from TMEM persistent accumulation to GMEM atomic reduce (`dK_as_reduce = True`), freeing TMEM for S/P/dP/dS intermediates. dV remains persistent in TMEM.

**TMEM layout (512 cols, 100% utilization):**
```
|--- S/P ---|--- dV_low ---|--- dV_high ---|--- dP/dS ---|
  [0, 128)    [128, 256)     [256, 384)      [384, 512)
```
TMEM [0, 128) is time-division multiplexed between S/P, dK_partial, and dQ_partial.

**10 sub-GEMM schedule (per M-block):**
| Phase | Sub-GEMMs | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| S^T (contraction split) | K_low @ Q_low^T + K_high @ Q_high^T | → softmax/mask |
| dP^T (contraction split) | V_low @ dO_low^T + V_high @ dO_high^T | → dS = P*(dP-D) |
| dV (output split, TMEM persistent) | P^T @ dO_high, P^T @ dO_low | accumulate across M-blocks |
| dK (output split → GMEM reduce) | dS^T @ Q_high, dS^T @ Q_low | fire to reduce warp |
| dQ (output split → GMEM reduce) | dS @ K_low, dS @ K_high | fire to reduce warp |

**Key techniques:**
- `producer_phase_dQ` variable with XOR toggling ensures correct pipeline synchronization for TMEM [0, 128) time-division multiplexing between MMA and reduce warps.
- Q and dO each loaded 3 times per M-block (load + reload) due to single-stage buffer reuse across sub-GEMMs.
- K persisted in 2 SMEM stages (K_low + K_high) throughout the entire M-block loop.
- dV epilogue splits into two 128-col passes with explicit SMEM async commit+wait between passes to prevent race conditions.
- Deterministic dV semaphore: acquire only on dV_low, release only on dV_high (one logical increment per slot).

### Interface Changes

- `_validate_head_dims`: Accept `(256, 256)` on SM100/SM110.
- FWD: Compute `is_split_d`, enforce `q_stage=1`, `pack_gqa=False`, `num_splits=1`.
- BWD: Compute `is_split_d_bwd`, enforce `cluster_size=1`, `use_2cta_instrs=False`, `dKV_postprocess=True`.
- BWD postprocess: Split dQ/dK/dV accumulators into low/high halves, call `_bwd_postprocess_convert(head_dim=128)` on each half, copy results back.
- Varlen: `dq_accum` allocated with `torch.zeros` (instead of `torch.empty`) to ensure the high-half region is properly initialized for Split-D's `[low|high]` layout.

## Constraints (d=256)

| Feature | Status | Reason |
|---------|--------|--------|
| 2CTA instructions | Disabled | TMEM > 512 columns |
| Persistent kernel | Disabled | `overlap_sO_sQ` incompatible |
| SplitKV | Disabled | `head_dim_v >= 192` assertion |
| Paged KV | Disabled | Non-TMA path not adapted |
| pack_gqa | Disabled | `load_Q_non_tma` not adapted |
| Block Sparsity | Not yet adapted | Load path not adapted |
| score_mod / mask_mod | Not yet validated | Theoretically compatible (S/P dimensions unchanged) |

## Files Changed

| File | Lines | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm100.py` | +440/−145 | Split-D FWD: TMEM layout, MMA tilers, 4 sub-GEMM loop, Q split-load, correction epilogue |
| `flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd_sm100.py` | +779/−213 | Split-D BWD: TMEM layout, 10 sub-GEMM loop, 4x reduce/M-block, dV 2-pass epilogue, pipeline sync |
| `flash_attn/cute/interface.py` | +107/−31 | Head dim validation, `is_split_d` flags, constraints, accum allocation, split-half postprocess |
| `tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py` | +4/−4 | Add d=256 to parametrization, enable BWD for d=256 |
| `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_fast.py` | +15/−7 | Add d=256, adjust batch sizes, enable BWD for d=256 |

| `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_varlen.py` | +1/−1 | Enable d=256 varlen tests |

**Total: 7 files, +1363/−396 lines.**

## Test Results

### Full Regression (all head dims)

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| `test_flash_attn.py` | **1506 passed**, 177 skipped |
| `test_flash_attn_fast.py` | **336 passed**, 24 skipped |
| `test_flash_attn_varlen.py` | d=256 added and passing |
| `test_flash_attn_combine.py` | **2394 passed** (combine kernel natively supports d=256) |
| `test_flash_attn_race_condition.py` | **89 passed**, 36 skipped, 8 failed (see known issues) |

### Regression Verification

- **d=64 / d=128**: All FWD and BWD tests pass — existing paths unaffected.

## Known Issues

### MQA dK bitwise non-determinism (8 test failures in race_condition)

Split-D BWD's dK uses per-M-block `cpasync_reduce_bulk_add_f32` atomic accumulation to GMEM. For MQA (`qhead_per_kvhead=6`), multiple Q heads atomically add to the same K head address. FP32 atomic addition is not associative, so operation ordering affects the result at the bit level (max diff ≈ 0.002). This affects **only MQA dK bitwise determinism**; MHA/GQA determinism is correct, and numerical accuracy is within tolerance.

### Varlen GQA + bf16 dK precision boundary

Split-D's dK GMEM atomic reduce path introduces extra FP32 round-off compared to the TMEM persistent accumulation used for d≤128. For GQA with bf16, this can marginally increase numerical error at extreme sequence lengths.

items.title: FA4 consumer Blackwell (sm_120) integration
[CuTe, SM100] Unify hd256 backward (5/7): cheaper deterministic dQ semaphore (overlapped release on the M=64 serial schedule, early acquire, relaxed release)
items.body:
Step 5 of the hd256 backward unification (#2964 → #2965 → #2966 → #2967 (merged) → this → #3059 → #2968), but independent of it: the change is on main's deterministic dQ semaphore and applies to every head dim. It is what makes the general kernel's deterministic hdim 256 backward faster than the dedicated kernels once the default flips; on hdim 128 it is a 0–9.5% deterministic speedup with no regression.

Deterministic backward on SM100 orders the dQ reductions of a (batch, head) through a per-m_block semaphore: tile `n_block` acquires `sem[m] == n_block` before adding its dQ tile and releases after. Three changes to that path, independent of the hd256 series (branch on main; the hd256 general-kernel path is where the cost showed, `FLASH_ATTENTION_HD256_GENERIC_BWD=1` on main):

1. **Overlapped release on the M=64 serial schedule, immediate release on short tiles.** `delay_semaphore_release` was off for every `TWO_CTA_SERIAL` kernel; the reason is the M=128 serial layout where `sdQaccum` aliases the dS exchange buffer and is handed back to the peer through `dQaccum_empty_mbar`. The M=64 layout (hdim 256) has no alias, so it now releases `m_block - 1` while `m_block`'s adds are issued, like the other schedules (hdim 192 unchanged). Under the varlen scheduler (no head swizzle) the sibling n_blocks of one sequence run in lockstep, and on tiles with fewer than 16 m_blocks the delay doubles every hop of the chain (varlen MHA 1k det: −11%), so those tiles release each m_block immediately (run-time choice per tile).
2. **Acquire before `pipeline_dQ.consumer_wait`.** The poll for the previous n_block's release overlaps the dQ MMA instead of sitting after the TMEM read; the adds are issued only after the acquire as before.
3. **Asynchronous release (`red.async.release.gpu`).** `barrier.arrive_inc` releases with `red.release.gpu`, i.e. `membar.gl` + `red`: the releasing thread drains every outstanding memory operation of its SM before the flag moves, and on the dQ chain that drain sat on the critical path of every stage (largest single cost of the deterministic path, det −17% → −8% on MHA 8k). `red.async.release.gpu` (PTX ISA 8.7, sm_100+) is the same strong gpu-scope release reduction performed asynchronously by the memory system: the consumer's `ld.acquire.gpu` still synchronizes-with it and sees the producer's bulk adds (completed by `cp.async.bulk.wait_group`, ordered before the release by the CTA barrier), but the issuing warp no longer waits for the SM-wide drain (SASS `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA` + `UREDGR.E.ADD.S32.STRONG.GPU` instead of `MEMBAR.ALL.GPU` + `ERRBAR` + `REDG`). New `barrier.arrive_inc_async`, used at the dQ release sites; the dK/dV semaphores and the window-tail releases keep `arrive_inc`. An earlier version of this commit used `red.relaxed.gpu`, arguing that `wait_group` completion implies the adds are performed at L2; NVIDIA's answer (see the 2026-10-28 note) is that `wait_group` only guarantees the request has left the SM, so that form is gone.

**Correctness** (B200)

- `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_hd256_bwd.py` (FP64 reference, general kernel): **88 / 8 / 0**; upstream `test_flash_attn_hd256_sm100_deterministic_backward` (dedicated path, untouched): 4 / 0 / 0.

**Performance** (B200 locked at 1965 MHz request / 1845 actual, two alternating rounds, `benchmark_attn.py --backend fa4 --bwd --deterministic`, 32k tokens per shape)

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Unify hd256 backward (2/5): 64-row KV tile per CTA (M=64 TMEM layout) with GQA, varlen and deterministic support
items.body:
> Stacked on #2964 (merged as 76d93310); rebased onto it, so the diff is now just this PR's two commits.

Adds the accumulator layout the hd256 backward needs to the general kernel, behind a test knob.

**Series**
1. Tests first, named 2CTA schedules and TMEM widths (#2964)
2. **64-row KV tile per CTA (M=64 TMEM layout) with GQA, varlen and deterministic support** ← this PR
3. hdim 256 on the general kernel (opt-in)
4. Pack the query heads of a KV head into the Q tile (GQA)
5. Make it the default and delete the dedicated kernels

**Default configurations compile to byte-identical CUBINs**; the layout is reachable only through `FLASH_ATTENTION_BWD_TILE_N=64` (hdim ≤ 128) until step 3.

**Changes** (`acc_m64`, `NOTE [M=64 accumulator layout]`)

Commit 1 — the 64-row KV tile
- S / dP are read through the layout-aware `tcgen05.make_tmem_copy`; each thread owns one (row, 32-column) chunk.
- P^T and this CTA's dS^T are staged in SMEM as the A operands of the dV / dK MMAs (as the dedicated dKdV kernel does); TMEM no longer holds P / dS.
- The dS exchange half for dQ is chosen by the thread's lane half; the dK / dV TMA epilogue stages the whole tile per CTA.

Commit 2 — GQA, varlen, deterministic on that tile
- GQA: the fp32 dK/dV accumulate tile is written row-major; the postprocess gets an `accum_row_major` mode.
- Deterministic GQA: one semaphore slot per KV tile, driven by one thread of the CTA.
- Varlen (non-TMA epilogue): the row predicate comes from the partition coordinates.

**Correctness** (B200)
- New `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_bwd_tile_n.py`, 64-row vs 128-row tile vs FP64 eager: whole file 72 / 20 / 0 = dense MHA 24 / 4 with dK, dV `torch.equal` + GQA 8/2, varlen, deterministic, local, softcap 48 / 16 (GQA within bf16 rounding, deterministic repeats bit-identical).
- CUBIN + PTX of the 36-configuration matrix byte-identical to the parent after each commit (280 files, 0 diffs). Full `test_flash_attn_output` + hd256 files: 12813 / 12380 / 16, the 16 = pre-existing learnable_sink `dSink` failures on main (#2969).

**Performance.** Defaults unaffected. The 64-row tile on hd128 is a vehicle only (half the MMA M per CTA, twice the Q/dO traffic per KV row); the real comparison is hdim 256 vs the dedicated kernels in step 3. hd128 MHA h8 (B200 @ 1400 MHz locked, two alternating rounds, `benchmark_attn.py --backend fa4 --bwd`, 32k tokens per shape, ms / TFLOPS):

items.title: [CuTe, SM100, bwd] fix: SM100 backward for padded head dimensions
items.body:
## Summary

- slice the backward preprocess O/dO predicate along the same `CPY_M` dimension as the source and destination tensors
- choose a non-2CTA dQ reduction width that divides the padded head dimension
- add an SM100 head-dim-72 regression covering forward and backward correctness

## Root cause

For head dimension 72, SM100 pads the kernel head dimension to 80. The backward preprocess created an O/dO predicate for the full `(CPY_Atom, CPY_M, CPY_K)` partition, but reused it after slicing the source and destination by `CPY_M`. CuTeDSL therefore rejected a predicate of shape `(1, (2, 3))` for a copy of shape `(1, (3))`.

After slicing the predicate consistently, the main backward kernel also needs a dQ reduction width compatible with the padded width. Using `gcd(32, tile_hdim)` preserves 32 columns for existing aligned configurations and selects 16 for an 80-column tile.

Issue #1909 provides broader context for B200 backward IR verification failures. This change addresses the padded-head-dimension predicate and reduction configuration described above; it does not claim to resolve the distinct pointer-alignment failure in that report.

## Testing

On an NVIDIA B200:

```text
pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_sm100_head_dim_72_backward -s
1 passed
```

The regression compares the FA4 output and dQ/dK/dV gradients with the reference implementation.

items.title: Add SM120 split-KV (FlashDecoding) with FP32 partial outputs
items.body:
## Summary

- Add split-KV (FlashDecoding) support for SM120 (Blackwell GeForce / DGX Spark) — enables `num_splits > 1` for decode-like workloads with short Q and long K
- FP32 partial outputs: split-KV kernel writes FP32 accumulators directly to GMEM, bypassing SMEM to preserve full precision for the combine kernel
- Paged KV support removed from this PR per review feedback — will be a separate follow-up

Builds on #2329, #2330, #2333.

## Key changes

**flash_fwd.py (FlashAttentionForwardBase + FlashAttentionForwardSm80)**:
- `is_split_kv` parameter wired through `__init__`, `_check_type` (allow FP32 mO), epilogue (`split_idx` O/LSE indexing), `__call__` (O/LSE layout transposes with split dimension, num_splits through tile scheduler), and kernel body
- Kernel body wrapped in `n_block_max > n_block_min` guard for empty-split correctness
- Remaining-iterations loop uses `n_block - n_block_min` to stop at split boundary
- **FP32 direct write epilogue**: for `o_dtype != dtype`, bypasses SMEM entirely and writes MMA accumulators directly to GMEM via `thr_mma.partition_C(gO)` with per-element bounds checking. This avoids the SMEM store/load layout mismatch between `make_tiled_copy_C` (MMA accumulator layout) and `gmem_tiled_copy_O` (GMEM coalescing layout) that corrupts FP32 data through SMEM.

**interface.py**:
- `out_partial` allocated as FP32 `torch.zeros`, `lse_partial` as `torch.full(-inf)`
- `is_split_kv` passed to SM120 constructor

**flash_fwd_sm120.py**:
- `can_implement` unchanged (FP32 direct write doesn't use SMEM for output)

## Validation on SM121a (DGX Spark)

```
Split-KV: 14/14 configs pass
  - num_splits: 2, 4
  - causal and non-causal
  - Sq=16/32/64/128/256, Sk=256/512/1024
  - H=1/2/4/8, D=64/128
  - split_diff matches nosplit precision (0.001-0.002 vs reference)

Non-split regression: 5/5 configs pass
  - B=1/2, Sq=64/128/256, Sk=64/128/256
  - causal and non-causal, D=64/128
```

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Unify hd256 backward (4/7): pack the query heads of a KV head into the Q tile (GQA)
items.body:
Packs the `qhead_per_kvhead` query heads of a KV head into the rows of the Q tile, the way the forward's `pack_gqa` does: one tile per KV head, K/V loaded once, dK/dV kept in TMEM and stored directly (no fp32 accumulate, no postprocess).

**Series**
1. Tests first, named 2CTA schedules and TMEM widths (#2964)
2. 64-row KV tile per CTA (M=64 TMEM layout) with GQA, varlen and deterministic support (#2965)
3. hdim 256 on the general kernel (opt-in) (#2966)
4. **Pack the query heads of a KV head into the Q tile (GQA)** ← this PR
5. Cheaper deterministic dQ semaphore release (#3058, on main, independent; needed for the deterministic numbers of 7)
6. Pack 2 query heads per tile and loop the KV head's remaining heads inside the CTA (#3059, stacked on this PR)
7. Make it the default and delete the dedicated kernels (#2968)

Steps 5–7 are the result of the hd256 perf audit after step 3: the general kernel still lost to the dedicated pair on deterministic, on small / odd GQA ratios at short seqlen and on causal MQA. With 5–7 every measured hd256 cell (238: dense / varlen / deterministic, 1k–32k, MHA / MQA / GQA) is at or above the dedicated kernels; the full tables are in 7. This PR is unchanged by them except that 6 relaxes the `qh | tile_m` requirement below.

**hd128 GQA 13–26% faster at 2k and 0–10% at 8k; hdim 256 GQA goes from 19–28% behind the dedicated kernels to 4–11% ahead.** Head-dim agnostic; placed before step 5 so the switch-over carries no GQA regression.

**Changes**

Kernel
- Q / dO (and the 2CTA transposed views) are `pack_gqa_layout` views: the `(qh, seqlen)` row mode becomes an extra TMA box dimension.
- `block_info`, the transposed mask and the deterministic lock values take `qhead_per_kvhead_packgqa` (position limits scale by `qh`); the KV tile scheduler keeps 1.
- One dQ semaphore slot per (KV head, packed m block) in deterministic mode.

Packed-row tensors (LSE, dPsum, dQaccum)
- Allocated per KV head in packed row order, because the kernel loads LSE / dPsum with 1-D bulk copies that need contiguous rows.
- The preprocess writes and zeroes them in that order (`PackGQA.PACKED_ROW_OUTPUTS`, next to the MLA backward's per-head-output mode); the dQ postprocess writes dQ through a `pack_gqa_layout` view `(b, (qh, s), h_kv, d)`, so there is no unpack pass. Varlen offsets of the packed-row tensors come from the same `cu_seqlens_q` / `seqused_q`: `seqlen_info.sequence_row_offset` scales the token offset by `qh` before the per-sequence padding; `SeqlenInfo` itself stays in tokens.
- Varlen passes `cu_seqlens_q · qh` / `seqused_q · qh` for them.

When it is used
- `qh ∈ {2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128}` (must divide `tile_m`; step 6 packs the largest power of two dividing `qh` instead and, for hdim 256, loops the rest of the KV head's heads in the CTA), no mask_mod / score_mod / block sparsity / learnable_sink.
- Heuristic: estimated gain `0.25 · 2048 / seqlen_q` (×0.6 − 2% for causal / local) must beat the wave-quantization loss of the `qh`× smaller grid; `FLASH_ATTENTION_BWD_PACK_GQA=0/1` overrides.

**Correctness** (B200)
- New `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_bwd_pack_gqa.py` (packed vs unpacked vs FP64 eager; hd 64/128/256, GQA 8/2, 16/4, 32/4, MQA, dense + varlen with an empty sequence, local, softcap, deterministic, causal): **480 / 96 / 0**. dQ bit-identical to the unpacked path; dK/dV within 1 bf16 ulp (one TMEM accumulation instead of fp32 atomics); deterministic repeats bit-exact.
- Full `test_flash_attn_output` + d=256 varlen subset + hd256 files with the heuristic active: **18,032 / 29 / 9,416** — 18 pre-existing learnable_sink `dSink` ids (#2969) + 11 scheduler bit-equality cases (subset of the parent's 32).
- Unpacked configurations: CUBIN + PTX byte-identical to the parent with `FLASH_ATTENTION_BWD_PACK_GQA=0` (280 files).

**Performance** (B200 @ 1400 MHz locked, two alternating rounds, `benchmark_attn.py --backend fa4 --bwd`, 32k tokens per shape, ms / TFLOPS)
