items.title: Add SM120 kernel-level paged KV cache support
items.body:
## Summary

Implement paged KV cache for SM120 forward kernel using PagedKVManager for in-kernel page table resolution. All page table lookups, pointer arithmetic, and cp.async loads happen inside the CUDA kernel — no PyTorch-level page gathering.

Builds on #2336 (split-KV), #2329, #2330, #2333.

## Key changes

**flash_fwd.py (FlashAttentionForwardBase)**:
- \`_paged_load_page_table_and_ptrs\`: helper that computes per-row GMEM pointers from page table using plain Int32 division. Avoids FastDivmodDivisor which causes MLIR SSA domination errors when used as a loop-carried variable inside the SM80 mainloop.
- \`paged_load_K\` / \`paged_load_V\`: per-row paged loads using shuffle_sync pointer broadcast + chunk-by-chunk cp.async to SMEM. Uses PagedKVManager's copy atom (identical thread layout to SM80's gmem_tiled_copy_K/V).
- Kernel body branches on \`mPageTable is not None\` to create PagedKVManager and use paged load functions instead of standard contiguous loads.

**interface.py**:
- Removed SM120 paged KV assertion
- Added seqused_k requirement for paged KV (since mK.shape[0] = page_size, not seqlen_k)
- For D>64: bumps tile_n from 64 to 128 for paged KV (PagedKVManager needs tile_n >= num_threads). Fits in 99KB SMEM (96KB data + 3KB alignment).

## Validation on SM121a (DGX Spark)

\`\`\`
Paged KV: 8/8 configs pass (D=64+128, page_size=128)

D=64:
  B=1 Sq=64  Sk=128 causal=False: diff=0.003906
  B=1 Sq=64  Sk=256 causal=True:  diff=0.001953
  B=2 Sq=128 Sk=256 causal=False: diff=0.003906

D=128 (tile_n bumped to 128 for paged KV):
  B=1 Sq=128 Sk=128 causal=False: diff=0.003906
  B=1 Sq=128 Sk=256 causal=False: diff=0.001953
  B=1 Sq=128 Sk=256 causal=True:  diff=0.001953
  B=2 Sq=64  Sk=256 causal=False: diff=0.003906
  B=1 Sq=64  Sk=512 causal=True:  diff=0.001953

Non-paged regression: passes
\`\`\`

Contributed by Second Nature Computing (https://joinsecondnature.com)

items.title: [CuTe] Route MLA forward through typed configs
items.body:
Stacked PRs:
 * #3099
 * #3098
 * #3087
 * #3086
 * #2743
 * #2738
 * #2735
 * #3056
 * __->__#3054
 * #3044
 * #3062

--- --- ---

## Human Note

## Agent Notes

This moves every MLA (qv) forward decision into `config.py` as a typed `MlaFwdConfig`, so forward has one
selection boundary for both kernel families. `_flash_attn_fwd` makes one `_get_fwd_config` call that returns `(config, inputs)`, with `config` a `FwdConfig` or an `MlaFwdConfig`; the launch reads config fields directly, and the parallel unpack of config
fields into locals shared with the MLA branch is gone. An explicit `config=` accepts an `MlaFwdConfig` when `qv`
is given and raises `ValueError` for the wrong config type.

- `config.py`: `MlaFwdConfig` (`kernel`: `"2cta"` | `"1cta"` | `"1cta_kb64"`, tiles, `q_stage`, `num_splits`,
  `pack_gqa`, `s_ahead`, `use_clc_scheduler`), `MlaFwdHeuristicInputs` (`FwdHeuristicInputs` plus
  top-k gather, `requires_grad`, `gather_bwd_recompute_p`, descale presence, `FLASH_ATTENTION_MLA_1CTA`), and
  `select_mla_fwd_config` / `validate_mla_fwd_config` (LRU-cached, host-only).
- Moved out of `interface.py`: `_mla_1cta_route`, `_MlaFwdTiles`, `_mla_fwd_plan`, the provisional-1CTA split
  re-check, sparse head padding, and the MLA `pack_gqa` default.
- Moved out of the MLA kernels: `Kb64.can_implement`, both `use_clc` and `use_s_ahead` rules, `TILE_MN`,
  `MIN_BLOCKS_PER_SPLIT`, and `SPARSE_HEAD_TILE`, with their measurement notes. The kernels no longer refine the
  config; the 2CTA kernel now receives `config.use_clc_scheduler`.

Behavior changes:

- The 2CTA MLA kernel always ran CLC (its constructor default) while its compile key carried the generic `FA_CLC`
  gate. The config now records `use_clc_scheduler=True` for 2CTA and passes it. The generated kernel is unchanged
  (1,355 affected calls had identical kernel attributes and tensor arguments); compile keys only merge.
- Dense MLA with a tensor `max_seqlen_q/k` used the tensor in the split math (`bool()` on a device tensor: a
  device-to-host sync on GPU, an error under fake tensors). Selection now uses the host capacity bound, as the
  other forward paths do.
- Descale tensors on 2CTA, a `tile_n` that does not fit the kernel, sparse MLA with fewer than 128 heads and more
  than one KV head, and sparse MLA with `pack_gqa=False` at 128 heads now raise `ValueError` from validation
  instead of a later `AssertionError`.

Also in this PR:

- `FA_CLC`, `_fa_clc_enabled` and `_get_use_clc_scheduler_default` are removed. MLA's default selection no longer
  reads a global request; an explicit `MlaFwdConfig.use_clc_scheduler` is the override. MLA defaults are unchanged
  with `FA_CLC` unset; dense 1CTA (128-key kernel) MLA no longer gets CLC from `FA_CLC=1`.

- kb64 always packs Q heads, so selection resolves its `pack_gqa` to `True` and validation rejects `False`.
- Validation mirrors the kernels' head constraints (0 < heads per KV <= 128 on every MLA kernel, so more than 128 on the 1CTA kernels now raises `ValueError` like 2CTA; packed dense 2CTA ratios divide 128).
- The MLA compile key is the normalized config (`fwd_codegen_config` zeroes `tile_m` and `q_stage`, which no MLA
  kernel consumes), so they no longer create duplicate compiles. Before the FP8 2CTA rejection, kernel attributes and tensor arguments were identical across all 6,048 captured calls; see Validation for the calls that rejection changes.

Review order: `MlaFwdConfig` and `MlaFwdHeuristicInputs`, then `select_mla_fwd_config` and
`validate_mla_fwd_config` in `config.py`, then `_get_fwd_config` and the launch dispatch in `_flash_attn_fwd`,
then the kernel deletions, then `tests/cute/test_mla_fwd_config.py`.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- FP8 is 1CTA-only: `validate_mla_fwd_config` rejects `kernel="2cta"` with FP8 inputs, so an explicit 2CTA
  config or `FLASH_ATTENTION_MLA_1CTA=0` with FP8 raises `ValueError` instead of compiling a kernel that
  faults (the env case also faults on main).
- MLA `tile_m` / `q_stage` validation is permissive because selection passes the caller's `tile_mn` through.
- `FLASH_ATTENTION_MLA_1CTA` is read on every call; any value other than `"1"` still means never.
- `test_flash_attn_mla.py`'s route-heuristic table moved to `test_mla_fwd_config.py` with unchanged expectations.

</details>

## Validation

- Policy parity: a frozen copy of the previous inline routing matches `select_mla_fwd_config` on 4 x 6,000 sampled
  cases plus routing edge cases; changing the 5-split re-route threshold to 4 makes it fail.
- Non-MLA forward selection is identical on 34,992 scheduler-metadata and 3,888 forward cases.
- A fake-tensor capture of 6,048 MLA calls (kernel attributes, tensor arguments, compile key) differs from the parent only in the three cases above. After the FP8 2CTA rejection, the same capture differs from before it only in 481 FP8 calls that reached the 2CTA kernel and now raise `ValueError`, and 127 existing 2CTA `ValueError`s whose message gains "fp8,".
- GPU (GB300, full stack): `test_flash_attn_mla.py` 1381 passed (2CTA default) and 3093 passed
  (`FLASH_ATTENTION_MLA_1CTA=1`); config, autotune and CLC fuzz files 443 passed; `test_flash_attn.py` forward and
  backward subset 42 passed.

items.title: [CuTe, Fwd, SM100] Prevent NaN contamination from unused V cache entries
items.body:
Addresses the SM100 nonpaged forward cases in [#2374](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/issues/2374).

## Summary

When a KV cache contains NaNs beyond `seqused_k`, SM100 forward can return NaNs even though those positions are excluded from attention. Score masking sets their probabilities to zero, but a full-tile V load still brings the unused values into PV, where `0 * NaN` contaminates the output. Packed sequences also need their V loads bounded at each sequence boundary.

Bound each nonpaged V tile by its logical sequence length and let TMA zero-fill the unused rows before PV. The five-dimensional descriptor preserves the real Dv extent, so padded feature columns are also zero-filled. Two address coordinates preserve large aligned head/batch offsets without moving the allocation base; address arithmetic uses Int64 before conversion to bounded coordinates. Existing K loads and pipeline synchronization are preserved.

This covers dense and packed-varlen forward, including `seqused_k` and boundaries supplied only through `cu_seqlens_k`. Public APIs and return types are unchanged. Valid V NaNs retain their existing behavior, and the paged-KV padding contract remains unchanged. Related [#2407](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2407) proposes an SM90 fix; this change addresses the independently reproduced SM100 behavior.

## Correctness

On B200, the original BF16 configuration uses B=4, H=8, D=64, Sq=1, cache capacity 128 and used lengths `[32, 64, 96, 48]`.

| Unused cache contents | Baseline | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V-only NaNs | All 2048 O entries are NaN, 10/10 attempts | Finite O matching tightly packed attention, 10/10 |
| K/V NaNs | All 2048 O entries are NaN, 10/10 attempts | Finite O matching tightly packed attention, 10/10 |
| Zero, finite values, or K-only NaNs | Pass, 10/10 each | Pass, 10/10 each |

The patched maximum absolute error against FP64 is **0.00217703 for O** and **0.00002045 for LSE**. O/LSE match the tightly packed run bitwise. Baseline and patched runs compiled in separate fresh processes with persistent caching disabled; repeated calls within each process reused its compiled kernels. A semantically neutral refactor retained both NaN failures in all 10 attempts.

A broader 40-configuration reproduction covering D64/128, Sq1/257, dense/packed and five tail modes passes **40/40** after the fix; the baseline fails all **16 V-poisoned configurations**. Each configuration was run 10 times, including an actual 2CTA specialization.

## Tests

**194 GPU correctness cases passed:**

- **96 new main-matrix cases:** FP16/BF16, D64/128, dense/packed, causal/noncausal, MHA/GQA/MQA, and SplitKV 1/3.
- **50 new edge cases:** actual 2CTA and forced 1CTA, Dv8/24/80, larger head-dimension controls, aligned noncontiguous and broadcast layouts, adjacent packed sequences, and FP8 E4M3/E5M2.
- **48 existing cases:** 36 dense/varlen fast tests, including supported backward paths, and 12 paged padding-contract tests.

The new tests check O against FP64 and low-precision references, LSE against an independent FP64 calculation, bitwise invariance to unused-tail poisoning, empty sequences, and propagation of valid V NaNs. All **146 new cases** passed both FakeTensor compilation and real execution; the execution phase recorded **zero kernel compilations**.

`compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` reports **zero device memory errors** for 44 of the new cases and four additional public-API cases with V batch offsets or row pitches exceeding 32GiB. Minimal descriptor-copy checks also cover padded feature dimensions and large offsets.

Disassembly confirms that the two V load sites in the focused packed kernel become five-coordinate TMA loads, while the other three tensor-load sites remain three-coordinate loads. The 2CTA specialization retains `UTMALDG.5D.2CTA`. The focused kernel uses 128 registers with zero stack/local memory in both revisions.

Test selections:

```bash
FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1 FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 \
  pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k sm100_unused_v_cache

FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=0 FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 \
  FLASH_ATTENTION_TEST_EXPECT_CACHED=1 \
  pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k sm100_unused_v_cache

pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn_fast.py \
  -k '(test_flash_attn_output or test_flash_attn_varlen_output) and 256'

pytest -q tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_paged_padding_contract
```

Kernel Ruff, formatting of the added tests, and `git diff --check` pass. The existing test file has no additional Ruff diagnostics relative to the baseline.

## Performance

Across **16 working controls**, aggregated complete-forward median latency changed by **−0.26% to +2.22%**. Three independent runs measured every control; the largest increase in any individual run was **2.23%**. No measured control exceeded the 5% regression threshold. Finite-input baseline/patched O and LSE matched bitwise throughout.

<details>
<summary>Full forward benchmark results, method and environment</summary>

All inputs are BF16. Full-sequence controls use B=2, Sq=Sk=2048 and Hq=Hkv=8. Partial-cache controls use B=4, cache capacity 2048, used length 2047, D128, Hq=8 and Hkv=2, with noncausal attention.

Measurements ran on a Slurm-allocated B200 with no other compute process present at preflight. Each of three fresh processes used separate baseline/patched compilation caches and CUDA Graphs. Each graph contains ten complete forward calls, including SplitKV combine when applicable. O/LSE are preallocated; compilation and allocation are excluded from replay timing.

After warmup, seven rounds alternate baseline/patched measurement order. Each round contains seven samples per revision; each sample replays its graph 20 times. Values below are medians of the three independent run medians, in microseconds per forward. Percentages use the unrounded aggregated latencies.

| Layout | Workload | D | Causal | Splits | Baseline µs | Patched µs | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Dense | Full | 64 | No | 1 | 25.465 | 25.482 | +0.07% |
| Dense | Full | 64 | Yes | 1 | 25.853 | 25.839 | −0.05% |
| Dense | Full | 128 | No | 1 | 31.547 | 31.779 | +0.74% |
| Dense | Full | 128 | Yes | 1 | 27.247 | 27.242 | −0.02% |
| Dense | Partial, Sq=1 | 128 | No | 1 | 18.080 | 18.033 | −0.26% |
| Dense | Partial, Sq=1 | 128 | No | 3 | 13.634 | 13.936 | +2.22% |
| Dense | Partial, Sq=257 | 128 | No | 1 | 27.650 | 27.859 | +0.76% |
| Dense | Partial, Sq=257 | 128 | No | 3 | 21.127 | 21.264 | +0.65% |
| Packed | Full | 64 | No | 1 | 33.168 | 33.217 | +0.15% |
| Packed | Full | 64 | Yes | 1 | 28.115 | 28.443 | +1.16% |
| Packed | Full | 128 | No | 1 | 32.995 | 33.136 | +0.43% |
| Packed | Full | 128 | Yes | 1 | 30.428 | 30.549 | +0.40% |
| Packed | Partial, Sq=1 | 128 | No | 1 | 18.847 | 18.983 | +0.72% |
| Packed | Partial, Sq=1 | 128 | No | 3 | 17.008 | 17.213 | +1.20% |
| Packed | Partial, Sq=257 | 128 | No | 1 | 28.679 | 28.656 | −0.08% |
| Packed | Partial, Sq=257 | 128 | No | 3 | 30.700 | 30.743 | +0.14% |

Environment: NVIDIA B200/SM100; driver 580.126.20; Python 3.12.14; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1; apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11; quack-kernels 0.6.5. Validation baseline: [94e22c9](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/commit/94e22c906678e5483fa0e9e24d8e787bc2c0ed4c).

</details>

## Limitations

GPU clocks were not locked. These measurements cover the listed controls. Earlier measurements with competing GPU workloads are excluded. SM90/SM110 execution, NaN-tail backward behavior and the full parameterized test suite were not exercised.

The raw validation logs and timing samples have not been published with this PR; the tables above summarize the local validation campaign.

items.title: [FA3,SM90,Fwd] Enable symmetric head dim 512 forward
items.body:
Hi, from [novita.ai](https://novita.ai)

## Summary

Enable forward attention for **symmetric head_dim=512** on SM90 (Hopper), targeting models like **Gemma 4 31B** (nq=32, nkv=4, d=512).

- **Forward only** (no backward kernels for d=512)
- **SM90 only** (Hopper H100/H200)
- **BF16 / FP16** (no FP8)
- PagedKV via TMA path supported; non-TMA paged path disabled (register pressure)
- Reuses the existing `LargeHeadDimV` two-warp-group path originally built for MLA (hdim=64, hdimv=512)
- Adds `FLASH_ATTENTION_DISABLE_HDIM512` build flag
- Adds d=512 to `test_flash_attn.py` parametrization
- Fixes a latent pipeline_v consumer count bug (see below)

## Tiling Strategy for d=512

**Tile size**: `kBlockM=64, kBlockN=32, kStages=2, MmaPV_is_RS=false`

### SMEM Budget Analysis (228KB available on SM90)

For BF16 (2 bytes/element), 2 pipeline stages:
- **Q tile**: 64 × 512 × 2B = 64KB (1 copy, not pipelined)
- **K tile**: 32 × 512 × 2B × 2 stages = 64KB
- **V tile**: 32 × 512 × 2B × 2 stages = 64KB
- **P tile**: 64 × 32 × 2B = 4KB (softmax output in SMEM for MmaPV SS)
- **O tile**: 64 × 512 × 4B ≈ scratch (accumulated in registers)
- **Pipeline barriers + misc**: ~1KB
- **Total**: ~197KB (fits in 228KB)

### Why kBlockN=32 (vs kBlockN=64 for MLA)

The MLA path (hdim=64, hdimv=512) can afford kBlockN=64 because Q/K are only 64-dim, so SMEM for Q+K is much smaller. With symmetric d=512, Q+K SMEM doubles, forcing kBlockN down to 32 to stay within the 228KB budget while keeping 2 pipeline stages for double buffering.

### WarpGroup Strategy (LargeHeadDimV path)

Two warp groups with asymmetric roles:
- **WG1**: Computes QK^T (64×32 @ 32×512 → 64×32 scores) → softmax → writes P to SMEM → computes half of P×V
- **WG0 (mma_pv)**: Only computes P×V (reads P + rescale factors from SMEM)

This avoids cross-WG softmax reduction — WG1 owns the full score row and computes softmax independently. P matrix and rescale factors are communicated via SMEM + `PFull`/`PEmpty` named barriers.

### WGMMA Configuration

- **QK MMA**: AtomLayout (1, 1, 1), tiler (64, 32) — single WG, SS mode
- **PV MMA**: AtomLayout (1, 2, 1), tiler (64, 256) — 2 WGs split headdim_v, SS mode (MmaPV_is_RS=false required by `static_assert`)

## Bug Fix: pipeline_v consumer count for SameHeadDim + LargeHeadDimV

Fixed a **latent bug in FA3's template code** (`flash_fwd_kernel_sm90.h`) where the pipeline_v consumer count was incorrectly set when `SameHeadDim=true && LargeHeadDimV=true && Use_TMA_KV=true`.

**Root cause**: The original code coupled the V consumer count update to the `!SameHeadDim` condition (since V transaction bytes only differ when head dims differ). But the consumer count for pipeline_v should always be `NumMmaThreads` (2 WGs) when `LargeHeadDimV`, regardless of whether head dims match.

**Before (broken for symmetric d=512)**:
```cpp
if constexpr (Use_TMA_KV && !SameHeadDim) {
    pipeline_params_vt.transaction_bytes = ...;
    if constexpr (LargeHeadDimV) { pipeline_params_vt.num_consumers = NumMmaThreads; }
} else {
    // When Use_TMA_KV && SameHeadDim: sets consumer_arv_count (wrong field for TMA!)
    if constexpr (LargeHeadDimV) { pipeline_params_vt.consumer_arv_count = NumMmaThreads; }
}
```

**After (correct)**:
```cpp
if constexpr (Use_TMA_KV && !SameHeadDim) {
    pipeline_params_vt.transaction_bytes = ...;
}
if constexpr (LargeHeadDimV) {
    if constexpr (Use_TMA_KV) {
        pipeline_params_vt.num_consumers = NumMmaThreads;
    } else {
        pipeline_params_vt.consumer_arv_count = NumMmaThreads;
    }
}
```

This bug was never triggered before because `LargeHeadDimV && SameHeadDim` (symmetric d>256) was never instantiated — the MLA path always has `SameHeadDim=false`.

## Benchmark Results (H200, BF16, Gemma 4 31B shape: nq=32, nkv=4, d=512)

<details>
<summary>Decode Attention (memory-bound, GB/s)</summary>


</details>

## Test plan

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Put the forward shared-memory layout in the config
items.body:
Stacked PRs:
 * #3099
 * #3098
 * #3087
 * #3086
 * #2743
 * #2738
 * #2735
 * __->__#3056
 * #3054
 * #3044
 * #3062

--- --- ---

## Human Note

## Agent Notes

The SM100 forward kernel decided its own shared-memory layout: whether O aliases Q (`overlap_sO_sQ`) and how many
K/V pipeline stages fit (`kv_stage`). Both change the generated kernel and its performance, but the config never
saw them, and `config.py` kept a hand copy of the hd192 case only. This makes them `FwdConfig` fields, so the
kernel takes the layout instead of deriving it, validation can reject layouts that do not fit, and autotune can
search them.

- `config.py`: `select_sm100_smem_layout` returns `(overlap_sO_sQ, kv_stage)` with today's rules (224 KB budget,
  32-stage cap, the hd192/128 uneven `[K, V, K]` three-stage layout, the persistent hd256 2CTA separate-O rule).
  `sm100_fwd_smem_bytes` models the kernel's whole shared-memory struct (barriers, row statistics, scheduler
  buffers, 1024-aligned O/Q/K/V) and replaces `sm100_hd192_uneven_kv_smem_bytes` and its overhead constant.
  `validate_fwd_config` rejects `kv_stage` outside [2, 32], an uneven layout with `tile_n % 32 != 0`, and any
  layout over the SM100 limit. Non-SM100 configs carry neutral values (`False`, `0`).
- `flash_fwd_sm100.py`: `FlashAttentionForwardSm100` reads `overlap_sO_sQ` and `kv_stage` from its config and
  asserts the struct fits; the byte arithmetic and `_setup_attributes` are gone. Both reach the compile key
  through the config.

Behavior changes:

- None for selected configs.
- Explicit configs with `kv_stage < 2` or a misaligned uneven `tile_n` raise `ValueError` instead of deadlocking or
  hitting a kernel assert. The hd192 `tile_n=192` rejection keeps its 247808-byte calibration with a generic
  message.
- Explicit configs derived with `dataclasses.replace` keep their layout fields. Changing `tile_n`, `q_stage`, or
  2CTA without a matching `kv_stage` can be rejected for size; that is intended, the config owns the layout.
  `derive_fwd_config` with only `overlap_sO_sQ` changed sizes `kv_stage` for the requested overlap.

Also in this PR:

- The uneven `[K, V, K]` layout is 1CTA-only. Its stage offset assumes full K/V tiles, so under 2CTA V at stage 1
  overlapped K at stage 2: an explicit 2CTA hd192/128 config with `kv_stage=3` gave wrong output (max error about
  0.2 vs the default kernel; 0 after the fix). The same bug exists on main for an explicit `tile_mn`; default
  selection never chose it.
- `derive_fwd_config` (from #2733) also re-derives the layout after edits unless the caller sets it, so benchmark arms and autotune candidates built from a selected config stay consistent (#2735 and
  #2743 use it).

Review order: `select_sm100_smem_layout`, `sm100_fwd_smem_bytes`, and the layout checks in `validate_fwd_config`
(`config.py`), then the `FlashAttentionForwardSm100` constructor, then `tests/cute/test_fwd_config.py`.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- Flat fields rather than a typed SM100 record, matching the other SM100-only flags (`use_tma_o`,
  `use_s_ping_pong`).
- No explicit "hd192 needs overlap" or "SplitKV hdv>=128 needs overlap" rules: the kernel has no code depending on
  them; they follow from the size limit (hd192 with `q_stage=1` and separate buffers fits).
- The struct size is checked twice: by `sm100_fwd_smem_bytes` in validation and by an assert in the kernel after
  it builds its struct, so kernel edits that change the struct fail at compile time.
- SM90 forward has no equivalent hidden decision (O always aliases Q; two stages fixed by the interface).
- `derive_fwd_config` re-derives the layout after a change, and the benchmark (#2735) and autotune (#2743) build candidates with it.

</details>

## Validation

- A frozen copy of the kernel's old formula matches the selected layout over dtype (bf16/fp16/fp8), head dims
  (64, 96, 128, 192/128, 256), `q_stage`, `tile_n` (64/128/192), 2CTA, scheduler (single-tile, static, CLC,
  dynamic semaphore), and SplitKV; breaking the hd256 overlap rule fails 3 tests.
- Forward selection is unchanged on 34,992 scheduler-metadata and 3,888 forward cases.
- Fake-tensor capture of 1,843 kernels per arch (sm_100, sm_103): identical `overlap_sO_sQ`, `kv_stage`, uneven
  layout and offset, register split, and struct bytes vs the parent; `sm100_fwd_smem_bytes` equals the real struct
  size in every captured kernel.
- GPU (GB300): `test_flash_attn.py` forward subset 1352 passed (on this commit) plus 22 config/CLC/metadata;
  `test_clc_fuzz.py` 199 passed; on the full stack, config/autotune/MLA config files 235 passed.

items.title: [CuTe, SM120] Forward kernel with optimized TMA path and full features support
items.body:
This PR introduces separate sm120 forward kernel with optimized TMA path and full features support (except block sparsity).

I started developing it about two months ago with primary focus on improving performance relative to sm80 (which also executable on sm120 hardware), then this PR was opened 
 https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2349 and I discovered that its performance is slightly worse than mine and other features were split into separate PR's

Summary about performance relative to sm80 kernel: 
- In most cases TMA version is slightly better by 2-3%, but there are cases of about 5% better and worth both. Detailed performance and correctness tables are below.
- Its performance slightly improves with greater batches and degrades with greater heads count. Performance delta with `pack_gqa` is smaller.
- I think further speed up attempts should utilize quantization in some way, not necessary in using sm120 mma ops for quantized inputs, but maybe transferring big quantized tiles into smem and upcast to half in registers. TMA benefits are limited on sm120 because of its smem capacity.

## Feature matrix comparing with https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2349

| Area | `Sm120Tma` | `Sm120TMAOptimized` |
|---|---|---|
| Core transfer model | TMA for Q/K/V | TMA for K/V always; Q can be TMA, cp.async, or direct gmem->regs decode |
| O global store | SMEM->GMEM copy path only (`use_tma_O = False`) | Supports TMA S2G O-store in eligible cases; otherwise SMEM/copy path |
| Decode q1 direct Q gmem->regs | Not implemented | Implemented via `direct_q_gmem_regs_decode`, it can be faster in some cases |
| pack-GQA handling | Supports pack-GQA mode, but no dedicated packed-Q TMA atom path | Dedicated pack-GQA Q TMA atom path (`make_packgqa_tiled_tma_atom`) + pack-aware load/store helpers. Changes in pack_gqa.py were necessary for kernel correctness when `cute.arch.WARP_SIZE % threads_per_row != 0` (head dims 96, 192) |
| Split-KV | Not supported (`num_splits = 1`, `is_split_kv = False`) | Supported (rank-based split detection, split-aware LSE/O writes) |
| Paged KV (`mPageTable`) | Explicitly unsupported (assert) | Supported with restriction: K/V must be batched dense (no varlen K with page table) |
| Varlen (`cu_seqlens`) | Supported | Supported |
| SeqUsed (`mSeqUsedQ`, `mSeqUsedK`) | Supported | Supported |
| Persistent scheduling | Not used (`is_persistent=False`) | Used for non-causal non-local dense Q; varlen and causal/local use non-persistent schedulers |
| Scheduler variants | SingleTile / SingleTileVarlen | SingleTile / SingleTileLPT / SingleTileVarlen with dynamic selection |
| Pipeline/barrier model | Separate Q/K/V TMA pipelines | Unified SM100-style configurable barrier layout, optional Q-K barrier sharing, K/V stage-offset interleaving |
| Shared-memory reuse | Separate sQ, sK, sV regions | Aliases O with Q, and in decode-direct mode aliases Q/O into KV region |
| Register policy | `Q_in_regs=False` | `Q_in_regs=True`, `K_in_regs=True` (default), with explicit preload behavior |
| Block sparsity | Not implemented (no active path) | Explicitly rejected (`NotImplementedError`) |

Currently I don't wired my kernel into interface.py, I can either:
- rename it to `flash_fwd_sm120_tma.py` and wire this into interface, if this PR won't be merged https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2349
- when https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2349 will be merged - can rebase my features onto it

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Add swap-AB split-KV decode
items.body:
This PR adds a single-token decode kernel adapted from NVIDIA CUTLASS `gqa_decode_opt`. It computes `Sᵀ = KQᵀ` and `Oᵀ = VᵀPᵀ`, putting KV tokens on the 128-row MMA dimension and query heads on the smaller N dimension. For small query-head groups, this wastes less work on padding than the regular forward layout.

The kernel keeps the two alternating softmax warpgroups, lagged output correction, PDL and cluster atomic reduction. The main reduction change is in **kernel mode**: the combine kernel reduces per-split maxima directly, removing the global running-max buffer and its memset. **Atomic mode still zeros the output** before TMA reduce-add. Both modes support `seqused_k` and LSE.

This adds a separate `flash_attn_decode_func` entry point for dense, single-token fp16/bf16 attention; it does not change `flash_attn_func` dispatch or add paged KV support.

## Benchmarks

B200, BF16, against FA4 at `3451a2a` (including the S/P ping-pong from #2817). CUDA graphs, at least 512 MiB of rotating KV inputs, default split heuristics. Results use the minimum of three round medians, seven replays per round. Atomic timings include output zeroing.

![FA4 vs swap-AB: groupwise bandwidth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ighoshsubho/flash-attention/sm100-swapab-decode/agent_space/sm100_decode/figures/decode_groupwise_bandwidth.png)

![FA4 vs swap-AB: bandwidth across batch sizes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ighoshsubho/flash-attention/sm100-swapab-decode/agent_space/sm100_decode/figures/decode_batch_bandwidth.png)

items.title: [CuTe] Route forward through typed configs
items.body:
Stacked PRs:
 * #2743
 * #2741
 * #2738
 * #2735
 * #3056
 * #3054
 * #3044
 * #3062
 * __->__#2733

--- --- ---

## Human Note
Wire it up 


## Agent Notes

This routes the real forward path through the typed config layer from #2732. `_flash_attn_fwd` now builds one
`FwdHeuristicInputs` from host-visible metadata, then either selects a config (`config=None`) or validates the
explicit `FwdConfig` passed through the new keyword-only `config=` argument, and launches exactly that config. The
inline policy it replaces (`_get_fwd_config`, `_tile_size_fwd_sm90`, and the 2CTA, CLC, static-persistence, and
S ping-pong blocks, plus the kernel-side TMA-O rule) is deleted; `select_fwd_config` reproduces it. Public wrappers
and autograd functions are unchanged.

The forward compile key holds the config itself, normalized by `fwd_codegen_config` (SplitKV on/off rather than the
split count), instead of a hand-listed subset of its fields, so a new config field cannot be left out of the key.
Forcing `num_splits=2` and `4` still reuses one main and one combine specialization. `FlashAttentionForwardSm100`
takes `config: FwdConfig` instead of the config-derived arguments, so an explicit config cannot be silently
overridden in the kernel; `use_tma_o` and the register split are config fields. `FlashAttentionForwardSm90` takes
`registers=` from the config. Generated register splits match main for every non-MLA kernel; MLA keeps its own
splits (`registers=None`). `derive_fwd_config(base, inputs, **changes)` recomputes the dependent fields (registers,
ex2 emulation) after an edit unless the caller sets them.

The SM100 softmax exp2 emulation follows the same pattern. `ex2_emu_freq` (0 = off) and `ex2_emu_start_frg` are
config fields chosen by `select_ex2_emu` with the kernel's former rules (default enable rule, `SM100_TUNING`
and FP8 table lookups, packed-GQA varlen frequency); disabled emulation is `(0, 0)`, and other architectures carry
`(0, 0)`. The kernel takes both from the config instead of deciding them in `__init__`/`__call__`, and both are in
the compile key. Compile-only capture on sm_100/sm_103 (1,980 kernels each, 660 FP8): identical ex2 and register
settings vs the previous tip; 7 representative cubins byte-identical.

`pack_gqa` is also a config field. `FwdHeuristicInputs.pack_gqa` carries the caller's request (`None` = default),
and `select_fwd_config` resolves it before any other policy reads it: the default rule, or the request, forced off
when block-sparse masks are not head-broadcast (`sparse_mask_per_head`). `validate_fwd_config` rejects an explicit
config that disagrees with a `pack_gqa=` request or packs with per-head sparse masks. The interface reads
`config.pack_gqa`.

The input -> config path in `_flash_attn_fwd` is: derive host facts once (`total_k`, `q_capacity`/`k_capacity`,
`host_max_seqlen_q/k`, `caller_max_seqlen_q`), then `config = _get_fwd_config(...)`, which builds the inputs
through `_get_fwd_inputs` (shared with `get_scheduler_metadata`, so the two cannot drift) and selects or
validates. No policy remains in the interface.

Behavior changes against the previous inline path:

- An explicit `config` together with caller-built `scheduler_metadata` raises `ValueError`; that metadata encodes the
  default tile, stage, split, and scheduling choices. Metadata passed with `disable_scheduler_metadata=True` is
  ignored by both this check and the selector (`has_caller_scheduler_metadata`).
- Block-sparse PackGQA fallback now runs inside selection, so `q_stage`, splits, and 2CTA eligibility see the layout
  that actually runs.
- Tensor `max_seqlen_q/k` (non-SM100) resolve to the same host bounds as the other paths instead of a tensor value;
  this can enable single-M-block static persistence for dense causal decode.
- When caller metadata carries a tile-count semaphore (`has_tile_count_semaphore`), varlen-Q selection does not pick
  static persistence or CLC over the dynamic persistent scheduler.
- `get_scheduler_metadata` uses the same selector (including `seqlen_k_per_split`) and builds the tile-count semaphore
  from the selected config (`use_clc_scheduler=config.use_clc_scheduler`) instead of the raw `FA_CLC` flag. With
  `FA_CLC=1`, varlen MHA does not select CLC, so its metadata now keeps the semaphore the forward expects.
- `seqlen_k_per_split` now reaches selection in direct calls too: when automatic SplitKV engages, the split count is
  raised to cover `max_seqlen_k / seqlen_k_per_split`.
- `get_scheduler_metadata` gains an optional keyword-only `dtype=` (default `torch.bfloat16`, the previous
  assumption) and launches the metadata kernel with `config.pack_gqa`.
- `benchmarks/tune_ex2_emu.py` is removed: it regex-patched `SM100_TUNING` at runtime, and explicit configs
  now carry the ex2 and register fields directly (`benchmarks/fwd_config_bench.py`).
- The dead `num_threads` argument of `_flash_attn_fwd` is removed (SM80/SM120 always used 128; SM90 derives it).
- MLA (`qv`) keeps its own planner (`_mla_fwd_plan`, now returning `_MlaFwdTiles`) and rejects an explicit `config`.
- Automatic `num_splits` (`num_splits < 1`) resolves to one split outside SM100/SM110 (#2732). On SM120 this matches
  the old path; on SM80/SM90 automatic selection of a decode shape no longer fails with a SplitKV assertion.

Review order: `_get_fwd_inputs` and `_get_fwd_config`, the `qv is None` block in `_flash_attn_fwd`
(`interface.py`), the `pack_gqa` resolution at the top of `select_fwd_config`/`validate_fwd_config`, then `get_scheduler_metadata`,
then the `use_tma_o` change in `flash_fwd_sm100.py`, and the tests.

## Performance

No policy change: on H100 (SM90) all 18 shapes of the stack-wide sweep (dense, causal, hd192/hd256, FP16, varlen, decode) are within 0.997–1.002x of main with identical outputs, and B200/B300 cells that no later PR tunes are within ±0.5%.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- `FwdHeuristicInputs.has_lse` is `lse is not None` after LSE allocation, so it is true for a preallocated LSE,
  `return_lse`, or autograd.
- `requested_num_splits` is `None` for `num_splits < 1` (automatic); `FA_CLC`, the 2CTA disable flag, and the
  S ping-pong disable flag are read once and passed as `requested_use_clc_scheduler`, `disable_2cta`, and
  `disable_s_ping_pong`.
- On the MLA path the CLC choice is computed locally with the old rule (no CLC for varlen MHA or dense
  noncausal) and then refined by the 1CTA kernel's `use_clc`; the other SM100 flags are fixed to `False`.
- `FlashAttentionForwardSm100` asserts that `use_tma_o` is not combined with the hd256 SplitKV chunked epilogue.
- `get_scheduler_metadata` passes `pack_gqa=None` to the selector instead of its old inline `qhead_per_kvhead > 1`
  default, so metadata and the forward agree. This changes one case: SM100 hd256 GQA with only `cu_seqlens_k`
  (e.g. 24/8 heads, `seqlen_q` 512 or 4096) now builds metadata for the unpacked 2CTA config the forward selects,
  not packed 1CTA. With caller metadata, selection never depends on dtype (4,608-case sweep), so the BF16 default
  is safe.
- Refactor parity: the selector inputs, selected configs, and errors match the previous inline path on 34,992
  `get_scheduler_metadata` cases and 3,888 FakeTensor forward cases.
- After the simplification pass: 47,124 selected configs identical over 52,488 metadata + 3,888 forward cases
  (the only differences are SM80/SM90 neutral-field error texts), distinct compile-key counts unchanged (7,190
  forward keys on `test_flash_attn.py`), and 7 representative SM100 cubins byte-identical.
- Host overhead (review follow-up): `fwd_codegen_config` is cached and the register check no longer deep-copies
  via `astuple`. Enqueue time per call vs main (GB300, median of 3 alternating rounds): dense tiny hd128
  42.3 → 41.3 µs, varlen hd128 causal 2k 52.2 → 49.9, decode GQA 42.4 → 40.9, varying `max_seqlen_q`
  50.0 → 49.4 (previous head: +4–6 µs).

New GPU tests in `tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py` (SM100/SM110) use `maybe_fake_tensor_mode`, so they run in the
FakeTensor compile pass:

- `test_flash_attn_forced_split_config_reuses_specializations`: main and combine cache keys are unchanged between
  `num_splits=2` and `4`; both match an SDPA reference.
- `test_flash_attn_explicit_config_rejects_caller_scheduler_metadata`: an explicit config succeeds alone and raises
  with caller metadata.
- `test_flash_attn_explicit_config_ignores_disabled_scheduler_metadata`: the selected hd256 varlen 2CTA config is
  accepted when metadata is disabled.
- `test_scheduler_metadata_semaphore_follows_selected_scheduler`: with `FA_CLC=1`, varlen MHA metadata keeps
  `tile_count_semaphore`.

</details>

items.title: [CuTe, SM90] Bound the K/V TMA loads by seqlen_k (fwd + bwd, packed varlen and dense seqused_k)
items.body:
Related: #2374, #2999, #2407. SM100 backward counterpart: #3012 (merged as `2bdeddd1`; this PR is rebased onto it and only carries the SM90 commits). SM100 forward counterpart: #2983 (merged).

## Problem

Whenever the logical K length is shorter than the buffer — packed varlen (`cu_seqlens_k`) or dense `(b, s, h, d)` with `seqused_k` — the SM90 forward and backward TMA-load whole K/V tiles, so rows in `[seqlen_k, tile_n)` arrive as whatever the buffer holds past the end. Masking makes `P` and `dS` exactly zero there, but `0 * NaN = NaN`:

- forward: `O = P @ V` reads the V tail → NaN output (the #2374 / #2999 report on Hopper). A NaN K tail is harmless (masked to -inf before exp).
- backward: `dP = dO @ V^T` reads the V tail and `dQ = dS @ K` sums over the whole K tile → `dQ` all-NaN from a NaN tail in **K or V**, for every sequence whose last K tile straddles the tail; `dK`/`dV` stay finite. Independent of the forward: with a finite `O` and `D`, `dQ` is still NaN. In the dense layout this is the worse case: once the forward is bounded, `O` and the loss are clean and only the gradient is NaN.

## Fix

Same change as #2983 / #3012: build the V (forward) and K, V (backward) TMA descriptors with `flash_attn.cute.copy_utils.create_ragged_tensor_for_tma_load` (the load-safe 5-D form #2983 introduced; #3012 generalises it to any rows dimension and to a whole-sequence view) and offset the view by `(offset_k, seqlen_k)` per sequence (forward) or per K/V tile (backward), so each load is bounded by the logical length and TMA's own OOB zero-fill clears the tail. The ragged path is taken when `cu_seqlens_k` or `seqused_k` is given; plain dense calls are untouched. No change to the pipeline, barriers or byte counts. The forward excludes paged KV (finite rows past `seqused_k` inside a page are a caller contract) and broadcast (seq-stride 0) V views, like #2983. The dK/dV and O stores keep quack's `ptr_shift` form.

Supersedes #2407 (thanks @NJX-njx for the first SM90 forward attempt, which zeroed the partial V tile in shared memory).

**Not covered:** FA3 C++ (`hopper/`) is untouched.

## Validation (H100 SXM, main `a6fcdfdb` + #3012)

- Probes, `seqused_k` 100/256/37/200 in a 4×256 K/V buffer, packed and dense, hd64 / 96 / 128 / 192-v128 (forward) and hd64 / 128 (backward), NaN past `seqused_k` in K / V / both: output and `dQ` NaN counts 393216 (hd64) / 786432 (hd128) on main → **0** on both layouts; `O`, `dQ` and the valid `dK`/`dV` rows bitwise equal to the zero-tail run.
- New tests `test_flash_attn_sm90_fwd_unused_v_tail` and `test_flash_attn_sm90_bwd_unused_kv_tail` (fp16/bf16 × hd64/128 × causal × MHA/GQA × packed/dense, 32 cases each, FakeTensor pass supported): against main's kernels all 64 fail (`out has NaN/Inf` / `dq has NaN/Inf`); here 64/64 pass in both passes, 0 kernel compiles in the execution pass.
- Existing tests: 400 sampled `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` with `cu_seqlens_k` plus 1357 ids that pass `seqused_k` in the dense layout (`varlen_output` with `unpad_kv=False`, all `kvcache` with `page_size=None`, `lse_grad_unused`, `seqlen_k_zero`, the metadata/paged contract tests): 0 numerical failures. The two-pass harness flags a set of causal ids as "compiled during the execution pass"; main shows the same set (pre-existing compile-key drift, all pass when run normally).
- Timing, alternating rounds main vs PR (µs, bf16): every forward and backward shape within ±2 %; dense controls unchanged. Forward 28 cases (packed, packed uneven + `seqused_k`, dense control, dense + `seqused_k` prefill B4×512 and decode B32×1 over a 4096 cap), backward 14 cases.

items.title: Performance Degradation for Variable-Length Batching on FA3 (H100)
items.body: I am benchmarking the FA3 kernel on an H100, and I observed a significant performance gap between uniform-length and variable-length batches. Specifically, scenarios where most requests are decode (q_len=1) and just one is a prefill (q_len=L) perform much worse than when all requests are decode-only. - GPU: NVIDIA H100 SXM - FA3 version: vLLM 0.9.1 complied FA3 binary (_vllm_fa3_C.abi3.so) - FA3 usage: Pack q, k, and v by squeezing the batch size dim and q_len dim. Prepare the cumulative q_len and cumulative k_len meta data. Set rest arguments as default or None. ``` torch.ops._vllm_fa3_C.fwd(q, k, v, None, None, None, None, cu_q, cu_k, None, None, None, max_q, max_k, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, SCALE, True, -1, -1, 0.0, None, None, 0, None, 0) ``` - Model shape: - head_dim: 128 - num_heads: 32 - num_kv_heads: 8 - Batch configs: - decode_only: all B requests with q_len = 1, k_len = L - decode_dominate: (B - 1) requests with q_len = 1, 1 request with q_len = L. All B requests with k_len = L Plots below show the measured latency across different B and L for two batch configs. The results show that decode_dominate batch config performs much worse than decode_only batch config, though including only one prefill request in the batch. Could you please clarify why this happens? Is this an expected limitation of the current FA3 implementation, or is there room for optimization?

items.title: [Cute,Fwd,Sm120] Fix three forward-pass correctness bugs (use_tma_O, smem-store atom, pack_gqa)
items.body:
## Summary

Three independent bugs prevent FA4's forward kernel from producing correct output on consumer Blackwell (SM_120) GPUs as of `flash-attn-4==4.0.0b12`. All three reproduce on `main` at the current HEAD.

- **Compile crash in the epilogue.** `use_tma_O` was True on SM_120 but the SM80 base class never wires a TMA atom for O — it passes `None` to `self.epilogue`, and the epilogue crashes inside `quack.copy_utils.tma_get_copy_fn`.
- **Silent numerical wrongness.** The rmem→smem store atom in the epilogue was the SM90 `stmatrix` (chosen by `get_smem_store_atom` for any `arch >= 90`), but the SM80 base class's `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16` output register layout is not compatible with it. The kernel completed, returned the correct shape, and the output norm matched SDPA — but **element-wise values were wrong** by 0.5–3.9 (bf16/fp16, vs SDPA-bf16's own ~0.003).
- **Compile crash on every default-policy GQA/MQA shape.** `pack_gqa.compute_ptr` trips `cute.crd2idx` because cuTeDSL 4.4.2 collapses the composite `(qhead_per_kvhead, seqlen_q)` mode in `mO[None, 0]` to a rank-1 layout. Pragmatic mitigation here: default `pack_gqa=False` on SM_120 until the deeper cuTeDSL issue is fixed; explicit `pack_gqa=True` is still honoured.

After this PR, the SM_120 forward kernel matches PyTorch SDPA-bf16's own numerical accuracy across a 240-shape grid (240/240 pass, max abs diffs bit-identical to SDPA's on 219/240 shapes and within `3.5e-5` on the rest) and is ~1.15× faster on average (range 0.74×–1.95×).

## Bugs and fixes at a glance

Each commit has a focused message with the full root-cause writeup; this is the summary.

| # | File | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `flash_fwd.py:652` | `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '_trait'` at trace time | `self.use_tma_O = False` unconditionally in the SM80 base class |
| 2 | `flash_fwd.py:347` | Kernel runs to completion, returns plausible output, but max abs diff vs fp32 reference is 0.5–3.9 (vs ~0.003 for SDPA-bf16) | Force `get_smem_store_atom(80, ...)` so the SM80 base class always uses the universal copy, not the SM90 stmatrix |
| 3 | `interface.py:430` | `ValueError: Operation creation failed` (`unable to compute crd2idx`) on every default-policy GQA/MQA shape | Default `pack_gqa=False` on SM_120 |

Bug 2 (the stmatrix mismatch) is the headline fix — silent numerical wrongness is the worst kind of bug to ship and this one would propagate into training loss / eval quality for any model using FA4 on consumer Blackwell.

## How the headline bug was found

The error profile was very specific and ruled out most hypotheses up-front:

- Bitwise-deterministic across reruns → not a race / scheduler issue.
- Uniform across all M-tiles (not concentrated in m_block=0) → not a kernel prologue / initialisation issue.
- Scales linearly with input magnitude → precision / permutation signature, not a logic bug.
- Output norm preserved to ~3 significant digits → values are reshuffled with their same-magnitude neighbours, not zeroed.

That pattern points at a memory transfer using the wrong layout. Grepping `self.arch` for arch-conditional branches in the SM80 base class surfaces exactly one candidate: `get_smem_store_atom` in the epilogue. The branch picks the SM90 `stmatrix` path for any arch ≥ 90, but `stmatrix` is hardware-paired with WGMMA's output register layout, not SM80 MMA's. Patch is one literal arg change.

## Test plan

**Hardware:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, capability (12, 0), driver 590.48.01, CUDA 12.8.

**Software:** Python 3.11.15, `torch==2.10.0+cu128`, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.4.2`, this branch installed editable.

### Correctness (240 shapes × 3 backends = 720 evaluations, all pass)

```
dtypes    : fp16, bf16
causal    : True, False
B         : 1, 2
S         : 128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096
heads     : MHA(Hq=Hkv=16), GQA(Hq=16,Hkv=8), MQA(Hq=16,Hkv=1)
D         : 64, 128
backends  : sdpa_bshd (reference), fa4 (default pack_gqa), fa4_no_packgqa
reference : PyTorch SDPA in fp32 on the same inputs

status by backend:
  sdpa_bshd       240 / 240 pass
  fa4             240 / 240 pass
  fa4_no_packgqa  240 / 240 pass
```

FA4's per-shape `max_abs_diff` vs the fp32 SDPA reference is bit-identical to SDPA-bf16's own on 219/240 shapes; the remaining 21 differ by ≤ 3.5e-5 (FP reordering noise).

Before this PR the analogous run was 240 SDPA pass, 80 FA4 "pass" (MHA only — actually producing element-wise diffs of 0.5–3.9 against fp32 reference, flagged `fail` by the harness; the kernel had reported success), 160 FA4 error (GQA/MQA, the `pack_gqa` cute crash).

### Performance

Same harness, 10 warmup + 50 measured iters per cell, `torch.cuda.Event` timing, hard per-process memory cap so we don't disturb other GPU tenants.

| backend | mean TFLOPs/s | peak |
|---|---|---|
| `sdpa_bshd` (PyTorch eager + repeat_interleave for GQA) | 87.9 | 193.7 |
| `fa4` (this PR) | **94.8** | **196.2** |

FA4 speedup vs `sdpa_bshd` across 240 shapes: mean **1.15×**, median 1.07×, max 1.95×, min 0.74×. Biggest FA4 wins are GQA at small S (SDPA pays for `repeat_interleave`); the few shapes where FA4 still loses are S=512 D=128 causal MHA, which is a tile-size tuning opportunity orthogonal to this PR.

## Minimal reproducer for the silent-wrongness bug

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from flash_attn.cute.interface import flash_attn_func

torch.manual_seed(0)
B, S, H, D = 1, 256, 4, 64
dt = torch.bfloat16
q = torch.randn(B, S, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=dt)
k = torch.randn(B, S, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=dt)
v = torch.randn(B, S, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=dt)

out = flash_attn_func(q, k, v, causal=False)
if isinstance(out, tuple):
    out = out[0]

ref = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
    q.float().transpose(1, 2),
    k.float().transpose(1, 2),
    v.float().transpose(1, 2),
).transpose(1, 2).contiguous()

print(f"max abs diff: {(out.float() - ref).abs().max().item():.4f}")
# before this PR: ~0.61   (bf16 elementwise tolerance should be ~0.003)
# after this PR:  ~0.002
```

## Limitations / out of scope

- **Backward pass.** This PR is forward-only. `flash_bwd_postprocess.py:537` calls `get_smem_store_atom(self.arch.major*10+self.arch.minor, ...)` and almost certainly needs the analogous fix when going through `FlashAttentionBackwardSm120`. A backward-correctness check (autograd + `grad.allclose(grad_ref)`) should follow as a separate PR.
- **The cuTeDSL composite-mode flattening (deeper root cause behind commit 3).** Commit 3 only flips the default to `pack_gqa=False` on SM_120; it does not fix `pack_gqa.compute_ptr` or the cuTeDSL behaviour itself. A proper fix lives in either `pack_gqa.compute_ptr` (compute the flat index directly, without relying on the slice preserving compositeness) or in cuTeDSL.
- **No new tile-size tuning for SM_120.** The few shapes where FA4 loses to SDPA after this PR are tile-tuning candidates but out of scope.

items.title: [CuTe, Bwd, SM100] Bound the K/V TMA loads by seqlen_k so unused rows cannot poison dQ (packed varlen and dense seqused_k)
items.body:
Related: #2374, #2999. Forward counterpart: #2983 (merged). SM90 counterpart (stacked on this): #3013.

## Problem

With NaN in K or V rows past `seqused_k` — in a padded packed buffer (`cu_seqlens_k`) or in the dense `(b, s, h, d)` layout — the SM100 backward returns an all-NaN `dQ`; `dK`/`dV` stay finite. This is independent of #2983: with a finite `O` and `D` from that forward fix, `dQ` is still all-NaN, so in the dense layout the loss is clean and only the gradient is poisoned.

The backward is KV-stationary and TMA-loads whole K/V tiles. The masked `dS` is exactly zero past the sequence end, but

- `dP = dO @ V^T` reads the V rows → `0 * NaN = NaN` in the masked `dP` columns;
- `dQ = dS @ K` sums over the whole tile → NaN from the poisoned `dS` **or** directly from NaN K rows.

So unlike the forward, a NaN **K** tail is enough on its own.

## Fix

When `cu_seqlens_k` or `seqused_k` is given, build the K, V and 2-CTA Kt TMA descriptors with `flash_attn.cute.copy_utils.create_ragged_tensor_for_tma_load` (the load-safe 5-D form #2983 introduced) and take one descriptor view per K/V tile with `offset_ragged_tensor_for_tma_load(..., n_block, block_size=tile rows)`, so each load is bounded by the logical length and TMA's own OOB zero-fill clears the tail. Plain dense calls are untouched; no change to the pipeline, barriers or byte counts.

The helpers gain a `rows_dim` argument (K/V are `(s, d, h, b)`, Kt is `(d, s, h, b)`) and a whole-sequence view (`block_size=None`, used by the SM90 forward in #3013); the existing #2983 call sites are unchanged.

Commits: packed-varlen fix → `ruff format` of `flash_bwd_sm100.py` → helper generalisation → dense `seqused_k`.

**Not covered (follow-up):** the dedicated hd256 backward kernel (same hazard, being retired by the hd256 unification series).

## Validation (B200, main `a6fcdfdb`)

- Probe, `seqused_k` 100/256/37/200 over 4×256 K/V rows, packed and dense, NaN past `seqused_k` in K / V / both, hd64 and hd128 (2-CTA): `dQ` NaN count 393216 / 786432 on main → **0**, bitwise equal to the zero-tail run.
- New `test_flash_attn_sm100_bwd_unused_kv_tail` (fp16/bf16 × hd64/128 × causal × MHA/GQA × 2-CTA on/off × packed/dense, 64 cases, FakeTensor pass supported): drives `_flash_attn_bwd` from a clean forward, so independent of #2983. Fails on main (`k: dq has NaN/Inf`), 64/64 here.
- Existing tests: every test selected by `-k "unused or seqused"` (226, including #2983's 146) passes; earlier, 400 sampled `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` with `cu_seqlens_k` (hd64/128) → 0 failures and 160 sampled `deterministic=True` → 0 failures.
- Backward-only timing, alternating rounds main vs PR (µs, median of 15×30; B4 H16 bf16): every packed and dense shape within ±2 % (the hd128 `seqused_k` rows, noisy over 3 rounds, re-measured over 8 rounds), dense control identical.

| shape (B4 H16 bf16) | main | PR | PR/main |
|---|---|---|---|
| packed S2048 hd64 non-causal / causal | 248.1 / 182.4 | 250.3 / 184.4 | 1.009 / 1.011 |
| packed S2048 hd128 non-causal / causal (2-CTA) | 383.5 / 264.2 | 383.9 / 268.0 | 0.999 / 1.014 |
| packed uneven + seqused_k hd64 non-causal / causal | 145.2 / 107.3 | 145.4 / 108.8 | 1.001 / 1.014 |
| packed uneven + seqused_k hd128 non-causal / causal (8 rounds) | 208.8 / 168.1 | 207.5 / 166.4 | 0.994 / 0.989 |
| dense + seqused_k S2048 hd64 non-causal / causal | 181.9 / 111.0 | 182.1 / 111.3 | 1.001 / 1.003 |
| dense + seqused_k S2048 hd128 non-causal / causal (8 rounds) | 267.8 / 159.3 | 268.2 / 159.4 | 1.002 / 1.001 |
| dense S2048 hd64 / hd128 causal (control) | 168.8 / 233.9 | 168.7 / 234.0 | 0.999 / 1.000 |

items.title: [CuTe, Fwd] Fix PackGQA predication for padded head dimensions
items.body:
## Summary

Fix the CuTe PackGQA load/store predicates for head dimensions that are 8-byte-vector aligned but not multiples of 16 elements, such as 72, 88, 104, 120, and 136.

PackGQA slices Q loads and O stores into one K group. The sliced copy operand retains its vector layout, while the old predicate contains only one Boolean transaction value. CuTe IR verification therefore rejects the default GQA path.

Representative main failures:

- `D=72, Dv=64`: expected predicate shape `((8),(1))`, got `(1,(1))`;
- `D=64, Dv=72`: expected predicate shape `((8,1),(1))`, got `(1,(1))`.

The patch materializes a Boolean fragment matching the sliced operand and fills it with the existing transaction predicate. The branch is compile-time eliminated when no head-dimension predicate is needed.

## Correctness coverage

RTX 5090 / SM120:

- unmodified main: the first three representative dense cases fail during IR verification;
- patch: 25 focused real-GPU cases pass;
- patch: 24 dense FakeTensor compile cases pass;
- BF16 and FP16;
- causal and non-causal;
- `D/Dv` combinations `(72,64)`, `(64,72)`, `(88,88)`, `(104,104)`, `(120,120)`, and `(136,136)`;
- varlen coverage and FP32-reference numerical checks;
- tests exercise the public default dispatch, where GQA automatically selects PackGQA.

## RTX 5090 performance

BF16/FP16, batch 1, 8 Q heads / 1 KV head, D=72. Each cell uses seven alternating unpacked/PackGQA timing blocks with 50 launches per block. Values are `pack_gqa=False latency / PackGQA latency`; greater than 1 means PackGQA is faster.

| dtype | sequence | non-causal | causal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 | 512 | 1.052x | 0.997x |
| BF16 | 2048 | 1.003x | 0.967x |
| BF16 | 8192 | 1.002x | 1.125x |
| FP16 | 512 | 1.064x | 0.998x |
| FP16 | 2048 | 1.004x | 0.967x |
| FP16 | 8192 | 1.001x | 1.168x |

The 12-cell geometric mean is 1.027x. The optimization is shape-dependent: causal S2048 is about 3.3% slower, while causal S8192 is 12.5%-16.8% faster. This PR's primary capability is making the already-selected default PackGQA path compile and run for these dimensions; it does not claim a universal speedup.

## Related work and scope

#2634 introduced related full-fragment predicates in partial-row PackGQA branches. Its current tile-aligned generic path still retains the compressed predicate and reproduces this padded-dimension failure, so the focused fix remains independently useful.

The global predicate helper, TMA paths, pointer/layout mapping, and backward kernels are intentionally unchanged.

items.title: [De-quant findings]
items.body: Hi, i was looking into turbo quant[1]. And for inference, i thought why not add it to for possible faster inference. The paper highlights 2 de-quant methods, for both their respective bottom half portion[2], [3]. Specifically, i was looking into impl the inverse quantization part of the paper[4], for two reasons. a. support on serving side like vLLM, SGLang is already being requested, if serving side handles the quant, it would be nice if the de-quantization is handled with FA b. The rotation that occurs, both for quant and de-quant, actually has a overhead of O(d) dequant per KV row. I figured this can be minimized, the dequant portion. But what I didn't know was just whether the dequant's O(d) compute is cheaper than the bandwidth saved by loading 4x less data (16 -> 4). For baseline on H100, it was 46 us. --- **V1** — With the first version, i added a de-quant path to kv_cache that did this: load packed 4-bit data → unpack → codebook lookup → write fp16 to shared memory. This came to 3,823 us The performance was worse but expected for a first version, it was: - single thread - unroll=1, no optimization --- **V2** — Int32 vectorized loads where changed from byte loads to Int32 loads (4 bytes at a time), 16 loads instead of 64, using range_constexpr for full unrolling. This came to 3,205 us This was slightly better but still used single thread per row, and codebook lookup still generating branch-heavy code. --- **V3** — Fully unrolled both the Int32 iteration and per-element unpacking with range_constexpr. The codebook lookup `cb[code]` with a register tensor and dynamic index generated a compiler switch/case. This came to 500 us This was the biggest improve so far, but i left it at one thread per row. --- **V4** — I tried `cb[code]` lookup with arithmetic: `val = t * poly(t²)` using precomputed odd polynomial coefficients, my assumption was it would take a load off the branch-heavy lookup code. This was significantly worse at 2,338 us. --- **V5** — Since `for k in range_constexpr(cute.size(tXsX, mode=[2]))` loop already distributes column chunks across threads via `gmem_thr_copy_KV`, i thought why not make the dequant to load and process only 1 Int32 (8 elements) per thread per k iteration. This removed the 1 thread doing 128 elements, and instead moved to 16 threads each do 8 elements in parallel. This went down to 123 us. --- ### Full Benchmarks ``` GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 Config: bf16, GQA 32 query heads / 8 KV heads, head_dim=128, page_size=64, causal, seqlen_q=1 (decode) ``` **Baseline** (fp16 paged KV, non-TMA cp.async path) ``` b=1 sk=2048: 46 us b=1 sk=4096: 59 us b=1 sk=8192: 111 us b=1 sk=16384: 220 us b=8 sk=4096: 66 us b=16 sk=4096: 94 us ``` **v1** — Byte-by-byte serial load, register codebook ``` b=1 sk=2048: 3823 us (81x slower) b=1 sk=4096: 7691 us (130x slower) b=1 sk=8192: 15559 us (140x slower) b=1 sk=16384: 31398 us (143x slower) b=8 sk=4096: 7968 us (121x slower) b=16 sk=4096: 8090 us (86x slower) ``` **v2** — Int32 vectorized loads, constexpr unrolled loops ``` b=1 sk=2048: 3205 us (68x slower, 16% faster than v1) b=1 sk=4096: 6411 us (109x slower, 17% faster than v1) b=1 sk=8192: 12868 us (116x slower, 17% faster than v1) b=1 sk=16384: 25997 us (118x slower, 17% faster than v1) b=8 sk=4096: 14382 us (218x slower) b=16 sk=4096: 15196 us (162x slower) ``` **v3** — Fully unrolled cb[code] with constexpr inner loops ``` b=1 sk=2048: 570 us (12x slower, 5.6x faster than v2) b=1 sk=4096: 1138 us (19x slower, 5.6x faster than v2) b=1 sk=8192: 2282 us (21x slower, 5.6x faster than v2) b=1 sk=16384: 4807 us (22x slower, 5.4x faster than v2) b=8 sk=4096: 2529 us (38x slower) b=16 sk=4096: 2922 us (31x slower) ``` **v4** — Polynomial approximation *(REVERTED)* ``` b=1 sk=2048: 2338 us (50x slower, 4x SLOWER than v3) b=1 sk=4096: 4755 us (81x slower, 4x SLOWER than v3) b=1 sk=8192: 9688 us (87x slower) b=1 sk=16384: 19349 us (88x slower) b=8 sk=4096: 6645 us b=16 sk=4096: 7873 us ``` **v5** — Parallelized dequant across thread partitions ``` b=1 sk=2048: 122 us (2.7x slower, 4.7x faster than v3) b=1 sk=4096: 240 us (4.1x slower, 4.7x faster than v3) b=1 sk=8192: 476 us (4.3x slower, 4.8x faster than v3) b=1 sk=16384: 1135 us (5.2x slower, 4.2x faster than v3) b=8 sk=4096: 350 us (5.3x slower, 7.2x faster than v3) b=16 sk=4096: 363 us (3.9x slower, 8x faster than v3) ``` --- All benchmarks were standard flash_attn_func(q, k, v, causal=True) with pre-existing fp16 K and V tensors (non-paged). ### Further Work My hopes was to just share this information, if useful, as well as some advice. I was thinking of a single fused kernel of quantized load_KV branch as a standalone CUDA C kernel compiled separately, which might come to ~3-4 us extra but, if we factor in the 3-4x speedup over baseline, it would mean not much. I will explore that and share my findings. I welcome feedback, any advice or comments. 1. https://research.google/blog/turboquant-redefining-ai-efficiency-with-extreme-compression/ 2. 3. 4. https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/compare/main...Lazarus-931:flash-attention:turboquant-dequant

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Support 1..128 Q heads in sparse MLA via in-kernel TMA padding
items.body:
Stacked PRs:
 * #2884
 * __->__#2883


--- --- ---

## Human Note

Support [1, 128] Q heads in the public sparse MLA (DSA) forward and backward paths. I saw that there was a comment for supporting n_qheads = 64 not sure if you planned to do something fancier here. I did the easy thing (just pad out).  This does infact come up both for dsv4 flash and when doing tp sharding. I found this when trying to integrate into torchtitan. I consider this a naive unblock but it does help :)


I thought about the multi tokens e.g. true pack-gqa but didnt want to visit the union + masking (although ill prototype this) -> same reason why I didnt support this for blocksparse impl

## Agent Notes
TMA pads heads inside the kernel without padded operand copies in global memory. This enables training with 64-head models and tensor-parallel shards.

Each forward tile still covers one token and one top-k gather list: 2-CTA UMMA, 128 packed Q heads, 64 rows per CTA, with K/V split across the pair. Backward uses a 64- or 128-head tile. The dQ/dQv GEMM keeps its 128-row tile with a dynamic head extent.

Unchanged: attention math, the 128-head TMA path, MMA tile sizes, and pipeline synchronization.

### Mechanism

- `padded_qheads_tma_source` builds a heads-first view `(h, d, s, b)` with a dynamic head extent, so CuTe tiles it without requiring divisibility. TMA zero-fills out-of-bounds loads and drops out-of-bounds stores. `regroup_padded_qheads` restores the packed coordinate layout `((tile, s), d, 1, b)`.
- LSE, row_max, and learnable-sink accesses guard the packed head index. Without guards, the hierarchical packed layout wraps padded heads into the next token.
- TMA loads zero padded Q rows in forward and dO/P rows in backward. These rows produce `dS = 0` and contribute nothing to dK/dV. Only `scaleP`/`dPsum` need tile-width global buffers with finite padding.

### Two latent bugs

1. **Backward dV staging at `tile_m=64`.** The split-0 epilogue could overwrite dOt/Qvt operands still used by the split-1 MMA, producing NaNs in `dV[:, 256:]`. If staging equals one operand stage, each split now stages in place over its consumed stage. Otherwise, both splits take turns using one staging area allocated after the operands.
2. **Non-power-of-two preprocess tiles.** A 48-row tile (2 tokens × 24 heads) produced incorrect `dpsum`. Padded head counts now use trivial packing (`qhead_per_kvhead=1, nheads_kv=H`) with the existing 128-row tile. Not all head counts divide that tile; resizing it to a non-power-of-two is not a valid workaround.

### Validation (GB200)

- Sentinel-focused run: 44 passed. `test_flash_attn_mla_sparse_bwd_sentinel` covers H ∈ {128, 64, 96, 24, 1} × shared_kv × causal × 2 lengths.
- `test_flash_attn_mla_absorbed`: 96 BF16 cases passed for `1024-1024` and `255-1025`, including the 128-head path.
- Probe against global-memory padding to 128 heads, H ∈ {1, 8, 16, 24, 48, 64, 72, 96, 100, 120}: out/LSE/P/row_max/dQ/dQv bit-identical; dK/dV within 1e-5.

### Performance at DeepSeek-V4 shapes

Measurement contract: GB200, B=1, D_qk = D_v = 512, shared KV, sliding window 128 + compressed causal top-k, via attention-gym `selected_attention`. Flash uses top-k 512; pro uses top-k 1024. Times are medians over CUDA-graph replays, in µs per call (lower is better). Peak memory is MB (lower is better).

Calculated rates (higher is better): fwd FLOPs = 2*T*H*K*(D_qk + D_v), K = valid gathered slots (top-k + window); bwd FLOPs = 2.5× fwd. TB/s counts gathered KV rows plus Q read and O write.

| T | config | fwd us | fwd TFLOPS | fwd TB/s | bwd us | bwd TFLOPS | fwd+bwd us | peak MB |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 | flash H=64 in-kernel pad | 859 | 400 | 3.75 | 1874 | 458 | 2733 | 2114 |
| 4096 | flash H=64 gmem pad->128 | 1061 | 324 | 3.04 | 2835 | 303 | 3896 | 4557 |
| 4096 | H=128, flash topk 512 | 918 | 749 | 4.10 | 2465 | 697 | 3382 | 4046 |
| 4096 | pro H=128 topk 1024 | 1349 | 917 | 4.38 | 3798 | 814 | 5147 | 5109 |
| 8192 | flash H=64 in-kernel pad | 1666 | 412 | 3.87 | 3702 | 464 | 5368 | 4095 |
| 8192 | H=128, flash topk 512 | 1775 | 774 | 4.24 | 4876 | 705 | 6651 | 7959 |
| 8192 | pro H=128 topk 1024 | 2650 | 933 | 4.46 | 7539 | 820 | 10189 | 10087 |
| 16384 | flash H=64 in-kernel pad | 3293 | 417 | 3.91 | 7347 | 468 | 10640 | 8061 |
| 16384 | H=128, flash topk 512 | 3506 | 784 | 4.29 | 9723 | 707 | 13229 | 15789 |
| 16384 | pro H=128 topk 1024 | 5262 | 940 | 4.49 | 15029 | 823 | 20292 | 20045 |

At T=4096, H=64 in-kernel padding reduces fwd+bwd time by about 30% and peak memory by about half versus global-memory padding. H=64 forward takes about 93% of the H=128 time. NCU on the H=64 forward (T=4096): DRAM throughput 8%, L2 hit rate 74%, 74% of stall cycles are long-scoreboard waits on the per-thread cp.async gather. The forward is gather-latency-bound, so the padded MMA rows cost little; the gather itself is the lever for a follow-up.

Separate T=2048 comparison: GB200, top-k 512, D=512, fwd+bwd via attention-gym `selected_attention`; time in µs per call (lower is better).

| Configuration | fwd+bwd us |
|---|---:|
| H=64 in-kernel padding | 1416 |
| Native H=128 | 1740 |

items.title: [CuTe] Add typed forward configurations
items.body:
Stacked PRs:
 * #2743
 * #2741
 * #2738
 * #2735
 * #3034
 * #2733
 * __->__#2732

--- --- ---

## Human Note

## Agent Notes

This adds the typed config layer for FA4 forward in a new `flash_attn/cute/config.py`; nothing calls it yet.
#2733 routes `_flash_attn_fwd` through it, and the tuning PRs higher in the stack change policy on top of it.
Landing the model and its tests first keeps the routing diff about plumbing and the tuning diffs about policy.

- `FwdConfig` is a frozen dataclass holding one fully resolved forward choice: `tile_m`/`tile_n`, the SM90
  `mma_pv_is_rs`/`intra_wg_overlap` flags, `q_stage`, `num_splits` (where 1 means no split and anything larger
  is the exact SplitKV count), and the SM100 switches `use_2cta_instrs`, `use_clc_scheduler`,
  `is_static_persistent`, `use_tma_o` and `use_s_ping_pong`, plus `registers`: the per-role register split
  (`Sm90Registers` producer/MMA, `Sm100Registers` softmax/correction/other, `None` on SM80/SM120).
- `FwdHeuristicInputs` is an immutable `NamedTuple` of host-visible metadata: device arch and SM count, dtype,
  head dims, head counts, sequence bounds, and feature presence bits. It also carries the legacy request knobs
  (`requested_tile_m`, `requested_num_splits`, `disable_2cta`, ...). Features that are absent take defaults.
- `select_fwd_config(inputs)` (LRU-cached) reproduces the current inline forward policy and validates its own
  result. `validate_fwd_config(config, inputs)` rejects unsupported explicit configs instead of normalizing them.
  Each SM100 feature has one support predicate (`is_2cta_eligible`, `can_use_clc`, `can_use_static_persistent`,
  `can_use_tma_o`, `can_use_s_ping_pong`) that selection and validation share, so the selector cannot pick a
  config that validation would reject.
- `select_registers` resolves the split after the final tile, stage and 2CTA choices, from the kernels' former
  inline tables (`SM100_TUNING`, `SM100_FP8_TUNING` and the SM90 TMA-Q/KV rule), which now live in `config.py`.
  `validate_registers` checks direction and budget: SM100 softmax >= 128, other <= 128 and
  `q_stage*softmax + correction + (3-q_stage)*other <= 512`; SM90 producer <= launch <= MMA and
  `num_wg*mma + producer <= 512`.

Review order: `FwdConfig` and `FwdHeuristicInputs`, then the support predicates, then `select_fwd_config` and
`validate_fwd_config`, then `tests/cute/test_fwd_config.py`.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- Policy parity: the selector covers hd256 on the generic SM100 kernel, S/P ping-pong (with minimum KV blocks per
  split under SplitKV), the 2CTA and static-persistence rules, the hd256 single-wave decode 2CTA case, and the
  legacy diff-head split re-selection (`tile_n=64`, or one split for short KV or DV512). That re-selection also
  re-resolves a requested split count, as the old `num_splits` argument did; an explicit `FwdConfig` is the way to
  force an exact diff-head split.
- `select_sm90_tile`, `fit_sm90_tile_to_block_sparsity` and `num_splits_heuristic` copy the logic of
  `_tile_size_fwd_sm90`, `_fit_sm90_fwd_tile_to_block_sparsity` and `num_splits_heuristic` in `interface.py`,
  returning plain tuples. The `interface.py` versions (and its existing `FwdConfig` tile record) stay in place
  until #2733 switches callers.
- Automatic split selection resolves to one split outside SM100/SM110, the only kernels with SplitKV; the old
  inline path ran the split heuristic on SM80/SM90 and then failed the kernel's SplitKV assertion. An explicit
  split count other than 1 on SM120 raises `ValueError` (the old inline path asserted).
- A new rule: a SplitKV config with fewer splits than a fixed `seqlen_k_per_split` extent requires is rejected,
  and automatic selection raises the split count to cover that extent. `seqlen_k_per_split` must also be
  divisible by `tile_n`.
- Validation also checks tile geometry, the SM90 `tile_m` set, the 512-column TMEM budget for S and O,
  SplitKV head-dim limits, non-TMA paged KV head-dim alignment, and per-architecture support: outside SM100/SM110,
  configs must use `q_stage=1`, one split and no SM100 scheduler options, and only SM90 may set the SM90 flags.
- `sm100_hd192_uneven_kv_smem_bytes` mirrors the hd 192/128 uneven three-stage KV plan in
  `FlashAttentionForwardSm100`, so explicit `tile_n` values that would not fit in shared memory fail at
  validation. Its overhead constant is calibrated to the observed launch failure at `tile_n=192` (247808 bytes).
  The one-line comment in `flash_fwd_sm100.py` points at this mirror.
- Register parity: `test_*_registers_match_the_legacy_kernel_policy` compare `select_registers` against a frozen
  copy of the kernels' inline register code over dtype, head dim, causal, 2CTA, arch family, paged/TMA and
  `q_stage`, and through `select_fwd_config` for hd256 decode, FP8 2CTA and SM90. A compile-time capture of 960
  kernels on sm_100/sm_103/sm_90 matched main's register split everywhere at this commit.
- SM100 validation requires `tile_m=128`: each softmax warp group owns 128 rows, and smaller tiles would overrun
  the row statistics in shared memory.
- MLA (`qv`) forward is out of scope; it keeps its own kernel, tile and split routing in `interface.py`.

</details>

items.title: [CuTe, SM100] Sparse MLA bwd: keep P normalization and dS product in fp32
items.body:
## Summary

The softmax warps of the sparse-MLA backward (`flash_bwd_mla_sm100.py`) rounded three intermediates to bf16 before forming `dS = P ⊙ (dP − dPsum) · softmax_scale`: the normalization scale `scale_p`, the normalized `P`, and `(dP − dPsum) · softmax_scale`. This PR keeps an fp32 copy of `P^T` and forms the product in fp32, rounding to bf16 exactly once for the dS store.

- **Load-P path (default):** the saved bf16 `p` is upcast, normalized with the fp32 `scale_p`, and rounded to bf16 once for the `dV += P^T·dO` mma operand; the fp32 copy is used for dS.
- **Recompute-P path (`gather_bwd_recompute_p=True`):** the fp32 `exp2` result already exists; it now stays live for dS instead of being re-read from the bf16 staging copy.
- Unchanged: forward kernel, saved activations, dS storage dtype, all mma operand dtypes, smem layout.
- `AI/SPARSE_MLA_RECOMPUTE_P.md` numerics section updated.

Both backward paths (load-P and recompute-P) get the same treatment so their dS numerics stay on one scheme.

## Validation (GB200, CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1, torch 2.14)

- `pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k mla_sparse`: **34 passed** (sentinel, sentinel_varlen, recompute_p, fully_masked_rows, token_chunk_rect, token_chunk_varlen, learnable_sink).
- `pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k "mla_absorbed and True-64-"` (the 104 `kv_sparsity=True` cases): 88 passed, then case `[0-1-8192-False-True-64-False-0-False-False-mqa-dtype0]` (seqlen_q=1, seqlen_k=8192) hit a CUDA illegal memory access whose sticky error failed the rest of that process. The same case fails identically on unmodified `main` (e81a70c) in a standalone run, so it is pre-existing and unrelated to this change. Rerunning the other 96 `kv_sparsity=True` cases in a fresh process: **96 passed**.
- `pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k mla_absorbed_varlen` (832 cases, all `kv_sparsity=True`): the first `seqlen_q=1, seqlen_k=4096` case hits the same illegal memory access (also reproduced standalone on unmodified `main`), taking the rest of that process down. Excluding the 128 `seqlen_q=1` cases and rerunning: **704 passed**, 0 failed.
- Net: every sparse-MLA backward test that does not hit the pre-existing `seqlen_q=1` fault passes (34 + 96 + 704).
- Main backward kernel resource usage (`cuFuncGetAttribute` + `nvdisasm` on dumped cubins), 512 threads:

| Kernel | regs/thread | local bytes/thread | STL | LDL | SASS insts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| load-P, main | 128 | 560 | 91 | 101 | 3987 |
| load-P, this PR | 128 | 560 | 80 | 83 | 4027 |
| recompute-P, main | 128 | 1024 | 134 | 136 | 5390 |
| recompute-P, this PR | 128 | 248 | 57 | 65 | 5393 |

## GB200 benchmark

One GB200, bf16, B=1, 128 q heads (`pack_gqa=True`), 1 kv head, rope/latent dims 64/512, top-k 2048, T = S = 16K and 32K, seeded synthetic inputs (seed 1234), indices sampled from the causal window, `causal=False`. Accuracy is relative L2 error against an independent chunked **fp64** reference that includes the fully accumulated dK/dV over all rows. Timing is the mean of 2 runs × 100 CUDA-event-timed calls each (5 warmup), variant order main→PR→PR→main, compilation excluded. Forward `out`/`lse` hashes are bitwise identical between main and this PR in every configuration. Script: `agent_space/fp32-ds/bench_fp32_ds.py` (local scratch, not part of the PR).

### Load-P path (default)

| Metric, main → this PR | 16K | 32K |
|---|---:|---:|
| dQ rel-L2 error | 0.4013% → 0.2850% (**−29.0%**) | 0.4032% → 0.2861% (**−29.0%**) |
| dQv rel-L2 error | 0.3294% → 0.2335% (**−29.1%**) | 0.3232% → 0.2288% (**−29.2%**) |

### Recompute-P path (`gather_bwd_recompute_p=True`)

|---|---:|---:|
| dQ rel-L2 error | 0.3353% → 0.2393% (**−28.6%**) | 0.3343% → 0.2382% (**−28.7%**) |
| dQv rel-L2 error | 0.2650% → 0.2060% (**−22.3%**) | 0.2572% → 0.2021% (**−21.4%**) |

Notes:
- Max-abs errors also drop for every gradient in every configuration except load-P dV at 16K (0.176 → 0.176, unchanged); e.g. load-P 16K dQ 0.033 → 0.015, dK 0.091 → 0.059.
- dQ/dQv are deterministic; dK/dV are fp32-atomic accumulations with small run-to-run order noise.
- The recompute-P backward is ~1% slower despite fewer spills (fp32 `P^T` is now live across the dP TMEM wait). If that matters, the recompute path could instead upcast the bf16 staged `P^T` at the dS step (keeps the fp32 `(dP − dPsum)·scale` product but reintroduces one P rounding); not done here to keep both paths on the same, more accurate scheme.
